The other disabled modernize analyzers (`atomictypes`, etc.) remain disabled and will be tackled in follow-up PRs.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: allow boundary attestations while head state lags
body:
## Summary
- allow attestation validation to accept the next epoch when forkchoice has seen it or the local clock has reached it
- keep aggregate-and-proof validation conservative by only widening to epochs forkchoice has actually seen
- add focused tests for next-epoch boundary acceptance and beyond-next-epoch rejection

## Root cause
At epoch boundaries on Chiado, the validator client could request aggregates for the next epoch while Caplin's head state still pointed at the previous epoch. The first r3.5 fix handled the case where forkchoice had already seen the next epoch, but production logs showed cases where the local slot had crossed the boundary while the next epoch block was not imported yet.

## Validation
- go test ./cl/phase1/network/services -count=1
- focused boundary tests in cl/phase1/network/services
- make lint
- git diff --check

Main-port of the fix deployed and observed on Chiado via release/3.5 PR #22251.
author: domiwei

title: cl, db/snapshotsync: don't freeze empty caplin block/state roots
body:
Caplin state reconstruction that anchors below a checkpoint leaves the pre-anchor history unreconstructed. `dumpCaplinState` reads each slot's value from the DB and freezes it verbatim, checking only the word count — so an un-reconstructed (or already-pruned) range is frozen as `block_roots`/`state_roots` segments full of empty words. `process_slot` writes those roots every slot, so an empty word is never valid state. The blank segments then shadow the DB (snapshots take read precedence) and inflate `BlocksAvailable`, so historical-state reads for the range break and the antiquary treats the range as done and never reconstructs it. Two adjacent caplin-state snapshot bugs are fixed alongside: `.idx`-path derivation broke when the datadir path itself contained `.seg`, and a 15s fsync sleep needlessly widened the window where a `.seg` is published before its `.idx`.

## Changes
- `dumpCaplinState` refuses to freeze an empty `block_roots`/`state_roots` word (`errIncompleteStateRange`), gated to those two dense tables; a non-empty word of the wrong length is surfaced as corruption. The caller logs and skips the range, which stays unfrozen and is retried once the DB is repopulated. Other caplin-state tables are legitimately sparse and keep dumping empties.
- `readHistoryHashVector`/`ReadRequiredQueueSSZ` return a typed `ErrMissingHistoryVectorData` for a missing dense entry, and the antiquary backs off to re-antiquate past it (alongside `ErrMissingGloasData`) instead of a hard fatal.
- `openIdxIfNeedForCaplinState` derives the `.idx` path by trimming only the trailing `.seg` extension, so a datadir path that itself contains `.seg` no longer corrupts it.
- Dropped the 15s fsync grace-period sleep before index build: the compressor already fsyncs and atomically renames the `.seg`, so there is no read-after-rename window; the existing un-indexed-segment invisibility gate keeps the (now-narrower) publish-before-index window safe.
author: awskii

title: cl, engineapi: encode client versions in default block graffiti
body:
## What

When a validator proposes a block without specifying graffiti, Caplin now fills the graffiti with the client-version encoding from the [client identification standard](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/identification.md) instead of the literal `"Caplin"` string:

```
<EL code><EL commit><CN><CL commit>    e.g. EGa53eCNa53e
```

This lets client-diversity tooling attribute proposed blocks to both their execution and consensus clients. Today an Erigon + Caplin node leaves no execution-client fingerprint in its blocks.

## Why

Execution-layer client diversity is largely unmeasurable from block data. The standard addresses this by having the consensus client embed the execution and consensus client codes and their commit prefixes in the default graffiti. Caplin previously emitted only the literal `"Caplin"`, contributing no execution-client signal.

## How

- Adds `GetClientVersionV1` to the `ExecutionEngine` interface; Caplin obtains the execution client's code and commit via `engine_getClientVersionV1`. The result is cached, so steady-state block production performs no extra engine API calls.
- Caplin identifies itself with the reserved consensus client code `CN`.
- When the execution client does not support the method, the graffiti degrades to the consensus-client identifier only (`CN<commit>`).
- User-specified graffiti is unchanged.
- Deduplicates the local client-version construction into `engine_types.NewClientVersionV1` / `LocalClientVersionV1`, now shared by the engine API handler and the in-process execution client.

## Dependency

Caplin's consensus client code `CN` is registered in ethereum/execution-apis#844. This change can merge independently: the encoding works before registration (consumers must accept any two-letter code), and attribution tooling recognizes `CN` once that PR lands.

## Testing

- New `cl/beacon/handler/block_production_graffiti_test.go`: encoding, execution-client-unavailable fallback, no-engine fallback, and cache behavior (the engine is queried once across multiple proposals).
- `make lint`, `go vet`, and the affected package tests pass.
author: lystopad

title: cl, execution: don't log context canceled on shutdown
body:
## Summary

- Silence the `closing backfilling routine` WARN in `cl/phase1/stages/stage_history_download.go` when it fires because of a canceled context (normal shutdown), not an actual downloader failure.
- Same fix for `Could not notify fork validator of current height` in `execution/execmodule/exec_module.go`, matching the `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` convention already used twice earlier in the same `Start` function for the semaphore-acquire and `ProcessFrozenBlocks` error paths.

No behavior change beyond suppressing the log line — control flow and return values are unchanged.

TDD note: skipped per the pragmatism carve-out in CLAUDE.md — this is a narrow, mechanical consistency fix (extends an already-established local pattern) with no functional behavior change, so a dedicated regression test would require disproportionate harness/log-capture scaffolding relative to the 3-line diff.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/persistence: fix caplin historical state reconstruction loop at bellatrix transition
body:
#### **What was the issue?**
The first Bellatrix-era slot is `4,636,672`. Since the Merge did not happen yet at this point, this block has an empty execution payload header with `BlockHash = 0x000...000` and `BlockNumber = 0`. 

Previously, if the block version was post-Altair, we were unconditionally trying to fetch EL transactions. This means we queried `executionReader.Transactions(0, 0x00...)`. 

Because of a recent change (commit [`04d330df0b`](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/commit/04d330df0b3a9a52135358ebcdcc7132e15029f7) which routes block `0` queries to the database instead of snapshots), this lookup went to the DB. Since the database requires a matching hash and the zero hash doesn't match our real genesis block hash, it returned `nil`, throwing the error: `transactions not found for block 0`. This caused the antiquary loop to crash and rollback to the previous checkpoint, looping forever.

#### **What is the fix?**
We added a simple check to check if the execution payload `blockHash` is the zero hash. If it is, this is a pre-Merge block where execution is not yet active under consensus rules, so we skip the EL transaction/withdrawal lookup completely. 

Checking the block hash instead of the block number also keeps custom networks safe where execution block `0` can have a valid non-zero block hash.

closes #22337
author: Sahil-4555

title: cl/antiquary: commit reconstructed state in bounded batches SEGV
body:
`IncrementBeaconState` accumulated up to `timeBeforeCommit` (30 min) of replayed beacon state into a single mdbx transaction. On large caplin indexing DBs (archive mainnet/hoodi, 100+ GB) that one commit overflows libmdbx's `gc_fill_returned` while serializing the transaction's retired-page list, faulting with `SIGSEGV (SEGV_ACCERR)` in `txn_basal_commit`. `rp_augment_limit` scales with DB size, so only large DBs reach the regime.

## Changes
- Flush + commit every `maxSlotsPerCommit` (`4 * SlotsPerDump`) slots and start a fresh collector, so no single commit carries a huge retired-page list.
- Extract the flush/commit path into one `commitBatch` closure, used for both the in-loop bounded commits and the final remainder.
- Throughput unchanged: a call still processes up to `timeBeforeCommit` of slots, now split across bounded commits.
- `TestStateAntiquaryCommitIsBounded`: bounded and single-commit runs reconstruct identical slots, and the bounded run commits more often.
author: awskii

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: replace latestMessagesStore interning with a flat per-validator slice
body:
Fixes #22351

## Summary

Replace `latestMessagesStore`'s deduplicating inverted index (`messageByIdx`/`idxByMessage`/`countOfMessages`/`currID`) with a flat `[]LatestMessage` indexed by validator — the same shape as the spec's `Store.latest_messages`. `set`/`get` become O(1) with no pruning and no id space.

## Problem

The interning store ran `doPrune()` on **every** `set()`, scanning the whole `countOfMessages` map (and allocating a slice) while `OnAttestation` holds the fork-choice exclusive lock — roughly 27k times per slot on mainnet. Two mechanisms make the scanned map grow with uptime:

- entries leave the map only at zero refcount, so any validator that stops voting pins its last message forever, and since `LatestMessage` gained a `Slot` field every `(epoch, root, slot)` combination is distinct (~30-100 new entries per epoch);
- `currID` is a `uint16` that wraps every 65,536 distinct messages (~3-5 days on mainnet), after which `messageByIdx[currID] = m` clobbers ids still referenced by live votes — count bookkeeping then decrements the wrong entries, the map grows without bound, and `get()` returns wrong votes (LMD weight corruption).

On an affected mainnet validator node (7 days uptime) this held the fork-choice lock for 1.5-2.5s per slot: goroutine samples showed `OnAttestation` inside `doPrune`'s map range in 12 of 12 samples where the stage loop's `GetHead` was blocked on `f.mu`, pushing FCU (p50 3.35s / p90 4.40s from slot start) and head-state publication (~4.5s median REST-visible) past the 4s attestation deadline. Full evidence in #22351.

The old grow path additionally lost all stored votes: growing `latestMessages` past capacity did `make()` without `copy()`.

## Trade-off

Memory goes from ~2B to ~56B per registry index (~123MB at today's ~2.2M mainnet registry; ~246MB at a hypothetical 2x), in exchange for removing the O(map)-per-vote scan and the id-wrap corruption class from the consensus hot path. The constructor no longer pre-allocates 1.5x capacity; growth amortizes at 1.5x inside `set` on the rare occasion the registry outgrows the anchor-state length.

## TDD

Both tests were written first and fail on the old implementation for the intended reasons:

- `TestLatestMessagesStoreSetSurvivesDistinctMessageChurn` — a pinned vote is lost after >65,536 distinct messages churn through another validator's slot (uint16 wrap);
- `TestLatestMessagesStoreGrowthPreservesEntries` — growing past capacity wipes previously stored votes (missing `copy`).

`BenchmarkLatestMessagesStoreSetWithPinnedMessages` (10k pinned distinct messages, mirrors the mainnet shape): **61,418 ns/op → 8.5 ns/op**. At ~27k `set` calls per slot that is ~1.66s of fork-choice-lock hold time per slot removed, matching the stall observed live.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... -count=1` green
- `make lint` clean (two consecutive runs)

An `[r3.5]` backport will follow once this merges.
author: lystopad

title: cl: repair permanently-truncated caplin static validators table
body:
Caplin historical-state reconstruction can loop forever. The `StaticValidatorTable` is persisted to `kv.StaticValidators` and restored at startup with `slot = StateProcessingProgress`. Once it is persisted incomplete (fewer entries than the validator set — e.g. a partial `Fill` off empty state-event snapshots that then advanced the slot), it becomes permanently unrepairable: `FillStaticValidatorsTableIfNeeded` early-returns when `slot != 0`, and genesis-init's `AddValidator(slot=0)` is skipped by the `slot <= s.slot` guard once the table slot has advanced. Reconstruction then fails at the first proposer slashing of a validator beyond the truncation and retries from genesis forever (seen on hoodi at slot 66082, validator 975067; genesis has 1,060,000 validators).

## Changes
- `AddValidator`: idempotency by index rather than slot — skip already-tracked indices, append the next, error on a gap. A restored-short table is refilled by the genesis re-add instead of skipped.
- `FillStaticValidatorsTableIfNeeded` and genesis-init propagate the `AddValidator` error instead of swallowing it, so a truncated table can no longer be silently persisted with an advanced slot.
- `IncrementBeaconState` refuses to start reconstruction on a table shorter than the state it tracks.

title: cl: `ComputeShuffledIndicies` to not alloc hash on every call
body: ## What `ComputeShuffledIndicies` passes a closure to `eth2shuffle.UnshuffleList` as the hash function. The closure declared `hashed` **inside its body** and returned `hashed[:]`: ```go eth2ShuffleHashFunc := func(data []byte) []byte { hashed := hashFunc(data) // fresh local, escapes → heap alloc every call return hashed[:] } ``` The fix hoists `hashed` into the enclosing function's scope so it is allocated once and reused: ```go var hashed common.Hash eth2ShuffleHashFunc := func(data []byte) []byte { hashed = hashFunc(data) // copy 32 bytes into the captured buffer, no alloc return hashed[:] } ``` ## Why it helps Both versions heap-allocate `hashed` — `return hashed[:]` hands a slice pointing into `hashed` back to `UnshuffleList`, which reads it after the closure returns, so the array must outlive the call and escape analysis moves it to the heap. The difference is **frequency**: - **Before** — `hashed` is declared inside the closure body, so a fresh one is created and escapes on **every invocation**. `UnshuffleList` calls the closure `ShuffleRoundCount` (90) × pivots times per `ComputeShuffledIndicies`, i.e. thousands of allocations per call. - **After** — `hashed` is captured from the outer scope, so it is heap-allocated **once** when the closure is created. Every invocation then just copies 32 bytes into that one buffer. Rule of thumb: an escaping variable is allocated every time the scope it's *declared* in runs. Moving the declaration up one scope turned thousands of allocations into one. ## Why reuse is safe `innerShuffleList` reads each hash result immediately and overwrites it on the next call — it never retains a previous result. Reusing a single backing array across calls is therefore correct, and the hash output bytes are byte-for-byte identical. No consensus semantics change. ## Impact In a CPU/heap profile of Caplin historical-state reconstruction, this closure (`ComputeShuffledIndicies.func1`) was the single largest allocator in the whole process — **~1.17B objects, ~24.5% of all heap allocations** — and fed GC pressure back into the shuffle CPU cost. Committee shuffling also runs constantly during live attestation validation, so this helps the live node, not just archive reconstruction. Micro-benchmark of one `ComputeShuffledIndicies` call over 300k validators: | | allocs/op | B/op | ns/op | |---|---|---|---| | before | 52,974 | 1,696,403 | 48.4M | | after | 9 | 494 | 43.4M | `moved to heap: hashed` now points at the outer `var` (allocated once), and `func literal does not escape`.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/persistence/base_encoding: avoid per-scalar heap allocs in Rabbits codec
body:
## Problem

Heap profiling shows `encoding/binary.Write` accounting for **~10% of all allocations** (475M objects), and 100% of those come from `base_encoding.WriteRabbits`, called on the antiquary state-collection path (`beaconStatesCollector.collectActiveIndices`) that serializes validator index sets.

`binary.Write(w, order, uint64Value)` allocates a fresh `[]byte` for each scalar — the buffer escapes to the heap because it's handed to the `io.Writer` interface. `WriteRabbits` calls it ~2× per non-contiguous run, so serializing a large sparse index set produces hundreds of millions of tiny 8-byte allocations. `ReadRabbits` has the identical anti-pattern via `binary.Read`.

## Fix

Use a single reused 8-byte buffer with `binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64`/`Uint64` and `io.ReadFull` instead of letting `binary.Write`/`binary.Read` allocate per scalar.

## Results

`BenchmarkWriteRabbits` on a 100k-element sparse list (~200k scalar writes):

| | allocs/op | B/op | ns/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 200,080 | 1,652,629 | 3,235,850 |
| after | 78 | 51,502 | 1,313,157 |

~2,565× fewer allocations (residual 78 are zstd internals), ~2.5× faster.

## Wire format: unchanged

The encoding is still a zstd frame of little-endian `uint64` scalars, byte for byte, so existing data reads back identically.

`TestRabbitWriteWireFormat` / `TestRabbitReadWireFormat` pin this against a golden payload (`[0,1,2,5]` → scalars `4,3,2,1`) hand-computed from the format itself rather than captured from either codec — so the assertion doesn't rely on the writer and reader having changed together. Both tests, plus the existing `TestRabbit` round trip, pass **unmodified against the pre-change codec on `main`**; that is what establishes byte-level compatibility.

## Behavior change: malformed input is now rejected

This is not a pure no-op refactor. `ReadRabbits` now validates what it decodes instead of silently returning a truncated or garbage list. It returns an error when:

- the header length overflows `int`
- the decoded element count doesn't match the header
- an active run exceeds the remaining declared elements — this bounds the allocation a corrupt `count` can force, rather than growing `out` far past the header and only noticing at the end
- `current + count` overflows the index space
- the stream ends while a trailing contiguous-run count is still expected (header-only payload). `WriteRabbits` always emits one last, so that shape is corruption
- extra run-length scalars remain after the run that completes the declared output — a trailing gap scalar, or an appended zero-length gap/active pair that doesn't change the decoded list. `WriteRabbits` stops right after the final contiguous run, so the reader now requires immediate EOF there

Each has a subtest in `TestRabbitReadMalformed`. Checked against `main`: every one of those six inputs is currently accepted **silently, with no error** — which is the strictness this PR adds. Truncated scalars mid-stream already errored before and still do (now surfacing `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` from `io.ReadFull`); they're covered too.

Well-formed input produced by `WriteRabbits` is unaffected — `TestRabbit`, `TestRabbitEmpty` (the `length == 0` edge case) and the antiquary / `persistence/state` round-trip tests pass unchanged.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/antiquary: prune caplin state indexing DB after freezing to snapshots
body:
Caplin's indexing DB keeps the entire per-slot state history even after those ranges are frozen to state snapshots. The historical reader serves any covered slot from the `.seg` segment and only falls back to the DB for the un-frozen tail, so every frozen row is dead weight. Nothing pruned it — only beacon *blocks* were pruned, never state — so the DB grows unbounded (a gnosis snapshotter reached ~112GB shadowing ~79GB of the same data already in snapshots).

## Changes

- Prune the frozen state tables from the indexing DB on the antiquary's commit cadence and after each dump.
- Boundary is per-table contiguous-from-genesis snapshot coverage (`ContiguousCoverageEnd`): a row is deleted only when its slot is below the point where every read for that table is already served by an indexed visible segment. Fully-drained sparse/rounded-key tables jump their marker straight to the boundary.
- Deletes run as batched cursor deletes (1000 keys/txn — mdbx dislikes large txns) under an EL-style adaptive time budget, with per-table progress markers (`StatesPruneProgress`) so a pass is resumable and the deadline is only checked at txn boundaries.
- Unconditional under archive-state; `CAPLIN_STATE_PRUNE_DISABLE` turns it off and `CAPLIN_STATE_PRUNE_TIMEOUT` overrides the budget (env only, no new CLI flag).

Prune bounds future growth; it does not shrink the mdbx file (deleted pages are reused, not returned to the OS). The prune set is derived from the state-snapshot schema, so `StaticValidators` and progress markers are excluded by construction.

title: cl: reduce per-call hashing allocations in shuffling, sync committee, merkle proofs
body:
Several Caplin hot paths heap-allocate a hash or scratch buffer on every call — a per-iteration `append`/`make` in sync-committee selection, merkle-branch verification, blob inclusion proofs, and shuffling pre-inputs. Follow-up to #22390, which removed the same per-call allocation in `ComputeShuffledIndicies`.

Pure allocation refactor, no behavior change (identical bytes hashed); covered by the existing shuffling / merkle_proof / fork-upgrade / finality spectests.

## Changes
- `ComputeNextSyncCommittee`: reuse a stack seed buffer and cache the random-bytes hash per group (`i/16` Electra, `i/32` pre-Electra) instead of allocating and re-hashing every iteration — mirrors `ComputeBalanceWeightedSelection`.
- `IsValidMerkleBranch`: hash operands via `Sha256`'s `extras` argument instead of `append`.
- `VerifyCommitmentInclusionProof`: hash from a reused 64-byte buffer.
- `ComputeShuffledIndexPreInputs`: reuse a 33-byte seed buffer.

`IsValidMerkleBranch` at depth 33: 67 → 34 allocs/op, 3201 → 1088 B/op.

title: db, execution, cl, node: nil external pointers before returning objects to sync.Pool
body:
## Problem

Several `sync.Pool` users returned an object to the pool while it still held a pointer to **externally-owned, shorter-lived memory** without nil-ing that field first. The field is re-assigned on the next `Get`, so there's no stale-read/correctness bug — but while the object sits idle in the pool it keeps that external memory reachable, so the GC can't reclaim it (a leak-while-parked). The codebase already had the correct convention in `rlp.PutStream`, `compress.putDec`, and `bufiopool.PutWriter`/`PutReader` (all reset the external ref before `Put`); these sites just diverged from it.

Two sub-shapes:
- a single external-pointer field (`*zstd.Decoder` source reader, `*gzip.Writer`/`*snappy.Writer` destination) — reset it before `Put`;
- `slice[:0]` on a **slice of pointers/interfaces** (`[]Task`, `[]journalEntry`) — `[:0]` only moves the length header, the backing array still references every old element, so `clear()` is needed first. (`[:0]` alone is fine for value-element slices like `[]byte`.)

## Fixes

| Package | Pool / type | Was pinning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks` | `decompressorPool` / `*zstd.Decoder` | block-sized (mmap-backed) compressed buffer | new `putDecoder` (`Reset(nil)`), 3 sites |
| `execution/exec` | `queuePool` / `QueueWithRetry` | whole-block `TxTask`s via the `[]Task` retry heap | `clear(q.retires)` before `[:0]` |
| `execution/state` | `journalPool` / `journal` | last tx's boxed `journalEntry` values | `clear(j.entries)` before `[:0]` |
| `execution/vm` | `contextPool` / `CallContext` | frame calldata + contract code/analysis | nil `input`, zero `Contract` in `put()` |
| `cl/sentinel/.../ssz_snappy` | `writerPool` / `*snappy.Writer` | caller's `io.Writer` | new `putWriter` (`Reset(nil)`) |
| `node` | `gzPool` / `*gzip.Writer` | per-request `http.ResponseWriter` | new `putGzip` (`Reset(io.Discard)`) |

The `exec` and `state/journal` ones are the highest value — both are `[]interface`/`[]pointer` heaps that can pin a whole block's execution state.

Audited every `sync.Pool` site in the repo; all other pools already reset/clear their external references correctly. One dead-code path (`execution/state/rw_v3.go` `readListPool`, no live `Get` caller) has the same latent shape and was intentionally left untouched.

No behavior change: every affected field is re-assigned on `Get` before use.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/antiquary: snapshot compact effective balances instead of full validator set
body:
## Motivation

CPU profiling of Caplin showed `runtime.memmove` at ~20% flat — the single largest cost — with `peek` attributing **97.65%** of it to `Antiquary.IncrementBeaconState`.

The state antiquary snapshotted the **entire validator set** (121 bytes/validator — **266MB** at mainnet's current 2.31M validators) into a scratch buffer **every slot**, purely to diff effective balances. But the effective-balance diff only ever reads 8 bytes at offset 80 of each 121-byte validator record.

## Change

- Snapshot only the packed 8-byte effective balances (`base_encoding.AppendEffectiveBalances`) — a **15× smaller copy** per slot (266MB → 17.6MB).
- Diff the compact lists with `ComputeCompressedSerializedUint64ListDiff`; the now-redundant `ComputeCompressedSerializedEffectiveBalancesDiff` is removed. **The on-disk diff format is unchanged — no re-antiquation needed** (see Safety).
- Fuse `ComputeCompressedSerializedUint64ListDiff`'s two passes (materialize all deltas → RLE-scan them) into a single pass, dropping the `plainUint64BufferPool`; the uncompressed header is written through a fixed-size buffer instead of `binary.Write`. This function also serves the **every-slot balances diff** (7.66% flat in the same profile), so the fusion pays on both paths.
- `collectEffectiveBalancesDump` reuses `AppendEffectiveBalances` through a collector-owned scratch buffer: one large zstd write instead of one 8-byte write per validator, and the validator-record layout (`validatorSSZSize`, `effectiveBalanceOffset`) now lives in one place, used by all call sites in the file.

## Measured

Real mainnet states one epoch apart (slots 14765888/14765920, 2,307,854 validators), M4 Max, benchstat n=5:

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| per-slot snapshot (runs every slot) | 4.65ms | 2.76ms |
| epoch-cross diff (once per 32 slots) | 4.76ms | ~4.4ms (2.9 extract + 1.46 fused diff) |
| **effective-balance machinery, total per epoch** | **157ms** | **~94ms** |
| balances diff, run-heavy regime (38% of balances changed) | 6.55ms | 4.22ms |

Retained snapshot buffers shrink from 266MB to 2×17.6MB. The M4 Max's memory bandwidth flatters the old full-copy path; on production servers (where the profile was taken) the relative win should be larger.

## Safety

- Diff output is **byte-identical** to the removed implementation — verified on the real mainnet epoch boundary above (60-byte diff) and on the balances regime (38% churn), plus synthetic high-churn and length-growth cases. Existing archives stay readable; new writes match what the old code would have written.
- New `TestAppendEffectiveBalances` pins the extraction (offset 80, stride 121; a truncated trailing record is ignored).
- `TestDiff64Effective` retargeted onto the production path (extract → uint64-list diff → apply → compare).
- `historical_states_reader` round-trip reconstruction (`ERIGON_RUN_HEAVY_TESTS=1`, Phase0/Bellatrix/Capella) passes — reconstructed state roots match.
- Validator record layout (121 bytes, effective balance at offset 80) is identical across all forks, so the extraction is fork-agnostic.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: close zstd frame in WriteBeaconBlock instead of flushing
body:
WriteBeaconBlock finalized its pooled zstd encoder with `Flush()` rather than `Close()`. As a result the bytes persisted to `kv.BeaconBlocks` — and copied verbatim into caplin `.seg` snapshots — were **unterminated zstd frames**: no last-block marker, no content checksum.

It has round-tripped in practice only because every reader (`ReadBlockFromSnapshot`, and the snapshot dump path which copies the blob verbatim) parses a self-delimiting SSZ block and stops before it needs the frame terminator. Any consumer that decodes to EOF (`DecodeAll` / `io.ReadAll`) fails with `unexpected EOF`, and zstd cannot detect corruption of these blobs.

`Close()` writes the frame epilogue, producing a complete, standalone frame — matching every other zstd streaming site in the tree (`base_encoding/uint64_diff.go`, `base_encoding/rabbit.go`, `antiquary/beacon_states_collector.go`).

`PagedWriter` was also checked and is fine: it compresses via `compress.EncodeZstdIfNeed` → `EncodeAll` (one-shot, complete-frame API) and reads with `DecodeAll`; its own `Flush()` is a page-buffer flush, unrelated to zstd frame finalization.

Backward compatible: old `Flush`-written blobs (in DB and existing snapshots) remain readable via the streaming path, so no migration is needed.

Added `TestWriteBeaconBlockStoresCompleteZstdFrame`, which decodes the stored blob to EOF. Confirmed red→green: with `Flush()` it fails with `unexpected EOF`; with `Close()` it passes.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/beacon: add missing metadata fields to blob_sidecars response envelope
body:
### Issue
#22413, the `GET /eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/{block_id}` endpoint is missing the full response envelope defined in the Beacon API. Instead of returning version, execution_optimistic, finalised, and data at the top level, it only returns a JSON object with the data field. Neither of the consensus-layer Beacon REST API specifications [v2.5.0](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/v2.5.0/apis/beacon/blob_sidecars/blob_sidecars.yaml) or [v4.0.0](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/v4.0.0/apis/beacon/blob_sidecars/blob_sidecars.yaml) match this, with all four fields being marked as required. These metadata fields are necessary for downstream tools, explorers and validator clients to interpret the output, as they expect a compliant response envelope.

### Answer
We modified the GetEthV1BeaconBlobSidecars handler to compute and include finalised, version, and execution_optimistic metadata in the response. The fix fixes the block slot to determine the consensus fork version, checks block canonicity against the finalised slot and checks the optimistic status of the block root. And then these properties are added to the response using the existing `BeaconResponse` builder methods.

We chained the builders in the order `.WithFinalized().WithVersion().WithOptimistic()` to avoid a latent bug in `BeaconResponse.WithFinalized` that would overwrite the optimistic status to `false`. This is consistent with the pattern correctly used in other block related endpoints in the codebase. Existing API semantics, error handling, content negotiation (JSON/SSZ), index filtering all the same.

### Tests
We changed the test fixture to contain the fields that we expect to be in the envelope. We also added two regression unit tests.
* `TestBlobSidecarsResponseEnvelope`: Verifies that a successful response with data correctly contains `version`, `execution_optimistic` and `finalised` in the JSON envelope.
* `TestBlobSidecarsEmptyResponseEnvelope`: Verifies that the response envelope is still populated with all expected metadata fields when no blobs are found for a block.

Closes: #22413

title: cl, db/kv/mdbx: don't drop caplin/history db dir on every chain-tip flush
body:
Closes #22422

At chain-tip `PersistentBlockCollector.Flush` runs on every block, and its clean path unconditionally closed the DB, removed the whole `datadir/caplin/history` dir and reopened it — every 12s, even with an empty DB.

The clean path is now layered:
- no rows seen by the cursor → return early, touch nothing (the every-block chain-tip case; detection is free since Flush already iterates the table)
- DB file ≤ 1GB → clear rows in place, keep the directory
- DB file > 1GB → drop the directory as before, reclaiming disk after large backfills (MDBX never shrinks the file)

The size check uses a new `(*MdbxKV).DBSize()` — `env.Info(nil)` reads geometry from the memory-mapped meta page, no filesystem syscall — and only runs on the non-empty path. File geometry is used rather than `BucketSize` deliberately: a ballooned file with little live data still gets reclaimed on the next flush.

The gap-detected path is unchanged — it must keep rows for retry and never dropped the dir.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/sentinel: lower undialable-peer discovery log from error to debug
body:
## What

Lower the `[Sentinel] Could not convert to peer info` log in `listenForPeers()` from `error` to `debug`.

## Why

Caplin's Sentinel pulls random nodes from the discv5 DHT and, for each, tries to build a libp2p address — which requires a TCP port in the peer's ENR. discv5 only requires a **UDP** endpoint, so the `tcp` entry is optional; NAT'd, discovery-only, and IPv6-tcp-only nodes routinely omit it. Such records simply aren't dialable as CL peers and are correctly skipped — but this path logged one `error` line per skipped node:

```
[Sentinel] Could not convert to peer info err="node 9520ea19... does not provide a tcp port"
```

That is benign, expected discovery behavior, not an error. The two sibling paths that hit the identical `ConvertToSingleMultiAddr` failure already treat it as non-noteworthy:

- `ConvertToMultiAddr` (`cl/p2p/utils.go`) logs it at `debug`
- `findPeersForSubnets` (`cl/sentinel/discovery.go`) skips silently

This makes the third path consistent with them.

## Testing

Pure log-level change, no behavior change — mechanical, so no test added (per the repo's TDD guidance). `make lint` clean; `cl/sentinel` builds.

title: db: rename db/services package to db/dbservices
body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/22445#discussion_r3576119507.

The `db/services` package was named `services`, which clashes with other `services` packages in the tree (notably `cl/phase1/network/services`) and forced a `services2` import alias in `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`.

This renames the package and its import path to `dbservices`, removing the clash and the need for aliases.

title: cl/phase1/stages: fix uint64 underflow in history-download progress log
body:
## Problem

Fixes #22455. A user on 3.5.2 reported garbage progress/ETA logs:

```
[INFO] Downloading Execution History progress=16441/18446744073709427663 ETA=-2120675h43m6.2s blk/sec=12.9
[INFO] Downloading Execution History progress=17223/18446744073709427663 ETA=318118h37m52.5s  blk/sec=13.0
```

The denominator is a `uint64` underflow: `2^64 − 18446744073709427663 = 123953`.

## Root cause

In the "Downloading Execution History" branch the total is computed with unguarded `uint64` subtraction:

```go
toprocess := highestBlockSeen - effectiveLowest   // highestBlockSeen = initialEth1Progress (frozen at start)
                                                  // effectiveLowest  = engine.CurrentHeader().Number (live EL head)
```

`highestBlockSeen` is frozen at the EL block number of the highest beacon block seen when the backwards history download starts; `lowestBlockToReach` tracks the **live** EL head, which keeps climbing as the node follows the tip. Once the EL head advances past the frozen start point, the subtraction underflows to ~2⁶⁴. That huge value then feeds `time.Duration(remaining/speed) * time.Second`, overflowing `int64` nanoseconds and producing the nonsensical (sign-flipping) ETA.

This is a pre-existing latent bug (the subtraction dates back to March 2025), not a regression from a recent change. It's logging-only — no functional/consensus impact — which is why it went unnoticed and untested. It surfaces on long-running nodes doing the persistent background history download while following the chain tip.

## Fix

- Extract a clamped `clampProgress` helper so `processed`/`total` can never underflow, and route **both** the Execution and Beacon History log branches through it.
- Add `historyDownloadProgress` which additionally caps the ETA so the `time.Duration` (int64 ns) multiplication can't overflow.

## Tests

Added `TestHistoryDownloadProgress_*` and `TestClampProgress`. The reproduction test fails on the old code with the exact reported denominator (`18446744073709427663`) and passes with the fix.

## Backport

Will cherry-pick to `release/3.5` (the branch the reporter is on).
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/stages: guard forward-sync progress log against under/overflow
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #22461 (issue #22455). The "[Caplin] Forward Sync" progress log uses the same unguarded arithmetic pattern that produced the garbage `Downloading Execution History` log:

```go
progressMade := chainTipSlot - currentSlot.Load()
distFromChainTip := time.Duration(progressMade*cfg.beaconCfg.SecondsPerSlot) * time.Second
timeProgress := currentSlot.Load() - prevProgress
estimatedTimeRemaining := 999 * time.Hour
if timeProgress > 0 {
    estimatedTimeRemaining = time.Duration(float64(progressMade)/(float64(currentSlot.Load()-prevProgress)/float64(secsPerLog))) * time.Second
}
if distFromChainTip < 0 || estimatedTimeRemaining < 0 {
    continue
}
```

Three latent issues:
- `chainTipSlot - currentSlot` underflows to ~2⁶⁴ when the current slot overshoots the captured tip.
- `currentSlot - prevProgress` underflows on a reorg (current slot dips below the previous sample), so the `> 0` guard passes with a garbage denominator.
- Both feed `time.Duration(...) * time.Second`, which overflows `int64` nanoseconds. The existing `< 0` guard only catches a wrap to **negative** — an underflow that wraps back to **positive** still logs a garbage distance/ETA (same failure mode as the `+318118h` seen in #22455).

Lower severity than #22461 (in normal forward sync `currentSlot <= chainTipSlot` and slots advance monotonically), but the same class of latent bug.

## Fix

Extract `forwardSyncProgress` (clamps both slot differences) and `boundedDuration` (saturates instead of overflowing the `time.Duration`), and drop the now-unnecessary `< 0` guard.

## Tests

`forward_sync_test.go` covers the overshoot, the reorg-below-prev-progress case, a normal case, and the duration saturation. The overshoot/reorg tests fail on the old code.

## Backport

Will cherry-pick to `release/3.5`.

title: common/math, cl, polygon/bor, execution/cache: deduplicate NextPowerOfTwo

title: cl/block_collector: reuse encode buffers in PersistentBlockCollector
body:
`PersistentBlockCollector` re-encoded every downloaded block into freshly allocated buffers: `payload.EncodeSSZ(nil)` (growth-doubling), a prefix-copy buffer, and a fresh snappy destination — ~8× the payload size in garbage per block (~743 KB per 100 KB block, ~8 MB per 1 MB block). During Caplin backward history download this was a visible share of GC pressure in CPU profiles.

Since `AddBlock`/`AddGloasBlock` already serialize on the collector mutex, `encodeBlock` becomes a method that reuses two scratch buffers on the collector: SSZ encodes directly after the `version+parentRoot[+requestsHash]` prefix into `encodeBlockBuf`, and snappy compresses into `blockCompressBuf`. The result aliases the scratch buffer and goes straight to `tx.Put`, which copies.

`BenchmarkEncodeBlock` (new, M4 Max, default benchtime):

| payload | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| empty | 665 ns, 3.5 KB, 18 allocs | 396 ns, 0.9 KB, 11 allocs |
| 100 KB | 38.2 µs, 743.6 KB, 34 allocs | 5.8 µs, 0.9 KB, 11 allocs |
| 1 MB | 323 µs, 7.95 MB, 42 allocs | 54 µs, 1.2 KB, 11 allocs |

Remaining allocs are inside `EncodeSSZ` schema construction.

Also adds `TestEncodeDecodeBlockRoundTrip` pinning the encode/decode contract across consecutive encodes on one collector (scratch-buffer reuse), and replaces the synthetic buffer-construction benchmark with one that exercises the real `encodeBlock`.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/merkle_tree: stack-allocate HashTreeRoot leaf buffer
body:
`HashTreeRoot` sized its leaf buffer with a non-constant `make`, so every call heap-allocated it — 512 B/op, and 71% of the bytes allocated in a hashing benchmark. The buffer never outlives the call, so it goes on the stack, with a heap fallback for oversized schemas.

### Why 32

Sized from the schema-length distribution measured on **mainnet** (590k calls), not a source scan. A scan can't see call frequency, and misses `Eth1Block`/`Eth1Header`, which build their schema per fork (14 base, +1 Capella, +2 Deneb = **17 leaves**):

```
leaves     2:20.5%  3:14.2%  4:29.3%  5:21.9%  13:7.1%  17:7.1%
coverage   8(256B):85.8%   16(512B):92.9%   32(1024B):100%
```

benchstat, 12 runs, on that distribution:

| maxStackLeaves | sec/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| _current_ | 276.6n ± 1% | 468 | 2 |
| 8 | 234.3n ± 1% | 103 | 0 |
| 16 | 244.9n ± 6% | 69 | 0 |
| **32** | **234.3n ± 1%** | **0** | **0** |

32 is fastest-or-tied with the tightest variance and alone in never falling back — skipping the 1 KB allocation on the 17-leaf path pays for zeroing a larger array. Frame is `$1328-56`, well inside Go's 128 KB stack-var limit.

Also: return an error for an empty schema (previously panicked), and fix swapped arguments in the unsupported-type panic, which passed the index to `%T` and the value to `%d`.

### Not in scope

`merkleHasher` takes a package-global mutex for all merkleization, so `HashTreeRoot` at 16 threads is *slower* than at 1 (745 vs 554 ns/op). Removing it measured ~16× but needs a `sync.Pool` — `gohashtree.Hash`'s params are `leaks to {heap}` (assembly), so any buffer handed to it is forced off the stack. Separate PR.

title: crypto: drop per-call allocations from `Keccak256` and `Sha256`
body:
`Sha256` and `Keccak256` hashed through a `hash.Hash` / `KeccakState` **interface**. The compiler can't see the callee, so it assumes `Write`/`Sum`/`Read` leak — which heap-allocates the digest *and*, because escape analysis is flow-insensitive, forces every caller's buffer onto the heap, even on paths that never touch the pooled hasher.

A mainnet Caplin heap profile put `Sha256` at **8.3% of all allocated objects** (26.8M of 322M), mostly via `transactionsListRoot` — once per transaction per block.

### Fix

Hash through the concrete `sha256.Sum256` / `keccak.Sum256`, whose results provably don't escape. A single argument goes straight to `Sum256`; multiple arguments are joined into a 64-byte stack buffer, or above that into a pooled scratch buffer (`append` copies, so the pooled buffer doesn't leak — a pooled *hasher* would).

Benchmarked with **caller-local** buffers:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `Sha256(32B)` | 52.7 ns, 32 B, 1 alloc | **45.9 ns, 0, 0** |
| `Sha256(32B, 32B)` | 78.2 ns, 64 B, 2 allocs | **52.1 ns, 0, 0** |
| `Keccak256Hash(32B)` | 160.9 ns, 32 B, 1 alloc | **124.5 ns, 0, 0** |
| `Keccak256(32B, 32B)` | 169.1 ns, 64 B, 2 allocs | **~160 ns, 32 B, 1 alloc** |

`Keccak256` returns a slice, so its result allocates by construction — prefer `Keccak256Hash` where a slice isn't needed. Under `-cpu=16` the gap widens (SSZ shape 19.5 → 4.3 ns), because the allocations, not the pooling, bound scaling.

### Shape

- `Keccak256Hash` takes **one** argument. It had no multi-arg caller (115 sites, all single-arg; the 5 multi-arg sites are all `Keccak256`). Single-arg is also the only shape that fits the inline budget — a variadic needs a call to the multi-arg path (cost 61 vs 129).
- Joins pool a scratch buffer, not a hasher. A pooled hasher can't reach zero allocs (its `Sum` still escapes the digest) and would re-taint every caller. Streaming through `io.Writer` is kept only where genuinely needed (`RlpHash`, `bor.SealHash`, `aura.sealHash`, …).

  The buffer pool isn't chosen for raw speed — against a pooled hasher it only wins in a middle band (per-op, `-cpu=16`, joined path):

  | join | pooled hasher | pooled buffer |
  |---|---|---|
  | 64B+64B | **14.3 ns**, 1 alloc | 21.2 ns, 0 |
  | 512B+512B | 151.5 ns, 1 alloc | **87.1 ns**, 0 |
  | 8K+8K | 450.8 ns, 1 alloc | 452.7 ns, 0 |
  | 64K+64K | **3355 ns**, 1 alloc | 3568 ns, 0 |

  Below the band the round-trip + copy costs more than one alloc; above it the O(n) concat loses to streaming. It's chosen because a pooled hasher isn't usable here at all (it leaks), and because it's allocation-free at every size — strictly better than the only other option available, `make([]byte, 0, total)` per call.

### Moves / cleanups

- `Sha256` moves `cl/utils` → `common/crypto`, beside `Keccak256`; they now share one stack buffer, pool, and keep-cap instead of a duplicate set each. `cl/utils` keeps `blob`/`bytes`.
- The keccak hasher pool moves `common/hasher.go` → `common/crypto` (package `common` didn't use it). Its `Hasher` type and `NewHasher`/`ReturnHasherToPool` are dropped: every caller only ever `Write`+`Read` a single input into a `[32]byte`, i.e. `Keccak256Hash` (16 `StateCache` sites, `ethash.seedHash`, `db/snaptype2` header indexing). `db/snaptype2` also shared one hasher across every index-builder callback, so this decouples it from `BuildIndex` being single-threaded.
- `common.HashData` was the same one-shot keccak under another name (plus an always-nil error); folded into `Keccak256Hash`, dead `if err != nil` checks removed.
- `common.BytesToHash(Keccak256(x))` → `Keccak256Hash(x)` tree-wide (AST rewrite), one alloc saved per site.
- `OptimizedSha256NotThreadSafe` removed — the direct path is faster than the pool it existed to skip.

### Note on an earlier revision

An earlier version of this PR kept a pooled-hasher `sha256Streamed` fallback and reported `Sha256(32B, 32B)` at "0 allocs" — measured against heap-resident globals, which hid the caller-side escape. With local buffers it was still 64 B / 2 allocs. All benchmarks here hash a local buffer.

### Tests

`TestKeccak256Hasher` duplicated `TestKeccak256Hash` and asserted nothing; replaced with equivalence against `x/crypto` across sizes straddling the stack buffer and sponge rate, both join positions, and per-path alloc assertions.

title: cl/merkle_tree: reuse packing buffer in transactionsListRoot
body:
## Problem

`transactionsListRoot` allocated a fresh `[][32]byte` via `packBits` for **every transaction**, and `MerkleizeVector`'s odd-length padding `append` reallocated on top of that because `packBits` sized capacity to exactly `ceil(len/32)` with no room for the pad element. A heap profile attributed ~1.5% of all execution allocations to this one loop (`packBits` alone accounted for 1.44%, 98% of it from this call site).

## Change

- Pack each transaction into a reusable scratch buffer (`packBitsInto`) held on the hasher, reused across the loop under the existing `mu` lock. The buffer keeps spare capacity so `MerkleizeVector`'s padding append stays in-cap (the max layer length during reduction is `n+1`).
- Remove the now-dead `getBufferForSSZList` / `internalBufferForSSZList` / `mu2`, unused since `ListObjectSSZRoot` switched to local allocation.

`packBits` is kept for the bitlist/bitvector callers, which rely on its `nil`-for-empty and exact-capacity contract.

## Result

`BenchmarkTransactionsListRoot` (256 txs × 200 bytes, M4 Max):

| | allocs/op | B/op |
|---|---|---|
| before | 1283 | 196,771 |
| after | 771 | 24,680 |

**−40% allocations, −87% bytes.** The trie root is unchanged: `TestHashTreeRootTxs` (fixed known root) and `TestHashTreeRoot` (full Deneb beacon-state root) both pass, including under `-race`.

Pure performance refactor with no behavior change, so the existing root tests are the safety net rather than a new failing test.

title: cl/spectest: make Test re-runnable under -count (guard global config init)
body:
`go test -shuffle=on -race -count=2 ./...` panicked the `cl/spectest` package on the second in-process iteration:

```
--- FAIL: Test (0.00s)
panic: globalConfig already initialized [recovered, repanicked]
    cl/clparams/global.go:16 InitGlobalStaticConfig
    cl/spectest/tests_test.go:42 Test
```

## Root cause

`clparams.InitGlobalStaticConfig` panics if the process-global beacon/caplin config is already set (a deliberate guard against double-init in production). `cl/spectest.Test` called it unconditionally, so under `-count=2` (or a `-shuffle` re-run) the second execution re-initialized the already-set global and panicked.

## Fix

Only initialize when the global config is unset (`clparams.GetBeaconConfig() == nil`). The mainnet config is identical across iterations, so reusing the one set by the first run is correct, and the production double-init guard is left untouched.

Verified with `go test -shuffle=on -count=5 ./cl/spectest/` (the panic reproduces at `-count=2` before the fix, at the init call — independent of whether the `cl_mainnet` fixtures are present).
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/phase1/network/services: restore swapped signature globals in tests
body:
`go test -shuffle=on -race -count=2 ./...` panicked the `cl/phase1/network/services` package:

```
--- FAIL: TestExecutionPayloadBidServiceDifferentParentHashes
panic: Fail in goroutine after TestProposerSlashing has completed [recovered, repanicked]
    gomock/controller.go:214 (*Controller).Call
    services/global_mock_test.go:33 (*mockFuncs).ComputeSigningRoot
    services/execution_payload_bid_service.go:438 validateBuilderBidSignature
```

## Root cause

The service tests swap package-level function variables (`computeSigningRoot`, `blsVerify`, `blsVerifyMultipleSignatures`) for gomock-backed mocks bound to the *running* test's `gomock.Controller`. Several suites/tests never restored them:

- `TestProposerSlashing` sets `computeSigningRoot = mock` and, on teardown, calls `ctrl.Finish()` but leaves the global pointing at the (now finished) mock.
- Under `-shuffle`/`-count`, whichever test runs next and computes a signing root without setting its own mock (the epbs bid service, proposer-preferences, …) invokes a mock bound to a completed controller → `t.Fatalf` fires on a finished `T` → panic.

The victim varies by shuffle order; the source is always a leaker that doesn't restore. Reproduced locally on the first shuffled run (victim: `TestProposerPreferencesServiceDuplicate`).

## Fix

Add `saveSignatureGlobals(t)` (snapshots the three globals, restores them on `t.Cleanup`) and call it from the setups that were missing restoration: `proposer_slashing`, `voluntary_exit`, `attestation`, `sync_contribution`, `sync_committee_messages`. The `bid`, `data_column`, `bls_to_execution_change` and `proposer_preferences` tests already restore their own swaps and are unchanged.

Verified with `go test -shuffle=on -count=2 ./cl/phase1/network/services/` — 15/15 green after the fix; the unfixed tree panics within one shuffled run.

title: cl: apply curated go-critic static analysis improvements
body:
This PR introduces targeted code quality and style enhancements across the `cl/` package by applying curated rule suggestions from [go-critic](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic). 

Keeping this PR focused purely on `go-critic` changes makes it easier to review and verify safety. The specific improvements applied include:

- **`httpNoBody`**: Replaced `nil` HTTP request body values with explicit `http.NoBody` instances across client and server-side request builders to guarantee robustness and prevent nil-pointer dereferences.
- **`shadow`**: Resolved variable shadowing of both built-in Go identifiers and package imports to prevent variable declaration collisions and improve legibility.
- **Control Flow Simplifications**: Flattened nested, redundant `if-else` blocks and control structures to make the logical paths cleaner.
- **Symmetrical Parameter Naming**: Standardized naming conventions in diff-related functions so that parameter pairs are named symmetrically (specifically `oldVal` and `newVal`), aligning with code clarity and self-documentation.

title: all: enable gocritic unnecessaryDefer check and resolve issues
body:
This PR adds `gocritic`'s `unnecessaryDefer` and `appendAssign` style checks to our `golangci-lint` configuration and fixes all the matching issues in the codebase.

The unnecessaryDefer check reports defer statements that come right before a function returns and are unnecessary and could be replaced with straight calls. The appendAssign check warns when the result of an append() call is assigned to a slice variable other than the first argument. This prevents accidental slice capacity sharing, subtle side-effects from array mutation, and sub-optimal slice allocations.

- **Linter settings**:
  - UnnecessaryDefer (enabled by removing from the disabled checks list in linter configuration) 
  - AppendAssign (enabled by removing from the disabled checks list in linter configuration)
- **Clean up defer on duplicate**
  - Removed unnecessary `defer` statements at the end of functions and replaced them with close, rollback or unlock calls.
- **Append Assignment Refactoring**
  - Replaced multiple `append()` calls with various slices in the codebase with explicit slice initialisations with pre-allocated capacity, direct slice copies or corresponding in-place assignments to avoid unintentional modifications of the underlying array and improve performance of slices
- **Dealing with Linter Conflicts**:
  - Added explicit linter suppression comments (`//nolint:gocritic`) where existing logic strictly required assigning to another slice structure (trie iterator state tracking) or where removing `defer` conflicted with mandatory rules.
- **Modernisation & Formatting**
  - Modernised to zero-allocation `fmt.Appendf` calls for the pattern `[]byte(fmt.Sprintf(...))` to keep all active linter checks green.

title: cl: fix Gloas checkpoint sync with external execution clients
body:
## Summary

Fix the standalone-Caplin Gloas checkpoint-sync path when using an external execution client.

- Preserve the skipped-slot checkpoint state root across fork-choice disk persistence.
- Validate Gloas anchor and downloaded payloads through the external EL even when insertion is unavailable.
- Encode empty Engine API transaction and versioned-hash inputs as arrays instead of `null`.
- Bound remote-EL and pending-envelope retry work, release the fork-choice mutex during envelope `NewPayload`, and refresh identity before committing the result.
- Terminate stale pending-envelope retries below finalized history or implausibly ahead of the local clock while retaining recent, DA-unavailable, storage, and EL-retry work.
- Bound selected-head recovery to two requests per uninterrupted head episode: the initial request plus one retry for a timeout, sparse response, late response, or failed application.
- Bound payload-attestation validation memory by sharing same-root state builds, admitting one full-state build at a time, and caching compact validation contexts.
- Start PeerDAS only after data-column gossip topics are registered.

## Scope

This PR contains the original checkpoint-sync/external-EL/empty-encoding work plus the minimal lifecycle corrections required by those paths, the stale pending-envelope terminal rule observed on devnet, the payload-attestation OOM fix, and the PeerDAS startup-order fix.

The later downloader/resolver/journal/canonical-ingress work remains in draft #23249. This PR does not add a general request scheduler, a negative cache for payload-attestation contexts, or a pre-Gloas `OnBlock` lock-yield refactor.

Pending-envelope expiry uses the Gloas finalized epoch start as its inclusive lower bound. A next-slot envelope is retained only within `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY`; farther-future slots are rejected before slot-time conversion. Gossip and local-self-build origins use the same terminal policy, removals are identity-checked against concurrent replacements, recent DA/storage failures remain retryable, and a nil index-repair marker is removed only when its durable envelope no longer exists.

Selected-head recovery separates in-flight ownership from completed attempts and guards callbacks with a monotonically increasing claim ID. Every inconclusive or failed outcome can open one additional attempt, but a stable EMPTY/malicious head can consume at most two root requests total until the selected head changes.

## Review follow-up at `4259ba8243`

- Zero-blob anchor/stage payloads now pass a non-nil empty versioned-hash array to external Engine API clients.
- Local context cancellation/deadline errors from envelope gossip are converted to gossip `IGNORE`, not peer-invalid rejection.
- Pre-Gloas target slots skip missing-envelope recovery before touching fork choice; the selected block's actual version remains independently checked.
- Selected-head claims release on every exit, retry fetched-but-unapplied envelopes, tolerate one sparse/timeout result, and remain bounded to two attempts per uninterrupted head.
- Missing durable nil repair markers terminate, and DA-unavailable entries use the same finality boundary as missing-state retries.
- The duplicate outer `NewPayload` latency observation was removed.

The requested global head sample was not adopted: earlier recovery/application phases can change fork-choice eligibility, so later consumers intentionally obtain a fresh selected head. The pre-Gloas early gate removes the needless current-network work without widening the consistency window.

## TDD and validation

Red-to-green regressions cover:

- zero-blob anchor and chain-tip Engine arguments;
- gossip cancellation/deadline classification;
- stale versus recent DA retries and missing nil repair markers for both origins;
- selected-head timeout, sparse, late, canceled, invalid, transient-DA, ABA, and bounded two-attempt behavior;
- pre-Gloas and exact-Gloas recovery activation.

Validation on the pushed source:

- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice ./cl/phase1/network/services ./cl/phase1/stages -count=1`
- focused selected-head and pending-envelope tests under `go test -race`
- `make erigon integration`
- `git diff --check`
- repeated adversarial Standards, Spec, boundary, fix-delta, and lifecycle reviews converged on generation `c9a9d3f602e7ffa5f290d0375106c0c1319c9bdf7f0263553ba8fa0b2e021989`

`make lint` reports 0 issues for the changed surface, then the macOS secondary pass fails on the pre-existing `db/seg/decompress.go:residencyOnce` field, which is referenced only by `residency_gate_linux.go`. This PR does not change that unrelated platform-specific baseline.

title: all: enable gocritic rangeValCopy and regexpMust rules and fix all violations
body:
This PR adds `gocritic`'s `rangeValCopy` and `regexpMust` checks to our `golangci-lint` configuration and fixes all matching issues across the Erigon codebase.

The `rangeValCopy` check flags `range` loops that copy large struct values (>128 bytes) on every iteration, causing unnecessary memory allocations, stack/heap copy overhead, and CPU cache pollution. The `regexpMust` check identifies places where `regexp.Compile` is called with static literal expressions that should be pre-compiled using `regexp.MustCompile` at package scope.

### Changes Included

- **Linter settings**:
  - `rangeValCopy` (enabled by removing from `disabled-checks` in `.golangci.yml`)
  - `regexpMust` (enabled by removing from `disabled-checks` in `.golangci.yml`)
- **Range Value Copy Refactoring (`rangeValCopy`)**:
  - Replaced value-copy range loops (`for _, v := range slice`) with zero-copy pointer indexing (`for i := range slice { v := &slice[i] ... }`) or direct index access across codebase files.
  - Completely eliminated heavy struct copy overhead during iteration over large ABI arguments, events, methods, transactions, and snapshot file infos.
- **Regex Pre-compilation (`regexpMust`)**:
  - Replaced repeated runtime `regexp.Compile` calls on literal string patterns with package-level `regexp.MustCompile` static package variables to eliminate runtime regex compilation overhead on hot paths.
- **Correctness & Type Safety**:
  - Ensured in-place slice element mutations update the actual underlying slice elements rather than operating on transient loop value copies.

title: common: make common.Copy a func and inline it away
body:
`common.Copy` was a package-level func-valued **variable**:

```go
var Copy = bytes.Clone
```

A `var` of function type is reassignable, so every `common.Copy(x)` is an indirect call: the compiler cannot inline it and escape analysis must assume the argument escapes. That verdict propagates to callers — `execution/cache.GenericCache.putStriped` is `leaks param: key` purely because it passes the key to `common.Copy`.

The visible symptom is in the EVM. `(*Contract).isCode` builds its cache key in a local 32-byte array:

```
contract.go:100:6: codeHash escapes to heap in (*Contract).isCode:
  flow: cache.key ← &codeHash:
    from codeHash[:] (slice) at contract.go:117:29
  flow: {heap} ← cache.key:
    from (*cache.GenericCache[...]).put(..., cache.key, ...)
contract.go:100:6: moved to heap: codeHash
```

Escape analysis is path-insensitive, so the promotion applies to the cache-**hit** path at line 107 too, which never reaches the `Put`. Result: one 32 B allocation per call frame that executes a JUMP.

## Change

- `common/bytes.go`: `var Copy = bytes.Clone` → a real function carrying `//go:fix inline`. Semantics are identical (`bytes.Clone` still returns `nil` for `nil`).
- Every call site rewritten to `bytes.Clone`. The bulk came from `go fix -inline ./...`; the fixer skipped ~67 sites in `execution/commitment`, `db/state/execctx`, `db/migrations`, `db/seg` and `db/datastruct/btindex` (it reports `fixes skipped (e.g. due to conflicts)` and stops making progress on re-runs), so those were done directly with the same substitution plus import fixes.
- `Copy` itself is kept, so the exported API is unchanged. It now has no in-tree callers, and the `//go:fix inline` directive means `go fix` auto-migrates any new use.
- `execution/tests/testutil/state_test_util.go`: drops `var rlpHash = types.RlpHash`, the same pattern with a single call site.

## Effect

`isCode` fresh-frame benchmark (`analysis = nil` each iteration, so the jumpdest cache lookup runs), Apple M4 Max, `-count=5`:

| | ns/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 33.7 | 32 | 1 |
| after | 24.8 | 0 | 0 |

Diffing full `-gcflags=-m` reports over `./execution/... ./db/...`: **9 stack promotions removed, zero regressions** — `execution/vm/contract.go:100 codeHash`, `execution/state/triedb_state.go:465 a`, and seven in `execution/engineapi/engine_types/ssz.go`. Every rewritten call site also loses the indirect call.

## Sweep for the same pattern

An AST scan for package-level `var X = <bare ident/selector>` turned up no other harmful cases. The remaining func-valued vars are benign and deliberately left alone:

- `execution/vm/gas_table.go:312-316` (`gasReturn`/`gasRevert`/`gasMLoad`/`gasMStore8`/`gasMStore = pureMemoryGascost`) and `execution/vm/memory_table.go:93` (`memoryStaticCall = memoryDelegateCall`) are only ever stored into the jump table as `gasFunc`/`memoryFunc` values, so the call is indirect either way.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/*` (`blsVerify`, `computeSigningRoot`, `verifyDataColumnSidecar*`, …) and `cl/aggregation` `blsAggregate` are test seams.
- The rest are plain values, not functions (`ConsensusTables = ChaindataTables`, `be = binary.BigEndian`, `b64format = base64.RawURLEncoding`, various `= false` debug flags).
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: resume Caplin from a local finalized state on restart
body:
On every restart of an existing datadir, Caplin re-fetches a fresh remote finalized checkpoint (`ReadOrFetchLatestBeaconState` fetches remote first, reads a local state only on network failure). The fresh checkpoint sits ahead of the execution layer's persisted head, so `DownloadHistoricalBlocks` backfills the gap ("Downloading Execution History") and blocks before the node can execute or serve RPC.

This persists the state the node itself finalized and resumes from it, entirely from local data. A finalized state is the only locally-safe fork-choice anchor: `NewForkChoiceStore` treats the anchor's latest block as finalized+justified, and a head state is reorg-eligible (a saved head can be orphaned by a post-shutdown reorg). The finalized anchor sits at/below the EL's persisted head, so the CL resumes below the EL and re-feeds already-present blocks — no backfill.

## Changes
- Persist the finalized state to `finalized.ssz_snappy` on the existing 5-epoch save cadence, via a fixed-name temp file that is fsynced and renamed into place; retire the head-state save.
- `ReadOrFetchLatestBeaconState` resumes from it when present, the genesis validators root matches, and it is within a resume horizon; otherwise falls back to remote checkpoint.
- Resume horizon is the blob / data-column sidecar retention window of the anchor's fork (a forward-sync data-availability bound, not weak-subjectivity), configurable via `caplin.resume-max-staleness-epochs` and clamped to that window.
- Route the remote-failure fallback and the `--caplin.checkpoint-sync.disable` path to the finalized file too, so bootstrap is always from a finalized state. All three paths reject a file whose genesis validators root belongs to another network.
- GLOAS: accept the HTTP anchor envelope only when its root matches the resume anchor, else request it by root over P2P.

An existing datadir run with `--caplin.checkpoint-sync.disable` re-syncs Caplin from genesis once on the first restart after this change: `latest.ssz_snappy` holds a head state, so there is no safe migration from it. It is left on disk rather than deleted so a downgrade still has its resume path.

author: JackCC703

title: cl: reject sidecars and blocks with inconsistent fork schema
body:
## Problem

The SSZ schema a req/resp response decodes with is chosen by the **peer**, via the fork-context digest it sends. Two consumers derived the fork a second time from the object's own slot and read whichever fields that second inference implied. Where the two disagree across the Gloas boundary, the branch taken reads a field the decoded schema never populated — a nil dereference, in paths with no `recover`.

`NewEthereumClock` registers every configured fork digest, including forks scheduled at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`, so a peer can select the Gloas decoder on mainnet today.

**Data column sidecars** (`cl/das/peer_das.go`). Gloas removed `SignedBlockHeader` from `DataColumnSidecar`, replacing it with `Slot` and `BeaconBlockRoot`. A peer answers `DataColumnSidecarsByRoot` with the Gloas digest so `SignedBlockHeader` decodes as nil, sets the embedded `Slot` to a pre-Gloas value, and the pre-Gloas branch dereferences the absent header. This runs in a per-sidecar `wg.Go` goroutine, ahead of all KZG, inclusion-proof and signature validation. Requires a post-Fulu, pre-Gloas network and a node with a column download in flight, i.e. one missing a custody column.

**Beacon blocks** (`cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block.go`). Gloas moved `ExecutionPayload` and `BlobKzgCommitments` out of `BeaconBody`. `OnBlock` gated its pre-Gloas branch on the slot-derived version while the reads inside that branch are gated on the decoded `block.Version()`, so a Gloas-digest block at a pre-Gloas slot reaches several nil reads — `solid.ListSSZ` has no nil-receiver guard. It precedes the pipeline's only version cross-check (`ProcessBlock`) and all signature validation, so an unsigned crafted block suffices. Requires a pre-Gloas network with Gloas in the fork schedule, a Deneb-or-later block, and `newPayload` with an execution engine attached. Nothing need be in flight, so wider than the sidecar path.

Impact in both cases is a remote liveness kill: process exit, Beacon API down until restart. Caplin-only; no consensus split, state corruption or code execution.

## Fix

Both sites require the fork implied by the slot to agree with the decoded schema across the Gloas boundary before reading any schema-specific field. The two inferences are independent peer-influenced inputs, so they are checked against each other rather than trusted separately.

The check is `BeaconChainConfig.ForkSchemaMatchesSlot(slot, decodedVersion)`, shared by both call sites so the invariant carries one name and one rationale rather than two copies of the expression.

- `cl/das`: `resolveColumnSidecarSlotAndRoot` takes slot and block root only from the fields the decoded schema populates — `sidecar.Version()` is the structural truth — and bans the peer on a mismatch or a malformed sidecar.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice`: `OnBlock` returns `ErrForkSchemaSlotMismatch`. Both directions are rejected, keeping schema dispatch below the check uniform.

Honest traffic is unaffected: a req/resp server encodes each object with the fork digest of that object's own slot, so decode-fork and slot-fork always agree unless the peer is lying. Disagreement *below* the Gloas boundary is allowed, since no double inference exists there. Consensus spec fixtures are unaffected because `ReadBeaconState` activates every fork up to the test's version at epoch 0, matching the slot-derived version to the decoded one.

## Tests

- `TestResolveColumnSidecarSlotAndRoot` — the sidecar resolver's accept and reject cases.
- `TestRunDownloadRejectsGloasSidecarWithPreGloasSlot` — a malicious sentinel driven through the real `BeaconRpcP2P` decode path into `runDownload`; asserts the peer is banned and nothing reaches column storage.
- `TestOnBlockRejectsForkSchemaSlotMismatch` — a Gloas-decoded block at a pre-Gloas slot through the real `ForkChoiceStore.OnBlock`.
- `TestForkSchemaMatchesSlot` — the shared predicate in both mismatch directions and both agreement cases, including that a disagreement *below* the Gloas boundary is not a mismatch.
- `TestForkSchemaMatchesSlotFarFutureGloas` — the mainnet shape: with Gloas at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH` no slot maps to it, so a Gloas-schema object is inconsistent whatever slot it claims.

Each fails if the check it covers is removed.

## Credit

The data-column sidecar issue was reported through the Ethereum bug bounty program (private PoC, `ethereum-bounty/erigon#19`).

title: cl/rpc, cl/phase1/network/services: remove dead PeerDAS code
body:
Removes three unreachable functions from the Caplin PeerDAS code. No behaviour change.

Independent of #22797 — based on `main`, not stacked on it — though the second removal is motivated by it.

## `SendColumnSidecarsByRangeReqV1` (`cl/rpc`)

No callers. The column downloader only ever issues the by-root request (`SendColumnSidecarsByRootIdentifierReq`). Removed along with its `BeaconRpc` declaration; no generated mocks implement that interface, so nothing needed regenerating.

No callers either, and it was the sole caller of `validateGloasPartialHeader` and `validateFuluPartialHeader`, so all three go. The Fulu variant ends with

```go

```

which suggests it was never wired up.

Worth removing rather than leaving: `PartialDataColumnHeader` carries the same dual Gloas schema as `DataColumnSidecar`, where conflating the decoded schema with the fork implied by the slot was a remotely triggerable crash (fixed in #22797). An unused validator for that type is a surface with the same hazard built in.
