title: cl,db,diagnostics,p2p: pass log values as attributes
body:
`log/v3` does not format the message. These 11 calls pass a printf format string, so the verb prints literally and the argument meant to fill it is consumed as an attribute *key* instead:

```
logger.Error("decoding NewWitnessMsg: %w, data: %x", err, b)
EROR[...] decoding NewWitnessMsg: %w, data: %x  LOG15_ERROR="unexpected EOF"
```

`b` never reaches the log at all. Where the argument count is odd, the record also picks up a second `LOG15_ERROR` from the logger's own arity guard.

## Changes

- Converts the format strings to key/value pairs.
- Byte slices that relied on `%x` go through `hex.EncodeToString`.
- `commitee` -> `committee` in the attestation pool warning.
author: awskii

title: cl/pool: size operation pools by retention need
body:
`NewOperationsPool` takes a `*clparams.BeaconChainConfig` and ignores it. All five pools get the same `operationsPerPool = 512`, which `NewOperationPool` then silently multiplies by `operationsMultiplier = 20`, so every pool is really 10240 entries and no number in the file is the capacity you actually get.

The pools are gossip retention windows, not per-block buffers: `NotifyBlock` never removes attestations, so the LRU cap alone decides how far back a proposer can pack.

## Changes

- `NewOperationPool` takes `capacity` and passes it straight to the LRU. `operationsMultiplier` is gone, so the number at the call site is the capacity.
- Each pool gets a named capacity and the reason it holds what it holds.
- The attestation window is derived from the config: `attestationRetentionSlots(10) * MaxCommitteesPerSlot * TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee`.
- Tests pin each capacity by filling the pool past it.

Mainnet and Gnosis capacities are unchanged. The only behaviour changes are voluntary exits 10240 -> 16384, and the minimal preset, where the attestation pool is now sized to its own committee count (640) instead of inheriting the mainnet number.

The attestation window is deliberately not widened. A deeper window gives the proposer more partial aggregates to merge, but `electraMergedAttestationCandidates` is linear in pool occupancy and quadratic within one data root, with a `bls.AggregateSignatures` per merge (`block_production.go:2178`), on the proposal critical path — and the constant being replaced came from #10020, a latency PR. Changing that number is a latency trade that needs a measurement, not an argument.

Fixes #22790
author: awskii

title: cl/beacon: fix BLS-to-execution changes never being included in produced blocks
body:
An erigon proposer never includes a BLS-to-execution change. `getBlockOperations` requires the validator to carry `ETH1_ADDRESS_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX`, but a change is only valid while the validator still has `BLS_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX` — that is what the change migrates away from. So every eligible validator is skipped, and the `0x01` validators that do get through then fail the `sha256(from)[1:] == wc[1:]` comparison, since a `0x01` credential is `0x01 || 11 zero bytes || 20-byte address`.

Both other sites in the tree check the prefix correctly: `bls_to_execution_change_service.go:122` and `operations.go:1082`.

The same loop is also the only one of the four in that function with no `break` at its limit, and `ListSSZ.Append` does not enforce the list limit. That was unreachable while the filter emptied the list. With the filter fixed it is reachable: `HashSSZ` merkleizes to the limit's depth regardless of length, so an over-long list produces a wrong body root and peers reject the list on decode — the proposer loses the slot.

## Changes

- Compare against `BLSWithdrawalPrefixByte`, matching the gossip service and the state transition.
- Break at `MaxBlsToExecutionChanges`, matching the attester-slashing, proposer-slashing and voluntary-exit loops above it.
- Test builds validators with BLS credentials and a pool holding more changes than fit in a block, then asserts exactly `MaxBlsToExecutionChanges` come back. It returns 0 before the first fix and 20 before the second.

Fixes #22826
Fixes #22824
author: awskii

title: cl/beacon: cover the migrated-validator and duplicate-per-validator BLS change cases
body:
Follow-up to #22827, which landed with one test covering the cap. Two conditions it relies on were left uncovered, and both cost the proposer a slot if they regress.

`getBlockOperations` does not verify signatures — the pool only ever admits changes whose signature already verified (`bls_to_execution_change_service.go` inserts inside the batch verifier's success callback, and the REST POST path goes through the same `ProcessMessage`). So what block production must get right is the state-dependent part, and the produced block is re-run through `ProcessBlock` before it is returned, where a wrong answer aborts production.

## Changes

- `skips validators that already migrated` — pins the prefix constant. Reverting it to `ETH1AddressWithdrawalPrefixByte` packs a change for an already-migrated validator, which then fails `ProcessBlsToExecutionChange`.
- `packs at most one change per validator` — the pool is keyed by signature, so one validator can hold several changes. Processing one flips the credentials to 0x01, so a second in the same block fails the prefix assert and takes the block down. Drop the `slashedIndicies` guard and this packs 3 instead of 1.

Both were mutation-checked against the fix they protect.
author: awskii

title: fix log attribute keys that break logfmt
body:
The terminal formatter writes attribute keys unquoted, so a key containing a space or `?` emits output no logfmt parser can read back — `"block num"` renders as `block num=23847119`, which parses as key `block` with value `num=23847119`.

## Changes

- Renames 39 such keys to the repo-dominant camelCase spelling: `"block num"` -> `"blockNum"`, `"is deadline?"` -> `"isDeadline"`, `"peer count"` -> `"peerCount"`.
- Key names only. No message text, prefix or level changes.
author: awskii

title: cl/transition: gate BLS-to-execution change signature verification on FullValidation
body:
`ProcessBlsToExecutionChange` verifies the signature unconditionally. Its neighbours don't — attestation signature verification sits behind `FullValidation` (`operations.go:1144`), and block production builds its machine as `&eth2.Impl{}` with that off. Since #22827 started packing these changes, every produced block pays a full BLS pairing per change on the proposal path.

Measured on this machine (blst v0.3.17), per change:

| | ns/op |
|---|---|
| with `FullValidation` | 562,000 |
| gated | 366 |

A full block of 16 goes from ~9.0 ms to ~5.9 us. The cost is the pairing (397 us of a 462 us `bls.Verify`); it is inherent to BLS12-381, which is why the ingest path batch-verifies instead.

## Why this is safe

No untrusted block reaches `ProcessBlock` with `FullValidation` off:

- gossip (`block_service.go:286`), chain-tip sync (`chain_tip_sync.go:269`) and forward sync (`forward_sync.go:157`) all pass `true`
- the `false` paths are a proposer's own freshly built block (`block_production.go:506,2094`), fork-graph replay of already-accepted blocks (`fork_graph_disk.go:538`), and antiquary replay of finalized blocks (`state_antiquary.go:472`)

Operations reach the pool only through `blsToExecutionChangeService.ProcessMessage`, which inserts inside the batch verifier's success callback — so a pool entry has already had its signature verified. The REST pool endpoint goes through the same path.

This mirrors the existing argument for skipping attestation signature verification during production. Note it is an erigon-side optimisation, not something the spec sanctions: `process_bls_to_execution_change` asserts `bls.Verify` unconditionally, which is why the assert must stay for imports.

## Changes

- Signature verification (and the domain/signing-root computation it needs) moved behind `FullValidation`. The `validator_index`, prefix and credential-hash asserts stay unconditional, so the resulting state is identical either way.
- Test pins all four arms: valid accepted under full validation, bad rejected under full validation, bad not checked without it, and the credential asserts still applying without it.

The full consensus spec suite passes — 8119 cases, including the 42 `bls_to_execution_change` invalid vectors, which still fail correctly because `cl/spectest` runs `transition.ValidatingMachine`.
author: awskii

title: cl/phase1/execution_client: persist BAL in ExecutionClientDirect.NewPayload
body:
## What

`ExecutionClientDirect.NewPayload` (the integrated, single-process CL→EL path used by an embedded-Caplin node) built the block and called `InsertBlock` with a `nil` block access list, dropping the gloas payload's `BlockAccessList` even though it is populated on the `Eth1Block`. This threads it through instead.

## Why

`ExecutionClientEngine.NewPayload` (the external-EL-over-RPC path) already forwards the BAL (`request.BlockAccessList = payload.BlockAccessList.Bytes()`), but the direct path did not — so on an embedded-Caplin node `kv.BlockAccessList` was **never written**. Anything keyed off that table is silently degraded, most visibly the BAL-driven read-ahead warmuper (`execution/exec/blocks_read_ahead.go`): `warmBody` reads the block's BAL from `kv.BlockAccessList` and, finding it empty, always falls back to TX-decode warming. In practice the BAL warm path never runs on the integrated path.

## Change

In `ExecutionClientDirect.NewPayload`, for gloas payloads pass `payload.BlockAccessList.Bytes()` as the `bal` argument to `InsertBlock` (was `nil`). The bytes flow through `blocksToRaw` → `RawBlock.BlockAccessList` and are persisted by the existing insert path; `RlpHeader` already sets `header.BlockAccessListHash` for gloas so the insert guard is satisfied. This makes the integrated path match the engine path.

## Testing

`chainRW` (`ChainReaderWriterEth1`) is a concrete struct, not an interface, so a direct-path unit test would require introducing a mock seam. The BAL-extraction logic is identical to `ExecutionClientEngine`'s request builder, which is unit-tested (`TestBuildExecutionPayload_BlockAccessListGloasOnly`), and the persistence path is exercised by the execmodule insert tests. Builds and `make lint` clean for the changed file.
author: sudeepdino008

title: cl/pool: prune finalized operations asynchronously
body:
## Summary

- retain slashings, voluntary exits, and BLS-to-execution changes across non-finalized block imports
- prune only operations that are terminal in the finalized beacon state
- run finalized-state loading and pool scans in a bounded background worker outside the forkchoice mutex
- preserve gossip first-valid semantics with validator-based seen caches and explicit `IGNORE` handling

## Related issue

Related to #22790.

#22790 identified that operation-pool capacities should be chosen deliberately instead of ignoring the beacon-chain configuration. #22823 addressed that capacity sizing. This PR is a follow-up that adds the missing operation lifecycle: reorg-safe retention and finalized-state pruning. It does not change the capacity formula introduced by #22823.

## Why

The operation pools previously removed operations as soon as they appeared in an imported block, and the BLS-to-execution pool was purged wholesale. That can discard still-useful operations when the block is reorged out. Finalized-state pruning gives these operations a reorg-safe lifecycle while fixed capacities continue to bound memory.

## Implementation

- proposer and attester slashings are removed once all relevant validators are terminal at the finalized checkpoint
- voluntary exits are removed after the validator has a non-far-future exit epoch
- BLS changes are removed after finalized withdrawal credentials no longer use the BLS prefix
- attestation retention remains slot-based and is not part of finalized pruning
- finality updates coalesce to one worker plus the latest pending checkpoint; empty pools skip finalized-state loading
- duplicate BLS changes and voluntary exits are atomically deduplicated by validator
- the REST voluntary-exit path relies on immediate verification for its single pool insertion, avoiding a pre-verification bypass of seen-cache deduplication
- attester-slashing early `IGNORE` checks use order-independent, capacity-bounded set semantics before normal sorted-index validation
- imported-block processing suppresses expected attester-slashing `ErrIgnore` logs while retaining logs for rejected operations

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/pool ./cl/phase1/forkchoice ./cl/phase1/network/services -count=1`
- `go test -race --timeout 10m ./cl/pool ./cl/phase1/forkchoice ./cl/phase1/network/services -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler -count=1`
- `make lint` (repeated clean runs)
- `make erigon integration`

The final branch also completed adversarial review rounds covering consensus-spec behavior, concurrency/performance, and test/scope coverage, with no remaining actionable Critical, High, or Medium findings.

title: engineapi: add missing custodyColumns parameter in engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4

### What is changed?

Updated `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4` to accept 3 parameters by adding `custodyColumns` as the 3rd argument, strictly following the [Amsterdam Engine API specification](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/amsterdam.md#engine_forkchoiceupdatedv4).

### Why this change?

Right now, `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4` in Erigon takes only 2 arguments. When an Amsterdam-compatible consensus client sends 3 parameters (`forkchoiceState`, `payloadAttributes`, `custodyColumns`), Erigon's RPC decoder rejects the call with `"too many arguments, want at most 2"`.

This PR defines `CustodyColumns` (`[16]byte`) and updates `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4` across the interface, server, clients, and test mocks. This allows 3-parameter requests to work properly while fully preserving backward compatibility for 2-parameter requests.

### Testing

- Added unit tests for `CustodyColumns` hex parsing, length validation (must be 16 bytes), and null handling.
- Added regression tests for 3-parameter calls, `null` custody columns, non-null custody columns, and 2-parameter backward compatibility.

title: cl/phase1/stages: use live chain tip for forward-sync distance log
body:
## Problem

A user restarting a node near the head saw the `[Caplin] Forward Sync` log freeze:

```
progress=24016944 distance-from-chain-tip=1m5s estimated-time-remaining=12s
progress=24016944 distance-from-chain-tip=1m5s estimated-time-remaining=n/a
progress=24016944 distance-from-chain-tip=1m5s estimated-time-remaining=n/a
```

`chainTipSlot` is captured **once** before the log loop and reused for the `distance-from-chain-tip` display. Near the head the loop can run for minutes (until the 5-min stale-detection hands off to ChainTipSync), during which the real chain advances but the displayed distance stays pinned to the stale gap — here frozen at `1m5s` while the node had actually fallen further behind.

## Fix

Read the chain tip live (`cfg.ethClock.GetCurrentSlot()`) each log tick instead of reusing the captured `chainTipSlot`. The loop's exit condition is unchanged — only the display is made truthful, so the distance now grows during a stall, which correctly explains the subsequent handoff to ChainTipSync.

`estimated-time-remaining=n/a` is left as-is: it is the instantaneous per-interval rate, and `n/a` is the honest signal that no slots advanced in the interval (a genuine stall), not a bug.

## Notes

- `forwardSyncProgress` (and its unit tests) are unchanged; the fix is purely which tip value is fed to it, so this is a display-wiring change with no new pure-function behavior to test.
- Same bug is present on `release/3.6`; cherry-pick to follow.
author: lystopad

title: cl/rpc: reject Gloas schema-slot mismatches at the RPC boundary
body:
## Problem

For beacon block request/response traffic, the peer-provided fork-context digest selects the SSZ schema independently of the slot embedded in the decoded block. Across the Gloas boundary, those inputs can disagree: a block decoded with the Gloas schema can claim a pre-Gloas slot, leaving fields expected by slot-derived processing unset.

The reported BlocksByRange case produced a recovered ChainTipSync panic. It did not terminate Caplin, but repeated invalid responses can waste sync attempts while the serving peer remains eligible for selection.

Report: https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/issues/22
PoC: https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/pull/21

## Fix

Validate every decoded block in the shared sendBlocksRequest path with BeaconChainConfig.ForkSchemaMatchesSlot before returning it to a caller. On a mismatch, the RPC client:

- discards the response;
- returns the mismatch error and serving peer ID;
- requests the standard Sentinel peer ban.

The shared path covers BlocksByRange and BlocksByRoot responses. ForkChoiceStore.OnBlock independently enforces the same invariant for blocks received through other paths.

Sentinel retains peers when the active peer count is below its grace threshold. This change follows that existing policy: it always rejects the malformed response at the RPC boundary, but it does not override low-peer retention.

## Tests

TestSendBeaconBlocksByRangeReqRejectsForkSchemaSlotMismatch sends a Gloas-digest block claiming a Fulu slot through the request/response decoder and verifies that no block is returned, the mismatch error and peer ID are preserved, and a peer ban is requested.

- go test ./cl/rpc -count=1
- go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice -run ^TestOnBlockRejectsForkSchemaSlotMismatch$ -count=1
- make lint
- make erigon integration

The full PR CI suite passes, including Caplin, race, benchmark, and cross-platform jobs.

## Credit

Reported by @bshastry through the Ethereum bug bounty program.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/issues/22

title: cl, db: caplin snapshot pre-fixes and CaplinSnapshots on BaseRoSnapshots
body:
Two things, the second built on the first: a batch of correctness gaps in the caplin snapshot path, then `CaplinSnapshots` moving onto the shared `BaseRoSnapshots` lifecycle (#22997, merged here).

Pre-fixes:
- `Antiquary.Loop` busy-spun after context cancellation instead of returning
- blob sidecar removal errors were silently dropped during prune
- the beacon dump slept 15s per file waiting for an fsync the compressor already does before renaming
- torrent piece verification globbed non-recursively, so `snapshots/caplin/` and the state subdirs were never verified
- `caplin/`-prefixed preverified entries bypassed the version window and the newest-per-name dedup

Lifecycle: `CaplinSnapshots` kept its own copy of the dirty/visible model, its views pinned nothing, and `closeWhatNotInList` closed decompressors inline — a reader holding a view could reach a closed mmap as soon as anything removed a file. Embedding the base replaces that with the refcounted generation model, so `Close`/`OpenList` retire through the generation chain and unlink only at the reader watermark. It also cuts the retire/reclaim fold to two implementations before the planned extraction into shared erigondb code, rather than three.

The lifecycle change is a pure refactor: a characterization fixture pins `SegmentsMax`, `IndicesMax`, `BlocksAvailable` and `FrozenBlobs` before the embed and stays green after. The one intentional change is `IndicesMax` `To`→`To-1`, forced by the base, which fixes a `LogStat` off-by-one.

## Changes
- `cl/antiquary`: return from `Loop` on cancellation; log blob removal failures
- `db/snapshotsync`: drop the dump sleep; add `SetIndexBuilder` and an exported `OpenList` to `BaseRoSnapshots`; `CaplinSnapshots` embeds it (`alignMin=false` — blobs trail blocks from Deneb)
- four accessors stay caplin-owned because their contracts differ from the base: `SegmentsMax` is dirty-backed (the archive backfill stop condition needs a dumped-but-unindexed tail), `FrozenBlobs` is the exclusive `To` (consumers test `slot < FrozenBlobs()`), `BuildMissingIndices`, and `OpenFolder` — the base scans its directory unfiltered and caplin shares `dirs.Snap` with the EL segments; the base's `BuildMissedIndices` is shadowed to route through them
- `db/integrity`, `cmd/utils`: recursive torrent discovery; unreadable paths skipped rather than aborting the run; cancellation preserved on every return path and never counted as file corruption
- `db/snapcfg`: caplin entries go through the same version window and newest-per-name dedup as typed entries

Not here: no `.tmp`-sweep scoping and no antiquary semaphore change. Both are behavior changes and neither hazard is live — embedding makes `RemoveOverlaps` reachable on caplin, but nothing calls it until the merge tier. They belong with that work.

Follow-up worth filing: `SegmentsMax` being dirty-backed means the archive backfill stop condition keys off data that exists on disk but may not be indexed or visible.

Review surfaced three more defects, fixed here.

A pre-existing one in shared code: `BaseRoSnapshots.Close` gated the fd close on the immediately-outgoing generation's refcount, but generations share `*DirtySegment` values, so a reader pinned to an older generation had its segments closed under it — `Decompressor` nil, reads silently empty, `MakeGetter` panicking. `Close` now hands the detached segments to the outgoing generation as close-only retirees and lets the existing drain-gated reclaim run, rather than deciding inline whether closing is safe. The last reader to drain releases the fds. Affects EL blocks and bor/heimdall the same way.

`CaplinSnapshots` promoted the base `BuildMissedIndices`, which reopens the folder through the unfiltered base scan — Go embedding has no virtual dispatch, so the gap filter was skipped and `SegmentsMax` advanced past history the backfill cannot reach. Shadowed, delegating to `BuildMissingIndices`. Same trap `OptimisticalyOpenFolder` was already shadowed for.

`openSegments` deduplicates its input now: a repeated name opened one segment's indexes from two goroutines, racing on the index slice and leaking the losing mmap.

Exported API: `CaplinView.BeaconBlockRotx`, `CaplinView.BlobSidecarRotx` and `CaplinView.BlobSidecarsSegment` are gone, replaced by `BeaconBlocks()`, `BlobSidecars()` and `ViewType(snaptype.BeaconBlocks)` for a `*snapshotsync.RoTx`. No in-repo callers.
author: awskii

title: cl/utils/eth_clock: ENR next_fork_version must not use an unscheduled fork
body:
`ForkId()` picked `next_fork_version` from the first fork-schedule entry above the current epoch, including forks parked at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`. The `next_fork_epoch` half of the same 16-byte field already normalises those away (`NextForkEpochIncludeBPO`), so the two halves disagreed.

Decoded from the `eth2` ENR field of two live nodes (QA sync-from-scratch, 2026-08-01):

| network | fork_digest | next_fork_version | next_fork_epoch |
|---|---|---|---|
| chiado | `0x25f9148e` | `0x07000000` | FAR_FUTURE |
| gnosis | `0x3237dab6` | `0x07000000` | FAR_FUTURE |

`0x07000000` is **mainnet's** `GLOAS_FORK_VERSION`. Neither `gnosisConfig()` nor `chiadoConfig()` overrides `GloasForkVersion`, so both inherit it from `MainnetBeaconConfig` and advertise a foreign chain's fork version. The [p2p-interface spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#eth2-field) requires:

> `next_fork_version` is the fork version corresponding to the next planned hard fork at a future epoch. If no future fork is planned, set `next_fork_version = current_fork_version` to signal this fact.

After the fix chiado advertises `0x0600006f` and gnosis `0x06000064` — their own current (Fulu) versions. Mainnet moves from `0x07000000` to `0x06000000` for the same reason.

**The fork digest is unchanged**, so this cannot affect gossip topics or existing peering — only the advertised `next_fork_version`.

<details><summary>How this surfaced</summary>

Found while investigating why `chiado` fails `QA - Sync from scratch` on nearly every run (e.g. [30698597994](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/30698597994), [30645661555](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/30645661555)) with `outcome: "Unexpected error", reason: "Deadline reached"` — Caplin sits in `DownloadHistoricalBlocks` for the whole window with `peerCount=0`.

This PR is **not** claimed as the fix for that. Erigon's chiado fork digest is correct: `0x25f9148e` reproduces as `sha256(pad32(0x0600006f) || GVR)[:4] XOR sha256(le64(948224) || le64(2))[:4]`, the EIP-7892 Fulu XOR using the Electra fallback `GetBlobParameters` returns for an empty `BlobSchedule`, and [upstream chiado config.yaml](https://github.com/gnosischain/configs/blob/main/chiado/config.yaml) confirms the inputs (`ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH: 948224`, `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA: 2`, `FULU_FORK_VERSION: 0x0600006f`). The same code path on gnosis produces the digest that node held 127 peers with.

chiado's real problem is discovery: its bootnodes are largely gone (5 of the 7 in `ChiadoBootstrapNodes` do not answer on port 9000, and all 7 ENRs are Bellatrix-era, `next_fork_version 0x0200006f`). Refreshing them from upstream does not help — the 3 entries upstream has that we lack are dead too. That needs a separate decision.
</details>

Driven by `TestForkIdNextForkVersionWithoutScheduledFork`, which asserts the precondition (`next_fork_epoch == FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`) and then the version fallback for chiado and gnosis. Red before the change with `actual: 0x07000000` on both.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/beacon: don't refetch the execution client version after a race
body:
`triggerELClientVersionFetch` checks the version cache and then takes the fetch slot in two separate steps:

```go
if a.engine == nil || a.elClientVersion.Load() != nil { return }
if !a.elClientVersionFetching.CompareAndSwap(false, true) { return }
```

A proposal that reads the cache as empty can win the slot *after* the fetch it raced against has cached the version and released the slot, so it spends a second engine round-trip for a value that is already there. The version is static for the lifetime of a connection, so the extra call is pure waste. Fixed by rechecking the cache after winning the slot, and releasing it if the value has landed.

This is what makes `race-tests / tests-linux (consensus, parallel)` fail intermittently on unrelated PRs: `TestDefaultGraffiti/concurrent cold-cache proposals trigger at most one fetch` sets a `Times(1)` expectation, and its `require.Eventually` poll runs a thousand proposals a second straight through the window.

The existing test only opened the window while its fetch was blocked on a channel, so it hit this by luck. The added test drives proposals against a fetch that *completes*; on main it fails in ~10ms without `-race`, and under `-race` on Linux it reproduces the CI error verbatim.

title: cl/ssz, common/ssz, engineapi: add recursive SSZ offset and length validation
body:
## Summary

- add opt-in validation for SSZ container and list offsets, encoding lengths, and boolean encodings
- reject gaps between fixed and dynamic sections, malformed dynamic-list offset tables, oversized extra data, non-canonical boolean encodings, and trailing bytes in all-static schemas
- propagate validation through nested lists, execution payloads, and payload attributes
- fall back to permissive nested decoding when a type has no strict decoder, with coverage tests guarding every current Engine schema fallback
- correctly decode the canonical four-byte representation of a single empty element on permissive dynamic-list paths
- keep Electra and Fulu `PayloadAttributes` on the Cancun-compatible wire shape; add `slot_number` and `target_gas_limit` only from Gloas
- keep strict decoding opt-in at existing decoder call sites

## Motivation

SSZ offsets define the canonical boundary between fixed and variable sections, and a fixed-size type has exactly one encoding length. A decoder that validates only the outer container can still accept unreferenced gap bytes or trailing padding inside nested values. SSZ booleans likewise have only two canonical byte encodings.

#21729 is the first consumer of these strict APIs. Its Engine API REST-SSZ request decoders require canonical offsets and encoding lengths throughout their nested request schemas. This PR provides that reusable validation while keeping strict decoding opt-in.

## Testing

- `go test ./common/ssz ./cl/ssz/... ./cl/cltypes ./cl/cltypes/solid ./execution/engineapi/engine_types -count=1`
- `go test ./execution/engineapi/... -count=1`

title: all: enable and resolve sprintfQuotedString and deferInLoop linter checks
body:
### Summary

Enables and fixes all codebase-wide violations for the `gocritic` linter checks **`sprintfQuotedString`** and **`deferInLoop`**.

### Why We Need It

#### 1. `sprintfQuotedString`
- **Proper JSON/String Escaping**: Replaces manual quote wrapping (like `"\"%s\""`) with `%q`. This ensures string variables containing special characters or quotes are safely escaped.
- **Readability & Clean Code**: Eliminates messy backslash escapes `\"%s\"` in format strings, making template strings cleaner and easier to maintain.

#### 2. `deferInLoop`
- **Memory Efficiency ($O(1)$ RAM)**: `defer` inside a loop delays cleanup until the outer function exits. Wrapping iterations in closures frees memory and allows Garbage Collection immediately after each loop step.
- **Resource & OS Handle Protection**: Prevents file descriptor and socket leaks (`EMFILE: too many open files`) by closing open files and HTTP bodies per iteration.
- **Database (MDBX) Health**: Releasing DB transactions and cursors on each iteration prevents MDBX page-map inflation and keeps B-tree lookups fast.
- **Timer & Goroutine Cleanup**: Immediately cancels `context` timers after each step instead of leaking background timer routines.

### What We Have Done

1. **`sprintfQuotedString` Fixes**: Refactored `fmt.Sprintf` calls across 9 files to replace manual quote escapes (`"\"%s\""`) with clean `%q` format specifiers.
2. **`deferInLoop` Refactoring**: Resolved 60 loop-deferral sites across 34 files:
   - **Scoped Iteration Closures**: Wrapped loop bodies in IIFEs (`func() { ... }()`) so `defer` runs at iteration end.
   - **Explicit Releases**: Replaced `defer` with explicit cleanup calls (`cancel()`, `file.Close()`, `r.Body.Close()`) where appropriate.
   - **Targeted Suppressions**: Added `//nolint:gocritic` on intentional loop deferrals (e.g. DB rollbacks in test/benchmark loops).

title: db/kv/mdbx: embed mdbx.Cursor by value in MdbxCursor
body:
`MdbxCursor` held `mdbx.Cursor` as a pointer, so every cursor cost a second heap object for a two-word wrapper (`txn`, `_c`) plus a pointer hop on each cursor operation. `mdbx.Cursor.Open` (erigontech/mdbx-go#248) initializes a cursor in place, so it becomes a plain field:

```go
type MdbxCursor struct {
	c mdbx.Cursor // was: c *mdbx.Cursor
	...
}
```

All other call sites are unchanged — method calls work the same on a value field.

### Where the closed marker lives now

The old code used the Go pointer being nil as the marker and nilled it by hand:

```go
if c.c != nil { c.c.Close(); delete(c.toCloseMap, c.id); c.c = nil }
```

A value cannot be nilled, so the marker moves inside: `mdbx.Cursor.Close()` already clears its own C handle, and `mdbx.Cursor.IsClosed()` reads it. `MdbxCursor.IsClosed()` keeps its behavior, which matters because `db/state/domain.go` asserts on it structurally via `interface{ IsClosed() bool }`.

`rawCursor` hands out the field address.

### Dependency

`mdbx-go v0.40.3 → v0.42.0`. The vendored libmdbx is **unchanged** — v0.40.3 and v0.42.0 carry the same tree (`ba27cbcd…`, libmdbx v0.14.2), so this bump is Go-side only.

The Go-side delta also brings:

- **#229** — cursor leak on `Close` after a write txn ends. mdbx-go used to skip `mdbx_cursor_close` for cursors whose write txn had already finished, assuming libmdbx had freed them; libmdbx does not. `MdbxCursor.Close` now actually releases.
- **#250** — `Cursor` and `Txn` carry a `noCopy` marker, so `go vet` copylocks rejects copying either. `go vet ./db/kv/... ./db/state/...` is clean.
- **#236** — `Txn.Unpark` gains a `restarted bool` result. Erigon does not call it.

### Scope

The C `MDBX_cursor` body is still `malloc`ed per cursor by `mdbx_cursor_open` — `MDBX_cursor` is opaque with no placement API. Dropping that needs `mdbx_cursor_create` + `Bind`/`Renew` reuse and is a separate change. `tx.toCloseMap` churn is untouched.

### Testing

`go build ./db/... ./cmd/...`, `go vet ./db/kv/... ./db/state/...`, `go test ./db/kv/...` (9 packages) and `go test ./db/state/...` (5 packages) pass on darwin/arm64.

title: cl/network: fix blob history backfill boundary and sparse-peer startup
body:
## Summary

- treat `FrozenBlobs()` as the exclusive end of frozen snapshot coverage and refresh it between scan batches
- start blob history backfill with any positive peer count while bounding active work, preserving exact process-local retry ownership, and revoking completion whenever a new hole appears
- accept legal short or reordered Deneb/Fulu column responses, reject responses outside the actual peer-filtered request before KZG or storage work, and persist only complete verified recovery results
- make PeerDAS recovery, pruning, req/resp, Sentinel, and embedded libp2p stream lifetimes cancellation- and progress-safe

## Root cause

Snapshot coverage owns slots strictly below `FrozenBlobs()`, but the downloader stopped at the watermark itself. The first unfrozen slot therefore belonged to neither snapshots nor history backfill. The downloader also required 16 peers before starting, so nodes with a healthy but smaller peer set never attempted recovery.

Lowering the peer threshold requires explicit progress and ownership invariants: empty responses must not advance cursors, active work must remain bounded, retry identities must not be silently coalesced or evicted, completion must be revoked as soon as a new retry appears, and cancellation must reach the underlying embedded libp2p stream. Legal partial responses must accumulate within the request window, while unrequested or duplicate data must be rejected before expensive verification or durable writes.

## Scope

This PR includes:

- exclusive and per-batch refreshed `FrozenBlobs()` handling
- any-positive-peer admission, with peer rechecks immediately before network recovery
- a backfill-only 15-second request window with exponential no-progress backoff and at most two active request workers, canceled and joined on every exit
- legal short or reordered Deneb accumulation by `(block_root, index)`, with proof/KZG verification and complete-block persistence
- no cursor advancement for empty successful range responses; repeated no-progress responses back off and trigger the configured HTTP fallback
- an initial best-effort scan of the current non-frozen range; later passes scan the latest two epochs plus process-local retry identities for blocks whose recovery failed in this process
- exact sparse retry identity retention without synthetic/coalesced slots, indexed scheduling, at most eight retry slots per pass, global retry pacing, fair live-versus-delayed selection, and release below frozen, retention, or prune floors
- compact process-local PeerDAS recovery ownership with metadata upgrades, queue-overflow handoff to the delayed scheduler, bounded 16 MiB reconstructed-result caching, and retry after transient storage validation or final-write failures
- monotonic process-local BlobStore and DataColumnStore prune floors that prevent active recovery from recreating data below a completed prune while still allowing cleanup removes
- exact validation of each data-column response against the peer-filtered wire-request snapshot `(slot, block_root, column_index)` before KZG verification or storage access; over-cardinality, duplicate, nil, schema-inconsistent, and unrequested responses are rejected as a whole
- exact validation of each response chunk's raw fork digest against the sidecar slot epoch, including same-`StateVersion` BlobSchedule/BPO transitions, before the response reaches PeerDAS, KZG verification, or storage
- whole-response preflight of Fulu signed-header signatures against immutable canonical full/blinded block metadata, preventing a valid-proof column with a poisoned proposer signature from becoming durable recovery input
- durable completion publication only when retry ownership is empty, plus immediate true-to-false revocation propagated to Antiquary when a new retry is added
- count-only admission for already stored blocks, while Deneb/Fulu/Gloas data recovered by this pass has independent durable read-back, identity, commitment, and KZG postconditions
- caller-context propagation through Sentinel, prompt reset of an established pre-response libp2p stream, preservation of explicit caller deadlines, and a 30-second fallback for no-deadline req/resp calls
- at most two active forward probes, canceled and joined on completion, timeout, or caller cancellation
- when the HTTP fallback successfully advances forward sync before P2P, subsequent batches prefer HTTP until a preferred HTTP attempt cannot commit blocks or make progress
- envelope batch and attempt timeouts that own the active RPC, with cancellation-aware retry pacing
- cancellation-aware unsynced waiting and safe low-slot arithmetic

### Resource and lifecycle boundary

Exact same-process retry conservation cannot be combined with a fixed identity-count cap without silently losing a recovery owner. This PR therefore keeps compact retry metadata in memory in proportion to the actual delayed recoverable roots/failures, while using indexed scheduling, constant global retry pacing, prune/retention cleanup, bounded live queues/workers, and a separate 16 MiB reconstructed-result cache. PeerDAS delayed roots already have an over-half quorum of durable column data, so the retained metadata is proportional to durable recovery input rather than an independent untrusted payload cache.

The retry ledger, recovery generations, and prune admission floors are intentionally process-local and reset on restart. This PR does **not** add durable retry persistence, startup reconstruction, or crash-consistent handoff. Those restart/durable-ownership semantics, together with permanent-hole policy and universal recovery-state reconstruction, are tracked in follow-up #23213 and will be implemented in a separate PR.

## Validation

- full affected package tests for `cl/das`, `cl/rpc`, `cl/phase1/network`, `cl/antiquary`, `cl/phase1/stages`, `cl/sentinel/httpreqresp`, `cl/sentinel/service`, and `cl/persistence/blob_storage`
- focused race tests for request/validation ownership, storage/prune ordering, exact retry scheduling, completion revocation, peer-filtered response membership, cancellation, and stream lifetime
- repeated RED-to-GREEN tests for sparse retry identity, PeerDAS ownership, transient storage/final-write failures, prune races, empty-response progress, completion revocation, and unrequested/duplicate/over-cardinality column responses
- `make lint` repeatedly with isolated caches: `0 issues`
- `make erigon integration`
- independent Deep Standards, Spec, state/lifecycle, boundary/integration, fix-delta, and evidence-truth review passes against a pinned immutable generation

Fixes #22429

Durable lifecycle follow-up: #23213
author: domiwei

title: cl: harden Gloas envelope persistence and ingestion
body:
## Summary

- replace Gloas envelope files through a temporary file and atomic rename so failed or concurrent replacements cannot expose partial data
- record and validate the supported envelope fork version in the file, P2P, and gossip representations; require the standard envelope version and blob-data HTTP headers
- reuse the fork graph SSZ buffer while detaching transaction bytes that alias decoder input
- keep `HasEnvelope` on its cache-only hot path; only successful writes and validated reads promote the cache
- serialize envelope reads, writes, and pruning so stale writers cannot restore pruned envelopes
- retain structurally invalid files for diagnosis while marking them unusable in memory; transient I/O failures remain retryable
- validate Gloas envelopes across gossip, RPC, HTTP, checkpoint, block production, and persistence boundaries before promotion or publication
- bind forward, backward, and recovered P2P envelopes to the canonical block and signed bid before satisfying roots, suppressing fallback, or advancing progress
- allow bid and payload fee recipients to differ while retaining payload integrity through the recomputed block hash
- keep progressive deposits semantically unbounded behind a resource guard while enforcing the four protocol-limited execution-request lists
- strictly decode parent execution requests and execution payload bids carried by block gossip
- reject invalid self-build envelopes before gossip while preserving queued and post-persistence index-repair outcomes
- keep local persistence and index-repair failures separate from gossip validation outcomes, and start blob backfill independently of envelope recovery completion
- enforce persisted envelope/block-root identity, reject decompressed RPC chunks above the 15 MiB transport bound before decoding, and validate matching nested versions, collection bounds, and complete nested representations
- bound JSON list and transaction materialization before allocation, require list decoders to be explicitly configured, reject trailing JSON values, and retain validated P2P response prefixes on a malformed suffix
- bound prune lock hold time per root and remove envelope files after invalidating their in-memory lineage
- retain bounded best-effort post-persistence index repair without allowing stale retries to overwrite newer indices or gating primary envelope persistence
- keep skipped-FULL recovery bounded while releasing stage readiness, and retry chain-tip blocks whose parent envelope is only temporarily unavailable
- preserve blob-backfill completeness transitions for late or replaced subscribers without invoking callbacks under the downloader lock or losing concurrent updates
- validate blob-inclusive REST envelopes for config, persistence size, and canonical block commitments before KZG expansion or column writes; keep the contents SSZ size contract exact
- construct locally produced Gloas data-column sidecars with progressive cell/proof lists so their roots match decoded sidecars
- use the first slot of the finalized epoch for the Gloas gossip cutoff, matching the specification's finalized-epoch boundary

## Production scope

Caplin creates the fork-choice filesystem under `dirs.Tmp/caplin-forkchoice` and clears it before constructing the fork graph on every process start. This PR therefore provides intra-process atomicity, ownership safety, and prune ordering; it intentionally does not claim crash durability or startup recovery. Directory fsync, quarantine files, startup scavenging, and committed-with-durability-warning handling are outside the real lifecycle and are not included.

Beacon-state persistence remains unchanged. It has a different file format and lifecycle and should be hardened separately rather than expanding this envelope-focused change.

The bounded in-memory envelope-index repair tracker is best-effort. When it is saturated, primary envelope persistence remains non-gating and auxiliary index recovery falls back to the existing pending/redelivery path. A durable overflow journal or startup reconciliation mechanism remains outside this PR.

## Root cause

Envelope writes truncated the final file in place, so a failed replacement could destroy the previously readable envelope and a concurrent reader could observe partial data. Reads decoded transaction slices from the fork graph reusable SSZ buffer, allowing a later read or write to mutate an envelope already returned to a caller. Pruning also removed envelope files without coordinating with writers, allowing a concurrent rename to restore a pruned file.

Envelope validation was also inconsistent across ingress paths. Canonical SSZ, configured resource bounds, progressive request semantics, JSON allocation limits, partial P2P progress, canonical block and bid commitments, and self-build publication errors were not uniformly enforced before decoded envelopes or parent execution requests reached hashing, caching, forkchoice, or gossip.

## Validation

- all `cl/...` short-test packages passed; packages affected by local linker disk exhaustion were rerun with `-p=2`
- affected CL packages: `cl/cltypes`, `cl/cltypes/solid`, `cl/beacon/handler`, `cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/phase1/network`, `cl/phase1/stages`, `cl/phase1/core/checkpoint_sync`, `cl/phase1/forkchoice`, `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph`, and `cl/rpc`
- focused `go test -race` for network services, RPC/network partial responses, fork-choice index repair, JSON decoding, blob-recovery lifecycle, and fork-graph envelope persistence
- two clean `make lint` scans on the final scoped head
- `make erigon integration`

The behavior changes were driven Red to Green through public handler, network-service, RPC, forkchoice, stage, and fork-graph methods. Regressions cover destructive replacement failures, shared-buffer mutation, prune/write resurrection, unrelated I/O during multi-root pruning, cache misses waiting on state I/O, transient open/read failures preserving trusted availability, structural corruption evicting warm cache, supported-version loss, nested-version mismatch, null list members before hashing, protocol-versus-decoder bounds, progressive deposits beyond the legacy Electra limit, alternate collection representations before persistence, root/file identity mismatch, oversized allocation and HTTP/P2P responses, malformed nested offsets, bounded JSON decoding, trailing JSON values, mixed-validity P2P response prefixes, invalid self-build publication, queued `ErrIgnore` behavior, post-persistence index repair, bounded blob-recovery retries, parent-envelope redelivery, blob-content prevalidation, and failed-removal cache exposure.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon: publish fork-choice head before state copy
body:
Fixes #23154.

## Problem

Beacon API `head` identity came from the memoized head state. That identity advances only after the new state has been copied, so block/root endpoints could return the parent for roughly 750 ms after fork choice had already selected the new head.

Calling `forkchoiceStore.GetHead(nil)` from public handlers avoids that lag, but it can perform expensive fork-choice/checkpoint-state work on a cache miss and can expose a selected root with the previous memoized state.

## Change

- Publish the selected `(root, slot)` from `ForkChoiceStore.GetHead` at the successful selection boundary, while the fork-choice lock still orders concurrent selections.
- Store selected-head and memoized-state identities as separate atomic pairs.
- Route identity-only `head` endpoints to selected head; state-backed endpoints continue using memoized state identity.
- Add an identity-aware state view so state, root, and slot are obtained from the same locked generation.
- Publish before EL notification/state copying, including cached, anchor fallback, pre-Gloas, Gloas, forward-sync, and local-block paths.
- Keep local side-branch submissions aligned with the actual selected root/state, and report head headers as canonical before canonical DB promotion completes.
- Report the selected root's fork-choice optimistic status from the debug heads endpoint.

Public read-only endpoints no longer invoke fork-choice computation when memoized head state is enabled.

## Trade-offs

- During the state-copy window, identity-only endpoints can report the newly selected root while state-backed endpoints still report the previous memoized state head. Each response remains internally consistent, but clients correlating separate endpoint responses can observe different heads.
- The selected identity is published before the EL fork-choice update. A head that EL later rejects can therefore be visible temporarily as execution optimistic until fork choice invalidates and replaces it.
- Local block submission resolves the actual selected root and state before notifying EL. A state lookup or replay, particularly after a side-branch submission, can therefore add latency to that notification.

## Testing

- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/beacon/synced_data -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/stages -count=1`
- `go test -race ./cl/beacon/synced_data -run '^(TestSelectedHeadRootAndSlotStayInOneGeneration|TestStateHeadRootAndSlotStayInOneGeneration|TestViewHeadStateWithIdentityStaysInOneGeneration|TestViewHeadStateRejectsMissingStateAfterReadinessPublished)$' -count=1`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

Focused coverage includes lower-slot replacement, cache hit, checkpoint-sync anchor fallback, Gloas selection, local side-branch selection, root/slot generation coherence, explicit current-head state roots, cold-state 503 responses, optimistic debug-head metadata, and pre-commit canonical header responses.
author: lystopad

title: all: enable makezero errchkjson noctx linters
body:
Enables 3 bug-catching linter rules in `.golangci.yml` (`makezero`, `errchkjson`, and `noctx`) and resolves all existing violations across the codebase to ensure continuous CI protection against subtle runtime bugs.

#### 1. `makezero`
- **What it prevents**: Prevents silent slice corruption where `make([]T, n)` is followed by `append()`, which unintentionally prepends `n` zero-value items at the beginning of a slice.
- **Benefits**: Guarantees slice allocations in Erigon are safe and clean, ensuring new code additions cannot introduce zero-padded array bugs into memory or state processing logic.

#### 2. `errchkjson`
- **What it prevents**: Prevents unhandled JSON serialization failures from `json.Marshal`, `json.MarshalIndent`, or `json.Encoder.Encode` failing silently when structs contain unsupported types, custom marshalers, or map keys.
- **Benefits**: Improves API reliability and logging accuracy by ensuring JSON encoding errors in RPC, REST endpoints, and tools are caught and logged rather than producing corrupt/empty payloads.

#### 3. `noctx`
- **What it prevents**: Prevents network request hangs and uncancelable HTTP/socket operations created with `http.NewRequest` instead of context-aware functions.
- **Benefits**: Ensures HTTP requests respect parent context timeouts and cancellation signals, preventing leaking goroutines and stuck network calls under heavy load or shutdown.
author: Sahil-4555

title: execution, cl, common/math: fix unchecked integer overflows on untrusted input
body:
Two unchecked integer overflows in code that parses untrusted input, found by compiling the unit suite with [gosentry](https://github.com/trailofbits/gosentry)'s arithmetic instrumentation (`go test -short ./...` surfaced 116 panics across 18 sites; the rest were intentional wraparound in SWAR, hashing and crypto code).

**RIP-7560 gas limits sum without an overflow check.** `ValidationGasLimit`, `PaymasterValidationGasLimit`, `GasLimit` and `PostOpGasLimit` come off the wire unvalidated and were added in four places. `chargeGas` turns the wrapped total into `preCharge` and compares it against the payer's balance, so a wrapped-small total passes the insufficient-funds check; `refundGas` then computes `preCharge - actualGasCost` from the same value.

**A bitlist with no sentinel bit corrupts its hash tree root.** `parseBitlist` reads `bits.Len8(last) - 1`; when the last byte is zero that underflows to 255 and inflates the length mixed into the root. An empty buffer indexed out of range.

| case | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GetGasLimit()` with `ValidationGasLimit = MaxUint64` | `15000` (base cost alone) | `MaxUint64`, checks fail closed |
| `chargeGas` / `refundGas` on an overflowing sum | wrapped total used | rejected with `ErrGasLimitReached` |
| `BitlistRootWithLimit([]byte{0x00})` | length 255 mixed into root | length 0 |
| `BitlistRootWithLimit([]byte{})` | `index out of range [-1]` | length 0 |

Both regression tests were confirmed to fail on unfixed code before the fix landed.

**`SafeSub` restored.** geth's `common/math` carries `SafeAdd`, `SafeSub` and `SafeMul`; erigon's copy dropped `SafeSub`, even though subtraction is the most common unchecked case. Two call sites computed the result first and detected the wrap afterwards — correct Go, but it relies on the wraparound it is trying to reject:

| site | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backward_beacon_downloader.go` | `slot - count + 1`, then `if start > slot` | `math.SafeSub(slot, count-1)` |
| `txn_executor.go` | `stNonce+1 < stNonce` | `math.SafeAdd(stNonce, 1)` |

Sites that already guard *before* subtracting (`eon_tracker.go`, `polygon/sync`, `txpool/pool.go`) are left alone — they are correct and converting them would be churn.

<details>
<summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `GetGasLimit()` is on the `Transaction` interface and cannot return an error, so it saturates to `MaxUint64`. That is the fail-closed direction: gas-pool and block-gas-limit checks then reject, where a wrapped-small value would pass. If the AA owners prefer validation to happen strictly earlier, the helper `TotalGasLimit` is there to build on.
- The `cl/merkle_tree` change is deliberately conservative: a bitlist whose last byte is non-zero — every well-formed one — hashes bit-identically to before. Only the malformed shapes change, from garbage/panic to a defined length of 0. Rejecting malformed bitlists outright may be more spec-correct than computing a root for them; that is a call for the Caplin owners, and `BitlistRootWithLimit` already returns an error if they want it.
- `TotalGasLimit` uses the existing `common/math.SafeAdd`, which carries out via `bits.Add64` rather than adding and testing for a wrap. A wrap-based guard is correct Go but is itself an overflow, so it trips the same instrumentation on every future sweep.
- Verified against `./cl/merkle_tree/...`, `./execution/types` and `./execution/protocol/...` — 9 packages, 0 failures.
- Not included: the `stage_senders.go` debug-log underflow and the Caplin epoch-0 wrap, both of which are wrapped-then-discarded and change no behavior.

</details>

author: domiwei

title: cl/antiquary: back off retirement steps that keep failing
body:
Refs #23224.

`antiquateBlobs` and `antiquate` only log their error, and `retirementLoop` re-enters every 12s, so a failure that is **deterministic rather than transient** is retried on every tick for the life of the process. Nothing about the node's state changes between attempts, so each retry redoes the same work and logs the same line.

Measured on a Gnosis archive node running `release/3.5`: a missing blob sidecar at slot 29403906 failed the same range **328 times in 65 minutes** at a flat 12s period. Each attempt re-read ~3900 beacon block bodies and, before #23233, abandoned a `seg.Compressor` and leaked its pattern workers — which is what actually OOM-killed the node at `alloc=58.7GB`.

With #23233 merged the leak is gone, but the retry storm itself remains: the CPU burn, the log spam, and blob pruning blocked indefinitely.

## Change

Each of the two retirement steps gets its own tick-counting backoff. On consecutive failures the number of skipped ticks doubles — 1, 2, 4, … capped at 300 ticks, roughly an hour — and a success resets it. A step that is simply idle is unaffected, since `ready()` only refuses ticks after a failure.

Counting ticks rather than reading a clock keeps the loop's existing cadence as the only time source and makes the unit deterministic to test.

`antiquate` gets the same treatment as `antiquateBlobs`: it shares the log-and-continue shape, and `dumpBeaconBlocksRange` has its own fatal paths (`skipped too many blocks in a row`, `expected %d blocks, got %d`) that can wedge the same way.

The shutdown path is unchanged — a cancelled context is still neither logged nor counted as a failure.

## What this does not do

It does not repair the underlying gap. A node wedged on a missing sidecar stays wedged, just quietly and cheaply instead of every 12 seconds. #23224 tracks what a missing sidecar *should* do — backfill it, record the gap and continue, or fail permanently — which changes what a blob snapshot means and wants a Caplin owner's call.

## Test

`TestRetirementBackoff*` pins the four behaviours: an unfailed step runs every tick, consecutive failures double the gap, the gap caps, and success resets. Written before the implementation; the type did not exist, so the package did not build.

`cl/antiquary/...` green, including under `-race`. `make lint` clean. `make erigon` builds.

author: lystopad

title: execution: key builders by payload timestamp and give them a lifecycle
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece. The payload-preparation work there depends on this, but every problem below is reachable on `main` today, so it stands alone.

Depends on #23343 (now merged), which wakes the real txpool condition wait when a builder's context is cancelled; without it a discarded builder can remain parked until another block or shutdown broadcasts the condition.

### Deduplication remembered only the last request

`lastParameters` held a single set of parameters, so any interleaved request for a different timestamp destroyed the deduplication for the first one. A repeated request then started a second builder for a payload already being built, and the first kept running unreachable.

Builders are now kept by the payload timestamp they are for, next to an immutable copy of the parameters they were created with. The copy matters: the caller owns the withdrawals slice and the pointer fields it passed, and could otherwise mutate them and change what a later comparison sees. The payload id is written to that copy, never back to the caller's parameters.

### A failed builder was reused forever

`BlockBuilder` latches its error, so once a build failed every later request that deduplicated onto it got that error back — spending the slot waiting for a payload that could never arrive. A failed builder is now treated as absent and dropped when its error surfaces.

Being stopped is deliberately not failure: a stopped builder still holds the payload it was stopped for, which is exactly what a repeated request is asking for.

### Eviction did not bound a builder's lifetime

This is the problem in #23101. Setting the interrupt flag is not enough, because `Builder.Build` ran its database read view and its transaction provider on the node-lifetime context, and the flag is not read until whichever of those is blocking returns on its own — up to most of a slot. An evicted builder therefore left the map while its goroutine and read view stayed alive.

A builder now answers two different requests:

- **Interrupt** — return the block you have so far. This is how a payload is collected and how the maximum build time is enforced; both want the payload.
- **Discard** — the payload is not wanted, release what you hold. This cancels the context the build runs under, so a read view or a transaction provider blocked on it returns at once.

Eviction discards. `BlockBuilderFunc` takes a context, `NewBlockBuilder` derives a per-builder cancellable one, and `Build` uses it for `BeginTemporalRo`, `NewSharedDomains`, `createBlock` and `execBlock` — which is how it reaches `ProvideTxns`. `Builder.ctx` is removed rather than left beside it.

The maximum-build watchdog interrupts first and then gives the build a grace of half a slot to finish up — the transaction in flight, the packing tail, payload finalization. A build that has not returned by then is taken as stuck and discarded. The grace deliberately bounds finalization too: an earlier acknowledgement-based variant let a build that wedged after acknowledging — in finalization, say — keep its resources forever, and a healthy build inside a single heavy transaction could not acknowledge at all and was discarded together with its payload.

Two deliberate limits:

- eviction stays asynchronous, so this is not a hard bound on live builders at any instant. It changes the window from "until the blocking call gives up on its own" to "as fast as a cancelled call returns", and a discarded builder reads as gone at once to new callers — deduplication passes it over and a new `GetAssembledBlock` answers unknown-payload — while its goroutine winds down. A collector already waiting keeps a valid payload that completes as discard lands. Making eviction wait would block `AssembleBlock` while holding the module semaphore.
- the build context carries no deadline of its own; `buildDuration` and the stop grace are both derived from the chain's slot length. The grace bounds only finishing up after the stop, not the build itself, so it is not a fork-specific build budget.

Fixes #23101.

### Cancellation

Both entry points check for a cancelled caller before acting, so an expired request reports why it stopped instead of looking like contention, which callers retry; `AssembleBlock` also refuses once the module's own context is over, so no builder is born after shutdown. `GetAssembledBlock` asks the builder whether the build itself failed rather than inspecting the returned error, which a build can populate with a context error of its own.

Discard may race a caller already waiting in `GetAssembledBlock`. `BlockBuilder.Stop` owns that race: discard without a payload returns `ErrDiscarded` immediately, while a valid payload that completes as discard lands remains available to the waiting collector and later retries. A completed payload or build error also wins over simultaneous caller cancellation, so `Stop` reports the latched outcome rather than the caller's context error. A failure completed before discard also remains the build's failure instead of being rewritten as unknown-payload. Execmodule maps only `ErrDiscarded` to unknown-payload and drops that builder.

Cancellation reaches finalization and the asynchronous seal-result wait as well. `finishBlock` checks the context before clearing or publishing the assembled block and before starting the seal, and `Build` stops waiting for a seal result when the context ends. `Seal` implementations must not retain the transaction-backed chain reader after `Seal` returns, so the cancelled build can release its read resources safely.

The in-process Caplin adapter and `ExecModuleTester` turn an unknown result into `ErrUnknownPayload`. `IsUnknownPayloadError` recognizes both that sentinel and the remote Engine API `-38001` error. Block production treats either form as terminal, warns once, and does not keep polling an id that cannot produce.

### Tests

Deduplication and lifetime are covered directly: builders kept apart by timestamp, a superseded builder still packing and still retrievable by an id already handed out, a collected payload handed back to a repeated request rather than starting a second builder, a failed builder not reused and dropped once its error surfaces, a caller cancelled *while `Stop` is waiting* leaving the builder collectable, an evicted builder blocked in its provider actually completing rather than merely having a flag set, a discarded builder reading as gone at once — passed over by deduplication and answered as unknown by `GetAssembledBlock` — the watchdog discarding a build that never observes its stop while keeping a healthy one that is merely slow to observe it, a build that wedges after observing the stop released at the end of its grace, eviction passing over a failed builder however live its slot, `AssembleBlock` refusing to register a builder after shutdown, and the caller's parameters never written to.

The completion boundary is covered in both directions: discard while `Stop` is waiting returns unknown when no payload survives, while a valid payload that completes as discard lands remains replayable; a failure completed first remains visible; and an unfinished discarded builder reads as gone immediately. Builder coverage also pins replay idempotency, the discarded fast path, both finalization cancellation checks, cancellation of the seal-result wait, and preference for a completed payload or build error over simultaneous caller cancellation. The tester and both local and remote Caplin paths cover unknown-payload conversion, terminal polling, and the warning emitted for that terminal result.

author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1, execution: give the execution module a typed busy signal and the caller's context
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece. Independent of the other parts of that series.

### Contention was indistinguishable from rejection

`AssembleBlock` and `GetAssembledBlock` reported a busy execution module as `errors.New("execution data is still syncing")`. That message is inaccurate — it is weight-one semaphore contention with a forkchoice update or another payload request, not syncing — and being an untyped error, callers could not tell it apart from a real rejection.

Both now return `chainreader.ErrExecutionBusy`, and the assemble retry waits only on that. Previously a permanent rejection — mismatched withdrawals, for instance — was retried thirty times across six seconds before surfacing, which spends the proposal slot rather than reporting the problem.

### The retry ignored its caller

The loop was `for range 30 { ...; time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond) }`, with no context check anywhere. A cancelled caller still waited the full six seconds. It is now an extracted helper that checks the context before each attempt and waits on it rather than on a bare sleep.

While there, `ChainReaderWriterEth1.AssembleBlock` and `GetAssembledBlock` take the caller's context instead of substituting `context.Background()`, so the deadline a caller sets actually reaches the execution module.

### Tests

The helper is covered directly: first success, stopping on a rejection, exhausting attempts on contention, cancellation mid-flight and before the first attempt, and the zero-attempts guard.

Part of a series splitting #23105.
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon: report a failing payload poll once, and an unregistered fee recipient at all
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece.

### A failing window reported once

`pollAssembledPayload` retries at the retry cadence, so a slot whose payload never arrived reported itself once per attempt and buried everything else in that slot.

It is now reported when the window is over, once, carrying the slot, how many attempts failed and the first reason — the first rather than the last, because a hundred repeats of "connection refused" followed by one "still syncing" should not be attributed to the latter.

An unknown payload ID is terminal rather than a transient collection failure: polling stops after the first response and the request reports one Warning.

Two cases stay out of warning and error logs:

- a window that fails and then succeeds. That is a healthy slot.
- a caller that went away. A validator client timing out or a node shutting down cancels the request context, which comes back through the collection call; that is the slot ending, not the execution layer failing.

A failure that happened *before* the caller left is still reported, since giving up is often the consequence of it.

### An unregistered fee recipient is worth saying once

Production falls back to the zero address when nothing is registered for the proposer, which gives that block's fees away, and said nothing about it.

It now warns once per proposer, claimed in one step so that block template requests for the same slot arriving together do not each decide they are the first, and bounded so an unregistered proposer cannot accumulate. A dev chain rotates through 64 proposers and never registers any of them, so remembering only the most recent one warned on nearly every proposal.

The warning names the registration it consulted rather than claiming none exists anywhere: under Gloas a signed proposer preference can carry one, which this lookup does not read. That is #23300.

### Production failures have one owner

`produceBlock` owns the actionable record for failures returned by body production. Body steps return their causes instead of logging locally, so a failed proposal produces one record carrying the slot and the underlying reason. An unknown payload is a Warning; other actionable failures are Errors.

This covers every body failure path, including an empty payload ID from `ForkChoiceUpdate`: the returned cause keeps the "EL may be syncing" hint without a separate warning or a generic follow-up error. Concurrent body steps report through separate error variables, which are read after all steps finish.

Caller cancellation is classified at the same boundary and remains a debug event rather than an error. A failure observed before cancellation is still returned and reported.

Part of a series splitting #23105.
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon: resolve payload withdrawals in one place
body:
Split out of #23105, which grew too large to review in one piece.

### What this does

`produceBeaconBody` chose between three withdrawal sources inline — a Gloas head whose payload was revealed, a Gloas head whose payload was not, and everything before Gloas — each with its own hand-written conversion loop, and then assembled the payload attributes around whichever it picked.

The choice is now a method that names what it selects between, and the attributes come from a single version-aware constructor. What is left inline is the genuinely fork-specific part: the two fields only Gloas sends. The three conversion loops go through the shared converter from #23271, which are the call sites @yperbasis pointed out as still hand-written when reviewing that PR.

### Behaviour change

The refactor itself is behaviour-neutral, but the constructor also fixes two cases where the old inline construction built a request the chosen wire version cannot express:

- **the parent beacon block root is omitted below Deneb** — Capella and Bellatrix dispatch to `forkchoiceUpdatedV2`/`V1`, and `validatePayloadAttributesPreFCU` rejects a non-nil parent root there with `InvalidPayloadAttributesErr`;
- **withdrawals are omitted below Capella** — Bellatrix dispatches to `forkchoiceUpdatedV1`, which has no withdrawals field, and the expectation is a non-nil empty slice, so one was being sent.

Both only bite on the engine transport, and both made the request fail rather than be ignored.

### Withdrawal source equivalence

The routing is otherwise unchanged, including the details that are easy to lose in a refactor:

- a FULL Gloas head reads from the state copy with the parent payload applied, not from the head state;
- an EMPTY Gloas head reads the expectation the state already cached, and does not compute a fresh one;
- before Gloas the expectation is computed from the head state;
- the resulting slice keeps its nil-ness in every case.

`TestExpectedWithdrawalsReadsTheRightSourcePerFork` gives the two Gloas states different withdrawal outcomes, so it fails if the source selection is removed rather than passing either way. `TestPayloadAttributesOmitFieldsTheChosenVersionCannotCarry` pins the two gates across every fork.

title: all: resolve errorlint linter findings
body:
This PR resolves `errorlint` warnings across the codebase to enforce proper Go error handling and error wrapping practices.

- **Error Wrapping:** Replaced non-wrapping `%v`/`%s` format specifiers with `%w` in `fmt.Errorf` calls wrapping `error` parameters.
- **Error Comparison:** Replaced direct `==` and `!=` error checks with `errors.Is(err, target)`.
