- **Intentional Guard:** Preserved the intentional bare sentinel check in `execution/types/block.go` via `//nolint:errorlint`.
author: Sahil-4555

title: cl/beacon: preserve actionable production failures
body:
Payload polling and concurrent block-body production can hide a useful failure behind busy/unknown-payload responses or cancellation. Preserve that failure in the returned error and production log.

- Rank errors by diagnostic value: concrete failure > unexpected internal cancellation > unknown payload > execution busy > caller cancellation. A terminal unknown-payload response takes precedence over transient contention.
- Keep the earlier polling error on equal priority. When concurrent execution-payload and sync-aggregate failures have equal priority, prefer the execution error. If both are concrete failures, retain the sync-aggregate failure as text in the same returned error and log.
- Identify fork-choice and payload-collection cancellations observed while the request is still active. Keep them distinct from caller cancellation even if the request is canceled before reporting.
- Use consistent log levels: caller cancellation at debug, unknown payload at warning, and busy responses, unexpected internal cancellation, and concrete failures at error.
- Document and test bounded fee-recipient warning deduplication: warnings can repeat after eviction. Runtime cache behavior is unchanged.

Follow-up to #23274.
author: yperbasis

title: cl/phase1: report forkchoice timeouts and missing payload IDs
body:
First of two, extracted from #23105. It addresses the third blocking concern in domiwei's review and a defect in every Engine API forkchoice path today, not only the one #23105 adds.

## Problem

`ExecutionClientEngine.ForkChoiceUpdate` had two ways to report a failed payload request as an empty success.

First, a returned deadline error was mapped to `(nil, nil)`:

```go
if err.Error() == errContextExceeded {
    return nil, nil
}
```

Second, Erigon's configured internal FCU timeout does not reach this client as an error. The execution module returns `ExecutionStatusBusy`, the Engine API maps that to `SYNCING` with a null payload id, and the client returned `([]byte{}, nil)` because `SYNCING` is not a payload-status error.

For an update carrying payload attributes, a missing id means no payload build started. A caller treating `err == nil` as success skips the retry it would otherwise make, so a slow or busy execution layer can cost a proposal. Block production also reported the empty id as "execution layer may be syncing", hiding an actual returned deadline.

A head-only update is different: without payload attributes, a null payload id is expected.

Deadline recognition was also a string comparison against one exact gRPC message. Any rewording, or a transport that phrases it differently, silently stopped matching.

## Change

`ErrForkChoiceUpdateTimeout` wraps a returned deadline cause. It is recognised through a wrapped `context.DeadlineExceeded`, the gRPC status code, or the old message as a last resort for a transport carrying neither.

`ErrForkChoiceUpdateNoPayloadID` reports an attribute-bearing response with no payload id. Payload-status validation runs first, so a supplied validation error keeps priority. Head-only updates keep their existing empty-id success.

The missing-id result is not called a timeout. Engine API `SYNCING` can also represent execution contention, a missing segment, or a head that is too far away. The separate sentinel states what is known and lets each caller decide whether to retry or fail.

Call sites keep the behaviour they need:

- `stages/forkchoice.go` and `storeBlockAndBlobs` still tolerate returned timeouts because they do not need a payload id.
- `block_collector` already warns on any error.
- Block production treats a timeout or an attribute-bearing response without an id as a failure because it cannot build the block without that id.

## Verification

Regression coverage checks wrapped context deadlines, gRPC deadline status, the legacy message, unrelated errors, and a `SYNCING` response with a null payload id.

- `make test-short`
- `make erigon integration`
- `make check-generated`
- affected-package tests
- `make lint`
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon: prime the execution layer before a slot this node proposes
body:
Payload construction currently starts inside the proposal slot. A busy execution layer consumes time that the block needs for propagation and attestation. This PR starts the local payload builder one slot early when the next proposer belongs to a registered validator. Production can then collect the prepared payload instead of starting the same build from cold.

## Scope

Preparation runs only with the validator API and the direct in-process execution client. It starts at Capella and retires at Gloas, where builders gossip bids instead. Work is limited to the next slot and stops early when the proposer is not registered.

Fulu proposer lookahead is consulted before copying and advancing the full beacon state. A Fulu node that is not due to propose therefore avoids the large copy and epoch-transition allocation. At a pre-Fulu epoch boundary, proposer lookup still advances a state copy because the proposer cannot be read from the unadvanced state.

## Design and correctness

Preparation reads the beacon root, proposer and state from one atomic head view. It derives the fee recipient, withdrawals and payload attributes for the target slot, then confirms that the selected consensus head and local execution head still match the intended parents.

The direct execution client starts the payload builder directly without changing fork choice. Production keeps its normal forkchoice update. Both paths use the same payload-attribute helper, so an identical head and attributes reuse the existing execution-module build and return the same payload ID.

A prepared record changes the payload collection window only when its slot and payload ID exactly match the production result and the builder has been running for the required minimum time. A changed head, changed inputs, missed preparation or failed attempt therefore falls back to ordinary production.

## Liveness and cost

The admission gate covers only each short builder-start attempt. Production holds the other side of the gate while constructing a validator block and while storing a locally produced block. Production can wait only for an attempt that has already entered; new preparation attempts are refused until production finishes. Preparation never holds the gate while copying state, advancing slots or waiting to retry.

If the local execution module is busy or has not yet adopted the intended parent, preparation retries every 100 ms until the target slot begins. Each builder-start attempt is one-shot; preparation does not add retry or cancellation behavior to canonical or production forkchoice updates.

Preparation is best effort. Its failures do not fail a proposal, and production keeps the cold path when no matching prepared payload is available.

## Follow-up

An operator setting, preparation metrics and real-execution-module reuse coverage remain tracked in #23419.
author: lystopad

title: execution: optimise incoming bal encoding/decoding/validation path
body:
for https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/14522

noticed that we were doing unnecessary operations for the incoming bal at new payload and other places:
- we were doing unnecessary bal validations every time we called rlp Decode - unnecessary, Decode has only 1 responsibility - to decode rlp bytes in a struct - validation is a separate check that can be done only once at API entry point
- we were doing 4 bal rlp Decode calls in 1 new payload request - 1 in engineapi on receiving it, 1 in `stage_exec` as part of `bal.Process`, 1 more in stage_exec as part of `(*parallelExecutor).execImpl`, 1 in the read aheader
- we were doing 1 avoidable bal rlp Encode in `bal.Process` as part of `stage_exec`
- we were also missing the opportunity to do static bal validation as early as possible and return early in new payload instead of proceeding forward with execution to later on find out an invalid bal

this was improved by:
- decoupling bal validation checks from bal rlp decoding
- moving decoding and validation at the API entry points, doing them only once - engine_newPayload, Caplin CL payload consumer, EL block downloader, InsertBlocks
- introducing `BlockAccessListSidecar` to carry the raw input bytes and the decoded BlockAccessList type attached to the block so that we eliminate the unnecessary Decode (need in `stage_exec`) and Encode (needed in `InsertBlocks`) 
- we also introduce memoization of the block access list hash computation on the sidecar so that the work is not repeated. same goes for validation too (safe since the sidecar is immutable)

results:
| Operation | Before | After | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| RLP decode | 4 | 1 | 3 |
| RLP encode | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| BAL validation | 7 | 1 | 6 |
| **Total operations** | **12** | **2** | **10** |
author: taratorio

title: cl, common: reuse snappy stream codecs from a pool
body:
Every `snappy.NewReader` / `NewBufferedWriter` allocates ~142 KB of scratch buffers (2 allocs). `parseResponseData` built one per response chunk, so a 64-block `BeaconBlocksByRange` response burned ~8.7 MB of garbage; the sentinel handlers and the fork-graph state dump paid it per message.

New `common/snappypool` holds a reader and a writer pool, and every call site in `cl/` takes its codec from there — including the tests, so copy-paste keeps using it. `PutReader`/`PutWriter` reset to nil first, otherwise a parked codec pins the caller's stream or buffer.

The `forkGraphDisk.sszSnappyReader`/`sszSnappyWriter` fields go away with it: the pool replaces the hand-rolled per-struct cache, and a closed `afero.File` is no longer retained after a read.

Existing `cl/sentinel/...`, `cl/rpc` and `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph` suites pass, `-short` and `-race`.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/persistence, db: pool zstd decoders, lower what zstd encoders hold
body:
Eight caplin decode sites built a zstd decoder per call and released it with `Close`, which is permanent — so nothing was ever reused. `base_encoding` now owns a `zstdReaderPool` next to its writer pool, and the six sites in `historical_states_reader.go` plus `uint64_diff.go` and `rabbit.go` take from it.

`WithLowerEncoderMem(true)` flips the encoder history buffer from two windows to one window plus a block (`enc_base.go` `ensureHist`), and `Reset` keeps that buffer for the encoder's life — so it is what a pooled or long-lived encoder holds, not a per-call cost. Applied to the `beacon_indicies` pool and the `db/compress` encoder.

Output is byte-identical, which these paths need: `WriteBeaconBlock`'s bytes are copied verbatim into the caplin `.seg` files, and `db/compress` feeds `db/seg`. `TestZstdWriterPoolMatchesReferenceEncoderOptionsOnLargePayload` pins that at 4MiB — above zstd's 128KiB block size, where window options start to change output.

`WithEncoderConcurrency` is deliberately not set: in `db/compress` it is what serves concurrent `EncodeAll` callers.

Behaviour changes:

- The four `freezeblocks` reader sites propagate the `Decoder.Reset` error they used to drop.
- All three release helpers drop a decoder whose `Reset(nil)` fails instead of pooling it. `Reset` returns only `ErrDecoderClosed`, and a closed decoder cannot be revived, so pooling it poisoned the pool for the life of the process.
- `historical_states_reader` returns each decoder right after the read rather than at function exit, so a large-frame decoder is not pinned across the per-slot diff loop that borrows from the same pool.

Not addressed here: pooled decoders retain their frame-history buffer, so a multi-MB dump decoder can be reused for small diffs; both decoder pools use the default `GOMAXPROCS` concurrency, which suits large payloads and not small ones, so the fix is probably a second pool rather than one setting. `cl/antiquary/beacon_states_collector.go` holds a long-lived encoder that did not get `WithLowerEncoderMem`.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: harden local payload preparation and Gloas fallbacks
body:
Follow-up to #23399. ## Why Starting the local execution builder in the slot before a known proposer duty reduces cold-start work. Production can reuse that work only for an identical build request and payload ID; preparation must also yield to production, publication, and adoption. ## Behavior - From Capella onward, nodes with the validator API and direct execution client use `StartPayloadBuild`, never a speculative fork-choice update (FCU). - Before Gloas, preparation builds on the selected execution head; a Gloas target with a pre-Gloas head uses the pre-fork parent. - Steady-state Gloas preparation covers genuine EMPTY paths whose parent is already the execution head. It waits for PTC only for a current-slot head; FULL and FULL-to-EMPTY paths stand down. - Production resolves its proposal's parent, sends the normal FCU, and inherits warmup only for an exact payload-ID match. - Gloas production verifies the beacon parent before execution work, including the fork-transition slot. A root mismatch or failed head lookup rejects the proposal. Only unresolved payload status or an unreadable FULL envelope on a verified head uses the EMPTY-parent fallback; read failures carry their cause. - The registered-builder bid endpoint checks the beacon root and execution parent from one coherent head snapshot, then rechecks the root, payload status, and live PTC-derived parent path after envelope resolution and before caching. It shares production's parent-resolution rules, including the EMPTY fallback. Head changes return HTTP 404 whether detected before building or during revalidation. - A missing MEV-Boost client or a relay bid that fails validation keeps the local payload. Relay checks include the expected withdrawals root and fork-correct blob limits, with schedules applied from Fulu. - Proposer-preference retries receive HTTP 200 only when the stored message and signature both match. Conflicts return indexed HTTP 400 errors without replacing the accepted preference. ## End-to-end flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Slot N: proposer duty for N+1"] --> B["Wait for slot N selected head
or bounded stale-head fallback"] B --> C{"Fork and parent path"} C -- "Pre-Gloas" --> D["Derive production-equivalent inputs"] C -- "Gloas target with pre-Gloas head" --> E["Use pre-fork parent
and transition withdrawals"] C -- "Current-slot Gloas head" --> F["Wait for PTC deadline
and re-read head"] C -- "Older Gloas head" --> G{"Resolved Gloas path"} F --> G G -- "Genuine EMPTY" --> D G -- "FULL or FULL-to-EMPTY" --> H["Stand down"] G -- "Pending, root mismatch,
or lookup failure" --> I["Retry later"] E --> D D --> J["StartPayloadBuild without FCU"] J --> K["Record payload ID, head,
and earliest successful start"] K --> L["Production resolves proposal parent"] H -. "proposal time" .-> L I -. "proposal time: re-resolve" .-> L L -- "Gloas root mismatch
or head lookup failure" --> X["Reject proposal"] L -- "resolved parent or EMPTY fallback" --> P["Send normal FCU"] P --> M{"Same payload ID?"} M -- "yes" --> N["Advance first collection by
inherited warmup, capped"] M -- "no" --> O["Use normal collection timing"] ``` The scheduler waits for the current slot's selected head through its attestation deadline. It may then use an older head unless local block work or an active `OnBlock` call blocks the fallback. A rejected block does not suppress it for the rest of the slot. ## Input and state guarantees - Preparation and production share parent resolution. A Gloas proposal with a pre-Gloas parent uses the advanced state's withdrawal sweep. Gloas-at-genesis follows the EMPTY path and uses cached withdrawals. FULL production applies the parent's execution requests before deriving withdrawals. - Shared attributes cover timestamp, `prevRandao`, fee recipient, withdrawals, parent beacon root, slot, and target gas limit. Payload-ID mismatches log both heads. - Preparation and normal v3/v4 self-build production use the validator registration's fee recipient. The registered-builder bid endpoint uses the proposer preference's recipient; different recipients are different build requests. - Head root, proposer, and state come from one view; the root is rechecked before and after builder startup. - Head-event publication reads the root, slot, and payload status from one coherent snapshot, avoiding inconsistent data or dropped events caused by separate reads. - Gloas head calculations use one slot snapshot for filtering, weights, and payload tiebreakers. Pre-fork calculations recheck the fork after checkpoint I/O to avoid overwriting a newer Gloas head, and pre-Gloas results carry PENDING status. - Scratch state reuses large buffers, resets to the source fork version on copy, and is released after a settled outcome or target-slot change. - Fulu lookahead rejects unregistered proposers before copying; pre-Fulu epoch-boundary checks advance state when needed. - A 500 ms lead floor is checked before and after state work; block work is checked before copying and builder startup. - Settled outcomes are keyed by target slot, head, registration generation, Gloas path, proposer index, and effective target gas limit (including whether it is set). Unrelated preference changes do not trigger re-preparation. - Pending or root-mismatched Gloas status is not primeable. Concurrent Gloas head readers recheck the cache under the store lock to avoid duplicate tree walks. Current-slot PTC votes leave the cache intact; slot transitions and accepted late PTC votes invalidate it. ## Coordination ```mermaid flowchart TB V["Validated production"] --> R["Shared block-work gate"] P["Active publication, storage, and adoption"] --> R E["Local envelope execution"] --> R D["Preparation tick"] --> C{"Gate idle?"} C -- "no" --> Z["Skip this tick"] C -- "yes" --> W["Derive state and attributes"] W --> X{"Exclusive TryLock"} X -- "busy" --> Z X -- "acquired" --> Q{"Produced-slot marker pending?"} Q -- "yes: release gate" --> Z Q -- "no" --> S["StartPayloadBuild"] R -. "blocks early probe" .-> C R -. "excludes builder startup" .-> X M["Bounded produced-slot markers"] -. "signing and queued-storage gap" .-> D M -. "recheck under lock" .-> Q I["Active OnBlock"] -. "suppresses stale fallback" .-> D ``` Shared block-work holders may overlap. Preparation derives state outside the gate, then uses exclusive `TryLock` and rechecks produced-slot markers before builder startup. This closes the production-to-signing race. Preparation never queues ahead of handler work; handler work may wait for a short builder-start call already in progress. Per-slot markers cover a bounded signing margin, not arbitrary signer or queue delays. A waiting publication call clears its marker only after successful integration. Non-waiting publication and failed attempts retain it, subject to expiry or selection of a head for that slot. Queued storage holds no gate; it takes the shared side when it runs. Separate envelope publication does not manage the marker. Network imports remain outside the gate; active `OnBlock` only advises the stale-head fallback. ## Collection timing Production advances collection only for an exact prepared payload-ID match: ```text collection advance = min(inherited warmup, maximum prepared advance) first collection = normal first collection - collection advance ``` The first poll is clamped to now. The cap leaves the builder running into the proposal slot; earlier successful collection trades some transaction recency for earlier readiness. | Fork timing | Normal first poll | Earliest prepared first poll | Maximum advance | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Pre-Gloas | 2.9 s | 0.9 s | 2.0 s | | Gloas EMPTY | 2.15 s | 0.65 s | 1.5 s | These values assume a 12-second slot. Shorter warmup advances collection proportionally; a missing or mismatched prepared build keeps the normal window. ## Suggested review order 1. `cl/beacon/handler/payload_preparation.go`: scheduling, supported paths, memoization, and coordination. 2. `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`: parent resolution, liveness fallback, collection timing, and publication markers. 3. `cl/phase1/forkchoice` and `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/copy.go`: head-status freshness, active imports, and version-safe state reuse. 4. `cl/pool/epbs_pool.go` and `cl/phase1/execution_client/execution_client_direct.go`: preference storage and direct builder startup. ## Verification Handler, state, and fork-choice unit tests, targeted race tests, `make lint`, and `make erigon integration` pass. Regression coverage includes head verification at the Gloas transition, head-lookup failure propagation, bid-endpoint head-change responses, relay withdrawals roots and fork-specific blob limits, queued-storage marker retention, missing Gloas payload data, and prepared Gloas EMPTY collection. Behavior-preserving cleanups and comment edits use existing tests rather than new red–green cycles. ## Remaining work - #23551: steady-state Gloas FULL priming needs a canonical execution-head update; envelope validation with `NewPayload` does not move the head. - #23419: broader execution coordination and observability, intra-slot builder reuse, repeated Gloas-envelope decoding, stable-failure memoization, an independent disable setting, and the hybrid engine client's payload-ID byte order. - Preparation policy for very short slots or expensive epoch transitions remains separate design work.
author: yperbasis

title: cl, cmd: collapse the caplin hot sidecar stores onto one bucket store
body:
`BlobStore` and `dataColumnStorageImpl` are the same object — an afero store bucketed by `slot / subdivisionSlot` — with path building and bucket pruning copy-pasted between them. This extracts the shared half into a `bucketStore`, fixes two bugs the duplication hid, and moves the retention floor out of the stores and into the caller.

Both `Prune` implementations walked every 10,000-slot bucket from slot 0 on every call, and `cleanupAndPruning` runs once per slot, so that was `(head-keep)/10_000` `RemoveAll` syscalls every 12 s on mainnet and every 5 s on gnosis, against directories the first pass already removed. It is now a readdir over the buckets that exist.

Closes #23413.

## Changes

- `bucketStore` in `cl/persistence/blob_storage/bucket_store.go` owns path derivation, write, read, exists, remove, stream and prune. It never locks; the façades take a slot lock at the granularity of the real operation — the whole `WriteBlobSidecars` batch, files-plus-count-row in `ReadBlobSidecars` and `RemoveBlobSidecars`, the whole `GetSavedColumnIndex` and `RemoveColumnSidecars` loops. Single-file reads and `stream` take nothing, so a slow peer holds no lock.
- `pruneBelow` readdirs the store root and accepts an entry as a bucket only when it is a directory whose name parses as `uint64` and formats back byte-identically. The blob index MDBX lives at `<CaplinBlobs>/chaindata`, a sibling of the numeric buckets, so a looser filter would delete it; the old integer-built paths could not reach it. It continues past a failed `RemoveAll` and returns the first error.
- Writes land by rename onto a temp file, so a failed encode no longer leaves a truncated file that `Stat` then treats as complete forever. `ssz_snappy.EncodeAndWrite` flushes in a defer and drops that error, so `write` hands it a writer that records one.
- `RemoveBlobSidecars` tolerates an already-absent file instead of returning on the first one and leaving the count row behind.
- `Prune()` and `Prune(keepSlotDistance)` become `PruneBelow(slot uint64)` on `BlobStorage`, `DataColumnStorage` and `PeerDas`; `slotsKept` leaves both constructors and the distance is computed in `cleanupAndPruning`, which is now the only place the three hot floors are decided. `PeerDas.PruneBelow` still advances the peer-advertised `EarliestAvailableSlot`.
- `RemoveAllColumnSidecars` is deleted — no production callers.

Retention is unchanged for every flag combination on every network. Blocks still cut against the stage's observed head and hot sidecars against the wall clock; unifying those is a separate decision.

## Notes

Overwriting a sidecar that another goroutine holds open fails on Windows, where `os.Rename` is `MoveFileEx` and needs delete access to the destination. The target is already a complete file for that `(slot, root, index)`, so `write` keeps it and reports success rather than surfacing an error that `gossip_manager` would turn into a peer ban.

Follow-ups this makes cheap, each filed separately: the flat bucket directory (#23426), the column custody bitmap that would replace 128 `Stat` calls per availability check (#23433), the kzg index rows that leak on prune (#23432), and a now-dead `ethClock` parameter (#23450).
author: awskii

title: cl/beacon: report a syncing node as 503, not 500
body:
Fixes #23462.

A node with no head state — starting up, restarting, catching up — answered **500 Internal Server Error** on endpoints where `beacon-APIs` declares **503 CurrentlySyncing**. It is transiently unavailable, not faulty, and 500 reads as a node fault to operators and alerting.

Same node, same cause, two different codes today: `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/attestations` already returns 503 (`pool.go` sets it explicitly), while the committee subscription endpoints return 500. That inconsistency is what makes this an oversight rather than a decision.

## Change

Two paths fed the same wrong code.

**The sentinel was discarded.** `AddAttestationSubscription` built a fresh error, so nothing downstream could classify it:

```go
-    return errors.New("head state not available")
+    return synced_data.ErrNotSynced
```

**The central mapper had no case for it.** `WrapEndpointError` already special-cases one sentinel, so this sits next to it — one change covering every endpoint that surfaces `ErrNotSynced` raw (`getAttesterDuties`, `getCommittees`, `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees`, `blockRootFromBlockId`, `PostEthV1ValidatorSyncCommitteeSubscriptions`):

```go
 if errors.Is(err, fork_graph.ErrStateNotFound) {
     return NewEndpointError(http.StatusNotFound, ErrorCantFindBeaconState)
 }
+if errors.Is(err, synced_data.ErrNotSynced) {
+    return NewEndpointError(http.StatusServiceUnavailable, err)
+}
```

Both subscription handlers now route through `WrapEndpointError` instead of hardcoding 500, and the syncing case no longer logs at `Error` — a node that is merely catching up should not fill the log with failures.

Also in this PR:

- **`WrapEndpointError` matched `*EndpointError` by value.** `errors.As` with a value target never matches the pointer `NewEndpointError` returns, so an explicit code reaching this helper collapsed to 500. `HandleEndpoint` checks the pointer form first, so **no endpoint hit this in practice** — it is latent, not live, and it is a trap for the direct callers this PR adds. Both forms now match.
- **`ApiHandler.committeeSub` held the concrete `*CommitteeSubscribeMgmt`**, so the already-generated `MockCommitteeSubscribe` could not be injected. It now takes the existing `CommitteeSubscribe` interface. No caller changes — the concrete type satisfies it.
- Removed a commented-out block in `subscription.go` that proposed this exact 503 check.

## Spec

[`types/http.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/types/http.yaml) — `CurrentlySyncing`: *"Beacon node is currently syncing, try again later."*

Declared on two affected endpoints: [`beacon_committee_subscriptions.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions.yaml) and [`duties/attester.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/duties/attester.yaml).

**Worth a reviewer's opinion:** the spec does *not* declare 503 for `states/{state_id}/committees`, `pool/sync_committees` or `sync_committee_subscriptions`, which the central mapping also changes. I went with consistency — the condition is equally reachable there, the error body shape is unchanged, and only strict response-code validation would notice. Happy to narrow it to the two spec-declared endpoints if you would rather stay literal.

## Scope

This is a conformance and observability fix, not a high-availability one. Lighthouse does not branch on 503 anywhere in its fallback or publish path — it derives health from `/eth/v1/node/health` and `/eth/v1/node/syncing`, and both codes arrive as the same `RequestFailed(ServerMessage(..))`. Client routing behaviour will not change.

## Test

TDD, and each guard was verified by mutation rather than by reading:

| Mutation | Test that caught it |
| --- | --- |
| 503 mapping → 500 | `TestWrapEndpointErrorStatusCodes`, both subscription 503 tests |
| sentinel → bare `errors.New` | `TestAddAttestationSubscriptionReportsNotSyncedWhileSyncing` |
| pointer match removed | `TestWrapEndpointErrorStatusCodes/explicit_code_is_preserved` |

The handler tests mock the subscription call, so they cannot catch a regression in `committee_subscription.go` — hence the separate package-level test for the sentinel. Coverage also pins the cases that must *not* change: an unrelated failure still returns 500, and a synced node still returns 200.

`./cl/beacon/... ./cl/validator/...` green (18 packages). `make lintci` reports `0 issues`.
author: lystopad

title: cl/antiquary: remove overlapping caplin state segments after each dump
body:
`CaplinStateSnapshots.RemoveOverlaps` is reachable only from `erigon snapshots retire` (`cmd/utils/app/snapshots_cmd.go:3490`, `onDelete == nil`), so a running node never removes a caplin state overlap. EL has done this since `BlockRetire.MergeBlocks` (`freezeblocks/block_snapshots.go:308`).

The overlap that reaches a default node is the equal-range version duplicate, not the subset. `--caplin.snapgen` gates local generation only (`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go:582`), and the published set is curated clean — mainnet 1328 caplin `.seg` entries / 24 tables, 0 overlaps, 0 same-range different-version pairs; gnosis 3540, the same; `keepNewest` (`db/snapcfg/util.go:125`) collapses them before the list is served. What is left is local: nothing unlinks `v1.0-000000-010500-X.seg` when an upgrade downloads `v1.1` of that range.

Wiring removal on without handling that makes it worse. `openIdx` skips an already-open slot (`snapshots.go:429`), otherwise `MatchVersionedFile` takes the highest version (`db/version/file_version.go:301`), so retiring the v1.0 segment unlinks the **v1.1** index and the survivor fails the `IsIndexed` gate at `snapshots.go:824`. Live on main today on the retire path.

## Changes

- **cl/antiquary** — removal runs on every `IncrementBeaconState`, not only after a dump (that moved to `dumpCaplinStateIfDue`), and before `Seed`, so a superseded subset is not hashed and announced microseconds before it is unlinked.
- **db/snapshotsync** — the index half of equal-range version duplicates; #23374 handled only the `.seg`. `keepIdxFiles` stops a retired segment unlinking the survivor's index, `removeOrphanedIdx` unlinks the older one once neither the dirty set nor a pinned retired segment holds it, `pendingUnlinkNames` keeps a rescan from rebuilding a `DirtySegment` for a file awaiting unlink. On `BaseRoSnapshots`, so every EL collection inherits it.
- **downloader keys** — the base reports names relative to the collection dir, the downloader registers `caplin/<name>` slash-separated (`db/downloader/util.go:87`), so a bare name matched nothing and `Delete` was a silent no-op. Same normalization at `fixPath`, `ensureCantLeaveDir`, `toRelativePaths`; the `seedableStateFilesBySubDir` and `db/state/dirty_files.go` hunks are that defect on the EL state seed path, not caplin.

Beacon blocks and blob sidecars stay unwired: both live in `dirs.Snap` and hit #23469 (`NoGaps` hides them from the dirty set, so removal drops the `.torrent` and leaves the `.seg`) and #23470 (the `.tmp` sweep can unlink an EL merge's in-flight output). Caplin state escapes the first via the unfiltered `AllTypedSegments` scan, and survives the second only because `DumpCaplinState` and `RemoveOverlaps` share the `loopStates` goroutine — now stated at `DumpCaplinState`.

Removal can also run while the EL Snapshots stage is still downloading `caplin/` items into the same directory (`db/snapshotsync/snapshotsync.go:519`); nothing in `cl/` waits on that batch and no completion signal reaches it (`DownloadComplete` fires only on the EL's own objects, `stage_snapshots.go:152`). Accepted: `.part` data is invisible to the scans, `keepUnindexedlyCovered` (`caplin_state_snapshots.go:196`) keeps an indexed file whose keeper has no index yet, and a `Delete` mid-batch fails that batch with `torrent unexpectedly closed` (`download-batch.go:155`) rather than hanging. The residual is a promoted file demoted back to `.part` after its predecessor was retired: unreadable until the download completes again, not lost.

Part of #23412 and #23024, item 2.
author: awskii

title: cl: complete errcheck rollout across cl/* and fix violations
body:
Completes the errcheck rollout for #22538 across the entire `cl/*` tree. Started as `cl/beacon`, `cl/cltypes`, `cl/phase1`, `cl/validator`; this PR adds every remaining `cl/*` package: `cl/aggregation`, `cl/antiquary`, `cl/das`, `cl/merkle_tree`, `cl/p2p`, `cl/persistence/blob_storage`, `cl/persistence/state(+historical_states_reader)`, `cl/rpc`, `cl/sentinel(+communication/ssz_snappy,handlers,httpreqresp,service)`, `cl/spectest/consensus_tests`, `cl/transition/impl/eth2(+statechange)`, `cl/utils/bls`. Only non-`cl/*` packages remain excluded for future PRs.

Notable fixes beyond lint-satisfying:
- `SetSlot`/`ResetEpochParticipation` left the state half-mutated on an antiquary-hook failure (slot changed but leaf not marked dirty; `previousEpochParticipation` reassigned before the hook ran) - both now roll back cleanly on error.
- `fork_graph.NewForkGraphDisk` panicked on a disk write failure during startup; now returns the error through the existing startup error path.
- `ProcessPendingConsolidations` resolved the target balance only while crediting it, so a bad target index drained the source and credited nothing - now resolved before touching the source, and a target-credit failure after the source debit landed rolls the source back instead of returning with the balance destroyed.
- `ssz_snappy.EncodeAndWrite` discarded both flush errors, so a send that never reached the peer still returned `nil`.
- `getFlagsTotalBalances`'s worker panicked on a bad validator index instead of using the error return added for it - now returns the error.

Review also caught and fixed:
- `errors.Is(err, io.EOF)` on the raw stream/reader reads in `cl/sentinel/handlers` and `httpreqresp` (five sites) is back to bare `err == io.EOF` with `//nolint:errorlint`, reverting part of #23303 ("resolve errorlint linter findings"), which mechanically replaced every bare `==`/`!=` error comparison repo-wide with `errors.Is` regardless of call site. Checked both concrete `network.Stream` implementations this repo negotiates - `go-yamux/v5` and `go-libp2p-mplex` - and neither wraps `io.EOF` in its `Read`, so at these specific lines the two forms are behaviorally identical today. The bare form stays anyway: it's a zero-cost, provably-safe default that doesn't depend on an unenforced, untested assumption about a third-party muxer's internals that a future dependency bump or a muxer swap could silently invalidate, and it matches the `err == rlp.EOL` / `//nolint:errorlint` convention already established for the same class of check in `execution/types/` and `p2p/enr/enr.go`. `bytes.Reader`-backed reads (`cl/rpc`, `sentinel_requests_test`) were never in question - a `bytes.Reader` cannot wrap an error at all - and were left as the bare form already in place there.
- Deduplicated the repeated `RemovePeer`/`ClosePeer` block (copied nine times across `service.go`/`discovery.go`) into a shared helper.
- Dropped a couple of error returns that could never fire (`runDownload` always returned `nil`; a one-worker `ParallellForLoop` became a plain loop).
- The aggregation pool test now allows only `ErrIsSuperset` from `AddAttestation` instead of masking any failure.

Everything else is peer/cleanup operations logging on failure instead of discarding silently, or straightforward test fixes.

title: cl: implement Gloas devnet 8
body:
## Summary

- align Gloas state upgrades, transition processing, progressive metadata, and consensus spectests with consensus-specs v1.7.0-alpha.14
- implement execution-payload-bid and proposer-preferences gossip validation, timing, compatibility, first-valid retention, and fork-boundary behavior
- fix Gloas fork-choice payload availability, execution-status transitions, head selection, checkpoint recovery, persistence, and pruning lifecycle
- make Gloas block production use a coherent fork-choice head/status snapshot and safe REST/P2P first-valid handoff
- implement the devnet-8 CL-facing Builder/Beacon API flow: dynamic builder transport and configuration, proposer preferences, execution payload bids/envelopes, strict Gloas publish parsing and validation, state builders, and Gloas event streams
- add focused reverse, boundary, overflow, cache-eviction, persistence-failure, cancellation, and concurrency regressions

## Validation

- `make erigon integration`
- `go test -tags=spectest ./cl/spectest -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler ./cl/beacon/builder/... ./cl/beacon/beaconevents ./cl/phase1/network ./cl/phase1/network/services ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/stages ./common/event ./cmd/caplin/caplin1 -count=1`
- targeted race tests for fork choice, fork graph, gossip reservation handoff, builder transport, events, pruning, payload-status lifecycle, published-block jobs, and backward Gloas retry ownership
- `make lint` passed twice with both Go and golangci-lint caches isolated
- `git diff --check`
- live Glamsterdam devnet 8 checkpoint sync and head following with an external Geth EL: distance 0, non-optimistic, Gloas FCU and payload imports advancing
- no test skips added
- focused spec, standards, fix-delta, boundary, and lifecycle review of the final changes; final narrow retry delta converged with no remaining in-scope finding

Final review-fix head: `b98c10c48b6e87377e7c8c925cb47ea4e4d828a8` (includes the latest `main`; the sole test-file conflict preserved both test suites).

## Scope and external-builder policy

This PR is limited to the devnet 8 consensus-layer and CL-facing API implementation. Remaining execution-layer work, including full EIP-8070 `engine_getBlobsV4` / FCU custody-column wiring and native Erigon EL devnet 8 execution issues, is intentionally out of scope.

The approved external-builder behavior implemented here is:

- a signed Gloas block may be forwarded to the echoed request-supplied `Eth-Builder-Url`, but an unbound URL is always restricted to strict-public targets and never inherits the private-target flag;
- validator-configured builder URLs are strict-public by default; private or loopback targets require the explicit `--caplin.builder.allow-private-urls` operator flag;
- when the local EL build fails, block production may select a validated external builder or P2P bid tied to the frozen requested parent; if no valid external candidate exists, the local build error is returned;
- gossip-only publication policy remains separate from configured-builder routing and does not make an unbound target trusted.

title: cl: seed the ENR custody group count instead of an empty entry
body:
`setupENR` wrote the `cgc` entry as an empty byte slice:

```go
// cl/p2p/p2p.go
node.Set(enr.WithEntry(p.cfg.NetworkConfig.CgcKey, []byte{}))
```

Empty is the canonical encoding of zero, so a node advertised custody of no groups.
Nothing corrected it: the only path that rewrites the entry is
`SetCustodyGroupCount`, gated on the count rising above `advertisedCgc`, which
starts at `CustodyRequirement` — so on a node without attached validators it never
fires. `p2p-interface.md` notes clients MAY reject a peer advertising below
`CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT`, so the entry was not merely uninformative.

## Change

Seed the entry with the value `advertisedCgc` already starts at, via a shared
`EncodeCgc` so the seed and the update path cannot drift on format.

Encoding is unchanged — `big.Int.Bytes()`, big endian with no leading zero bytes,
zero as the empty string, per `fulu/p2p-interface.md`. The increase-only gate is
unchanged: `fulu/validator.md` requires a node whose custody requirement falls to
keep advertising the previous (highest) count, which is what it implements. Both
are now covered by tests and a comment so neither gets "corrected" later.

Verified on a gnosis archive node: `cgc` decoded to `0x` before and `0x04` after.

## Scope

Present on `main`, `release/3.6` and `release/3.5`, and on every chain with fulu
scheduled — none override `CustodyRequirement`. Cherry-picks to follow once this
lands.

This does not change how a node computes its own custody, subnet subscriptions or
column requests: those read the in-memory value, not the ENR. It fixes what other
nodes believe about this one.

Two related gaps found in review, both pre-existing and filed separately rather
than widened into this PR: the highest count is not persisted across restarts, and
an archive node advertises `CustodyRequirement` while custodying all 128 groups.
author: lystopad

title: cl: reject incomplete GetPayload responses
body:
## Summary

- reject remote GetPayload responses that omit the execution payload or blobs bundle
- stop polling immediately for structurally invalid responses while preserving retries for transient errors
- guard block production against custom execution engines returning a nil blobs bundle using the same invalid-response sentinel
- pin Deneb, Electra, Fulu, and Gloas to GetPayload V3, V4, V5, and V6 in tests

## Behavior note

A successful response with a nil `executionPayload` previously produced an ordinary retryable error. It is now classified as structurally invalid and terminates polling after the first attempt. A spec-compliant EL must not return a successful V3-V6 response without an execution payload; transient unavailability remains on the existing retryable error paths.

## Testing

- go test ./cl/beacon/handler ./cl/phase1/execution_client -count=1
- go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler ./cl/phase1/execution_client -run TestGetAssembledBlockRoutesByVersion\|TestProduceBeaconBodyRejectsMissingBlobsBundle -count=1
- make lint
- make erigon integration

Fixes #23299

author: Sahil-4555

title: cl: validate Fulu cell proof widths
body:
## Summary

- reject Fulu and later `BlobsBundleV2` responses when any cell proof is not exactly 48 bytes
- validate all proof widths before fixed-array conversion or blob cache/body mutation
- preserve the existing pre-Fulu validation order

## Why

The Osaka Engine API defines each `BlobsBundleV2.proofs` element as a 48-byte `KZGProof`. Block production previously checked only proof cardinality for Fulu and later. A short proof could therefore panic during `[]byte` to `common.Bytes48` conversion, while an overlong proof could be silently truncated.

## Tests

- TDD repro: 47-byte proof panicked before the fix; 49-byte proof escaped validation
- focused 47/48/49-byte and pre-Fulu ordering tests
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler -count=1`
- focused `go test -race`
- `make lint` (twice, isolated cache)
- `make erigon integration`

This is the first of the follow-up hardening changes found while reviewing #23299. Broader Engine response and KZG semantic validation remain separate PRs.

title: cl/sentinel: reject invalid ping and status requests
body:
## Summary

- decode Ping/1, Status/1, and Status/2 request bodies before returning success
- return InvalidRequest for empty, truncated, oversized, malformed, and observably trailing requests
- enforce fixed SSZ sizes and bounded Snappy input; Status/2 uses the 92-byte Fulu schema
- update request lifecycle tests to close the write side and clean up handler contexts

Closes #23166.

author: domiwei

title: cl: fix Gloas bid selection, validation and publication
body:
## Summary

Gloas `ExecutionPayloadBid.value` is denominated in Gwei, while execution-layer values and block-production metadata use Wei. Production compared the raw Gwei bid with the local Wei value, so external bids almost never won. It also narrowed execution values to `uint64`, which corrupted metadata above the Wei limit of that type.

Once external bid selection became reachable, a bid validated when it entered the pool could still become invalid against the production state. Parent execution requests can change builder eligibility before the current bid is processed. Selecting such a bid made the final state transition fail even though a valid self-built block was available. Gloas selection also retained local blob data after choosing an external bid and made a legacy Builder API request whose result could not be used.

Consensus block value metadata was emitted in Gwei, while the beacon API requires Wei.

## Changes

- Keep execution values as exact `big.Int` Wei values through selection and response metadata.
- Convert external Gloas bid values from Gwei to Wei before comparison and reporting.
- Keep `builder_boost_factor` scoped to the legacy Builder API path; compare Gloas ePBS bids directly after converting both values to Wei.
- Run the complete canonical `ProcessBlock` transition for a winning external bid on copies of the production state and self-built block.
- Reuse the successful candidate state and reward collector instead of replaying the transition.
- Keep the original self-built block and state untouched while evaluating the external candidate, then process them if its transition fails.
- Evict only deterministically invalid external bids, including when the self-build fallback also fails, while preserving any newer concurrently stored bid.
- Clear local blobs and KZG proofs when an external bid wins.
- Build local Gloas data-column sidecars only for self-built bids; external builders publish their payload data.
- Keep cached self-build envelopes aligned with the produced block by retaining a same-slot envelope only when it commits to the same beacon block.
- Skip the legacy Builder API `getHeader` request on Gloas, where external bids arrive through ePBS gossip.
- Reject empty, non-decimal (including signed), and out-of-range Builder API block values before weighted comparison.
- Convert consensus block value metadata from Gwei to Wei with overflow-safe arithmetic.
- Log sidecars actually built by the node and avoid unused signed-header merkleization during Gloas publication.

Concurrent same-slot/DVT envelope caching requires a multi-entry design and is tracked in #23781.

The Gwei denomination follows the [Gloas `ExecutionPayloadBid` specification](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md#executionpayloadbid).
author: yperbasis

title: cl/sentinel: honour the peer ban on inbound connections
body:
Closes #23605.

The three-strike ban in `peers.Pool` was written and never read on the inbound path.
`RecordHandshakeFailure` installed the ban, but only `ConnectWithPeer` consulted it, and that
covers dials we initiate — not the connection events that arrive regardless. A banned peer
therefore got a fresh status handshake on every reconnect.

Measured on a gnosis archive node: 101 attempts against a single peer in two minutes, 13,827
handshake failures across 1,638 distinct peers in ninety minutes, and 460 dials refused by
libp2p's own dialer with `rate limit exceeded`.

## Change

- read `BanStatus` in the connection handler and close banned peers before handshaking
- split the callback body into `handleNewConnection`, reporting whether the peer was kept, so
  the inbound path is reachable from a test

Retained-peer behaviour is untouched. Keeping a peer whose status exchange failed on a
transport error ("may still work for gossip") is deliberate and unchanged — only the rate at
which a *banned* peer is re-attempted changes.

## Tests

`cl/sentinel/ban_on_connection_test.go` uses two real connected hosts, so closing the peer is
observable rather than a no-op against an absent connection. It covers entry through
`onConnection` with a real `network.Conn`, and drives #23605 end to end: three transport
failures reach the ban, then the next event closes the peer without validating again.

Mutation-verified rather than assumed: removing the ban read fails
`TestBannedPeerIsClosedInsteadOfHandshaked`; making `onConnection` bypass
`handleNewConnection` fails `TestOnConnectionClosesABannedPeer`.

## History, for anyone reading the commit message

Earlier revisions also added a per-peer gate admitting one handshake at a time. @domiwei showed
it dropped replacement connections created during `closePeer` and lost their validation, which
was a regression against the existing fork-mismatch path, so the gate was removed — the ban
read is the whole fix. The squash commit message predates that removal and still describes the
gate, the dropped concurrent events and a burst test, none of which are in the merged code.

Follow-ups tracked separately: duplicate-handshake coalescing done correctly, the
`ConnectWithPeer -> Host.Connect` failure path that never records a handshake failure, and
enforcing the ban in `Gater.InterceptSecured` so a banned peer is dropped before the connection
is upgraded.
author: lystopad

title: cl, cmd/utils: derive the column retention window from the chain config
body:
Closes #23411.

The spec states PeerDAS column retention in epochs (`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS`), so the slot count depends on `SLOTS_PER_EPOCH`. `cleanupAndPruning` already derives it from the active chain config when `ColumnKeepSlots` is zero — but the flag default was `131072`, mainnet's 4096 × 32, so that branch was unreachable. Gnosis and Chiado, at 16 slots per epoch, retained 131072 slots against a 65536-slot window: twice the columns they need. Wasted disk, no correctness impact.

Defaults `--caplin.columns-keep-slots` to `0` and lets the existing fallback compute the window. No pruning logic changes.

Help text and docs no longer name a fixed slot count, so adding a chain with its own slot timing needs no further edits here.

`0` meaning "use the spec window" rather than "keep nothing" is the code's existing convention, kept rather than replaced with a new sentinel — flagging it in case a reviewer would rather see it changed.

### Test

`TestCaplinColumnKeepSlots_UnsetDefersToChainConfig` runs `setCaplin` over a real CLI context and pins both directions: unset stays `0`, a user-set value reaches the config. It fails with `131072` on the current default. The chain-config resolution itself was already covered by `TestCleanupAndPruningResolvesZeroColumnKeepSlotsToTheSpecWindow`.

title: cl/beacon: report pool syncing as unavailable
body:
Follow-up to #23464.

## Summary

`POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` is registered as a direct HTTP handler, so its head-state errors do not pass through the central endpoint error mapper. While the node was syncing, `ErrNotSynced` was added to the indexed failure list and returned as 400.

title: exec, commitment, cl/beacon: clear pooled objects (which hold bytecode ptr)
body:
seems it's root cause of OOM in tests: https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23640

not all pointers was cleared before returning objects to `sync.Pool`

Same class, found by sweeping every `sync.Pool` in the repo:

- `BranchEncoder.ClearDeferred` — up to 50k `*DeferredBranchUpdate` stayed in the backing array, and that encoder lives inside a `HexPatriciaHashed` that `Release()` pools.

title: cl/services: share pending queue for payload gossip
body:
First PR in the split of #22177.

This PR extracts the duplicated pending scheduler used by execution-payload envelopes and payload attestations into an unexported `pendingJobQueue[K, M]`.

There are no intended behavior changes. Each service keeps its existing key, capacity, 100 ms polling interval, 30-second expiry, duplicate handling, full-queue fast path, removal-before-processing order, cancellation behavior, and logs. The existing service tests are mechanically adapted to the shared representation.

TDD was not used because this is a pure refactor; the existing service tests are the safety net.

## Stack

- #23643 — shared-queue refactor (this PR)
- #23644 — queue hardening and bid migration
- #23645 — deferred Gloas data-column sidecars
- #23646 — deferred beacon blocks

The last two PRs are sibling branches and can be reviewed independently after #23644.
author: yperbasis

title: cl/services: harden shared pending-job queue
body:
Hardens Caplin's shared pending-job queue for execution-payload envelopes and payload attestations.

- Enforces capacity with CAS reservations, including in-flight enqueues, and releases reservations after key-construction errors or panics.
- Uses coalesced wakeups, cancellation checks, and identity-checked removal. Expiry and post-removal callbacks run after deletion and may enqueue a replacement.
- Validates queue options, reports admission errors, and counts failed capacity reservations per queue. Attestation hash errors are returned instead of ignored.

Service capacities, expiry windows, retry cadence, signed-message identity, and envelope byte accounting are preserved. Failed gossip admission returns `IGNORE` without claiming the message was queued. The queue loop can be stopped and joined for deterministic test cleanup.

Execution-payload bids and REST handlers are unchanged. Beacon blocks and data-column sidecars are outside this PR; #23646 and #23645 cover them.

Validation covers queue admission, deduplication, expiry, wakeups, cancellation, and service integration, including race tests. TDD is skipped for pure refactors and test-only coverage of existing behavior.
author: yperbasis

title: cl/services: harden deferred Gloas data-column sidecars
body:
Use the shared bounded queue for Gloas data-column sidecars awaiting their block. Keep the existing 4,096-entry limit, 24-second expiry, and 500 ms retry interval.

- Store sidecars directly, keyed by their full SSZ root, so an unverified candidate cannot suppress a different candidate for the same block and column through deduplication.
- Check the subnet before queue admission. Bound column/proof lengths and check block-independent structure before hashing or retaining a sidecar. Failed admission preserves the missing-block gossip `IGNORE` verdict.
- Queue only at gossip ingress. Retain the original entry and expiry when processing reports a missing block. Remove expired or finalized entries and entries whose processing succeeds or returns a terminal result. Retries neither re-enqueue nor infer the error from a later block lookup.
- Keep per-sidecar queue-full diagnostics alongside the shared rejection counter. Fulu validation is unchanged.

Regression tests cover admission bounds, processing at the blob limit, content deduplication, subnet checks, changing block availability, original expiry, capacity, and finalized/expired removal. TDD was used for the retry and admission fixes; it was skipped for comments, behavior-preserving cleanup, and restoring Fulu behavior, using existing tests for those edits.

Closes #24398. Deferred candidate-flooding protection and peer penalties after deferred validation are tracked separately in #24416.
author: yperbasis

title: cl/services: handle local block errors and back off retries
body:
Fix failure handling in the existing beacon-block scheduler:

- Treat local block-index read/write failures as gossip `IGNORE` and retain blocks for retry, instead of penalizing the sender. Warn once per queued job for these failures. Canceled block-index reads or initial block writes still return gossip `IGNORE` and retain the block for retry, without storage-failure warnings or new backoff. After a successful import, warn on finalized-index write failures other than caller cancellation, without rejecting the block.
- Do not queue blocks ignored before signature verification.
- Back off queued `ErrNewPayloadNoStatus` failures from 250 ms to 2 s. The same backoff covers local block-index read/write failures in block-only imports, but not storage errors in publication callbacks. The first queued attempt stays on the normal 50 ms tick. Other dependency failures retain the fast retry cadence without resetting the accumulated retry backoff.

Retry backoff is scoped to each store generation. A newer publication callback resets the retry deadline and delay; ordinary duplicates and stale schedules preserve them.

Publication waiters, 30-second expiry and `block_gossip` timing remain unchanged. No shared-queue migration or capacity limit is introduced.

TDD was skipped for behavior-preserving refactors and comment changes; existing service tests, including race tests, were used for those edits. The log-only cancellation guard intentionally has no log-capture test; existing cancellation and finalized-index tests were used instead.
author: yperbasis

title: build, db, execution, cl, p2p, rpc, txnprovider: enable staticcheck (SA + S1) and fix what it found
body:
`staticcheck` runs by default in golangci-lint v2, but a global `text:` exclusion muted eight SA checks (`SA1019 SA6005 SA5011 SA4009 SA6002 SA9003 SA4006 SA4010`) and six S1 checks. So those never fired, and three of the classes fixed here could have regressed unnoticed.

Drops the SA and S1 entries from that exclusion and fixes the 32 findings. `checks:` is golangci's default set less `SA1019` — naming `SA*`/`S1*` directly would have silently dropped nine ST/QF checks that were already enforced.

## Two real bugs

**`txnprovider/txpool`** — `OnNewBlock`'s deferred block advances `lastSeenBlock` and broadcasts `lastSeenCond` when `err == nil`, but five error paths return through a shadowed `err` (`if err := …; err != nil`), leaving the outer one nil. The pool advanced its view of chain progress and woke waiters after failing to apply a block.

**`txnprovider/shutter`** — `readEonAtNewBlockEvent`'s deferred timing trace tested a `var err error` that no failing path set: two returns under `currentEon == nil` assign a shadowed `err`, and the invalid-activation-block return builds its error inline. It logged success timings for failed calls.

Both fixed with a named result, so every `return` sets what the defer reads.

## Lint findings

- `db/seg/parallel_compress.go` — `compressWithPatternCandidates` did `len(patternCode.word)` and then `if patternCode != nil`. `code2pattern` only ever holds `&Pattern{}`, so the guard is dead code, not a live crash; removed the guard rather than the deref.
- `rpc/jsonrpc/debug_api_test.go` — `t.Errorf("nil tx")` does not stop the test, so the next line dereferenced `tx` anyway. Now `t.Fatalf`.
- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go` carried `//nolint:staticcheck until <url>`, which golangci never applied — the reason needs a leading `//`. It only looked like it worked because SA9003 was globally excluded.

The rest are dead assignments, an `aaTxn` the only caller already passes, a `break` that was the last statement of a `switch` case, and the S1 simplifications (9 redundant nil-checks beside a `len`, 6 redundant `cap` args, 4 decl/assign merges, 1 single-case `select`, 1 struct conversion).

Also 18 `var err error` hoists scoped down to where they're used; three of them were closures quietly writing an enclosing `err`.

## Check selection

`checks: [all, -ST1000, -ST1003, -ST1016, -ST1020, -ST1021, -ST1022, -SA1019]` — golangci's own default minus `SA1019`, which waits on 42 deprecations. The noisy ST/QF checks stay muted by name in `exclusions`, unchanged from before this PR.

Known gap: `exclusions.presets: legacy` (EXC0005) still mutes `SA4011` repo-wide, so SA coverage is not total. It is clean today, but un-muting means narrowing the legacy preset — separate change.

One suppression: `superStringsPool.Put` (SA6002). The superstring crosses a channel, so the pool cannot hand back the same pointer, and making it `*[]uint16` would put an indirection in the scan-loop append to save one 24-byte box per 16MB superstring. Suppressed at the site so SA6002 stays enforced elsewhere.

title: common, cl: enable errcheck across common/* and resolve #23577 review follow-ups
body:
Continues the errcheck rollout from #22538 by removing the six `common/*` bootstrap exclusions from `.golangci.yml` and fixing every violation this surfaces, plus follow-ups from review on #23577.

#### errcheck: `common/*`

Exclusions dropped for:

`common`,  `common/crypto`,  `common/crypto/blake2b`, `common/iouring`, `common/log/v3`,  `common/mmap`, , `address.go`, `bytesn.go`, `blake2x.go`, `logger.go` — explicit `_ =` discards on `Write`/`Log` in `fmt.Formatter` paths, matching the convention the standard library uses for the same methods.`iouring_linux.go` — explicit discards on `Munmap`/`Close` in ring teardown, where there is no caller left to report to. `blake2b_test.go`, `crypto_test.go` — real error checks via `t.Fatalf`, in the message style each file already uses.

#### `common/mmap`: TestResidencyProbe on a tmpfs TMPDIR

`TestResidencyProbe` failed on any machine whose `/tmp` is tmpfs (Fedora's default). tmpfs stores files only in RAM, so `FADV_DONTNEED` cannot evict them and `mincore` always reports the mapping resident — the "pages should be cold" assertion was unsatisfiable by construction, independent of `Resident()`, which is a correct `mincore` wrapper.

The test now allocates on a filesystem whose page cache can actually be dropped, keeping `t.TempDir()` as the fast path and falling back only when `TMPDIR` is tmpfs. Behaviour is unchanged where `/tmp` is disk-backed, including CI. No skip was added; the test runs and asserts everywhere.

#### Review follow-ups from #23577

#23577 is already merged, so these land here rather than as amendments.

All three are resolved:

* https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23577#discussion_r3861076326 — the consolidation rollback had no coverage: the only exercise of `ProcessPendingConsolidations` is the `PendingConsolidationTest` spectest vector, which never makes `state.IncreaseBalance` fail. Added two unit tests driving that branch through the package's gomock `BeaconState`: one pinning that the source balance is restored, one pinning that a failed rollback is reported through the wrapped error. Both were mutation-checked — removing the rollback fails them on the missing restore.
* https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23577#discussion_r3861076329 — removing the two `defer`s in `EncodeAndWrite` made the comment at `bucket_store.go` false and the `errWriter` shim dead: both flush errors now reach the caller, so `w.err` was only reachable once `EncodeAndWrite` had already returned the same error. Dropped the stale comment, the shim and the now-unused type. `TestBucketStoreWriteSurfacesAShortWriteFromTheFinalFlush` still passes, since `bufio.Writer.Flush` raises `io.ErrShortWrite` itself.
* https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/23577#discussion_r3861076338 — `closePeer` had been inserted between `pruneExcessPeers`' doc comment and its function, so the subnet wording attached to the wrong function. Moved the doc back onto `pruneExcessPeers`; the wrapper is left undocumented.

Thanks @awskii for all three.
author: Sahil-4555

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: don't hold the fork-choice lock across blocking EL calls in OnBlock
body:
Closes #23529.

### The problem

`OnBlock` takes `f.mu` at the top and holds it for the whole function, with `engine.NewPayload` sitting inside that critical section. That is a round trip to the EL, tens to hundreds of milliseconds, and while it is in flight `OnTick`, `OnAttestation`, `GetHead` and every read-lock user are stuck behind the same mutex. One slow EL response stalls attestation processing and head computation for the whole node.

Not a data race — the old code was correct, just serialised on EL latency. The Gloas path already yields the lock through `newPayloadWhileYieldingForkChoiceLock`; the pre-Gloas path never picked it up.

### The fix

`NewPayload` now goes through `newPayloadForBlockWhileYieldingForkChoiceLock`, which releases `f.mu` for the call and takes it back before touching any store state. Admission is unchanged: `payloadValidationAdmission` still serialises every EL validation across fork choice and the sync stages.

### What gets rechecked after the lock comes back

Anything checked on entry can go stale during the window, so the whole entry check is re-run rather than picking off individual conditions: `validateBlockAdmissionLocked(block, rejectEquivocation, newPayload)`. That covers finality moving past the block or onto another branch, and an equivocating header inserted while we waited. `invalidateCachedHead` runs right after the relock, since a `GetHead` during the window would refill the cache from pre-block state.

The same check also runs inside the helper once the admission token is won, so a block that went stale while queued does not spend a slot on the shared gate. It needs `f.mu`, and the caller already owns the global token, so it uses `TryRLock` and skips when the lock is busy — waiting there would park the protocol-wide token behind whoever holds the lock. Skipping is not free: the block still reaches the EL, and the caller records a status and an optimistic entry before its own re-check rejects it. It is the cheaper of the two.

Ordering matters in one place. The post-EL re-run sits **after** the payload-status switch; putting it before means an `INVALIDATED` verdict or an EL error is neither recorded nor returned.

`getHead` also re-reads the justified checkpoint under `f.mu` and retries if it moved, matching `getHeadGloas` — this change widens its sample-before-lock window to span the whole EL call.

### Publishing the verdict

Holding the lock continuously meant a duplicate `OnBlock` could never issue a second `NewPayload`: the next caller saw the recorded verdict before reaching the EL. Releasing it breaks that, because the finishing caller has to reacquire `f.mu` before recording anything and the queue drains first.

So the helper records the verdict while it still holds the token — `verifiedExecutionPayload` for VALID, `payloadStatusByRoot` and `executionPayloadStatus` for INVALID, with invalid checked ahead of valid. Two constraints on the invalid side:

- **Keyed by the payload, not just the beacon root.** Two beacon blocks can differ in state root or graffiti and carry the same execution payload, so a root-only key lets the second one resend it.
- **Nothing is cached unless the payload names its own hash.** The claimed `BlockHash` is unauthenticated at that point, so the key is derived with `ComputeBlockHash` and the verdict cached only when derived equals claimed. Caching a mismatch would blacklist a hash the payload never owned.

Those two status caches are bounded, so a busy queue can evict the verdict before the caller relocks and makes it durable. `inFlightInvalidPayloads` bridges that gap: written behind the same derived-equals-claimed gate, read by `executionHashMarkedInvalid`, and cleared once the writer's own durable write has happened. It is deliberately not refcounted through `executionPayloadRoots`, so the writer has to clear its own key — the helper returns the hash it published, which is what lets a caller that merely short-circuited on the verdict avoid retracting somebody else's entry.

The Gloas path keeps the older behaviour, since its predicate is envelope persistence, which cannot be published without `f.mu`. That window pre-dates this PR.

### Tests

22 in `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block_lock_scope_test.go`, ordered with channels — no sleeps anywhere, the timeouts are only failure deadlines. They cover the lock actually yielding, each rechecked condition, verdict publishing and both constraints above, the in-flight set's write, clear and writer-gating, and two concurrency cases.

Every fix is mutation-checked: removing the line it protects makes the matching test fail.

Two things are covered by reasoning rather than a test, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise:

- The end-to-end queued-and-went-stale sequence, and the gossip-verdict mapping for an admission failure caught while queued. Both need a caller parked on the admission channel at a known moment, which is not observable from outside without a test-only hook. I wrote both, found they passed with the fix reverted, and deleted them.
- The `getHead` retry loop. The one-shot rejection of a superseded checkpoint is pinned; forcing a real retry needs the checkpoint to move inside a single call. The loop is a copy of `getHeadGloas`, whose retry is equally untested.

### Scope

`engine.GetBlobs` is also a blocking EL call under `f.mu` in the same function. An earlier revision of this PR yielded the lock there too; that was removed because it lifted the only cap on concurrent `GetBlobs` calls without adding one back. HEAD calls it exactly as main does. Tracked separately, along with the length-only `elHasBlobs` check.
author: Sahil-4555

title: cl/beacon/handler: reject a missing withdrawals list instead of dereferencing it
body:
Remote `getPayload` can hand back an `Eth1Block` with nil `Withdrawals`: the field carries no `gencodec:"required"` tag (`engine_types/jsonrpc.go:52`), unlike every field above it, so a response omitting `withdrawals` decodes to nil rather than erroring, and `executionPayloadToEth1Block` fills the list only when it is present. `produceBeaconBody` copied withdrawals unconditionally, so the nil reached `ListSSZ.Range` and dereferenced. The call sits inside a `wg.Go` closure, so the panic is unrecovered and kills the process. The embedded-EL path always builds a non-nil list and was never affected.

Two ways in: a pre-Capella payload, which legitimately has no withdrawals field, or a Capella-or-later EL that omits it. `validateBuilderPayload` already rejected this shape on the builder path; block production had no equivalent.

## Changes
- Reject a nil withdrawals list from Capella on with `ErrInvalidGetPayloadResponse`, mirroring the nil-`BlobsBundle` guard from #23575.
- Tolerate nil before Capella; the destination list is still initialized, so `Withdrawals.Len()` stays safe.
- Tests either side of the Capella boundary, driving a mocked engine that returns a payload with nil withdrawals, and pinning that a rejected payload never reaches the block-body cache.

title: cl/forkchoice: reuse Gloas contribution capacity
body:
## Summary

- reuse the existing `gloasVoteContribution` backing array when the requested length fits its capacity
- preserve amortized growth only for genuine capacity misses
- cover capacity reuse, data preservation, zero initialization, and no-growth boundaries

## Background

On glamsterdam-devnet-8, Caplin's live heap reached approximately 48 GiB. A heap profile attributed 46.84 GiB (98.6%) to `growGloasContributions`.

The helper allocated and doubled capacity whenever `size` exceeded `len`, even when `size` still fit within `cap`. As newly introduced validator indices first voted, a one-element logical growth could repeatedly double the retained backing array.

## TDD evidence

Before the production change, `TestGrowGloasContributionsReusesCapacity` failed with:

```text
expected cap 3, actual 6
```

The minimal production change makes that test pass by reslicing within existing capacity.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice -count=1`
- `make lint` (clean on repeated runs, including immediately before push)
- `make erigon integration`
- `git diff --check`
- independent state/lifecycle and boundary/integration reviews converged with no actionable findings

Fixes #23728.
