title: all: upgrade minimum Go version to 1.26
body:
Raises the Go floor from 1.25 to 1.26 (because `go 1.27.1` released today)

- `go.mod`: `go 1.25.7` -> `go 1.26.0` (no `go mod tidy` churn).
- `Makefile` version guard, `debug.Dockerfile` builder images, `test-hive.yml` / `test-hive-eest.yml` `go-version`, README and the contributing doc.
- `Dockerfile` and the release / docker-image workflows already build on `golang:1.26`. The main CI resolves its version from go.mod, so it moves to 1.26.x on its own.

No version-guarded Go code is left in the tree, so nothing to delete alongside. Whole tree plus every test binary compiles under go1.26.8.

`modernize` gates on the go directive, so 1.26 switches three sub-analyzers on. Two are applied here, one commit each:

- `errorsastype` (32) - `errors.As` -> `errors.AsType[T]`, 26 files.
- `stditerators` (7) - range `reflect.Type.Fields()` / `.Methods()` instead of `NumField`/`Field(i)` loops.

`newexpr` (10) stays parked in `.golangci.yml`: its fix marks `common.NewUint64` with `//go:fix inline`, which puts 391 call sites in scope of the next `go fix` run. That belongs in its own PR, not a toolchain bump.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/clparams: honor MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS
body:
## Summary

Erigon currently derives `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` from `MIN_VALIDATOR_WITHDRAWABILITY_DELAY + CHURN_LIMIT_QUOTIENT / 2` for every chain. That matches the Ethereum default, but it ignores networks that configure the value explicitly.

Gnosis and Chiado both specify 33,024 epochs, while their changed churn quotient makes the formula return 2,304. As a result, the Beacon API reports the wrong value and Caplin uses the shorter value when serving Gloas execution-payload-envelope requests.

This PR:

- adds `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` to `BeaconChainConfig` and prefers it when set;
- configures the official 33,024-epoch value for Gnosis and Chiado;
- preserves the formula as a fallback for existing configs that omit the field.

The Go field is named `MinEpochsForBlockRequestsConfig` because the type already exposes the `MinEpochsForBlockRequests()` method.

This is a pre-existing consensus-config issue noticed while validating #23708 and is intentionally separate from that pruning change.

References: [Gnosis config](https://github.com/gnosischain/configs/blob/2dd5746292ca298ae0695f1ee221098074574e04/mainnet/config.yaml), [Chiado config](https://github.com/gnosischain/configs/blob/2dd5746292ca298ae0695f1ee221098074574e04/chiado/config.yaml).

## Testing

The focused tests were written first. Before the implementation, Gnosis returned 2,304 epochs instead of 33,024 and a custom YAML value of 12,345 was ignored in favor of the 33,024 formula result.
author: yperbasis

title: rpc, db: gate historical requests by physical availability
body:
## Summary

Historical RPC pruning checks combine configured retention with observed state-history and block-transaction boundaries, returning `PrunedError` below the effective boundary. This applies to finite and unbounded modes without changing retention or restoring pruned data.

A wider configured window does not prove its data is present. #23708 should merge after or together with this PR to avoid advertising missing history after a retention increase.

Review order: gates in `rpc/jsonrpc/eth_api.go`, capabilities in `eth_system.go`, then pinned file views and `prune_floor_cache.go`.

## Behaviour

RPC history gates combine configured retention with physical boundaries matched to each reader's position. State-reader constructors retain their own boundary checks. Parallel block-tracing workers also check the first replay position when opening their separate read view; all jobs in that block read at or after it.

For requested block `B`, `Min(B)` is the txNum of its first system transaction:

| Reader | Required history position |
| --- | --- |
| Post-block state | `Min(B+1)` |
| State after the next block's initial system transaction | `Min(B+1)+1` |
| Transaction replay / indexed pre-state | `Min(B)+i+1` (`i = 0` for full replay) |
| Whole-block history | `Min(B)` |

`i` is a zero-based transaction position, including the position after the last user transaction. If the block-level replay boundary rejects a request, an exact txNum check can still admit retained pre-state within that block. This exception requires exact, known block bounds and an in-block position, so oversized indices cannot bypass the boundary. Availability checks do not use the latest-state fallback for missing mappings. They can recover missing mappings from snapshot bodies, but not MDBX body IDs, which also count side forks. Local readers use pinned body files; remote readers restrict this fallback to an observed frozen range and return an error while that range is unknown. Fully retained blocks keep existing index behaviour; broader validation is in stacked PR #24388.

- Rebuilding pre-Byzantium receipt roots requires history from `Min(B)`, including commitment history when enabled; receipt gates and capabilities enforce this. The commitment bound does not apply to post-Byzantium receipts or logs.
- Log-index checks do not require history for the initial system entry. Filtered queries check replay history once, also covering receipt generation when cached receipts are unavailable.
- Otterscan transaction searches check full replay history once per visited block, before skipping system entries. Ascending scans skip reward-only entries without requiring block transactions. Descending scans can still require block data for those entries because of an existing iterator limitation. A completed page stops before checking the next block.
- Count-limited `erigon_getLatestLogs` queries can finish within retained history even when the requested range extends into pruned data. If they cannot satisfy the count without entering unavailable history, they return `PrunedError` instead of incomplete results.
- The MDBX boundary includes genesis when block 1 is retained. With a gap after genesis, genesis remains individually readable, subject to configured pruning and chain-history expiry, without lowering the contiguous boundary or allowing ranges across the gap.
- In `eth_capabilities`, `oldestBlock` includes the observed state-history and block-transaction boundaries; `deleteStrategy.retentionBlocks`, where present, reports the configured window. Physical boundaries and configured windows are combined independently, so missing data does not hide a deletion policy. The window may be wider than available data. State proofs also account for commitment history and report the tighter state/commitment retention policy.
- Local boundaries use pinned database and file views. Local `MinimumBlockAvailable` requires a pinned block-files view even for MDBX-only reads and panics without one. History checks return errors for unsupported views. `HistoryStartFrom` propagates lookup and transport errors; optional commitment-history lookups run only when needed.
- Gas-price estimation skips unavailable samples and keeps its fallback. Fee history stops at the first unavailable block; reward requests starting at a pruned block return an empty result without a pruning error. Header-only fee history remains available, and backend errors propagate.

## Limits and performance

The history boundary uses the earliest start across accounts, storage, and code: a later first change may reflect a sparse domain, not pruning. This avoids rejecting valid reads but can still admit requests with missing history in another domain. Remote block boundaries and txNum-to-block lookups use separate server-side views and remain best effort.

Log and trace index files can start later than state history. The gates use the state-history boundary as a proxy instead of checking these index starts independently, so log queries, `trace_filter`, and Otterscan searches can still return incomplete results in that case.

Persisted receipt availability still uses the configured receipt-cache window, not its physical start. Receipt gates and `eth_capabilities.receipts` can therefore overstate availability after widening that window or enabling persistence late.

Some readers and range anchors still use latest-state fallback for missing txNum mappings. They can return incorrect historical results when both the mapping and its snapshot fallback are unavailable, including during startup with a stale cached zero frozen range. Exact historical position resolution is tracked in #25074.

RPC gates resolve the head even under an unbounded policy. They skip physical lookups at the current head or when the configured cutoff already rejects the request.

Each shared floor cache holds up to 64 entries with a one-second TTL and insertion-order eviction, keyed by head, MDBX view and relevant file generations. Local history keys include both history and block files because txNum conversion can read body snapshots.

Current remote servers include the pinned history generation and updated MDBX view ID in stream replies, enabling shared history caching without extra requests. History lookups and indexed checks retry after remote view renewal. `eth_capabilities` and pre-Byzantium receipt checks retry the state and commitment floors together. Views lacking generation metadata, including older servers, bypass the shared history cache. Remote block observations remain TTL-cached. The frozen-range cache loads on demand with a five-second fetch timeout and a 30-second backoff after failure. Lookups needing a snapshot mapping return an error until a frozen range has been observed.

Fresh floor-cache hits use `sync.Map.Load` and atomic value reads, avoiding both cache mutexes. `concurrent.CachedValue` coalesces same-key refreshes. After a shared failure, waiters retry once on their own transactions. Waiters can cancel independently; reads run synchronously within the caller's transaction lifetime. Errors do not extend floor-cache expiry, and panics do not leave keys blocked. Each gas-price backend caches its contiguous block boundary; genesis uses its single-block availability check.

On Apple M2 Max, fresh cache hits measure about 41 ns/op serially and 6–8 ns/op with eight workers using shared or distinct views, with zero allocations. Parallel figures measure aggregate throughput, not per-request latency; these are not end-to-end RPC measurements.

## Verification

Behaviour fixes were driven by failing regression tests covering missing txNum mappings, side-fork MDBX body IDs, unknown remote snapshot bounds and recovery, real mid-block retirement, ascending scans over reward-only entries without block data, capability policies, and zero-start log ranges below the block boundary. A characterization test confirms that log and trace indices can start later than state history. The commitment-renewal test fails without the paired retry. Direct oracle tests cover bypassed block floors and swallowed lookup errors. Cache tests cover non-blocking warm hits and bounded eviction under concurrent access. The unknown-range regression checks the specific error, so unrelated failures cannot satisfy it. Behaviour-preserving refactors use existing tests; assertion-only and documentation changes do not change production behaviour.

Passed on `46f148a574`: `make lint`, `make erigon integration`, `make test-short`, and full `db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks` tests. Full non-short tests for `rpc/jsonrpc`, `execution/bal`, `db/rawdb`, and `db/kv/rawdbv3` passed on `412e9365e8`, before the assertion-only update. Focused race tests passed on `11c8e3e322` for remote snapshot lookup/cache (10 runs), indexed-history gates, Otterscan searches, capability policies, log ranges, and genesis.
author: yperbasis

title: cl, p2p/rlpx: grow reused buffers with slices.Grow
body:
Follow-up to #23794: the same `make` + partial `copy` grow pattern, at sites where a **reused** buffer is grown. The win only exists there — for a fresh allocation Go has no non-zeroing sized `make`, so `slices.Grow` buys nothing.

**`ValidatorSet.expandBuffer`** — the big one. `validatorSetCapacityMultiplier` is 1.01, so on mainnet (~1.9M validators x 121B ~= 230MB) the buffer reallocates about every 1% of growth, and each time the 3-arg `make` zeroes the full new capacity while `copy` restores only the old length. `slices.Grow` zeroes only what is above the old capacity. The memmove stays.
Safe because all three callers overwrite everything past the preserved prefix (`Append` writes `v.buffer[offset:]`, `DecodeSSZ` does `copy(v.buffer, buf)`, `CopyTo` does `copy(t.buffer, v.buffer)`), and the in-cap fast path already resliced without zeroing.

**`writeBuffer.appendZero`** — zeroed byte by byte. The compiler's memclr idiom only matches `for i := range a`, not `for i := offset; i < newLen; i++`, so the loop really ran per byte. `clear` replaces it.

**`growGloasContributions`** — hand-rolled `slices.Grow` (`nextCap := max(cap(applied)*2, size)`). The two branches collapse into one; the explicit `clear` stays, since `Grow` does not zero the stale region between the old length and the old capacity.

**`BitList.Copy` / `ParticipationBitList.Copy`** — allocated twice (`NewBitList` built a buffer that was immediately discarded) and the 3-arg `make` zeroed the full `cap(u.u)` while only `len(u.u)` was copied and the tail is never read. `slices.Clone` is one allocation of exactly the length. Dropping the capacity carry-over is safe: `Append` uses `append`, and `Get`/`Set` index within the length.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/cltypes: size Gloas execution-request decode guards by the chunk limit
body:
Found while reviewing #23548; the bug is on `main` already, so it is here rather than in that PR.

Gloas encodes the five execution-request lists as progressive lists, which are semantically unbounded — `solid/list_ssz.go:84` says so — but `ensureLists` still builds them with the Electra per-payload maxima. `progressiveDecodeLimit` doubles that and floors at 16, so the effective decode caps are 16384 / 32 / 16 / 128 / 32.

Only `deposits` changes what a node accepts. The Gloas `apply_parent_execution_payload` asserts a per-payload bound on the other four:

```
assert len(requests.withdrawals) <= MAX_WITHDRAWAL_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD
assert len(requests.consolidations) <= MAX_CONSOLIDATION_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD
assert len(requests.builder_deposits) <= MAX_BUILDER_DEPOSIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD
assert len(requests.builder_exits) <= MAX_BUILDER_EXIT_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD
```

`deposits` is absent from that list. Erigon implements the four at `cl/transition/impl/eth2/operations.go:650-665`, reached on every import, so for those the assert bound sits strictly below the old decode cap and the guard was never the binding constraint — such a block now decodes and is rejected by the assert instead, with a clearer message. `deposits` (max 8192, old cap 16384, no assert) is the one with a real import-path effect, which is what #23548 fixes.

Size the guard by what one req/resp chunk can carry instead, so the container matches its spec type. Roots are unaffected — `HashSSZProgressive` ignores the limit.

The test targets the old guard directly (`max(count*2, 16) + 1`) and is red on `main` for all five lists. #23548 makes the same fix for deposits only; that hunk becomes redundant on rebase.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: bound badBlocks so a peer cannot grow it without limit
body:
Found while reviewing #23548; the bug is on `main` already, so it is here rather than in that PR.

`Prune` builds its delete set by walking `f.blocks` (`fork_graph_disk.go:570`), and two store sites put a root in `badBlocks` without it ever being in that walk.

The one a peer can drive is the invalid-block path (`:310-311`): the block is deleted from `f.blocks` and *then* its root is recorded, so the walk never sees it and the old `badBlocks.Delete(root)` at `:618` never fired. A peer with a known parent can submit many distinct invalid blocks off it.

The below-anchor path (`:229`) has the same shape but is out of a peer's reach: `OnBlock` caps `finalizedSlot` up to `AnchorSlot()` and returns for any block at or below it, so every block that reaches `addChainSegmentAndQueueLightClientEvents` is already above the anchor. The branch stays covered because `AddChainSegment` is exported.

Store the slot alongside the root and prune `badBlocks` by slot. `MarkHeaderAsInvalid` records the header's slot when the header is stored — which is the case for the `markPayloadInvalidLocked` callers — and `slotUnknown` otherwise, which is what the `PayloadStatusInvalidated` caller in `on_block.go:249` produces, since it returns before the header is stored. A `slotUnknown` entry is dropped by no prune.

Three tests are red on `main`: the two store sites and the known-slot mark. The fourth pins the `slotUnknown` fallback, which passes on `main` too — it guards the sentinel, so a zero-valued default would make it fail.

Note for #23548: that PR adds `IsBlockInvalid` — the first reader of this map — and a second store site for blocks below the *pruned boundary*, which rises on every prune rather than staying fixed like the anchor. That site needs the same slot, and `payloadStatusAuthorityWithRetention` mapping `IsBlockInvalid` to a latched `PayloadStatusInvalidated` makes a stale entry harmful rather than merely wasteful.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/services: claim the attestation seen slot only after signature verification
body:
`attestation_service.go` marks a validator seen for the target epoch before its signature is checked, and before the `block not seen` ignore path.

An attacker sends a `SingleAttestation` on the right subnet naming any real committee member (membership is publicly derivable), with a garbage signature and a `BeaconBlockRoot` this node has not seen. The entry is claimed, the message is dropped as `ErrIgnore` before any signature work, and the peer is not penalised. That validator's genuine attestation is then discarded as a duplicate for the rest of the epoch. Repeat per committee member to silence the subnets this node serves.

Every sibling service in the package already claims after verification — see the `// Mark as seen AFTER successful validation` comment in `execution_payload_service.go`.

The new test is red on `main`.

One behaviour change worth naming: the duplicate check (`Get`) and the claim (`Add`) are now separated by the batch verification interval rather than a few instructions, so an equivocating validator can get two attestations relayed where one would previously have been dropped. That is the cost of not letting an unauthenticated message claim the slot; the spec wording for the duplicate rule is `[IGNORE]`, not `[REJECT]`.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/services: drop the blob-sidecar pending map that nothing drains
body:
`blobSidecarsScheduledForLaterExecution` is written on the "parent block not seen yet" gossip path and read by nothing: the eviction goroutine is the commented-out `// go b.loop(ctx)`, and no `loop` method exists. So the map never retries anything and never shrinks.

The store happens before the KZG proof check and before the proposer-signature check, keyed on the sidecar's own `HashSSZ()`, and each entry pins a 128 KiB blob. A gossip peer publishing sidecars with a random `ParentRoot` retains roughly 700 KB/s for the process lifetime; honest traffic leaks too, just slower. Reachable pre-Fulu, where the subscription is gated.

Removing it is behaviour-preserving — those sidecars are already never reprocessed — so the unused `blobJobExpiry` and `blobJobsIntervalTick` go with it.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/services: ignore, and retry, a block the execution layer did not answer for
body:
`ErrNewPayloadNoStatus` means the execution layer returned no verdict — a local `InsertBlock`/`ValidateChain` failure or an engine-API error. The gossip manager bans on any error whose text lacks "ignore", so while the EL restarts the first peer to gossip each beacon block is banned, every slot, down to the grace floor. The block is also dropped rather than retried, even though the condition is transient, which is what `scheduleBlockForLaterProcessing` two lines above exists for.

Known gap this does not close: `execution_client_engine.go` collapses every engine JSON-RPC error into `PayloadStatusNone`, so an EL rejection of a proposer-shaped payload (e.g. `checkWithdrawalsPresence`) is indistinguishable here from the EL being down, and is now ignored rather than rejected. `main` cannot tell them apart either — it bans on both. Mapping invalid-params responses to `PayloadStatusInvalidated` in the engine client is the real fix and belongs in its own PR.

The empty-backfill half of this PR was split out to #23837 on review.

The new test is red on `main`.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/network: do not ban a peer for an empty BeaconBlocksByRange response
body:
An empty `BeaconBlocksByRange` response is protocol-legal, and is exactly what Erigon's own handler returns for a range it does not hold (`cl/sentinel/handlers/blocks.go`). Backfilling below other peers' `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` retention therefore bans every correctly-behaving peer in turn, down to the grace floor. The forward downloader already documents the intended behaviour: *"Peer returned an error response (e.g. rate limited, invalid request). Do NOT ban — apply backoff instead."*

No unit test: the ban is in `sendBlockRequest`, which calls `b.rpc.SendBeaconBlocksByRangeReq` on a concrete `*rpc.BeaconRpcP2P`. Widening the field to the existing `rpc.BeaconRpc` interface cascades through `RPC()` and `RequestEnvelopesFrantically` into the sync stages — worth doing, but not inside a bug fix.

Split out of #23836 on review: that PR is gossip validation, this is req/resp backfill.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: align Gloas consensus and APIs with v1.7.0-beta.2
body:
## Summary

Align Caplin's Gloas consensus behavior and Beacon/Builder APIs with `consensus-specs` v1.7.0-beta.2, including the missing beta.0 prerequisites required to reach the beta.2 target correctly.

The branch was rebased onto current `main` at `1ca363730a90ef2419d98f0150e1961d1eb27d84` and reduced from 51 changed files to 37. Operational hardening that is not required for beta.2 has moved to two stacked follow-ups.

## Main changes

- initialize anchor PTC votes as uncast and use the parent header slot for payload settlement, attestation processing, and rewards
- enforce pre-Gloas boundaries for proposer preferences, PTC duties, and payload attestations
- validate builder version/activity, parent-requested exits, equal block/parent hashes, gossip timing, and the beta.2 voluntary-exit wall-clock rule
- keep bounded parent builder-exit summaries so untrusted bid validation does not perform unbounded disk I/O, with restart/eviction fallback
- serve canonical FULL execution-payload-envelope ranges with bounded work and explicit unavailable-history behavior
- accept beta.2 invalid transition fixtures without `post.ssz_snappy` and apply per-case fork config overlays
- pin and pass the official beta.2 mainnet Gloas fixture corpus

## Scope split

- #24279: chain-tip payload-envelope recovery, persisted replay/revalidation, and checkpoint/P2P plumbing
- #24280: voluntary-exit admission, publication coalescing, eviction identity, and finalized pruning

Both follow-ups remain stacked on this branch and need rebasing onto this rewritten head before their next review.

## Latest main rebase

- Base: `1ca363730a90ef2419d98f0150e1961d1eb27d84`
- Head: `86f9315cdbaf3a00d2847352dbe54a0e2b6bd50a`

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services ./cl/phase1/forkchoice ./cl/sentinel/handlers ./cl/beacon/handler -count=1`
- `go test -tags=spectest ./cl/spectest -run '^Test$/^mainnet$/^gloas$' -count=1`
- focused race tests for PTC duties and execution-payload-envelope ByRange handling
- `make lint` (two clean consecutive runs)
- `make erigon integration`
- adversarial review covered fork-direction symmetry, zero/nil/genesis boundaries, stale or unavailable state, bounded untrusted work, cache refresh after waits, REST/gossip error-classification boundaries, and local-self-build ingress

The previous review's actionable failures and concurrency findings are covered by focused regression tests. GitHub CI passes on head `86f9315cdbaf3a00d2847352dbe54a0e2b6bd50a`.

## Devnet 11 experiment

The retained experiment used an older head with embedded Caplin and 15 active Lighthouse validator keys. Attestations and payload attestations were observed, but no proposer duty occurred before the public endpoints and discovered peers became unavailable. The beta.2 head has not been redeployed to the stopped devnet.

## Residual risk and deferred work

- the cold envelope disk-read path permits only one active read; acquisition waiters remain bounded by gossip validation concurrency, while a permanently wedged storage call can retain the token until the underlying API becomes cancellable
- full mandatory-range execution-envelope archival remains architectural follow-up; pruned, inconsistent, or incompletely scanned history returns `ResourceUnavailable`
- broader coordinated forkchoice ordering work tracked upstream in `ethereum/consensus-specs#5563`, `ethereum/consensus-specs#5586`, and `ethereum/consensus-specs#5125` remains outside this delta
author: domiwei

title: cl/sentinel: build one peers.Pool for the whole test package
body:
Follow-up to #23606, addressing @domiwei's second non-blocking review comment.

Every `peers.NewPool` starts two TTL-cache cleanup goroutines, and the upstream expirable LRU
never closes their `done` channel — `Close()` is commented out in the dependency with a note
that it will only arrive after v2. The goroutines therefore run for the rest of the process.
The `cl/sentinel` fixture built a pool per test, so the count grew with the size of the package.

Share one pool instead. It is safe because each test creates its own hosts, so peer IDs are
disjoint and ban state cannot carry between tests, and nothing in this package reaches
`Pool.Request` — the only method that uses the host.

Measured with a temporary probe counting surviving cleanup goroutines: **eight per suite
repetition before, a flat two after**, at `-count=1`, `2` and `3`.

`TestFixtureReusesOnePeerPool` pins the arrangement; restoring the per-test pool fails it.
Removing the ban read from `handleNewConnection` still fails
`TestBannedPeerIsClosedInsteadOfHandshaked`, so the shared pool has not weakened the tests it
carries. Package passes with `-shuffle=on` (three runs) and under `-race` at `-count=2`;
`make lint` clean.

Test-only change, so no new coverage beyond the pin above.

Not addressed here: production code has the same unstoppable-goroutine property, but every
call site is a process-level singleton, so nothing leaks at runtime. Making `lru.CacheWithTTL`
closable would need us to own the expiry sweep — `expirable`'s `Get` already checks `ExpiresAt`,
so the background goroutine only reclaims memory — and it would touch consensus-adjacent caches.
Filed separately rather than folded in here.
author: lystopad

title: cl/network: make the slow-probe rotation test deterministic with synctest
body:
## Problem

`TestForwardRequestMoreRotatesSlowP2PProbes` compressed the request window to 300ms against a 210ms probe timeout. That left 90ms for two probe rotations plus scheduling, and a loaded windows-2025 runner ended the window first:

```
--- FAIL: TestForwardRequestMoreRotatesSlowP2PProbes (0.30s)
    beacon_downloader_test.go:367: request window ended before a healthy probe was processed
```

The failing assertion is not about the behaviour under test. Probe rotation is genuinely time-based — probe timeout fires, attempt is cancelled, a new one starts — but the request window is scaffolding, and the test only passed while those two independent deadlines stayed far enough apart in wall-clock terms.

## Fix

Run the test inside a `testing/synctest` bubble. The bubble's fake clock only advances when every goroutine in it is durably blocked, so the rotation and the window are ordered by construction rather than by how fast the runner is.

That removes the tuning entirely:

- the four timing overrides are gone — the test now exercises the **shipped** values (30s window, 21s probe timeout, 300ms interval), which it never did before
- the two `time.After(time.Second)` guards are gone — a stalled bubble deadlocks with a goroutine dump instead of hanging
- runtime is 0.00s

`NewBeaconRpcP2P` is constructed outside the bubble: it starts background loops (an expirable-LRU janitor, `columnDataPeers.refreshPeers`) that outlive any single request, and a bubble may not end while goroutines are parked. Every deadline this test exercises is created inside `RequestMore`, so nothing under test leaves the bubble.

## Verification

- 50 sequential runs, 30 runs at `GOMAXPROCS=1` under 10 busy-spinning cores, and `-race`: all pass
- still fails for the right reason — replacing the probe `context.WithTimeout` with `context.WithCancel` (rotation disabled) fails in 0.00s with the same message

No skip added.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl, cmd/capcli: fail the chain download when blobs are not fully stored
body:
Replaces #23623, which targeted code that #23138 has since rewritten. Same defect, correct
target, fresh base.

## The defect

`VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` stops at the first identifier a response
does not match and returns a **nil error** with a partial count. Its only remaining production
caller discarded both counts:

```go
if _, _, err := blob_storage.VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore(
    ctx, blobDB, ids, blobs, ...); err != nil {
```

So a block whose blobs stored partially — or not at all — was reported as downloaded. The chain
endpoint moved on to the parent, leaving a gap nothing later notices.

## Change

- check the stored count against the request and fail with both numbers plus the response count
- document the contract on the insert itself, since that count is the only completeness signal
  it gives a caller
- extract `storeRemoteBlobs` so the check is reachable from a test

## Why not #23623

#23623 put the same check in `BlobHistoryDownloader.storeDenebBlobs`. #23138 replaced that whole
path with `denebRecoveryBatch`, which handles it more thoroughly than a warning would: `validate`
returns errors for unrequested, duplicate and empty responses instead of breaking silently,
`store` writes a group only when complete, and `recoverDenebBlobs` re-checks each block with
`storedBlobSidecarsComplete` and calls `addRetrySlot` on a shortfall. The backfill no longer
calls the insert at all, so that half of #23623 is obsolete — and its test targeted a function
that no longer exists.

What #23138 did not change is the insert's contract or the capcli caller, which is what this
picks up.

## Tests

`TestStoreRemoteBlobsRejectsAnIncompleteInsert` drives a sidecar whose header hashes to a
different root, so the insert breaks on the first identifier, stores nothing and returns nil.
`TestStoreRemoteBlobsRejectsAnEmptyResponse` covers the empty-response path to the same end.

Mutation-verified rather than assumed: disabling the count comparison fails both.

`cmd/capcli`, `cl/persistence/blob_storage` and `cl/phase1/network` pass; `make lint` clean.
author: lystopad

title: types: put the wire types on Withdrawal, drop gencodec
body:
Follow-up to #23766, same move applied to `types.Withdrawal`.

The three `uint64` fields become `hexutil.Uint64`, which removes `gen_withdrawal_json.go` along with its mapping struct, `MarshalJSON` and `UnmarshalJSON`. With no `Marshaler` on the type, `encoding/json` stops re-scanning each withdrawal's bytes when the enclosing `ExecutionPayload` or block encodes it, and the leaves go through `MarshalText` instead.

16 withdrawals, the per-payload maximum (`MAX_WITHDRAWALS_PER_PAYLOAD`), Apple M4 Max, n=10:

| | old | new | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `MarshalJSON` | 5.862 us | 3.320 us | **-43.4%** |
| `UnmarshalJSON` | 11.458 us | 6.439 us | **-43.8%** |
| `MarshalJSON` allocs | 35 | 3 | -91.4% |
| `UnmarshalJSON` allocs | 102 | 22 | -78.4% |
| `MarshalJSON` bytes | 4.799 KiB | 2.049 KiB | -57.3% |
| `UnmarshalJSON` bytes | 2.266 KiB | 1.016 KiB | -55.2% |

## RLP is unchanged

`Withdrawal` is not only a wire type - it is RLP-encoded and it feeds the withdrawals root, so that had to be checked rather than assumed. `EncodeRLP`, `EncodingSize` and `DecodeRLP` convert at the `rlp.EncodeU64` / `s.Uint64` boundary, so the encoded bytes do not move.

`TestWithdrawalRLPGolden` pins the encoded bytes, the encoding size, the round-trip and `DeriveSha` against values captured on `main` **before** the type change, over a single-byte, a multi-byte and a max-uint64 value for each integer field. `TestWithdrawalJSONGolden` does the same for the JSON. The pre-existing `TestWithdrawalsHash` only covered `Index=0, Validator=0, Amount=1`, so it would not have caught a multi-byte encoding regression.

## One encode change, on the graphql_ surface

`graphql_getBlockDetails` and `graphql_getBlockDetailsByHash` return a `map[string]any`, so each value carries its own encoding rather than one a struct tag imposes. `amount` was put into that map as a plain `uint64` and marshalled as `1000000000`; it is `hexutil.Uint64` now and marshals as `"0x3b9aca00"`. The sibling `index` and `validator` entries were already cast to hex explicitly, so only `amount` moves, and the new form matches them.

The `eth_` block path is unaffected: it went through the generated `MarshalJSON`, which already emitted all three as hex. The in-tree GraphQL resolver reads the field via `convertDataToStringP`, whose `uint64` and `hexutil.Uint64` cases render the same string below 2^63 - and the new path also fixes a `-`-signed render above it, from an `int64` cast in the old branch.

The map construction moved into `marshalWithdrawals` and `TestMarshalWithdrawalsEncoding` pins all four field encodings. There was no withdrawals coverage in `graphql_api_test.go` before.

## One decode behaviour does change

The generated decoder read every field through a pointer, so an explicit `null` meant "field absent" and left a zero behind. Reflection on the `hexutil` fields rejects `null` instead. Both forms already rejected a bare number, so that is the only difference, and `TestWithdrawalJSONRejectsNull` pins it.

The engine API marks all four `WithdrawalV1` fields required, so rejecting `null` is the spec-correct read, and a payload carrying one was going to be rejected either way - previously by failing the withdrawals root rather than by failing to parse. Worth knowing that geth still decodes through gencodec here and so still accepts `null`.

`cltypes.Withdrawal` (the SSZ/consensus type) is a separate struct and is untouched; the conversions between the two now cast.

The rest of the diff is those casts at the conversion sites - engine API, protobuf, SSZ, aura and merge withdrawal processing.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: chainspec, clparams: replace EF bootnodes with NodeOps fleet
body:
I am on the Ethereum Foundation's Node Infrastructure team (NodeOps). We run the bootnodes
that ship in this repository as the "EF" entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. We are
replacing that fleet, and we would like the new records in a release before the Glamsterdam
client releases.

### What changes

- Add five new EF bootnodes per network. Every node serves all three networks.
- Remove the legacy EF entries. The new set is a replacement, not an addition.
- Third-party bootnodes and DNS discovery roots are untouched.

### The new fleet

Five bootnodes, each serving mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. They are geographically distributed,
multi-cloud, and dual stack (IPv4 + IPv6). Each node runs discv4 and discv5 on the EL port and
discv5 on the CL port, and the fleet spreads across several discovery implementations so one
implementation bug cannot take the whole set down.

### About the records

- The ENRs are generic bootnode records: no `eth2` field, no `tcp`, sequence number 1. Clients
  dial configured bootnodes regardless of fork, and a static list cannot be re-signed every
  fork, so we do not include fork data on purpose.
- Where an EL list accepts ENRs, we list the ENR. It covers discv4 and discv5 and carries the
  IPv6 endpoint. Enodes appear only where a list needs them, in the discovery-only form
  `enode://<pubkey>@<ip>:0?discport=<port>` (no RLPx listener).
- The records are derived from the node keys and are byte-identical across all the client
  PRs. The canonical copies are the eth-clients PRs (`metadata/bootstrap_nodes.yaml` and
  `metadata/enodes.yaml` for mainnet, sepolia and hoodi).

### Verification

- Each node answers discv4 and discv5 pings from the public internet on the advertised ports.
- The relevant tests in this repository pass with the new lists (details below).
- The legacy nodes stay online until client releases with the new records are widely deployed.
  We will announce the shutdown separately.

### Contact

Chase Wright, EF Node Infrastructure. Discord `MysticRyuujin` (ETH R&D and STEEL servers), or
chase.wright@ethereum.org.

### This repository

**Files:** `execution/chain/spec/bootnodes.go`, `cl/clparams/config.go`.

**Semantics:** `mainnetBootnodes` / `sepoliaBootnodes` / `hoodiBootnodes` hold the five EL ENRs
per network (same reasoning as go-ethereum). `V5Bootnodes` swaps the four EF CL ENRs for the
five mainnet EL ENRs. `sepoliaStaticPeers` loses the five EF entries; the new nodes serve no
RLPx, so they are not static-peer candidates. Caplin's `Mainnet/Sepolia/HoodiBootstrapNodes`
swap the EF CL ENRs (4 / 5 / 6) for the five new CL ENRs.

**Tests:** `go test ./execution/chain/spec/ ./cl/clparams/`.
author: MysticRyuujin

title: cl/phase1/network: read the blob count under the canonical root
body:
`collectIncompleteBlocks` hashed the block it had just read to look up how many sidecars the
blob store holds for it. `ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot` returns a block **without its execution
payload** — the interface documents this — so that hash is a root which never existed on chain
and the lookup always misses, reporting zero.

Every Deneb+ block carrying commitments was therefore treated as incomplete no matter what the
store actually held. The backfill re-requested data it already had, and on an archive node it
walked back toward the Deneb fork spending the 30s per-block column timeout on sidecars long
past the retention window. Since the blob dump is gated on that pass completing
(`antiquary.go`: `if !a.blobBackfilled.Load() { continue }`), the blob frontier could not
advance at all.

This fix reads the root from the canonical index instead, and skips a slot with no canonical
root rather than probing the store with a zero key.

Related: #23224 is the wedge this produces — `blob storage count mismatch at slot 29403906`
retried every 12s forever. That is one of the slots repaired while validating this fix, and the
frontier advanced afterwards. #23752 is a separate reason blob backfill cannot converge.

## Evidence

Found on a gnosis archive node whose blob frontier had been stuck at slot 29,400,000 for about
30 days while beacon blocks reached 29,969,999. One 10,000-slot chunk was repaired and
independently verified: 251 blob-bearing slots present, each confirmed by reading the sidecars
back and re-checking the count row. This code still classified all 251 as incomplete. The
goroutine stack showed the pass parked in `peerdas.DownloadColumnsAndRecoverBlobs` on a
`WaitGroup`, chasing columns no peer retains.

## Measured effect

Validated on the same node, after repairing its blob store out-of-band so the store genuinely
held the data:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| backward pass | 1.2 slots/sec, never completed across three restarts | **finished in 39 s** |
| blob dump | gated out, never ran | started 2 s later, completed in 15m25s |
| blob frontier | stuck at 29,400,000 for ~30 days | **29,400,000 -> 29,960,000** |

Before the fix the pass spent the 30s per-block column timeout on slots whose sidecars were
already stored, so it never reached the end and `blobBackfilled` was never set. The dump is gated
on that flag, which is why the frontier could not move at all.

## How to tell if a node is affected

`frozen_blobs` should track `frozen_blocks` at roughly the same height; a persistent and growing
divergence is the symptom. Equivalently `[Caplin] Stat blobs-static=... blocks-static=...` in the
logs. On the node above the two were 29,400,000 and 29,969,999.

## Tests

`TestCollectIncompleteBlocksSkipsSlotsCompleteUnderTheCanonicalRoot` keeps the indexed root
distinct from the block's own hash, as a stripped read does, and asserts a slot already complete
in the store is not queued. Mutation-verified: restoring `HashSSZ()` fails it.

My first version of that test passed under mutation, because the fixture seeded the canonical
root *as* the block's hash and the two roots were identical — worth knowing if you review the
fixture. `newBoundaryDownloader` now seeds the index from the blocks its reader serves, since a
downloader without an index sees every slot as a gap.

Whole package green, `make lint` clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR

Three sites in this file (`retryBlock`, `recoverDenebBlobs`, `recoverFuluColumns`) hash a
stripped block the same way and feed the result to `storedBlobSidecarsComplete`, so a
successfully stored slot is re-queued forever. Fixing those needs the root carried alongside the
block rather than re-derived per call — a per-block read-only transaction in those loops is the
wrong shape, and it changes signatures several tests call directly.

`BlobsIdentifiersFromBlocks` (`blobs.go:50`) also hashes the block, and those identifiers go on
the wire, so peers are asked for a root that never existed. Its only other caller is
`cmd/capcli`, which passes full blocks where the hash is correct, so that one cannot simply be
changed here.

Both are tracked in #23896. This PR is the one change validated against a live node.
author: lystopad

title: cl/validator/devvalidator: count the envelope post before queueing its body
body:
Fixes a flake in `TestGloasProposalRetriesSameEnvelopeWithoutRepublishingBlock`, which failed the `-race` consensus shard on an unrelated PR:

```
--- FAIL: TestGloasProposalRetriesSameEnvelopeWithoutRepublishingBlock (0.52s)
    proposal_submission_test.go:143:
        Error: Not equal:
        expected: 2
        actual  : 1
```

## Cause

The envelope handler queued the body and only then incremented the counter:

```go
envelopeBodies <- body
if envelopePosts.Add(1) == 1 {
```

`envelopeBodies` is buffered at 2, so the send never blocks. The test drains both bodies and immediately asserts `envelopePosts.Load() == 2`, but the assertion is ordered on the channel, not on the counter. The second post can be received before the handler has counted it, which is the observed 1.

Swapping the two lines makes the receive the test already waits on happen after the increment.

## Verification

The window is narrow — 300 local `-race` runs of the unpatched test all passed. Forcing it with a `runtime.Gosched()` between the two statements reproduces CI exactly, failing on the first runs with the same `expected: 2, actual: 1`. With the fix applied and that same `Gosched()` still in place, 30 `-race` runs pass, as does the package.

TDD note: no new test. The existing test is the reproducer; the change is to the fixture ordering it asserts on.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: db/integrity: validate frozen blob sidecar snapshots
body:
## Summary

- add `CaplinBlobSidecars` as an explicit slow check under `erigon snapshots integrity`
- validate required frozen blob coverage and the word/index geometry of visible blob and paired beacon segments
- validate canonical block identity, stored body-root linkage, sidecar count/order/identity, direct block-commitment equality, commitment inclusion proofs, and KZG proofs
- use the Caplin indexing DB for canonical beacon roots and return a non-zero error for missing or invalid data even when `--failFast=false`

Run it with:

```console
erigon snapshots integrity --datadir <path> --check=CaplinBlobSidecars
```

## Scope

This is the at-rest frozen snapshot verifier from #23911. It intentionally does not implement peer repair, atomic segment replacement, or the publication/seeding gate yet, so it does not close #23911.

#23918 fixes the separate `capcli blob-archive-store-check` preflight for the mutable blob archive store. The two checks are complementary: that command checks archive-store counts before freezing, while this PR checks the resulting `.seg/.idx` snapshots semantically. Peer recovery remains dependent on the canonical-root work tracked by #23896.

## Review feedback addressed

- pass the Caplin indexing DB and already-resolved beacon config to the checker; close the associated resources in dependency order
- remove the unreachable silent-skip and duplicate config lookup
- validate segment word count plus index presence, key count, base data ID, and ordinal offsets before slot traversal
- compare every sidecar commitment directly with the beacon block commitment, including Gloas
- make the non-canonical sidecar test reach the intended sidecar-root branch
- cover extra sidecars at empty slots and invalid commitment inclusion proofs
- verify stored pre-Gloas blinded and Gloas full body roots before using their commitment lists

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/format/snapshot_format ./db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks ./db/integrity ./cmd/utils/app -count=1`
- `make lint` (two clean runs)
- `make erigon integration`
- `git diff --check`

Focused tests cover complete and missing sidecars, wrong count/index/root/header signature, invalid KZG and inclusion proofs, extra sidecars at empty slots, malformed records, missing indexes and ranges, segment cardinality, canonical block availability, non-empty Deneb payloads, Fulu sidecars, and Gloas commitment/body-root mismatches.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network: require file availability before skipping an archive slot
body:
Forward-port of a fix made on `release/3.6` while backporting #23895 (see #23922). `release/3.6` was
the only branch carrying it, which @awskii spotted — `git log --all -S storedSidecarsAvailable` found
one commit, on that branch alone.

Pruning drops sidecar files but leaves their `BlockRootToKzgCommitments` rows. A datadir pruned as
non-archive and later reopened with `--caplin.blobs-archive` therefore carries counts that no file
backs. `collectIncompleteBlocks` finds the stale count, matches it against the block's commitments
and skips the slot, so the pass can report completion and move `nextBackfillTargetSlot` past work an
archive node still owes.

This only became reachable with #23895: the earlier payload-stripped hash missed every count and
queued those slots by accident. Fixing the root removed that accident.

## The check

On an archive node, a count-equal slot is only skipped once **every** sidecar index up to the
commitment count is backed by a file; the first miss re-queues the block. Two deliberate choices:

- **a stat, not a read-back** — no KZG work is added;
  `TestBlobHistoryDownloaderDoesNotDeepVerifyCountEqualStorage` still passes with `verifyCalls == 0`.
- **gated on `archiveBlobs`** — a non-archive node prunes on purpose and must not re-queue what it
  deliberately dropped.

An earlier revision probed index 0 only, reasoning that pruning removes whole bucket directories so
absence is all-or-nothing. That holds for pruning but not for a rewrite that publishes index 0 and
then fails, which leaves the count row whole with only part of the data on disk. @domiwei caught
that on #23922; the loop is the fix.

## Tests

`release/3.6` pins the non-archive direction with
`TestBlobHistoryDownloaderDoesNotRetryIntentionallyPrunedFiles`; this branch has no such test, so the
gate would have been unpinned here. All three directions are pinned:

- `TestCollectIncompleteBlocksQueuesArchiveSlotsWhoseFilesWerePruned` — archive node, stale row,
  pruned file, block stays queued
- `TestCollectIncompleteBlocksQueuesArchiveSlotsMissingALaterSidecarFile` — two sidecars written,
  index 1's file removed, leaving `count=2, index0=true, index1=false`; the block stays queued
- `TestCollectIncompleteBlocksLeavesPrunedNonArchiveSlotsAlone` — same state, non-archive, left alone

Mutation-verified in all three directions: dropping the availability check fails the first, reverting
the loop to probe index 0 only fails the second, and dropping the `archiveBlobs` gate fails the
third.

`TestCollectIncompleteBlocksSkipsSlotsCompleteUnderTheCanonicalRoot` pins the probe to the canonical
root and slot rather than `gomock.Any()`, so regressing it to the block's own hash or a wrong slot
fails the test — verified by changing the production call to `slot+1`.

The mock declaration is one helper called at the seven tests that can actually reach the check — it
runs only when `archiveBlobs` is set, the count matches and the block carries commitments, so
hand-built downloaders and tests whose count lookup errors never get there.

`make lint` clean, `cl/phase1/network` green.

`release/3.5` carries the same fix in #23932.
author: lystopad

title: cl/persistence/blob_storage: validate the stored inclusion proof shape
body:
Found while addressing @domiwei's review on #23923; the same defect is on `main`, reached through the Gloas gate that #23868 added.

Skipping the inclusion-proof check from Gloas on also skipped any check that the proof vector has the length the reader expects. `WriteBlobSidecars` encodes a short vector happily, but `ReadBlobSidecars` always constructs a fixed-length proof schema and rejects the shorter encoding. A response carrying an explicit `"kzg_commitment_inclusion_proof": []` therefore **replaces a previously readable sidecar with a file nothing can decode, and reports no error**. The count row still says the blobs are there.

Measured on this branch before the fix: `VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` returns `err=nil, inserted=1`, and the following `ReadBlobSidecars` returns `found=false` where it returned the sidecar a moment earlier. The beacon transaction that records the count is separate, so nothing rolls the replacement back.

The gate appears at two sites and both needed it:

- `VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` — the insert path.
- `VerifyBlobSidecars` — the shared verifier. `cl/das/peer_das.go` passes a version that can be Gloas and writes once verification succeeds, so fixing only the first would have left the same path open.

Whether the proof's *contents* are meaningful is fork-dependent; whether the sidecar is encodable in the shape the reader expects is not. The length is now checked for every version, before anything is written.

Pinned by `TestVerifyAgainstIdentifiersRejectsAShortProofWithoutLosingStoredData`, which asserts both the rejection and that the existing sidecar stays readable, and by an added case in `TestVerifyBlobSidecarsGloasDoesNotRequireInclusionProof`. Removing either check fails its test.

`make lint` clean; `cl/persistence/blob_storage`, `cl/das`, `cl/phase1/network` and `cmd/capcli` pass.
author: lystopad

title: cl/persistence/blob_storage: validate sidecar structure before dereferencing it
body:
Follow-up to #23934, which is already merged. Found by @awskii reviewing the same change on #23923 — the fix I added there introduced a panic where the code it replaced returned an error.

The shape check calls `sidecar.CommitmentInclusionProof.Length()` on a `solid.HashVectorSSZ` interface field without checking for nil. A JSON `null` leaves that field nil:

- `BlobSidecar.UnmarshalJSON` pre-fills `tmp.CommitmentInclusionProof` with `NewHashVector(17)`.
- For `null`, encoding/json does not descend into that pointer and calls `SetZero()` on the interface instead.
- So `"kzg_commitment_inclusion_proof": null` yields a nil proof, while `[]` yields a zero-length one.

Measured both, rather than reasoning about encoding/json's behaviour: `null` → `nil == true`, `[]` → `nil == false`.

**This is a regression #23934 introduced.** Previously the unconditional `VerifyCommitmentInclusionProof` handled it — it guards `commitmentInclusionProof == nil` and returns false (cl/cltypes/blob_sidecar.go:154) — so the caller got a clean "could not verify blob's inclusion proof". Now it panics.

Reachable through `capcli chain --blobs` → `retrieveBlobsFromRemoteEndpoint` (JSON decode) → `storeRemoteBlobs`, which checks only the nil sidecar, index and commitment. A response repeating the block's real header, index and commitment passes the root and index matches, then panics. It happens on every fork, because the length check runs before the version gate.

Severity is a tooling crash, not a node halt: the only production caller of the insert path is capcli, and the input is a malformed response from an endpoint the operator chose. The `VerifyBlobSidecars` copy has the same unguarded call; its callers do not take sidecars from JSON, so it is not reachable with nil today — guarded anyway, since the two sites should not disagree.

Both sites now check nil first, matching `blob_sidecar.go:154`. Pinned by a nil-proof case next to the existing `NewHashVector(0)` one; removing the guards panics the test.

`make lint` clean; `cl/persistence/blob_storage`, `cl/das` and `cmd/capcli` pass.

## Second guard: the nested header (`d42a9381c5`)

Raised by Copilot on #23923, and the same defect I filed as #23907 on 2026-09-10.

`VerifyAgainstIdentifiersAndInsertIntoTheBlobStore` dereferences the nested header twice before
validating anything — once to seed `lastProcessed` ahead of the loop, once to hash inside it — so a
response that decodes with `signed_block_header` or its `header` absent panics. `VerifyBlobSidecars`
has guarded exactly this all along; the insert path never did.

The pre-loop read is the one that bites first, so a check placed inside the loop would not help. The
guard therefore runs over the whole slice before the first dereference, reusing the existing
"blob response contains incomplete sidecar" wording.

Unlike the nil-proof guard above, this one is **not** a regression from #23934 — it predates that
change and is present on `main`, `release/3.6` and `release/3.5` alike. It is fixed here because the
surrounding validation is already being corrected, and leaving one field guarded and the next not is
how the next reader gets caught.

Pinned by `TestVerifyAgainstIdentifiersRejectsAnIncompleteHeader`, covering both a nil
`SignedBlockHeader` and a non-nil header struct with a nil `Header`.

Closes #23907.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/network, execution/execmodule: stop two tests racing the Windows clock
body:
Fixes both failures in `tests / tests-mac-linux (windows-2025, serial)`, seen on https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/34673097118/job/103499473721. Neither is caused by the PR that surfaced them, and both are specific to Windows: every other arm of that matrix passed, including `ubuntu-24.04, serial`, which runs the same commitment path.

## `TestForwardRequestMoreEmptyP2PDoesNotInvalidateHTTPFallback`

```
beacon_downloader_test.go:625: Not equal: expected: 1, actual: 0
    valid HTTP fallback was discarded after an empty P2P response
```

The test sequences itself on two channels. The HTTP handler signals `fallbackStarted` and then blocks until the test calls `release()`. In between, the test asserts on the cursor. It also capped `forwardBeaconRequestTimeout` at 100ms, which is a second clock running against that handshake. When the runner is loaded enough that more than 100ms passes before `release()`, the request context expires, the fallback blocks are discarded and the process function is never called.

Reproduced exactly by sleeping 150ms before `release()` on an otherwise unmodified tree: same line, same message, same expected and actual.

The test already bounds itself with its own one-second guards on `fallbackStarted` and on `RequestMore` returning, so it does not need the cap. Dropping the override lets the production default apply and the handshake decide the sequence.

Verified by keeping the 150ms sleep in place, which now passes, then removing it and running the `TestForwardRequestMore` family 20 times.

## `TestSlowBlockMetricsAreEmittedForValidatedBlocks`

```
block_metrics_test.go:185: Should be true
    state_hash_ms was zero in every record — commitment timing is not reaching the emitter
```

The assertion needed a measured commitment duration to be positive. Commitment over a test-sized block takes about 0.1ms, so the result depends on the clock resolution of the runner, and on `windows-2025, serial` it reads zero. The check races the clock.

It is replaced by two tests that do not read the clock:

- `TestComputeCommitmentReportsItsDuration` in `execution/commitment/commitmentdb`: `ComputeCommitment` calls `AddCommitmentTime` exactly once. It counts calls, not durations.
- `TestRecordBlockMetricsTakesCommitmentTimeFromSharedDomains` in `execution/execmodule`: with 5ms of commitment time in `SharedDomains` and a 12ms exec stage, the record gets `StateHash` 5ms and `Execution` 7ms, and the commitment time is drained.

For the second test, `recordBlockMetrics` now takes the exec stage duration as a parameter instead of reading it from the executor. No behavior change.

Each new test fails when its wiring is removed: deleting the `AddCommitmentTime(took)` call fails the first, dropping `StateHash` from the `Record` literal fails the second.

All other checks in `TestSlowBlockMetricsAreEmittedForValidatedBlocks` are unchanged.

Not covered without the clock: moving the discarding `TakeCommitmentTime()` in `validateAndStorePayload` after `ValidateBlock`.

## Notes

`make lint` reports one gofmt issue in `db/snapshotsync/snapshots_test.go`. It exists on `main`, and this PR does not touch the file.

TDD: for the beacon test the reproduction came first and the fix was verified against it. The execmodule test drove the `recordBlockMetrics` signature change (red on compile, then green). The commitmentdb test covers existing behavior, so it was checked by mutation instead.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: recheck the head root in the cached-state fast path and test the head-copy paths
body:
#24165 already copies the new head outside the reader locks. This PR fixes a race in the cached-state fast path and keeps two tests main lacks.

## Changes
- `useCachedStateIfPossible` matched `HeadRoot()` before taking the head-state lock, so a publish in between returned the new head's state for the old root. It now reads root and state together via `ViewHeadStateWithIdentity` and falls back to the previous head if the head moved. `TestHeadFastPathRechecksRootAfterHeadMoves` publishes right after `HeadRoot()`; before the fix the lookup returned slot 2 for the slot-1 root.
- `TestFailedHeadUpdateKeepsHead`: a failed copy leaves `StateHead()`, the head and the previous state unchanged.
- `TestPreviousHeadFastPathUsesAuthoritativePriorRoot`: the previous-head path returns the state for a root that depends on `previousStateRoot` and misses for the recomputed root.
author: awskii

title: cl/transition: restore parallel rewards and inactivity epoch loops
body:
#13007 set every epoch-processing `ParallellForLoop` to one worker. The inactivity and rewards loops write only their own validator's score or balance, and dirty-leaf marking is atomic, so they go back to `runtime.NumCPU()` workers. On an epoch's first block `ProcessEpoch` runs twice: on the gossip-validation copy, and again inside `OnBlock`.

| p50 ms | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| inactivity scores | 6.09 | 0.92 |
| rewards and penalties | 38.19 | 30.45 |
| registry updates (unchanged) | 33.11 | 33.30 |
| `ProcessEpoch` total | 153.98 | 143.02 |
| `OnBlock`, epoch-first slot | 280.92 | 265.63 |

title: cl: expire ttl cache entries on read instead of sweeping
body:
Closes #23848

## Summary

- `cl/phase1/core/state/lru.CacheWithTTL` wrapped an `expirable.LRU` built with a ttl, whose cleanup goroutine cannot be stopped (`Close` is commented out in golang-lru v2.0.7 and there is no newer release), so every cache built per request, per peer or per test leaked a goroutine for the life of the process.
- The cache is now a `simplelru.LRU` under the wrapper's own mutex with no background work at all: `Add` stamps a deadline on the entry under the lock and reclaims up to two expired entries from the least recently used end, and `Get` treats an entry past its deadline as a miss and drops it. There is no sweep goroutine, no separate expiry order and no `Close`, so there is nothing to wire and nothing left to leak.
- `p2pManager.bannedPeers` was declared, assigned and never read; it is deleted rather than converted. The sentinel peers pool keeps its own, separate ban cache.
- The beacon rpc client's peer refresh loop ran on `context.Background()` and never exited; it now ends with the client's ctx, and `TestNewBeaconRpcP2PStopsPeerGoroutinesWhenContextEnds` pins that with `goleak`.

## What lazy expiry changes

Reads are unchanged: a value past its deadline is never returned. What differs is residency. Nothing removes an expired entry on a timer any more. An entry that is never read again reaches the least recently used end in deadline order, where an `Add` reclaims it, up to two per `Add` and stopping at the first live entry, so a cache that is written to holds roughly a ttl's worth of entries, as it does on `main`. An entry a `Get` promoted is reclaimed once everything less recently used than it has gone, which under continued writes is within two ttls of its `Add`. A cache that stops being written to keeps what it holds, up to its size cap, until the next `Add`. `Len` counts residents, expired or not. Its one reader is `Pool.LenBannedPeers`, which feeds the disconnected figure of `Sentinel.GetPeersCount` (`cl/sentinel/sentinel.go:250`); that figure can now include bans past their 30 minutes until a `BanStatus` lookup, a later ban or the 100,000 cap drops them. It is a report, not a decision. Eviction order is by recency as before, and an expired entry can hold a slot that a live one would otherwise take, so hit rates can differ from the swept version at the cap. No other caller reads `Len`, and the wrapper has no `Contains` or `Keys`. `Get` does not extend an entry's deadline; only `Add` does.

## Decisions, against `main`

- **`simplelru.LRU`, not `expirable.LRU`.** On `main` the expirable cache brings its own goroutine, its own lock and 100 expiry buckets, and the goroutine cannot be stopped. The wrapper already serialises every call under one mutex, so the base only needs to be an LRU with nothing to stop. It rejects `size <= 0`, which `New` already refuses and no caller passes; `NewWithTTL` panics on it rather than growing an error return every call site would have to thread.
- **No sweep goroutine; `Add` reclaims the expired tail.** Expiry on read alone would let a cache fill to its size cap, and for three caches the ttl is the practical memory bound because their values are large and their keys are never read again: `shuffledIndiciesCacheReader` (64 entries of 8 bytes per active validator), `bid_validation_states` (4 full beacon state copies) and `aggregation_in_committee`. Dropping up to two expired entries from the least recently used end on every `Add` is O(1), needs no extra structure and nothing to stop, and keeps a written-to cache near a ttl's worth of entries; two per `Add` stays ahead of the one entry an `Add` inserts, so a backlog drains. Dropping the goroutine also removes the ownership question for caches with no natural owner: the historical states reader's `shuffledIndiciesCache` (#24148) no longer starts anything when the antiquary rebuilds the reader after a failed initialisation, so that leak goes with this change too.
- **The deadline is stamped under the lock.** Time spent waiting for the mutex is not charged to the entry's ttl, so a long wait cannot store a value that is already expired.

## Tests

`cl/phase1/core/state/lru`: 21 tests. A test back-dates an entry's deadline under the lock instead of sleeping past a short ttl; the one test that waits on the clock holds the cache lock for 100 ms to show the deadline is taken under it, and a slow scheduler can only make it pass. Covered: a live hit; an expired entry stays resident until read, then a `Get` returns the zero value, misses and drops it; the deadline boundary (live at the deadline, expired one nanosecond after); the deadline is stamped at `Add`, under the lock; `Add` on an existing key renews its deadline and replaces its value, before and after expiry; `Get` does not extend the deadline; size eviction is by recency and reports the eviction; the cap bounds a cache of live entries; an `Add` reclaims two expired entries from the least recently used end and stops at the first live one; writes drain an expired backlog; steady write traffic holds residency to the ttl, not the cap; an entry a `Get` promoted is reclaimed once it reaches that end; reclamation moves neither counter; `Remove`; a ttl of zero or less never expires and reclaims nothing; a non-positive size panics; hit and miss counters move exactly once per `Get`; concurrent `Add`, `Get`, `Remove` and `Len` on overlapping keys with a 1 ms ttl under `-race`.

Run: `go vet` on every touched package; `go test -race -count=1 ./cl/phase1/core/state/lru/ ./cl/rpc/`; `go test ./cl/p2p/ ./cl/sentinel/ ./cl/sentinel/peers/ ./cl/sentinel/handlers/ ./cl/phase1/network/services/ ./cl/aggregation/ ./cl/validator/attestation_producer/`.

The `WaitGroup.Go` lint fix is a mechanical test refactor, so it uses the existing tests without a new TDD cycle. Cache tests pass normally and with `-race`; `make lint` and `make erigon integration` also pass.

AI assistance: the fix and tests were drafted with AI tooling in my workflow and verified by running them as described. I am responsible for the change and will handle review feedback.

author: domiwei

title: cl: request blobs under the canonical root, and put the block signature on ColumnSyncableSignedBlock
body:
Fixes #23896.

`ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot` decodes blocks **without their execution payload** — its doc says so, and
both branches end at the same decoder, the database path (`slot > BlocksAvailable()`) as well as the
segment path. Hashing the result yields a root that never existed on chain, and peers index data
columns and blob sidecars by the real root, so every by-root request the blob backfill made matched
nothing and ran to its timeout.

The effect is that **`BlobHistoryDownloader` never recovered anything**. Blobs were present only where
live gossip had already caught them; a slot that missed live recovery stayed empty forever and the
archive dump wedged behind it.

## 1. Carry the canonical root

`collectIncompleteBlocks` already reads the canonical root from the index for its store lookup and
then discards it. It now carries it as `incompleteBlock{block, root}`.

- **Fulu** — the block is wrapped in a `rootedColumnBlock` overriding `BlockHashSSZ()`.
- **Deneb** — `blobsIdentifiersFromRootedBlocks` builds by-root identifiers from the supplied roots.
  The exported `BlobsIdentifiersFromBlocks` is unchanged: its one production caller,
  `cmd/capcli/blob_store.go`, works on a remotely fetched block that still has its payload, so its
  self-hash *is* the real root.

Three further sites derived the root by hashing and needed threading too, or the fix would have been
half-applied: `newDenebRecoveryBatch` keyed its group map on the self-hash (so identifiers could never
have matched), and `retryBlock`/`readRetryBlock` re-hashed on the retry path.

## 2. Put the block signature on `ColumnSyncableSignedBlock`

Found in review by @awskii and Copilot. This is why the PR touches `cl/das` and `cl/cltypes`.

`newBlobRecoveryMetadata` read the proposer signature with a **type switch on the two concrete block
types**. A wrapper matches neither, so `hasSignature` stayed false — and both comparisons guarding on
it were written `metadata.hasSignature && …`, so both short-circuited to accept:

- `peer_das.go:1566`, which rejects **and bans** a peer whose column-sidecar header signature does not
  match the block
- `peer_das.go:342`, in `validateStoredBlobRecoveryMetadata`

A peer could then answer a Fulu backfill request with an authentic header, valid cells and proofs and
an arbitrary signature: accepted, persisted, and copied verbatim into the reconstructed sidecars.
Nothing downstream covers it — `resolveColumnSidecarSlotAndRoot` binds the header to the requested
root by `HashSSZ` only, and `VerifyBlobSidecars` is called with a nil header-verification func.

It mattered **because** part 1 works: before it, that path asked for a root no peer had, so the check
protected nothing in practice.

`BlockSignature()` is on the interface now — both implementers already had the field — and the type
switch is gone, so a wrapper cannot drop the check.

## 3. Remove `hasSignature`

With the type switch gone the field was set true at the only construction site, making both readers
always-true conjuncts and the two assertions on it checks against a constant. Removing it leaves the
signature comparison unconditional, which is what moving the accessor onto the interface guarantees.

## Also from review

- `blobsIdentifiersFromRootedBlocks` is unexported — `incompleteBlock` is unexported, so nothing
  outside the package could construct the argument.
- The displaced doc comment is back above `BlobsIdentifiersFromBlocks`; the rooted variant has its own.
- A retry slot with no canonical row is logged rather than skipped silently. It is reachable only from
  the segment path, is never trimmed (`trimRetryRanges` drops only frozen slots), and would otherwise
  hold the backfill incomplete forever with no output naming the cause.

## Measured on a live gnosis archive node

**Before**, 12 hours at `caplin_peer_count` 127:

| | |
|---|---|
| backfill recovery attempts | 843 |
| failed with `context deadline exceeded` | **842** |
| unique slots affected | 202, retried up to 6× each |
| live gossip recoveries (`blobsRecover`) | 131 |
| overlap between the two sets | **0** |

Disjoint: a slot was either caught live or never recovered at all.

**After**, same node and datadir:

```
DownloadColumnsAndRecoverBlobs elapsed=1.247s   slots=[30104691]
[blobsRecover] recovering done slot=30104691 numberOfBlobs=1 elapsedTime=100ms
```

`elapsed` went from a flat 30.000 s to **~0.97 s**, and `[blobsRecover] recovering done` accompanied a
backfill target for the first time. The 30 s was never work; it was waiting for peers to answer a
request for a root that does not exist.

Twenty minutes later every sampled slot from the failing set was served and the frontier had unwedged:

```
frozen_blobs  30,060,000 -> 30,080,000
frozen_blocks               30,089,999
gap                              9,999   (the structural resting value)
```

That run used the `release/3.6` backport of part 1, before parts 2 and 3 existed.

## Tests

- `TestRecoverFuluColumnsRequestsTheCanonicalRoot`, `TestBlobsIdentifiersUseTheSuppliedRoot` — the
  request carries the canonical root, using a fixture where it differs from the block's own hash.
- `TestNewDenebRecoveryBatchGroupsOnTheCanonicalRoot` — response grouping is keyed on it. Added
  because every migrated fixture makes the two roots equal, so the old map would still have passed.
- `TestRootedColumnBlockPreservesTheSignature` — the wrapper exposes the wrapped block's signature.
- `TestNewBlobRecoveryMetadataCarriesTheSignature` — sets a **non-zero** signature and checks it
  survives both a plain block and a wrapper. The existing fixtures sign with zero, so an equality
  against them would have been vacuous.
- `TestReadRetryBlockReturnsTheCanonicalRoot` — the retry path re-resolves the root for a slot pulled
  off the retry ledger. Nothing covered it, so reverting that lookup to the self-hash would have kept
  every other distinct-root test green.

All mutation-verified: reverting each path fails its test, including restoring the concrete type
switch, which fails on the wrapper case specifically.

`./cl/...` passes; `make lint` clean.

## Related

- #23927 validates frozen blob segments at rest; this fixes the recovery that keeps them complete.
- #24037 covers `capcli dump-blobs-snapshots` writing hollow segments — a separate defect.
- Backports to `release/3.6` and `release/3.5` to follow.

title: docs: record the blob snapshot invariants agents keep getting wrong
body:
Four additions to the agent guidance, each from a mistake made during a mainnet blob sidecar repair. All references verified against `main`.

**`db/agents.md`**

- Blob segments are `<range>-blobsidecars.seg` but their index is `<range>-blocksidecars.idx` (`snaptype/type.go:155`). A glob on one name silently misses the other — this caused three separate incidents in one day: stale indexes after a delete, orphaned indexes after a version bump, and a cleanup that skipped a whole decade of files.
- Blob snapshots rest up to one `CaplinMergeLimit` behind beacon snapshots by design (`antiquary.go:499` refuses to dump a partial range), so a resting gap of 9,999 is healthy.

**`cl/agents.md`**

- Blob retirement is gated on `blobBackfilled` (`antiquary.go:240`), so a gap the backfill cannot fill stops **all** blob retirement, including provably complete ranges far below it. Observed live: 48 chunks of verified data parked behind ~2,000 slots. The gate returns silently, with no log or metric. `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` is how long peers *must* serve rather than a ceiling, so a gap past it is not guaranteed retrievable rather than certainly unfillable.
- In archive mode the backfill applies no retention floor (`blob_downloader.go:343`); only the non-archive path clamps `targetSlot` and `retryFloor`. Each batch is bounded by `requestBlobBatchExpiration` (15s, `blobs.go:35`) and returns early on a complete response, but the enclosing loop does not terminate for slots that stay unavailable.
- `frozen_blobs` is published only from the forkchoice stage (`phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:64`) and the gauge starts at zero, so zero cannot establish whether blob snapshots exist. The shipped dashboards already guard it with `> 0`.

**`AGENTS.md`** — a TDD note on changing bounds and constants.

A deliberate tolerance and an off-by-one are indistinguishable at the call site. The `(beaconTo - 1)` in the blob coverage check was nearly "fixed" to require the blob and beacon frontiers to match, which would have made the integrity check reject every healthy node and block snapshot publishing outright. The accompanying red test passed because it encoded the same wrong assumption as the change. A reviewer caught the premise, not the arithmetic.

Docs only, no code change.

_Updated after review: the retention, retry-bound and metric claims were over-absolute and have been qualified — see the review threads. One of them was not merely theoretical: a mainnet archive node recovered a 46-day-old gap from peers while I was asserting that could not happen._
