title: cl/beacon/synced_data: swap head state under lock instead of copying under it
body:
Fixes #24164.

## Problem

`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot`/`OnHeadState` copied the entire incoming `CachingBeaconState` while holding `s.mu`/`s.accessLock` for writing. `ViewHeadState`, `ViewPreviousHeadState`, and the single-field accessors (`ValidatorPublicKeyByIndex`, `ValidatorIndexByPublicKey`, `CommitteeCount`, `HistoricalRootElementAtIndex`, `HistoricalSummaryElementAtIndex`) all take the matching read lock, so every one of them was blocked for however long that copy took.

This is the state-backed remainder of #23154 that #23155 explicitly scoped out: #23155 publishes the selected head identity (root/slot) before the state copy runs, so identity-only reads no longer wait on it, but state-backed reads still do. Any duty computation needing actual state content - not just a root - goes through `ViewHeadState` and is still exposed.

Reproduced on a mainnet validator node running a release/3.7 dev build: sync-committee efficiency dropped to 94.60% (199/3686 missed) in a 24h window while attestation efficiency stayed at 99.59%, matching #23154's own description of this failure mode (attestation data is produced before the head-state update; sync-committee messages need the state after it). Full field evidence is in #24164.

## Change

Both `OnHeadState` and `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` now acquire a new `writeLock sync.Mutex`, independent of `mu`/`accessLock`, before doing any work - `OnHeadState`'s `BlockRoot()` resolution included, not just the copy - then call a shared `publishHeadStateLocked` (documented as requiring the lock already held), which:

1. Copies the incoming state under `writeLock`.
2. Takes `mu`/`accessLock` only to swap the copy in as the new head state and demote the current head state to previous (`previousHeadState = headState; headState = copied` - a pointer reassignment, no data copy) - an O(1) critical section regardless of state size.

`writeLock` matters because it isn't just about latency: without it, a writer that started earlier but is slower to resolve its root or copy its state could be overtaken and then overwritten by a writer that started later but finishes faster - a silent regression to a stale head, not just a slow reader. This applies equally to `OnHeadState` (root not yet known, one caller - `cmd/capcli`, called sequentially today, but still part of the exported `SyncedData` contract) and `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` (root given, used by every concurrent caller: forkchoice, forward sync, block production). `UnsetHeadState` also takes `writeLock` (before `mu`), so it can't land in the middle of an in-flight publish and then get resurrected by it.

Net effect: lock hold time for readers is now O(1); writers stay fully serialized in arrival order, same guarantee the old single-mutex design gave for free. `previousHeadState` is now the actual prior `headState` object (aliased, not copied into a reused buffer) - same observable content, one fewer full-state copy per update. No behavior change to any exported signature.

## Testing

Per this repo's TDD convention, each fix has a test that reproduces it against the commit before the fix and passes after:

- `TestViewHeadStateDoesNotWaitForHeadStateCopy` - a `ViewHeadState` reader is not blocked for the incoming state's copy duration (only the swap). Uses `copyHookForTest`, a package-level hook bound to the copy itself via a small `copyState` helper (not just called before it - so the hook's pause point can't be separated from the copy by a future reorder), to pause a writer at an exact point and prove a concurrent read completes while it's genuinely paused there.
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootSerializesConcurrentWriters` - a writer cannot be overtaken and overwritten by a writer that starts later. Deterministic: holds `writeLock` directly to represent a writer already inside its critical section.
- `TestOnHeadStateSerializesAgainstOnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` - `OnHeadState`'s root resolution is covered by the same serialization as `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot`'s copy, not just the copy step. Drives both writers through the real public API with a calibrated head start (documented in the test).
- `TestUnsetHeadStateSerializesWithPublish` - `UnsetHeadState` cannot be resurrected by a publish that was already in flight when it was called. Same hold-`writeLock` technique.

Plus:
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootColdStart` - first update populates head state, no previous state yet.
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootDemotesPriorHeadToPrevious` - `ViewPreviousHeadState` observes the state that was head right before the latest update, proving the alias-based swap is behaviorally equivalent to the old copy-based one.
- `TestOnHeadStateWithBlockRootConcurrentReadWrite` - races real writers against real readers through the public API. Passes under `-race`.

Full existing suite (`cl/beacon/synced_data`, `cl/beacon/handler`, `cl/phase1/stages`) passes unchanged, including the generation-consistency and TOCTTOU-regression tests added for #23155. All new tests pass under `-race`, repeated.

## Trade-offs

- `OnHeadState`/`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` now always allocate a fresh state copy (`newState.Copy()`), rather than reusing a preallocated buffer via `CopyInto` on the steady-state path. This trades a modest increase in per-block allocation for removing the reader-blocking lock hold - the copy's own cost is unchanged either way, only whether readers wait for it. Flagging in case reviewers want a buffer-pooling follow-up instead; I kept this PR to the minimal change that fixes the blocking behavior.
- Not backporting in this PR. release/3.6 already carries #23155's prerequisite (backported as #23172, included in v3.6.1) so this fix would cherry-pick cleanly there. release/3.5 never received #23155/#23172, so it still has the original (larger) #23154 bug, not just this remainder - a release/3.5 backport would need that fix first. Happy to open both as follow-ups if maintainers want them.
- #24197 tracks two remaining test-hardening items from review (real-path writer-ordering coverage, `accessLock` accessor coverage) - explicitly scoped as non-blocking follow-ups, not production bugs.

author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon: publish sync-committee messages in background instead of blocking the request
body:
Fixes #24258.

## Problem

`PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` published sync-committee messages to gossip synchronously, on the HTTP request's own context, before writing the HTTP response, and swallowed any publish error at `Debug`. The handler blocks for the full duration of gossip validation/handoff, coupling HTTP response latency to a single-threaded event loop shared with the much higher-volume attestation topics, and whatever error `Publish` returns never surfaced to the caller, an HTTP status, or any metric.

Cross-referencing a Lighthouse VC log against the beacon API's `rewards/sync_committee` endpoint confirmed real, on-chain misses on a mainnet node — see #24258 for the evidence.

**Correction (2026-09-24):** an earlier version of this description and #24258 claimed the request context being cancelled on handler return could abort an in-flight publish. That's wrong — the handler cannot return (and so `net/http` cannot cancel `r.Context()`) while it's still blocked on the synchronous `Publish` call, and go-libp2p-pubsub v0.11.0's `Topic.Publish` only consults its `ctx` parameter inside the optional `WithReadiness` path, which Erigon's no-options call never takes. Caught by an independent third-party review of this PR; full detail in the correction section of #24258. The on-chain misses are real; this PR does not establish their specific original cause, only that decoupling the publish call removes the HTTP-latency coupling and makes every failure path observable and, where the failure is known before the response is written, reported to the caller. A later review raised a further, specific, unresolved doubt about the original cross-reference's slot alignment — see the follow-up comment on #24258. Also unresolved either way in this session.

## Prior art

Both geth (`eth/handler.go`'s `txBroadcastLoop`) and reth (`TransactionsManager`) decouple RPC-accept from network-broadcast the same way: the RPC handler only inserts into a local pool and returns; a single long-lived background worker, subscribed to a pool/feed channel at node startup, does the actual broadcast, independent of any individual request's context.

## Fix

`GossipManager` already runs lifetime-scoped background goroutines off its own internally-owned context - this reuses that instead of introducing a new context-derivation pattern:

- A bounded `publishQueue` channel plus one dedicated worker goroutine, started alongside the existing ones. The queue is sized to `beaconConfig.SyncCommitteeSize` (with a 64 floor) so it can absorb a full sync-committee burst without dropping.
- `PublishBackground(name string, data []byte, expiry time.Time, logCtx ...any) error` on the `Gossip` interface: enqueues non-blockingly and returns a stable sentinel error (never nil-but-silently-dropped) when the message was never admitted - full queue, shutdown in progress, an unresolvable fork digest, or already past `expiry`. The fork digest is resolved and captured at enqueue time, not re-resolved when the worker drains the job, so a message accepted just before a fork activates still publishes to the topic it was actually validated against.
- `expiry` (slot end plus the protocol's maximum gossip clock disparity, computed with exact time arithmetic) is checked both at admission and again immediately before the actual publish - a message that goes stale while queued behind other work is dropped instead of spending a compress/peer-lookup/publish cycle on it, without blocking fresh work behind it. This is a staleness check, not a validity/authentication one - see Known limitations below.
- `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` calls `PublishBackground` instead of the synchronous `Publish(r.Context(), ...)`. A non-nil return - a *known* failure, not an unknowable later network one - is now surfaced as HTTP 500 for an otherwise-valid batch, instead of a silent 200. Validation failures (the existing indexed 400 behavior) take precedence when a batch has both, without discarding the admission failure: `PublishBackground` still logs and counts it either way.
- Every drop path is observable and correctly categorized: `caplin_gossip_publish_queue_rejected_total{topic,reason}` for admission-time rejections (never queued), separate from `caplin_gossip_publish_accepted_total{topic}` and `caplin_gossip_publish_outcome_total{topic,outcome}` (handoff_ok/publish_error/panic/expired) for work that *was* admitted.
- `PublishBackground` never blocks the caller - not on queue capacity, not on shutdown: it checks the manager's own lifetime context directly (a plain, already non-blocking read) and the worker simply returns on `ctx.Done()` without an explicit drain step. A message admitted right at shutdown may end up queued with nothing left to process it, which has no functional effect - it was never going to publish either way, the same as one correctly rejected at admission. An earlier version of this PR added an admission gate (atomics, a drain step, dedicated test-only hooks) purely to keep the accepted/outcome counters exactly equal at process exit; per review from domiwei and AskAlexSharov, that complexity wasn't worth what it bought, so it was removed - the counters still hold the invariant during normal operation, just not necessarily at the exact moment of shutdown.

Ordering across queued messages doesn't matter here - gossip has no ordering contract between different validators/subnets.

Scoped to sync-committee messages only, where the on-chain evidence is. The same synchronous-publish-with-swallowed-error pattern exists at 13 other call sites in `pool.go`, `block_production.go`, and `epbs.go` - left as a separate follow-up to keep this PR focused. Full histograms (queue-wait/publish-call duration) and an in-flight gauge were considered and deliberately left out of this PR's scope - the accepted/outcome counters above already fix the modeling gap (a rejected admission being counted the same as an accepted-then-dropped job); histograms are a real but separate enhancement.

## Known limitations (tracked, not fixed here)

- **#24305**: a seen-key cache hit doesn't re-validate replacement bytes under the same key, pre-dates this PR (unchanged service code), and requires Beacon API access to reach; left as its own change since it touches the shared seen-key cache used elsewhere too. (The other gap #24305 originally tracked - `ErrIgnore` exempted then published anyway - is now fixed here: `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` skips `PublishBackground` entirely on `ErrIgnore`, verified against the real service.)
- `handoff_ok` in the new outcome metric means the local pubsub library accepted the publish call - it is not evidence of remote peer receipt or sync-aggregate inclusion. Neither this metric nor the two-host delivery test below establishes that a duty reliably arrives before its useful deadline; treat the two-host test as a transport smoke test, not a timing/reliability guarantee.
- The captured fork digest is read from the wall clock at enqueue time, not derived from the validated message's own epoch; this predates the queue and is unchanged by it.
- **#24319**: if the single publish worker gets stuck on one call (e.g. the shared pubsub event loop is congested enough to back up its internal send buffer), the bounded queue can fill with jobs that expire before the worker reaches them, and admission then rejects fresh, still-valid messages with no path to reclaim that wasted capacity. A per-job context deadline doesn't fix this - go-libp2p-pubsub's local-publish path doesn't consult the caller's context past the `WithReadiness` option we don't use. The real fix (evicting expired entries from the queue on full-queue admission) is a genuine change to the queue's concurrency model, tracked separately.

## Testing

`cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager_test.go` and `cl/beacon/handler/pool_test.go`, each verified by mutation (the corresponding regression fails reliably when the fix is reverted):

- `PublishBackground` never blocks its caller on queue capacity or shutdown; drops rather than blocks once the queue is full, sized to hold a full `SyncCommitteeSize` burst.
- The fork digest used to publish is the one captured at enqueue time, even if it changes before the worker drains the job.
- Expiry: the exact inclusive boundary (just before/at/just after the deadline), a job going stale while queued behind other work without blocking fresh work behind it.
- A panic in one queued publish doesn't take down the worker, and its recovery log includes the same validator/subnet/slot context the ordinary failure path already logs.
- A queued message reaches the real gossip `Publish` path end-to-end, including a two-host test proving some bytes cross a real connection (see Known limitations - this is a transport smoke test, not a full protocol/timing test).
- A message is dropped observably once the manager has shut down, whether triggered via `Close` or the parent context passed into `NewGossipManager` being cancelled directly (the actual production path); `PublishBackground` racing concurrently with either never panics or deadlocks, and the worker always terminates.
- The accepted/outcome counters satisfy the invariant that at quiescence *during normal operation*, a topic's accepted count equals the sum of its terminal-outcome counts - compared as deltas against a baseline, since these are process-global collectors never reset between test runs (an earlier version of this test compared raw values and flaked under `-count=2`; fixed and verified up to `-count=5`).
- `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees` calls `PublishBackground`, never the blocking `Publish`; a full queue returns HTTP 500 for an otherwise-valid batch; a validation failure takes precedence over an admission failure when a batch has both.

`go build ./...`, `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/... ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/... -race`, and `make lint` all pass.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/stages, cl/phase1/forkchoice: replay persisted Gloas parent payloads
body:
## Summary

- recover retained FULL-parent Gloas envelopes during a later chain-tip batch when the parent payload has no usable EL verdict
- replay the stored payload to the EL with one bounded budget per batch, split fairly across the parent roots that FULL children in the batch actually need and that need an EL call, and deduplicate sibling retries
- preserve EMPTY-branch progress when a FULL sibling's parent replay fails, and never reserve replay budget for EMPTY children
- do not record a `None` status when the replay budget or context runs out before the EL answers, so a locally available parent is not marked unavailable
- preserve no-EL, known-status, validation-error, and pruning behavior

## Context

Within a running Caplin process, a stored FULL parent can still have payload status `None` when a chain-tip batch reaches its child: the earlier EL call failed or timed out, and the regular pending retry has not repaired it yet (the entry is still queued behind others, the per-cycle retry budget ran out, or the entry was dropped at the pending-queue cap). `validateParentPayloadPath` then rejects the child with `ErrParentEnvelopePending` in every batch, and chain-tip sync previously skipped the stored envelope, so nothing replayed it while the node was behind the tip.

The retained-root payload status itself lives in the fork graph, so this is not about losing the verdict cache. SYNCING/ACCEPTED map to `NotValidated` and are accepted optimistically; only a missing verdict blocks the child.

This PR is intentionally scoped to same-process retries while the parent graph entry remains retained. It does not provide process-restart recovery: production startup clears the temporary `caplin-forkchoice` directory and reconstructs an empty envelope index. Durable restart recovery and the separate block-collector catch-up changes investigated on Glamsterdam Devnet 8 remain outside this PR.

The per-batch body of `listenToIncomingBlocksUntilANewBlockIsReceived` is extracted into `processChainTipBatch` without behavior changes so the full batch sequence can be tested.

## Fork-choice changes

- `markPayloadStatus` no longer takes the fork graph's `lifecycleMu` read lock a second time when it invalidates descendants inside an outer `WithRetainedBlock` call. A nested `RLock` on a `sync.RWMutex` can deadlock when a writer (pruning) waits between the two acquisitions. For this, `WithRetainedBlock` now passes the retention check to its callback: `WithRetainedBlock(root common.Hash, fn func(isRetained func(common.Hash) bool)) bool`. All implementations and callers are updated.
- `MarkPayloadStatusAndGasLimitIfRetained` records the payload status and the gas limit under one retained-root guard. The no-engine apply path now also records the gas limit when it marks a payload `NotValidated`, so bid validation on no-EL nodes finds the parent gas limit.

## Testing

- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/stages -count=1`
- `TestStoredParentReplayRootsExcludeEmptyChildren` fails without the `parentEnvelopeRequired` filter in `storedParentReplayRoots` (EMPTY child's parent counted) and passes with it
- `TestChainTipBatchReplaysStoredParentPayload` drives `processChainTipBatch` with a real `ForkChoiceStore`: VALID replay unblocks the FULL child, a missing verdict keeps it for retry, and the EMPTY sibling progresses in both orders; it fails when the replay gate is disabled
- `TestChainTipBatchReplayBudgetSkipsParentsWithUsableVerdict` fails when a parent with a usable verdict takes a replay budget slot
- `TestOnExecutionPayloadWithoutEngineMarksPayloadOptimistic` fails when the no-engine apply path does not record the gas limit
- `TestStoredParentPayloadReplayWithoutVerdictKeepsStatus` fails without the context checks in `ensureStoredParentPayloadAccepted` (EL called with a spent budget; `None` recorded after the deadline) and passes with them
- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/stages -run 'TestStoredParent|TestParentEnvelopeRequired|TestEnsureStoredParent|TestChainTipBatch|TestGloasPayloadRetry|TestDrainPendingGloasPayloads' -count=1`
- `make lint` (clean)
- `go build ./cmd/erigon ./cmd/integration`

The branch has not been separately deployed as a full-node replacement.

title: cl/antiquary: give a blob backlog the same compression parallelism as EL catch-up
body:
Fixes #24310.

`antiquateBlobs` always passed `1` as `compressWorkers`, so a node behind on blob retirement compressed gigabyte segments single-threaded for the whole backlog.

Measured on a sepolia archive node clearing a 72-chunk range (10,470,000 → 11,189,999) after a store repair: **54 min per ~1.45 GB chunk**, about **2.4 days**, with exactly one `seg/parallel_compress.go` goroutine throughout.

One worker at the tip is deliberate and stays — retirement covers a single chunk there and should not compete with execution. EL retirement draws the same line by sync cycle:

```go
// execution/stagedsync/stage_snapshots.go
if s.CurrentSyncCycle.IsInitialCycle {
	cfg.blockRetire.SetWorkers(estimate.CompressSnapshot.Workers())
} else {
	cfg.blockRetire.SetWorkers(1)
}
```

Caplin had no equivalent, so it stayed at `1` however far behind it was. The pending range now decides: two chunks or more is a catch-up.

## The shared build limiter

Going parallel means honouring the limiter Caplin has been bypassing. `segmentsBuildLimiter` is created once in `node/eth/backend.go` and passed to both `NewBlockRetire` and `caplin1.RunCaplinService`; its size defaults to 1, "allows 1 kind of snapshots to be built simultaneously". Caplin's acquisition is commented out, and the commented code would not have worked — its `defer` re-acquires instead of releasing.

At one worker that omission was cheap. At full width it would not be: both sides size themselves from the same estimate, which budgets 50% of RAM per build, so two concurrent builds spend the whole budget.

A dump that cannot take the limiter **falls back to one worker** rather than skipping. Blob retirement is gated on the whole range landing, so a skipped dump leaves the gate shut and the node grinding — the failure mode in #24112. Slower is acceptable; stalled is not.

## Tests

`isBlobBacklog` pins the threshold deterministically, including a non-advancing range that must not underflow into an enormous backlog.

`blobCompressWorkers` pins the limiter behaviour without a live antiquary: the tip leaves it free, a backlog holds it and gives it back, a taken limiter falls back to one worker, and no limiter still goes parallel. Those assertions hold on a single-core runner, where a worker-count comparison alone would prove nothing.

Mutation-verified: lowering the threshold to one chunk, always reporting a backlog, dropping the underflow guard, always going parallel, going parallel without the limiter, and never releasing it are each caught.

**Known gap:** reverting the call site in `antiquateBlobs` to a hardcoded `1` still leaves the suite green. Covering that needs `antiquateBlobs` reachable in a test — a live DB, snapshots and blob storage — which is a larger change than this warrants. The selection logic it calls is fully covered; the line wiring it in is not.

**Not addressed here:** `DumpBeaconBlocks` in the same function has the identical shape, but its segments are far smaller so the effect is much weaker — worth its own change if measurements justify it.

title: lint: enable staticcheck's ST1019, ST1016, ST1012, ST1017, ST1005
body:
### Summary

Per #24021 (endorsed there by @taratorio): turns on the five staticcheck checks we'd left switched off, and fixes everything they find.

- **ST1019** — a package imported twice under two different names in the same file
- **ST1016** — a type's methods not agreeing on a receiver name
- **ST1012** — an error var not named `errFoo`/`ErrFoo`
- **ST1017** — Yoda conditions
- **ST1005** — error strings that are capitalized or end in punctuation

### Nature of the changes

All mechanical: dropping a redundant import alias, renaming a receiver consistently across a type's methods, renaming an error var (and every reference to it), flipping a comparison's operand order, or reformatting an error string's casing/punctuation. No behavior changes.

`gofumpt` (the other half of #24021) already landed separately in #24182 and #24183.

### One documented exception

`RwTx.AsyncClone` (`db/kv/temporal/kv_temporal.go`) keeps its outlier receiver name. Its body constructs a value of an embedded type also named `tx`; renaming the receiver to match the rest of `RwTx`'s methods would make that construction ambiguous with the receiver itself, so the rename isn't safe. Excluded narrowly for just this one file in `.golangci.yml`, with the same reasoning also left as a comment on the method itself.

### Verification

- Build passes clean
- `go vet` output matches the pre-existing baseline exactly, nothing new
- Full test suite passes
- Lint is clean, run twice per this repo's non-determinism note
- Diffed against `main` to confirm every change is exactly the intended fix, nothing else

title: cl/beacon, cmd: prepend EL+CL client identification to custom graffiti by default
body:
## Summary

Closes #24366.

Caplin's default block-production graffiti already implements the client-version graffiti standard (`engine_getClientVersionV1`-based EL+CL code and commit prefix), but only when the block-production request has no `graffiti` param at all. Any caller-supplied graffiti — including from an external validator client with its own graffiti (e.g. Lighthouse VC paired with Erigon EL + Caplin BN) — fully replaced it, leaving zero attributable client-identification data for client-diversity dashboards.

- Default behavior now **prefixes** the identification segment to caller-supplied graffiti as well, truncating the caller's text to whatever room remains in the fixed 32-byte graffiti field (a consensus-level SSZ `Bytes32`, not a convention). The segment stays at a fixed offset (bytes 0-N) regardless of custom-graffiti length. This matches the actual [flexible standard](https://hackmd.io/@wmoBhF17RAOH2NZ5bNXJVg/BJX2c9gja) Lighthouse itself links to — its default case is also identification-segment-first, with a ~20-byte threshold before degrading. Lighthouse's and Teku's own implementations instead put the segment *last* (append, not prefix), which needs a graduated truncation table on their side; putting it first here means tooling can read it at a fixed offset without one.
- New flag `--beacon.api.preserve-graffiti` (default `false`) opts out: caller-supplied graffiti is used verbatim (right-padded, not truncated or prefixed), for operators who want full control over their graffiti. It does not exactly reproduce pre-PR byte-for-byte behavior for a short/underspecified hex `graffiti` value specifically (right-pad vs. the old left-pad) — right-padding is now the one consistent convention on both the default and opt-out paths.
- **This is a default-behavior change** — see the `ChangeLog.md` entry. Operators who already set a custom graffiti will start publishing their EL+CL client identification by default, and a custom graffiti longer than 19 bytes (25 before the execution client's version resolves) will be truncated.
- Startup and diagnostic logging: `LogGraffitiIdentification` logs the default segment once at beacon-node startup and triggers the execution client's version lookup; `logGraffitiIdentificationOnce` logs it again, once, if/when that lookup resolves to something new; `warnGraffitiTruncatedOnce` warns once the first time a real proposal's graffiti is actually truncated.

## Changes

- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`: `identificationSegment()`/`identificationSegmentFor()`, `combinedGraffiti()` (prefix + truncate via `truncateAtRuneBoundary`), `graffitiFromHex()` (right-padded hex decoding), `requestGraffiti()` (dispatches on `PreserveGraffiti`), and the three logging functions above.
- `cl/beacon/beacon_router_configuration/cfg.go`: new `PreserveGraffiti` field on `RouterConfiguration`, already threaded into `ApiHandler`.
- `cmd/utils/flags.go`, `node/cli/default_flags.go`, `cmd/caplin/caplinflags/flags.go`, `cmd/caplin/caplincli/config.go`, `cmd/caplin/main.go`: CLI flag plumbing for both the main erigon binary and the standalone `cmd/caplin` binary.
- `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`: calls `LogGraffitiIdentification()` once at Beacon API startup.
- `docs/site/docs/fundamentals/caplin.md` (+ regenerated `llms-full.txt`): documents the flag and the default behavior.
- `ChangeLog.md`: breaking-change entry for v3.8.0.
- Test fixtures in `block_production_graffiti_test.go` that mock "the connected execution client" now use Erigon's own `EG` client code instead of `GE` (Geth), since these tests exercise Caplin's own default-graffiti mechanism — `TestGraffitiClientCode`, which tests the generic code-clamping utility on arbitrary strings, is left with its `GE`/`GETH` example since that's illustrating the clamp behavior, not simulating a paired client.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `combinedGraffiti` (short/truncated/empty graffiti, EL-unavailable consensus-only segment, UTF-8 rune-boundary truncation, non-UTF-8 graffiti, an invalid byte within budget not mistaken for a split rune), `graffitiFromHex`, `requestGraffiti` (default combine vs. `PreserveGraffiti` opt-out), `LogGraffitiIdentification`/`logGraffitiIdentificationOnce` (fires at most once each), and `warnGraffitiTruncatedOnce` (fires at most once).
- [x] `TestGetEthV3ValidatorBlockKeepsSelfBuildEnvelopeByBlockRoot` now also asserts on the produced block's actual `Body.Graffiti`, exercising the full HTTP call-site wiring (`graffitiFromHex` → `requestGraffiti` → `combinedGraffiti`), not just those functions directly.
- [x] Two other pre-existing tests send a non-empty `graffiti` param and previously never touched the execution client; updated them to seed a cached "EL version unavailable" so they don't need to additionally mock `GetClientVersionV1` for behavior unrelated to what they're testing.
- [x] `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/...` passes.
- [x] `go build ./...` passes.
- [x] `go tool -modfile=golangci-lint.mod golangci-lint run` on touched packages: 0 issues.
- [x] `go mod tidy -diff`: empty.
- [x] `python3 docs/site/scripts/generate-llms.py --check` passes.

title: db: remove unused function parameters and dead code
body:
Replaces the earlier blanket `_`-renaming approach for `db/` with actual parameter removal: this only touches free functions/methods that aren't bound to any interface or callback type (checked individually via `var _ Interface = ...` assertions, function-value passing, mock embedding, etc.). Anything still required by an interface or callback signature keeps its parameter name as-is, since Go only complains about unused imports/locals, not unused parameters.

Also deletes a few methods that turned out to have zero callers anywhere in the repo: `Aggregator.OpenList`, `SnapshotRepo.IntegrateMergedFiles`, and four `MemoryMutation` stubs (`Last`, `Stream`, `StreamAscend`, `StreamDescend`) that were just `panic("not implemented")`.

Verified with `go build ./...`, `go vet`, and the full test suite for every touched package.

things found along the way that look like pre-existing issues, left out of scope here:
- `PruneAncientBlocks`'s `timeout` param is required by the `dbservices.BlockRetire` interface, but the implementation never actually uses it, so callers' timeout values are silently dropped.
author: Sahil-4555

title: cl/phase1/network/services: authenticate sync-committee seen-key duplicates before acting on them
body:
Fixes findings 2 and 3 of #24305.

## Problem

`syncCommitteeMessagesService.ProcessMessage` deduplicates on `(subnet, slot, validator_index)` - a cache hit returned `nil` unconditionally, without checking whether the *submitted* `beacon_block_root`/`signature` matched what was actually verified for that key.

Two consequences, both on the same line:

- **Finding 2 (security):** a second submission with *different*, never-verified content for an already-seen key was treated the same as a genuinely re-validated message. On the REST path this reaches `PublishBackground` (unsigned bytes admitted to the gossip queue); on the raw gossip path, `ProcessMessage`'s `nil` maps to `pubsub.ValidationAccept` in `newPubsubValidator`, so the same content would be forwarded to peers, never having had its signature checked.
- **Finding 3 (efficiency):** even a *legitimate* retry of the exact same, already-published content hit the same `nil` path, so the REST handler called `PublishBackground` again and spent another queue slot on a message that had already gone through admission once.

## Fix

The seen-key cache now stores what it actually verified (`beacon_block_root`, `signature`), and a cache hit compares the submission against it:

- **Different content** → `ErrIgnore`, without verifying or acting on it - matching the spec's own same-slot dedup rule, just correctly applied to the case that slipped through before.
- **Matching content, not yet published** → `nil`, unchanged - a retry after a failed `PublishBackground` admission (e.g. a full queue) still gets a real attempt.
- **Matching content, already published** → `ErrIgnore` - no second queue slot spent on it.

"Already published" needs the service to learn about publish *outcome*, not just verification, since verification and publish are two separate steps (the service verifies; `pool.go` publishes, later, possibly failing). Added `MarkPublished(subnet, slot, validator_index, beacon_block_root, signature)` to `SyncCommitteeMessagesService`, called by the handler only after `PublishBackground` actually succeeds.

## Testing

`cl/phase1/network/services/sync_committee_messages_service_test.go`:
- A replacement with different content is `ErrIgnore` and never reaches `BlsVerifyMultipleSignatures` (a second, unexpected mock call would fail the test).
- The original message is unaffected by a rejected replacement in between.
- A retry of the same content, with no `MarkPublished` call, still succeeds (`nil`) - the queue-full recovery path is preserved.
- A retry after `MarkPublished` is `ErrIgnore`.

`cl/beacon/handler/pool_test.go`:
- A successful `PublishBackground` triggers `MarkPublished` with the message's own content.
- A failed `PublishBackground` does not.

Each behavior was checked by mutation (reverting the relevant code line and confirming the corresponding test fails for the right reason, then restoring it) before being left in place.

`go build ./...`, `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services/... ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/... ./cl/beacon/handler/... -race`, and `make lint` all pass.
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon/handler: fix PTC duties dependent root and fork-epoch duties
body:
Fixes #24116.

## Summary

Two fixes to `POST /eth/v1/validator/duties/ptc/{epoch}`, so that a validator client refetches PTC duties exactly when they change.

### 1. Use the PTC shuffling-dependent root

The endpoint returned the proposer dependent root (`epoch*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1`), read from a second head-state view. The [Beacon API](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/duties/ptc.yaml) defines it as `get_block_root_at_slot(state, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch - 1) - 1)`, or the genesis block root on underflow. This is the attester arithmetic, and it must equal `current_epoch_dependent_root` / `next_epoch_dependent_root` of `head_v2`.

Effects of the old root:
- at Gloas genesis, the next-epoch request returned 404;
- the root for a fixed next epoch changed on every head update, so validator clients downloaded the duties again without a reorg.

The handler now uses `computeDependentRootSlot(epoch, S, true)` and computes the root and the duties in one `viewHeadStateWithIdentity` callback. A failed root lookup is unreachable for the admitted epochs and now returns 500 instead of the undeclared 404.

### 2. Do not serve fork-epoch PTC duties from a pre-Gloas head

While the head is still in epoch `F-1` (`F = GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH`), a request for epoch `F` was answered by `ComputePTC` on the Fulu state. That prediction is not final. `upgrade_to_gloas` builds the PTC for `F` with `initialize_ptc_window` after `process_epoch` of `F-1`, and `compute_balance_weighted_selection` uses the effective balances updated there. The Beacon API root for epoch `F` is `(F-1)*S-1`, and it stays the same across the fork. So a validator client that cached the predicted duties never refetches them, and can act on wrong PTC duties for the whole first Gloas epoch.

The endpoint now returns 503 for a pre-Gloas head. The existing guards already limit requests to `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH <= epoch <= current_epoch+1`, so this only affects the fork epoch while the head is before the fork. From the first Gloas head onwards, the duties come from `ptc_window`. Returning an empty duty list would be worse: the client would cache it under the same root and miss epoch `F`.

This 503 is a deliberate choice that the Beacon API does not describe. It matters for the Sepolia Glamsterdam fork (epoch 353024).

Consequences for validator clients:
- during epoch `F-1`, a validator client logs failed PTC duty requests for epoch `F` (for example `Failed to download PTC duties` in the Lighthouse VC) and retries on the next slot;
- PTC members of the first Gloas slot learn their duty only after the first Gloas block is imported, because the head stays pre-Gloas until then.

Other clients behave in a similar way: Nimbus also returns 503 from a pre-Gloas head, and the Lighthouse BN returns 500 from a Fulu head because its `get_ptc` needs `ptc_window`. Prysm returns 200 with an empty list, which is the caching problem described above.

## Tests

- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootAtGloasGenesis`: head at slot 0, epochs 0 and 1 return the genesis root. On the old code, epoch 1 returned 404.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootAtEpochOne`: head in epoch 1 at a slot > 0 returns the slot-0 root, equal to `head_v2`.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootMatchesHeadV2`: current and next epoch roots equal `head_v2` and the Beacon API formula.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesDependentRootUnchangedWithinEpoch`: head advancement within an epoch keeps both roots unchanged.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUnavailableBeforeGloasHead`: a populated pre-Gloas head returns 503 for the fork epoch, where the old code returned 200 with predicted duties; a Gloas head then returns 200.

All tests were checked to fail against the pre-fix production code, or against the targeted mutation, for the intended reason.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler ./cl/beacon/beaconevents -count=1`
- `make lint` (two clean passes)
- `make erigon integration`

title: cl: schedule Sepolia's 200M gas limit at Glamsterdam
body:
Schedule Sepolia's default gas-limit target at **200,000,000 from epoch 353024**, implementing [eth-clients/sepolia#130](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/130).

Caplin now reads and exposes `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` and selects the active entry using the proposal epoch. Local payload construction and builder bid selection use the scheduled target, with matching signed proposer preferences taking precedence, including values below or above the schedule. The payload-attributes event at the Gloas boundary also advertises the scheduled target. The actual block gas limit follows the existing gradual adjustment rule.

Empty schedules are serialized as `[]` for validator-client compatibility. Custom config loading normalizes blank or null YAML schedules to an empty slice.

Tests cover empty and populated schedules, omitted, blank, null, and empty-array custom YAML values, the pre-Gloas guard, and proposer precedence. A later-Gloas regression test uses a Gloas base state and checks that the 200M scheduled target overrides a 60M parent bid. TDD was used for the API regression; the test split and comment clarification are refactoring/documentation exceptions.
author: yperbasis

title: cl/beacon/handler: publish blobs from the request on a node that did not produce the block
body:
Fixes #23112.

## Problem

`POST /eth/v{1,2}/beacon/blocks` decodes the block together with its `blobs` and `kzg_proofs`, but the broadcast builds sidecars only from the node's `blobBundles` cache. That cache holds only bundles the node produced itself. A validator client that publishes to several beacon nodes therefore gets 500 `missing blob bundle for commitment …` from every node except the one that built the block. This affects blocks with blobs, both before Fulu (blob sidecars) and from Fulu on (data column sidecars).

## Fix

`postBeaconBlocks` builds the blob bundles for the block with `requestBlobBundles` and passes them to the broadcast, which uses them instead of the cache.

- Cheap checks run before any KZG work. The fork the request is labelled with must match the block's slot. The number of commitments must be within the limit gossip uses (`MaxBlobsPerBlockByVersion`, and from Fulu on `GetBlobParameters(epoch)`). The numbers of blobs and proofs must match the commitments: one proof per blob before Fulu, `CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB` cell proofs per blob from Fulu on.
- A bundle the node already has is taken from the cache, unless its proof count does not fit the block's fork. The remaining bundles come from the request and are KZG-verified. From Fulu on the cells computed for verification are kept on the bundle, so the column build does not compute them again.
- Request data is never written to the cache. The block is validated only later, and a rejected request must not leave data that a later publish would use.
- A request that fails any of these checks gets 400. A request that has blobs but no commitment list gets its own message. A request without blobs, or without a block (for example JSON `"signed_block": null`), behaves as before.
- Gloas is not affected: its blobs travel in the execution payload envelope, not in the block request.

`blobBundleCacheSize` now sizes the cache for two full blocks at the highest blob limit in the schedule (`MaxBlobsPerBlockUpperBound`), with the previous 48 as a minimum. Above 48 blobs a block would evict its own bundles before it is published.

Behaviour changes:
- The producing node now returns 400 for a request whose blob or proof counts do not match the commitments, or whose fork does not match its slot. Before, it ignored the request's blobs. It still does not verify the request's copy of a blob it has cached, so a bad proof for such a blob gets 200 on the producing node and 400 on other nodes. The node publishes its own, correct copy either way.
- The KZG work runs before block validation. Block validation happens inside the broadcast, under the payload-preparation gate, and while the gate is held, speculative payload preparation is skipped. Verifying there would hold the gate about 200 ms longer. The blob limit bounds the cost of a request whose block is then rejected.
- Verification cost on a node that did not produce the block, for 21 blobs on a 16-core machine: about 13 ms for Electra and about 220 ms for Fulu. The Fulu column build then takes about 40 µs, since it reuses the cells.

## Tests

`cl/beacon/handler/block_production_request_blobs_test.go`, with real KZG data:

- Through `PostEthV2BeaconBlocks`, on a node with an empty cache:
  - Electra, SSZ and JSON: the blob sidecar with the request's blob, commitment and proof is published. Before the fix this returns 500 `missing blob bundle`.
  - Fulu: all 128 data columns are published, and each passes `VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofs`.
  - A block that fails validation gets 400. Nothing is published or cached.
  - A Fulu-slot block labelled `electra` gets 400. Nothing is published or cached.
- `requestBlobBundles`:
  - valid Electra and Fulu bundles are returned, with the Fulu cells kept, and nothing is cached
  - a cached bundle is used even when the request carries a bad proof for it
  - a cached bundle with the wrong proof count for the fork is replaced by the verified request copy
  - a fork that does not match the slot is rejected
  - at the edges: the last Electra slot and the first Fulu slot, both ways round, and the blob limit right before and at a blob schedule entry
  - blobs without a commitment list get their own error
  - too many commitments are rejected before verification, both for the Electra limit and for a Fulu blob schedule limit
  - a missing proof or blob is rejected
  - one bad proof rejects the whole request
  - a missing block is left to block validation, with no panic
- `collectPublishedPayloadData` reuses cells kept on a bundle, and `blobBundleCacheSize` follows the blob schedule.

Each behaviour was checked by mutation. Each of the following makes a test fail:
- removing the fork check, the blob limit, the Fulu schedule limit, the nil guard, the count check, or verification
- computing the epoch one slot early or late, `>=` for the limit, or reading the schedule for the previous epoch
- writing request bundles to the cache
- using a cached bundle with the wrong proof count
- ignoring the request bundles in the broadcast
- not keeping or not reusing cells
- one proof per blob on Fulu, a wrong cell index, or verifying only the first cell
- sizing the cache for one block

`go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler/...`, `go build ./...`, `make lint` and `make lintci` pass.

The same code is on release/3.7 and release/3.6, so both need backports.
author: lystopad

title: cl/utils/eth_clock: encode ENR next_fork_epoch as little-endian
body:
`ForkId()` writes `next_fork_epoch` in the ENR `eth2` field with `binary.BigEndian`. The [p2p-interface spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/82b6e507dc31f6f7052e79b16ecfe3778c1b38f6/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#eth2-field) defines the value as an SSZ-encoded `ENRForkID`, and an SSZ `uint64` is [little-endian](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/802485ec74a6986542bd53bf153189623aab440c/ssz/simple-serialize.md#uintn).

The bug does not show while no fork is scheduled, because `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH` (`0xffffffffffffffff`) is the same in both byte orders.

Decoded from the `eth2` field of a live Caplin v3.7.0 (`bdc78cc4`) node on Sepolia:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| fork_digest | `0x74d01459` |
| next_fork_version | `0x90000076` (Gloas, correct) |
| next_fork_epoch bytes | `00 00 00 00 00 05 63 00` |
| expected bytes for epoch 353024 | `00 63 05 00 00 00 00 00` |

A spec-compliant decoder reads the advertised epoch as `27871520252493824`, not `353024`. A crawler of the Sepolia network sees this on all 25 Caplin v3.7.0 nodes that it found. Prysm, Teku, Lodestar, and Nimbus nodes in the same crawl encode the epoch in little-endian order.

Caplin never decodes the `eth2` value of a peer (the only uses of `Eth2key` are the two `node.Set` calls in `cl/p2p/p2p.go`). Thus this PR changes only the encoder. The fork digest does not change, so gossip topics and Status handshakes are not affected.

`TestForkIdNextForkEpochIsLittleEndian` schedules Gloas at epoch `0x0102030405` on a copy of the Chiado config and checks the exact bytes. Before the change, it fails with `actual: 00 00 00 01 02 03 04 05`. The existing `TestForkIdNextForkVersionWithoutScheduledFork` now also decodes in little-endian order. It checks only `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`, so it could not find this bug.
author: MysticRyuujin

title: cl/utils/eth_clock: keep ENR next_fork_version at a BPO fork
body:
`ForkId()` takes `next_fork_version` from the next *regular* fork. `next_fork_epoch` comes from `NextForkEpochIncludeBPO()`, which also counts BPO forks. When a BPO fork is scheduled before the next regular fork, the two halves of the `eth2` value describe different forks: the version of the regular fork and the epoch of the BPO fork.

The [Fulu p2p spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/82b6e507dc31f6f7052e79b16ecfe3778c1b38f6/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#eth2-field) says:

> `next_fork_version` is the fork version corresponding to the next planned fork at a future epoch. The fork version will only change for regular forks, _not BPO forks_. Note that it is possible for the blob schedule to define a change at the same epoch as a regular fork; this situation would be considered a regular fork. If no future fork is planned, set `next_fork_version = current_fork_version` to signal this fact.

This PR sets `next_fork_version` to the version in effect at `next_fork_epoch`. If no fork is scheduled, it is the current version. Nimbus uses the same rule (`forkVersionAtEpoch(nextForkEpochAtEpoch(epoch))`).

Example: the current fork is Fulu, with a BPO fork at epoch A and Gloas at epoch B > A.

| | next_fork_version | next_fork_epoch |
|---|---|---|
| before | Gloas | A |
| after | Fulu | A |

`ForkId()` now derives all three fields from one epoch sample. Before, it sampled the epoch three times, so an epoch boundary between samples could give a mismatched triple that `updateENR` only repairs at the next fork.

### Why this matters for peering

Prysm's discv5 dial filter (`compareForkENR` in `beacon-chain/p2p/fork.go`, called from `filterPeer`, since OffchainLabs/prysm#15604) handles a peer whose current fork digest matches as follows:

- If `next_fork_epoch` differs, it allows the dial.
- If `next_fork_epoch` matches and is not `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`, it rejects the peer when `next_fork_version` differs.

Prysm gives BPO entries the version of the last regular fork. While the epoch was big-endian, Caplin's epoch never matched while a fork was scheduled, so Prysm always took the first branch. After #24405, the epochs match, and Prysm reaches the version comparison. In the window described above, Prysm would then not dial Caplin nodes that it finds through discovery. So #24405 makes this change necessary before the next network schedules a BPO fork before a regular fork.

<details><summary>Client survey (default branches, 2026-09-29)</summary>

`next_fork_version` when a BPO fork is scheduled before the next regular fork:

| client | next_fork_version | next_fork_epoch |
|---|---|---|
| Prysm | current | BPO |
| Lodestar | current | BPO |
| Nimbus | current | BPO |
| Lighthouse | next regular fork | BPO |
| Teku | next regular fork | BPO |
| Grandine | next regular fork | next regular fork |
| Caplin (before) | next regular fork | BPO |
| Caplin (after) | current | BPO |

Lighthouse and Teku have the same behavior as Caplin had before this PR. The clients disagree, so the spec could state this rule more explicitly (ethereum/consensus-specs#5701). This PR follows the spec text as it is written now.
</details>

No public network is in this state today. On mainnet and Hoodi, no regular fork is scheduled after their BPOs. On Sepolia, both BPO forks are in the past and only Gloas (epoch 353024) is ahead.

`TestForkIdNextForkVersionWithBPO` covers four cases: a BPO before Gloas, a BPO at the same epoch as Gloas, Gloas before a BPO, and a BPO with no Gloas scheduled. It checks the encoded version and epoch bytes. Before this change, only "bpo before gloas" fails (`expected: 0x0600006f, actual: 0x0700006f`). The test sets genesis relative to `time.Now()` and uses its own blob schedule, so it does not depend on the date or on Chiado's live schedule.

When two regular forks share one future epoch, `next_fork_version` is now the later fork (before: the earlier one). This is `compute_fork_version(next_fork_epoch)`, the version from which peers compute the digest at that epoch. `TestForkIdNextForkVersionWithForksAtSameEpoch` covers it and fails before this change. Only devnet or custom configs can reach this state.
author: MysticRyuujin

title: cl/clparams, cl/spectest: set PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS to 5000 and check mainnet config against spec fixtures
body:
## Summary

consensus-specs [#5414](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5414) (released in v1.7.0-alpha.12) changed `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS` from 7500 to 5000, which moves the payload deadline to 50% of the slot. Caplin still uses 7500.

Caplin uses this value in three places:
- the PTC `payload_present` deadline in `GET /eth/v1/validator/payload_attestation_data`;
- the builder handoff deadline;
- the dev validator's envelope deadline.

With 7500, Caplin reports envelopes first seen between 6 s and 9 s into the slot as present. Spec-compliant clients report them as absent. Sepolia activates Gloas at epoch 353024 (2026-10-06 13:53 UTC), so this also needs a backport to `release/3.7`.

## Why the spec tests did not catch it

The CL fixtures are pinned at v1.7.0-beta.2, which already has the new value. The spectest harness overlays each fixture's `config.yaml` onto Erigon's config, so the cases never see Caplin's built-in defaults. No state-transition case depends on this value.

## Changes

- `cl/clparams/config.go`: `PayloadDueBps` 7500 -> 5000.
- `cl/spectest/mainnet_config_test.go`: a new subtest, `Test/mainnet_config`.
  - It builds the spec mainnet config from the pinned fixtures. Per key it takes the value most `config.yaml` files agree on, ignores `*_FORK_EPOCH`, and fails on a tie.
  - It compares that config with `MainnetBeaconConfig` and the mainnet `NetworkConfig`.
  - Spec keys without a Caplin config field must be listed explicitly: `hardcoded` (Caplin's value is compared) or `notCompared`. Any other key fails, so a new spec key needs an explicit decision.
  - It runs inside the existing `Test`, so it has the same `ERIGON_SKIP_CL_SPECTEST` gate and CI's `-run=/mainnet/` selects it.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs_test.go`: the payload attestation deadline test now uses the default config (6 s boundary). It also has one case with a non-default `PayloadDueBps`, to check that the endpoint reads the configured value.

`MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` is excluded from the comparison: Caplin uses 15 MiB, the spec 10 MiB. This is tracked in #24417.

## Testing

- **TDD:** before the fix, the new subtest failed with `PAYLOAD_DUE_BPS: Erigon 7500, spec 5000`. The handler test fails with 7500, and also with 5000 hardcoded in `epbs.go`.
- **Mutation checks:** each of these makes the subtest fail:

author: domiwei

title: cl/p2p, cmd: add a QUIC disable switch and default the QUIC port to 4002
body:
Follow-up to #24117.

## Summary

- Add `--caplin.quic.disable` and `--sentinel.quic.disable`. When set:
  - the QUIC transport is never registered with libp2p, so no UDP socket opens at all; the endpoint is not just hidden from the ENR
  - the discv5/QUIC port-conflict check and the bind validation in `NewP2Pmanager` skip QUIC
  - the ENR carries no `quic` or `quic6` entry
- Default `--caplin.discovery.quicport` and `--sentinel.quic.port` to `4002` instead of `4001`. This matches the usual convention: Lighthouse, Lodestar, Teku, Nimbus and Grandine all default QUIC to the TCP port plus one. It also avoids a UDP port collision with discv5 under the upstream `ethereum-package` Caplin launcher, which starts Caplin with `--sentinel.tcp.port=4001 --discovery.port=4001`.
- Update the docs and docker-compose examples for the new port default and the disable switch, and regenerate the `llms-full.txt` artifacts.

## Why

Review on #24117 noted that the other major CL clients ship a TCP-only switch (Lighthouse `--disable-quic`, Lodestar `--quic=false`, Grandine `--disable-quic-support`) and Caplin had none: "operators who can't open a UDP port have no way out."

This matters for Docker and Kubernetes deployments. Exposing an extra UDP port is often harder than TCP: Services need an explicit `protocol: UDP`, some managed ingress and load-balancer setups don't forward UDP at all, and network policies can be stricter. Without a disable switch, the ENR keeps advertising a `quic` endpoint that such operators can never make reachable. The switch only helps when the QUIC port specifically can't be opened: discv5 still needs its UDP port (`4000`), and the docs say so.

## Connection deduplication: removed, moved to #24538

Earlier iterations of this PR also tried to deduplicate TCP and QUIC connections to the same peer in the connection gater. go-libp2p does not deduplicate across transports, so two peers that dial each other at about the same time can keep two connections. Review showed that every gater-based approach tried here was worse than keeping the duplicate:

- closing the "newer" or the non-QUIC connection can pick different survivors on the two sides, and races `cl/sentinel`'s handshake-failure and ban paths
- rejecting any new connection while one exists leaves zero connections when two gated nodes dial each other at once, and a dead connection blocks reconnection

So this PR no longer changes the gater: `InterceptSecured` allows every connection, as on `main`, and duplicates behave as before this PR. A deterministic dedup that both sides agree on is tracked in #24538. Taking it out also lets the switch and the 4002 default go into 3.7.1 together with the QUIC backport (#24413), so 3.7.1 does not ship QUIC on 4001.

## Testing

- `go test -race ./cl/p2p/... ./cl/sentinel/... ./cmd/caplin/... ./cmd/sentinel/... ./cmd/utils/...`: all pass
- `go build ./...` and `make lint`: clean
- Docs: `npm run build` in `docs/site` (Node 20), then `python3 docs/site/scripts/generate-llms.py --check` and `python3 -m unittest discover docs/site/scripts` (Python 3.11): all pass
- Earlier on this branch: `make erigon integration`, and checked by hand that `--caplin.quic.disable`, `--sentinel.quic.disable` and the new `4002` default show up in `--help` for both the `erigon` and `caplin` binaries

## Scope note

Bounded per-source-IP limiting of connection attempts came up while discussing this PR, but it is out of scope here. It is a separate problem (admission control before the handshake, not deduplication by peer identity), tracked in #24449 (#24448).
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon/handler: don't let a stalled /eth/v1/events client block the event emitters
body:
The `/eth/v1/events` handler writes to the socket on the same goroutine that drains its subscription channel (capacity 128). The emitters use the blocking `feed.Send`, which waits for every subscriber, and the beacon API write timeout defaults to a year. So one SSE client that stops reading fills the channel and then blocks `SendAttestation` (called from the batch signature verifier), `SendBlock` (block import) and `SendChainReorg` for as long as the connection stays open.

Writes now go through a per-connection writer goroutine with a queue limited to 1024 messages and 64 MiB. The handler only enqueues; if either limit is exceeded the stream is closed and both subscriptions are dropped, so emitters never wait on a client's socket. The writer stops at the next message boundary and the in-flight write is aborted with a past write deadline, so a slow client that keeps reading is cut immediately instead of being drained. `Send` keeps its blocking semantics for everything else (`TestFinalizedCheckpointEmittedOutsideLock` still relies on that).

The writer arms a 30s write deadline before each write and clears it after the flush, and stops on the first error. Without that, the teardown after an overflow would wait on a write stuck on the stalled socket until the server `WriteTimeout` (one year by default).

Behaviour change: a client that falls behind is now dropped; before, it was never dropped. The teardown aborts the in-flight write, so the chunked response ends without the terminating chunk: the client gets `unexpected EOF` and the last event can be cut in the middle, which a compliant SSE parser drops. 1024 messages and 64 MiB are budgets, not tuned values: the byte limit keeps a few slow clients from holding gigabytes of encoded `data_column_sidecar`/`blob_sidecar` events, and still fits a full per-block burst of column sidecars. For high-rate topics the queue, not the 30s deadline, decides when a client is dropped (a full stall overflows 1024 messages above roughly 34 events/s).

The 30s per-write deadline replaces `--beacon.api.write.timeout` (`a.routerCfg.WriteTimeout`, the value `router.go` passes to `http.Server.WriteTimeout`) for this endpoint, so a configured value below 30s no longer applies to the event stream.

Testing:

```
go test -count=3 -run 'TestEventStream|TestWriteEventStream' ./cl/beacon/handler/
go test -race -run 'TestEventStream|TestFinalizedCheckpointEmittedOutsideLock' ./cl/beacon/handler/ ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/
go test -short ./cl/beacon/...
```

Without the change `TestEventStreamSlowClientDoesNotBlockEmitters` fails with "a stalled event stream client blocked the event emitter", and without the write deadline `TestEventStreamOverflowClosesStalledStream` fails because the handler never returns.

Closes #24526.

author: yperbasis

title: cl: follow the spec's gossip slot window for current and future slots
body:
Fixes #24360.

## Problem

`EthereumClock.IsSlotCurrentSlotWithMaximumClockDisparity` is the gossip slot-window check for sync-committee messages, sync contributions, blocks, blob sidecars, data column sidecars and pending payload envelopes. It had three defects.

1. **Overflow.** It computed `genesis + SECONDS_PER_SLOT * slot` without bounds. With 12-second slots that product repeats every 2^62 slots, so `current_slot + k·2^62` (k = 1, 2, 3) mapped to the current slot and passed the check. The sync-committee message signature does not cover the slot, so a replayed message with such a slot passed the `[IGNORE]` check, entered the pool and was forwarded.
2. **Wrong window.** It applied `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` around the message slot's start instead of around the current time. In slot N it therefore:
   - accepted messages for slot N+1 during the whole slot, not only in its last 500 ms
   - rejected messages for slot N-1 in the first 500 ms of slot N, which the spec allows

   The spec's `is_current_slot` is `[start(slot) - D, start(slot + 1) + D]` around the current time. Lighthouse checks the same `now ± D` range.
3. **Late blocks were ignored.** The block gossip check compared the block slot with the head slot, not the wall-clock slot. When a block for slot N-1 arrived more than 500 ms into slot N, and the head was still at N-2, the block was ignored as "from a future slot". It was not scheduled or forwarded, so the node attested to the older head. The spec's rule is `is_future_slot`, which compares with the current time only.

## Fix

- `IsSlotCurrentSlotWithMaximumClockDisparity` now implements `is_current_slot`, inclusive at both ends. It first rejects any slot that is not the current slot or one of its neighbours. The disparity is shorter than a slot, so no other slot can qualify, and the time arithmetic then only runs for slots near the present and cannot overflow. The clock is read once per check.
- `blockService.validateGossip` compares with `ethClock.GetCurrentSlot()`. The ignore message now gives the block slot first: `block is from a future slot: <slot> > <current>`.
- Late blocks now reach the proposer signature check before the unknown-parent check, and the head state can predate the proposer (for example right after the forward-sync handoff). Then `ValidatorForValidatorIndex` fails with `ErrInvalidValidatorIndex`, which rejected the block and banned the sender. Only the parent's state is sure to know the proposer, so while the parent is unknown, `validateGossip` returns `ErrIgnore` and does not schedule the unverified block. With a known parent, and for any other signature error such as a malformed signature, the block is still rejected.
- `verifySyncCommitteeMessageSignature` and `verifySyncContributionProofAggregatedSignature` take the signing domain from the epoch of the message slot, as the spec does, not from the head state's epoch. Because previous-slot messages are now accepted for 500 ms, the head state can already be in a new fork while the message slot is still in the old one. The old code then failed the signature check and banned the peer that sent the message.
- No other caller changes. The sidecar and payload-envelope callers only reach the check for a slot ahead of the wall-clock slot, and for such a slot the fixed predicate is `!is_future_slot`.

Behaviour changes, all towards the spec:
- Messages and sidecars for the next slot are now ignored until 500 ms before that slot starts. Before, they were accepted and forwarded during the whole of the previous slot. Spec-following peers already ignore them, and an ignore does not lower peer score. A node whose clock is more than 500 ms behind the network now ignores such early blocks and sidecars instead of queuing them.
- Sync-committee messages and contributions for the previous slot are accepted for 500 ms after it ends.
- Late blocks for a past slot are no longer ignored when the head is behind them.
- A pending execution payload envelope for the next slot is retried only within 500 ms before that slot starts.

The node's own publishing is unaffected. Sync-committee messages go out about 4 s into the slot and contributions about 8 s in, and blocks and sidecars after the slot starts.

`GetSlotTime` and `GetSlotByTime` keep their unchecked arithmetic. No gossip-supplied slot reaches them unbounded: most callers take slots from the node's own state, the sync-committee publish path is already bounded, and the payload-attestation check (`isPayloadAttestationSlotCurrent`) bounds its gossip slot itself. The one unbounded input is the validator client's `until_epoch` in the subnet subscription endpoint, where an overflow can only produce a wrong subscription expiry.

## Tests

- `cl/utils/eth_clock/current_slot_window_test.go`, with an injected current time:
  - the window at millisecond edges: the next slot exactly one disparity before it starts, and 1 ms earlier; the previous slot exactly one disparity after it ends, and 1 ms later; slots two ahead and two behind
  - the slots `current + k·2^62` and `MaxUint64` are rejected
  - slot 0 at genesis
- `TestSyncCommitteesIgnoresForgedSlotThatAliasesToNow`: through the real sync-committee service and the real clock, a message for `current + 2^62` is ignored before any signature verification.
- `TestBlockServiceDoesNotIgnoreLateBlockAsFuture`: with the head behind and the wall clock past the block's slot, the block passes the slot check and reaches the signature check (`ErrInvalidSignature`). Before the fix it was ignored as a block from a future slot.
- `TestBlockServiceIgnoresUnknownProposerWhileParentIsUnknown`, `TestBlockServiceRejectsUnknownProposerWhenParentIsKnown` and `TestBlockServiceRejectsMalformedSignatureWhileParentIsUnknown`: a late block whose proposer is past the head state's registry is ignored and not scheduled while its parent is unknown, and rejected once the parent is known; a malformed signature is rejected either way. The first failed before the fix with `invalid validator index`.
- `TestVerifySyncCommitteeMessageSignatureUsesMessageSlotDomain` and `TestVerifySyncContributionAggregatedSignatureUsesContributionSlotDomain`: with the head state at the first slot of a new fork, a message for the previous slot is verified with the previous fork version. Before the fix the signing root did not match.

Each was checked by mutation, and each of these mutations fails a test:
- restoring the old implementation
- removing the neighbour bound
- dropping the disparity at either end
- a strict comparison at either end
- excluding the previous slot from the bound
- comparing the block with the head slot again

`go test -race ./cl/...`, the CL spec tests with `-tags=spectest` (including 272 fork-choice tests), `go build ./...`, `make lint` and `make lintci` pass.

After the second commit, `make lint`, `make erigon integration` and the tests of `cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/utils/eth_clock` and `cl/beacon/handler` pass.

After the review follow-up (merge of main, bcd19c9a3a, 0a2385c805), `make lint`, `make erigon integration` and `go test -race` for `cl/utils/eth_clock/...`, `cl/phase1/network/...`, `cl/beacon/handler/...` and `cl/phase1/stages/...` pass. Each of these mutations of the late-block fix fails a test: no ignore path, ignoring with a known parent, scheduling the unverified block, and ignoring any signature error while the parent is unknown.

The fork-domain case where the head lags behind a new fork is pre-existing and tracked in #24689.
author: lystopad

title: cl: use the Fulu inclusion proof depth for data column sidecars
body:
## Summary

When Caplin publishes a Fulu block with blobs, `broadcastBlockWithIntegrationWaitAndPublication` builds the data column sidecars. This helper builds the sidecars of the full blocks Caplin publishes for its validators; Fulu blinded blocks are published by the relay, not by Caplin. It creates the `kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof` vector with `cltypes.CommitmentBranchSize` (17, the Deneb `BlobSidecar` depth) instead of `cltypes.KzgCommitmentsInclusionProofDepth` (4, `KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH` in the Fulu spec). The first 4 hashes are the real proof, the other 13 are zero.

`DataColumnSidecar` encodes this field as a fixed vector of whatever length it holds, so the SSZ fixed part is 772 bytes instead of 356. Spec-conformant decoders reject it. The same sidecars are gossiped and written to storage, and the req/resp handlers serve the stored bytes.

On a local Kurtosis devnet (Lighthouse v8.3.0-rc.0, Teku 26.9.1, Caplin v3.7.1):
- Lighthouse logged `Could not decode gossipsub message ... OffsetSkipsVariableBytes(772)` on all 128 `data_column_sidecar_N` topics for the first Caplin block with blobs.
- A Lighthouse `data_columns_by_root` request to a Caplin peer failed with `SSZDecodeError(OffsetSkipsVariableBytes(772))`. Lighthouse treats this as a fatal peer action and banned the Caplin node.

With this change, in the same setup Lighthouse logged no `OffsetSkipsVariableBytes` errors and verified the columns of Caplin's blocks, and Lighthouse and both Caplin nodes had the same block roots for slots 60-75, across the Gloas fork at slot 64.

Caplin's own decoder reads the first 4 hashes and does not check the first offset, so Caplin peers accept these sidecars. The existing test decodes with Caplin and passed before this change.

Scope: Fulu blocks with blobs published by Caplin. Gloas sidecars have no inclusion proof and use another code path. The columns of blocks a node published before upgrading are also stored with the 17-hash proof (received columns are decoded with the 4-hash proof and stored that way), and req/resp served the stored bytes as they are. The second and third commits fix this: when serving a stored pre-Gloas column, `WriteStream` reads only the length prefix of the file, and only if the declared SSZ length matches the 17-hash layout it decodes the sidecar (Caplin's decoder reads the first 4 hashes) and encodes it again. Other pre-Gloas files are copied raw after that prefix read, and Gloas files are copied raw without it, as before. So an upgraded node stops sending undecodable sidecars right away instead of after they are pruned, without decoding the columns that are already canonical. The vector size comes from #16083 (2025-07). `release/3.7` has the same code.

## Changes

- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go`: size the Fulu inclusion proof vector with `KzgCommitmentsInclusionProofDepth`.
- `cl/beacon/handler/block_production_request_blobs_test.go`: `TestPostEthV2BeaconBlocksPublishesRequestColumnsOnNonProducingNode` now also checks that each published column is the canonical SSZ encoding (decode, re-encode, compare the bytes).
- `cl/persistence/blob_storage/data_column_db.go`: `WriteStream` re-encodes a stored pre-Gloas file whose length matches the 17-hash layout and copies every other file raw. It reads the uncompressed SSZ length from the prefix: the fixed part of a Fulu `DataColumnSidecar` is 356 bytes with the 4-hash proof and 772 with the 17-hash one, and each blob adds 2144 bytes (a cell, a commitment and a proof), so for a valid sidecar `length % 2144 == 772` holds for the 17-hash layout and never for the canonical one, for any number of blobs.
- `cl/persistence/blob_storage/data_column_db_test.go`: `TestWriteStreamServesLegacyInclusionProofCanonically` (a column stored with the 17-hash proof is served with the 4-hash proof) and `TestWriteStreamServesCanonicalFileVerbatim` (a canonical file with one junk byte appended is served byte for byte, so it is not decoded).

## Testing

- **TDD:** before the fix, the extended test failed on the canonical-encoding check (`column N must use the spec SSZ layout`).
- **TDD:** `TestWriteStreamServesLegacyInclusionProofCanonically` failed before the second commit.
- **TDD:** `TestWriteStreamServesCanonicalFileVerbatim` failed before the third commit (the re-encode dropped the junk byte).
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
- `go test ./cl/persistence/... ./cl/sentinel/... ./cl/beacon/handler/...`

title: cl/phase1/network/services: read same-epoch parent state in place for gossip block validation
body:
Fixes #24522

## Problem

`computeBlockValidationContext` copied the full parent beacon state and ran `ProcessSlots` on it for every gossip block. It only needs three values from that state: the expected proposer, the latest block hash and the latest bid. On mainnet this adds ~0.4s per block before the block can become head. That is enough to push about 11% of slots past the 4s sync committee and attestation deadline. Measurements are in the issue.

## Change

Epoch processing and fork upgrades run only at epoch boundaries. So advancing the parent state to a slot in its own epoch cannot change any of the values read here. In that case (31 of 32 blocks), the context is now read from the parent state in place via `ViewStateAtBlockRoot`. Blocks that cross an epoch boundary keep the copy + `ProcessSlots` path, so fork upgrades (including the Gloas upgrade that rewrites the latest bid and block hash) stay handled.

The rule does not depend on fork-specific dependent roots, so it works on every network and fork. Prysm, Teku and Lodestar use the same approach.

## Tests

- New `TestBlockValidationContextReadsSameEpochParentStateWithoutCopy` failed before the fix: it requested a copied parent state.
- New `TestBlockValidationContextAdvancesCopiedParentStateAcrossEpoch` guards the epoch-crossing path. It also passes without the fix, as expected for a guard.
- In `TestBlockServiceGossipRejectsUnexpectedProposer` and `TestBlockServiceUnrelatedReservationDoesNotRevalidateP2P`, the stubs required copied parent-state reads. They now also serve read-only views. Their real assertions are unchanged: one shared parent-state read under concurrency, and a single validation call.

`go test ./cl/phase1/network/services/` passes, and `make lint` reports 0 issues (2 runs).

The backport to `release/3.7` will follow after merge.

author: yperbasis

title: cl/phase1/network/services: verify gossip signatures with the message epoch's fork version
body:
## Summary

Around a fork, Caplin verified gossip and pool signatures with the wrong fork version and rejected valid messages.

- **Proposer preferences.** Preferences for the first Gloas epoch are signed in the last Fulu epoch with `compute_fork_version(proposal_epoch)`. Caplin took the domain from the dependent state, which is still Fulu, and rejected every preference for the fork epoch (`invalid proposer preferences signature`), from its own VC and from gossip.
- **Other gossip messages.** Attestations, aggregates, sync committee messages and contributions, and data column sidecar proposer signatures took the domain from the head state's fork. When the first slot of a fork has no block, the head state is still the old fork's, so attestations, sync committee messages and contributions signed for the new fork failed with `invalid bls signature` until the next block. Aggregates of that slot are still ignored earlier, by the epoch range check, until a block of the new epoch is seen; that check is unchanged. The aggregate selection proof and aggregator signature always used the head state's current fork version, so aggregates from the last epoch of the old fork that arrived after the head crossed the fork were rejected; they now verify. Data column sidecars of the first block of a new fork are checked against the pre-fork head state, so they fail even when no slot is skipped (the devnet below starts in Fulu, so it did not exercise the sidecar fixes). With slot 64 skipped, each Caplin node rejected about 130 valid messages from its own VC for that slot (128 sync committee messages and the slot's attestations). The blob sidecar proposer signature had a related bug: it took the fork of the parent block's slot instead of the sidecar's.

The fix adds `fork.ComputeDomainAtEpoch`, which uses the fork version the config schedules for an epoch, and calls it with each message's own epoch. This matches what honest validators sign (the validator spec signs with the head state processed through empty slots up to the duty) and how Lighthouse verifies these messages (`fork_at_epoch`). It also fixes two epoch arguments that were not epochs: the aggregate selection proof used `slot * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH`, and the aggregator signature used the state's slot.

Proposer and attester slashings are unchanged: they must stay valid when included in a block, whose processing takes the fork from the state, and they can carry evidence from older forks.

## Changes

- `cl/fork/fork.go`: `ComputeDomainAtEpoch`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: attestation, aggregate and proof, sync committee message, sync contribution, blob sidecar, data column sidecar and proposer preferences validation use the message epoch's fork version.
- `cl/phase1/network/services` tests: removes `TestVerifySyncCommitteeMessageSignatureUsesMessageSlotDomain` and `TestVerifySyncContributionAggregatedSignatureUsesContributionSlotDomain` (from #24489), which expected the domain from the state's fork field. `TestGossipSignatureDomainsUseMessageEpochForkVersion` now preserves their `"previous epoch"` regression case: the head is at the first slot of the new fork and the message is from the previous fork’s last slot.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs_test.go`: the proposer preferences boundary test signs with the spec domain.

## Testing

- **TDD:** each new test failed before the change: `TestGossipSignatureDomainsUseMessageEpochForkVersion` (sync committee messages, sync contributions and aggregates, at the first slot of the new fork with the head still in the old fork, and at the last slot of the old fork with the head already in the new one), `TestAttestationSignatureDomainUsesTargetEpochForkVersion`, `TestDataColumnSidecarProposerSignatureUsesHeaderEpochForkVersion`, `TestBlobSidecarProposerSignatureUsesHeaderEpochForkVersion`, `TestProposerPreferencesServiceSignatureDomainUsesProposalEpochForkVersion`.
