Each request publishes on one digest, not on both: in the epoch before a later digest change, Prysm, Lighthouse and Caplin stay subscribed to the current digest, and a node that accepts both copies ignores the later one.
- Publish errors are reported as in `pool.go`: a `ComputeForkDigest` error returns 500, a publish error adds a failure entry for that index (400), and an identical retry of a stored preference is published again instead of being acknowledged without a publish, so a retry after a failed publish gets another publish attempt (publishing a message again on the same topic is a no-op in libp2p while its ID is in the delivered-message cache).

## Not changed here

- `execution_payload_bid`, `execution_payload` and `payload_attestation_message` still ignore messages before the fork. The spec's pre-fork note covers only `proposer_preferences`, and the Altair fork transition rules allow ignoring messages on post-fork topics before the fork. A bid for the first Gloas slot sent during the last Fulu slot is still ignored. Passing the topic's version to the gossip conditions would change this, but also the boundary behaviour of the other version-gated topics, so it is left for a separate change.
- The fork-check goroutine still assumes, as on `main`, that service registration finishes before its first tick, one slot after the gossip manager starts, and the registration-time call runs concurrently with it. A copy made between adding a topic and subscribing it is now subscribed on the next tick by the existing-target repair. Starting the loop only after registration is left for a separate change.
- The old fork digest's topics are still removed 16 slots after the regular switch, about 8 slots after the fork; the Altair transition rules recommend two epochs.
- The no-service fallback of `postProposerPreferences` (not used by `run.go`) still acknowledges an identical retry without publishing it.
- Overlap with #24776: both PRs change the `proposer_preferences` registration line in `cl/phase1/network/registry/register.go` (this PR removes the version condition, #24776 replaces the rate limiter), so the second one to merge gets a one-line conflict. The resolution keeps both changes: `waitReady, proposerPreferencesRateLimiter()`. The registry test of this PR is in its own file.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/registry/register.go`: no version condition for `proposer_preferences`.
- `cl/phase1/network/registry/register_gloas_boundary_test.go`: new test.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: new `subscribeUpcomingProposerPreferences`, called on every fork-check tick and after each service registration; name filter, existing-target repair and removed-source skip in `subscribeUpcomingTopics`.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: `Get` returns a copy of the entry.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager_test.go`, `gossip_subscription_test.go`: four new tests.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs.go`: publish preferences with `PublishToForkDigest`, report publish errors, publish identical retries.
- `cl/beacon/handler/epbs_test.go`: one new test; three tests changed.

## Testing

- **TDD:** each test fails with its production change reverted and passes with it:
  - `TestRegisterGossipServicesProcessesGloasPreferencesOneEpochEarly` (current epoch G-1, current digest Fulu, next epoch's digest Gloas; one case publishes on the Fulu topic created at registration, one on the Gloas topic joined at registration, both through the validator because the test's host is nil): with `register.go` from `main` both cases fail with `validation ignored`; with the earlier topic-version condition the Fulu case does; without the join after registration the Gloas case fails with `topic not found`.
  - `TestGossipManagerSubscribesProposerPreferencesOneEpochEarly`: calls `subscribeUpcomingProposerPreferences` at slot 32G-35 (not joined) and 32G-34 (joined and subscribed; `beacon_block` not joined); with one slot instead of two, the topic is not joined at 32G-34.
  - `TestRegisterGossipServiceSubscribesProposerPreferencesForNextEpochImmediately` (registration in the last slot of G-1, with a BPO digest change at G+1): without the call after registration both topics are missing; joining only the digest one epoch and two slots ahead misses the G topic, and publishing on the G digest fails with `topic not found`.
  - `TestSubscribeUpcomingTopicsSubscribesExistingTargetAndContinues` (one target added but not subscribed): without the skip, `topic already exists`; without the repair, the target stays unsubscribed.
  - `TestTopicSubscriptionsGetReturnsSnapshot`: with `Get` returning the stored entry, a later change of the entry's expiry is visible to the caller.
  - `TestPostProposerPreferencesPublishResultsAndDigest`: a publish error returns 400 with a failure entry for that index and a `ComputeForkDigest` error 500 (both 200 before); with the current epoch at Gloas and a different digest for the next epoch, the preference is published on the current digest (the proposal epoch's before).
  - `TestPostProposerPreferencesAcknowledgesOnlyIdenticalRetries`: with the service, the identical retry is published again (no publish before).
  - `TestPostValidatorProposerPreferencesGloasForkBoundary` (real clock in G-1) and `TestPostProposerPreferencesWithoutServiceConcurrentRequests`: with the `Publish` call from `main`, unexpected `Publish` and missing `PublishToForkDigest`; with `PublishToForkDigest` on the current digest, the fork boundary test fails on the digest (Fulu instead of Gloas).
- The nil check for a source topic removed after the topic list was taken has no test: it needs the delayed cleanup to run between the two lookups.
- A probe on `main` with a remote gossipsub peer and the mocked current epoch at G-1 showed that a message on a topic registered with `withBeginVersion(clparams.GloasVersion)` never reaches `ProcessMessage`; with the current epoch at G it does.
- `go test -p 2 ./cl/phase1/network/registry/ ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/... ./cl/beacon/handler/`; `-race` on the registry and gossip packages; `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.
- Not run on a devnet across a Gloas fork.
author: domiwei

title: cl: pack locally aggregated attestations into proposed blocks
body:
Part of #24554 (point 1, partially: local aggregates become candidates; topping up partially overlapping aggregates is still open).

## Problem

Block production packs only gossip aggregates from the operations pool. A node also receives and verifies single attestations on its subscribed subnets, but it aggregates them only for committees with a local aggregator, and block production never reads the aggregation pool. Votes that the node has already verified are therefore missing from its own blocks.

## Change

- **`cl/aggregation`**: verified attestations are kept in bounded per-committee aggregates. Per-committee aggregates move from an LRU (100k entries, 30 min TTL, `Get` and `Add` without a lock) to a map under `aggregatesLock`, which also fixes lost votes when attestations of the same committee arrive concurrently. `Aggregates()` returns the current per-committee aggregates; the pool replaces an aggregate instead of changing it. They are pruned to the current and previous epoch, the window in which an attestation stays includable since Deneb. The map is bounded: at most 4 distinct `AttestationData` per (slot, committee) and two epochs' worth in total (16,384 on mainnet), returning `ErrPoolLimit`. A full committee keeps the votes of other data aside (at most 4 data, as aggregates, so a vote counts once per voter). New data enters this set unless every data in it is pinned: when it is full, one of the unpinned set data with the fewest voters gives way, picked at random, so a stream of fresh one-vote data cannot target one of several equally weak data. Such data replaces the committee's weakest data, with all its votes, once it has more voters, and the displaced data keeps its votes the same way. In a committee without a local aggregator, this is best effort for data the node did not serve: attesters who vote early for several data, or who keep one data the only weakest in the set, can keep it out of the store or flush its votes. Two cases are protected: the data the node serves its validators is pinned, and committees with a local aggregator keep the votes of every data (next points). A full pool prunes stale entries before refusing.
- **Pinned data**: `GET /eth/v1/validator/attestation_data` pins the data it serves in the pool (`PinAttestationData`). Our validators sign exactly this data and our aggregators ask for its aggregate. Once it is stored, gossip votes for other data cannot displace it: in a full committee it takes the place of the weakest unpinned data, and votes refused before the pin move into the store when the committee stores unpinned data it can replace. A vote that arrived before the pin waits with the refused data as unpinned data, and can be evicted there before the pin. When a committee stores only pinned data, more pinned data waits with the refused data, so the committee bound holds; refused-set eviction never picks pinned data, and when every refused data is pinned too, new data is refused with `ErrPoolLimit`. Gossip cannot influence which data is pinned. Pins are made from Electra on, where the pool uses them, and are pruned with the inclusion window.
- **`cl/utils/bls`**: `SignatureAggregator` keeps the running aggregate uncompressed. Adding an already verified signature decompresses only that signature instead of decompressing and group-checking both and recompressing.
- **Aggregator duties**: an aggregator's attestation data may come from another beacon node (a VC with several beacon nodes, or a distributed validator), so pinning does not cover it. A `beacon_committee_subscriptions` request with `is_aggregator` registers the duty in the pool (`AddAggregatorDuty`), for slots from the previous epoch to the next and committee indices below `MAX_COMMITTEES_PER_SLOT`. For such a (slot, committee) the refused data are bounded by `MAX_VALIDATORS_PER_COMMITTEE` instead of 4. An honest validator votes once per epoch, so every data that got an honest vote keeps it, as with the LRU on `main`. Nothing enforces one vote per validator and target epoch yet: a validator that equivocates (which is slashable) can add more data, up to that bound. Block production still sees at most 4 data per committee; the aggregate endpoint serves the rest. Duties are pruned with the inclusion window.
- **`cl/validator/committee_subscription`**: the per-committee aggregator tracking (`validatorSubs`, `NeedToAggregate` and its sweep) no longer gates anything and is removed, together with `AggregateAttestation` and the constructor parameters it used. The subscription passes `is_aggregator` to the pool instead. The attestation service takes the aggregation pool directly.
- **`cl/phase1/network/services`**: when a vote is verified, (validator, target epoch) is claimed with a check-and-set under one lock, so copies that passed the seen check concurrently (for example over REST and gossip) reach the pool and the event stream once. The winner adds every verified attestation to the pool and emits the attestation event even when the pool already holds the vote (`ErrIsSuperset`) or refuses it.
- **`cl/beacon/handler`**: Electra block production takes candidates from the operations pool and from `Aggregates()`, and drops candidates whose source is not the justified checkpoint for their target epoch before any per-candidate work (also in the Deneb path). When grouping candidates, a candidate replaces the ones whose bits it covers, so a local aggregate that covers a gossip aggregate does not add another layer. The timing log reports the local aggregates next to `poolSize`. The existing merge step only merges non-overlapping bitlists and works on copies, so overlapping gossip and local aggregates cannot produce an invalid signature; the selection from #24566 picks the best combination.

Local aggregators also benefit: `GET /eth/v2/validator/aggregate_attestation` now returns the committee's aggregate of the requested data, also while a full committee keeps that data aside (v1 serves pre-Electra data only and does not read the data kept aside). In a committee with a local aggregator, it keeps every vote of every data.

## Tests

Each behaviour has a test that failed before the change; mutation checks (no lock, prune window ±1 epoch, bits committed before the signature, hooks removed) make the matching test fail.

- `TestSignatureAggregatorMatchesAggregateSignatures`, `TestSignatureAggregatorRejectsMalformedSignature`
- `TestAggregatesReturnsEveryCommitteeAggregate`, `TestPruneStaleKeepsInclusionWindow`, `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsConcurrentVotes`, `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsAggregateOnSignatureError`
- `TestAttestationEventEmittedWhenPoolAlreadyHasVote`
- `TestBlockInclusionAttestationsIncludesLocalAggregates`
- `TestVerifiedAttestationIsClaimedOnce`, `TestAttestationEventEmittedWhenPoolRejectsVote`
- `TestAddAttestationElectraLimitsDataPerCommittee`, `TestAddAttestationElectraEvictsWeakestDataPerCommittee`, `TestAddAttestationElectraRefusedDataCountsVotersOnce`, `TestAddAttestationElectraBoundsRefusedDataPerCommittee`, `TestAddAttestationElectraNewDataEntersAFullRefusedSet`, `TestAddAttestationElectraTieBreakPicksTheEvictedRefusedData`, `TestAddAttestationElectraStoresPinnedDataInAFullCommittee`, `TestAddAttestationElectraPinPromotesRefusedVotes`, `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsPinnedDataAgainstStrongerData`, `TestPruneStaleDropsPins`, `TestAddAttestationElectraStoresPinnedDataBesideAFullRefusedSet`, `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsPinnedDataWithinTheCommitteeBound`, `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsWaitingPinnedDataInAFullRefusedSet`, `TestAddAttestationElectraRefusesNewDataWhenEveryDataIsPinned`, `TestAddAttestationElectraPinnedDataKeepsEveryVote`, `TestGetAggregatationByRootAndCommitteeServesRefusedData`, `TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataPinsOnlyFromElectra` (Deneb pins nothing, Electra pins the served data), `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsEveryVoteForALocalAggregator`, `TestAddAggregatorDutyKeepsOnlyDutiesInTheWindow`, `TestAddAttestationSubscriptionRegistersAggregatorDuties`, `TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataGloasPayloadIndex` (pins the served data with its index), `TestAddAttestationElectraLimitsTotalAggregates`, `TestAddAttestationElectraPrunesBeforeRefusingWhenFull`, `TestAddAttestationElectraKeepsFullCommitteeOnSignatureError`
- `block_production_packing_test.go`: real-BLS gossip and local aggregates through `electraMergedAttestationCandidates` (local alone, disjoint, partially overlapping, two committees), each packed signature checked with `bls.VerifyAggregate`; `TestPackingDropsCandidatesWithForeignSource`, `TestPackingUsesJustifiedCheckpointOfTargetEpoch`, `TestDenebPackingDropsCandidatesWithForeignSource`, `TestPackedLocalAggregateReplacesGossipSubset`, `TestPackedGossipSupersetCoversLocalAggregate`

`BenchmarkAddAttestationElectra` (425 single attestations of one committee, real BLS): ~10.7 ms/op on this branch vs ~51.4 ms/op on main, about 25 µs instead of 121 µs per attestation.

## Notes

- Before Electra, every verified attestation now also goes through the existing per-data-root path, which is pruned by time but has no count bound, and block production does not read it. This does not affect networks that are past Electra.
- The operations attestation pool has no time-based pruning, so it can hold entries that are no longer includable between proposals. That is separate from this change and left for a follow-up.
author: lystopad

title: cl/p2p: cap connections per /24 and /16 in the resource manager
body:
Refs #24444. Replaces #24449.

## Problem

`buildOptions` already installs go-libp2p's resource manager. In v0.49.0 its defaults cap connections per IPv4 address (8) and per IPv6 /56 (8) and /48 (64), rate-limit them per source, release each slot when the connection scope ends on every exit path, and act on QUIC before the handshake. It has no cap for larger blocks, so one operator holding a /24 or a /16 can still fill the peer pool, slowly, under the per-address limits.

## Change

`newResourceManager(cfg)` passes per-block limits through `rcmgr.WithLimitPerSubnet`:

| Block | Cap | At the default `--caplin.max-peer-count=128` |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address, IPv6 /56 | 8 (go-libp2p's default, repeated because the option replaces the defaults) | 8 |
| IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48 | max(16, max-peer-count/8) | 16 |
| IPv4 /16, IPv6 /32 | max(/24 cap, max-peer-count/2) | 64 |

A /24 (or a /48, one end site) may hold an eighth of the pool and a /16 half of it, so filling the pool takes several blocks. The floor of 16, two per-address caps, keeps small pools from refusing two busy hosts. The lists are ordered broadest first: go-libp2p stores a zero count for every prefix it checks before the one that refuses, and only a closed connection removes it, so with the narrowest prefix first refused connections would leave entries until restart.

With `--caplin.local-discovery`, private (RFC 1918, RFC 6598), link-local and IPv6 ULA networks are exempt from all of these caps through `rcmgr.WithNetworkPrefixLimit`, the per-address one included, so LAN and docker peers are not limited. All connections of one exempt network share one limit of max(32, 8 × max-peer-count), which never limits the pool; it stays finite because go-libp2p uses half of it as the network's QUIC source-address verification burst. Loopback keeps go-libp2p's unlimited default.

Static peers (`--sentinel.staticpeers`, including direct bootnodes) given by IP address are counted only per address: each gets its own network prefix limit on its IPv4 /32 or IPv6 /56 with go-libp2p's cap of 8, which skips the block caps, so a full block does not keep refusing the dials to them. A static peer on loopback or inside an exempt network keeps that network's allowance (go-libp2p matches the most specific prefix first, so no entry is added for it). Static peers given by DNS name are not covered.

There is no custom accounting: slots are go-libp2p connection scopes. Refusals are counted per /24 or /48 by a thin wrapper and logged at Info once a minute when there were any, with the five most refused blocks, because go-libp2p refuses them before its metrics count anything and logs them only at Debug.

## Behaviour changes (need a team decision)

- **New refusals:** more than 16 connections from one IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /48, or more than 64 from one IPv4 /16 or IPv6 /32, at the default pool size. Inbound and outbound connections both count, so our own dials into a full block are refused locally too. An IPv6 /32 is often a whole ISP or hoster.
- **New acceptances:** with `--caplin.local-discovery`, private, link-local and ULA addresses are no longer capped at 8 per address or /56.
- A ChangeLog entry under Breaking Changes is included.

## Operator overrides

- `--caplin.ip-block-limits.disable` restores go-libp2p's default limits exactly, including for private networks.
- `--caplin.ip-block-limits.trusted-cidrs=203.0.113.0/24,...` exempts the listed networks like private ones (sharing the same finite limit), with or without local discovery. Empty entries are skipped; values with host bits set, broader than an IPv4 /8 or an IPv6 /16, or invalid stop the node while flags are parsed. IPv4-mapped prefixes are converted to IPv4.

Both flags reach embedded Caplin and the standalone `caplin` binary and are documented in `configuring-erigon.mdx`.

## Tests

`cl/p2p/resource_manager_test.go` opens connection scopes on the resource manager built by `newResourceManager`, alternating inbound and outbound so each direction stays below go-libp2p's transient limits on small machines. Refusals are checked by the per-subnet error text.

- Caps: per IPv4 /24 (and that a closed connection frees its slot), per IPv4 /16, per IPv6 /48 and /32, the kept per-address caps.
- Private networks: capped like before without local discovery, exempt per block and per address with it; loopback (IPv4 and IPv6) unlimited with the default, local-discovery and trusted lists; the shared limit of an exempt network; QUIC source verification still applies.
- Overrides: trusted networks (including a spaced and an IPv4-mapped entry) exempt while other public blocks stay capped; `ParseTrustedCIDRs` (empty entries, host bits, breadth); `disable` gives the released limits; `TestCaplinIPBlockLimitFlagsReachConfig` through `setCaplin`.
- Static peers: one in a full IPv4 /24 and one in a full IPv6 /48 still connect while other addresses there are refused; a static peer keeps the cap of 8 per address; one inside a trusted network keeps the trusted allowance; static peers on loopback stay unlimited.
- `TestRefusalCounterSummarisesRefusedBlocks` (TCP and QUIC endpoints) and `TestResourceManagerCloseTwice`; `TestIPBlockConnLimitsScaleWithPeerCount` and `TestExemptNetworkConnLimitCoversThePeerPool` check the formulas.

Every cap, exemption and override has a mutation that makes the matching test fail.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/phase1/network/services: ignore local block import errors and attester slashings that need an unavailable justified state
body:
## Summary

A non-ignore error returned by a gossip service's `ProcessMessage` makes the gossip validator reject the message. Since #24629, when a peer banner is configured, that rejection also tries to queue a ban of the sender (an applied ban closes the peer's connection and keeps it banned for up to 30 minutes). #24629 already ignores local failures in the data column sidecar and execution payload envelope services. This PR does the same for two more paths where a local fault can reject a valid message: block import and attester slashings while syncing.

**Blocks.** After gossip validation, the block service imports the block with `OnBlock`. An `OnBlock` error that the service did not schedule or back off was returned as is, so the block was rejected and the validator tried to queue a ban of its sender. These errors include local ones, for example:

- the data availability check cannot determine the node's custody columns or read the index of saved columns (PeerDAS), cannot read the blob sidecars (Deneb), or cannot write the blob sidecars;
- the parent state cannot be loaded or replayed, including `ErrMissingSegment`;
- the EL returns an error together with a VALID, SYNCING or ACCEPTED status;
- a fork choice cache update fails after the state transition.

`OnBlock` marks a permanently invalid block with `ErrBlockInvalid` (failed state transition, EL `INVALID`, KZG commitments that do not match the transactions, a block that does not descend from the finalized checkpoint, an invalid parent payload path). For errors that the existing scheduling and backoff branches do not handle, the block service now returns `ErrIgnore` unless the error is `ErrBlockInvalid`. So after gossip validation a block is rejected only when fork choice marks it invalid.

Three invalid-block returns in `OnBlock` did not wrap `ErrBlockInvalid` and would have become ignores. They are now wrapped with `ErrBlockInvalid`:

- a payload that is already known to be invalid (`block is invalid`);
- a payload whose block hash does not match its contents (`OnBlock: invalid execution payload hash`);
- a payload that was marked invalid while its EL call was in flight (`ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadEnvelope` from `rejectKnownInvalidPayloadStatusLocked`).

With the marker, these errors also end the block's retry job, like other invalid blocks. So a REST v2 block publication with such a payload answers 202 (broadcast, failed integration) instead of retrying the import until the job expires after 30 seconds.

**Attester slashings.** While the node has no head state (`Syncing()`), `OnAttesterSlashing` checks a slashing against the justified state. A failure to load that state was returned as is, and a missing state made `onProcessAttesterSlashing` return `no state accessible`. Both rejected the slashing, and the validator tried to queue a ban of its sender.

Now a load error is logged and handled like a missing state. `onProcessAttesterSlashing` first runs the checks that need no state: that no index list is longer than its capacity, whether every index in the intersection was already seen, and whether both attestation data are present and slashable. Without a state, it also checks that both index lists are sorted sets. Only then does it return `synced_data.ErrNotSynced`, which the gossip validator ignores. So without a state, a slashing with non-slashable data or unsorted index lists is still rejected (unless all its intersecting indices were already seen, which is an ignore, as with a state), and validation against an available state is unchanged. `ErrIgnore` is not used here because the REST attester slashing endpoint publishes a slashing that returns `ErrIgnore`; with `ErrNotSynced` it keeps answering 400 for these cases. A slashing whose intersecting indices were all seen before, including index lists that do not intersect, returns `ErrIgnore` without a state too, as it does with a state, so the endpoint now answers 200 and publishes it while the justified state is missing, as it does on `main` when a state is available.

## Not changed here

These candidates were checked and left as they are:

- Execution payload envelopes: fork choice wraps several errors in `ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadEnvelope` that look local. Commitment validation hashes an already imported beacon block. The builder signature check reads the proposer (for a self-build) or the builder, and the domain, from that block's post-state. `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` can fail to hash that state or find fields missing. These failures can only happen if an invariant is already broken: the block was hashed when it was imported; a valid Gloas state (from the fork upgrade, the state transition or SSZ decoding) has the builder list, the latest bid and the expected withdrawals; the block's state transition already validated the bid's builder, and envelope validation checks the envelope's builder index against the block's bid first; and `GetDomain` does not fail. Fork choice also calls `blockState.SetPreviousStateRoot(block.Block.StateRoot)` before `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, so its state hashing fallback does not run. The mismatches these functions report (wrong builder, bad signature, wrong commitments) are peer faults and stay REJECT.
- Gloas block gossip validation returns a plain `parent block not found` when fork choice has the parent's header but not its block (`block_service.go:609`). Fork choice adds a block before its header and prunes both together; the anchor, which has a header and no block, has its own case. Only a prune running between the two lookups can reach it, and pruning drops only blocks more than three epochs before the finalized checkpoint.
- Payload attestations: the PTC, domain and PTC validator lookups (`payload_attestation_validation.go:188-222`) read the state of the attested block at the attestation's slot, which is checked just before. A missing state is already ignored.
- Execution payload bids: a nil builder list or nil builder entry (`execution_payload_bid_service.go:777-784`) cannot occur in a valid Gloas state. An out-of-range, inactive or wrong-version builder is a REJECT in the spec and stays one.
- If finality advances while `OnBlock` runs and the block stays above the finalized slot but no longer descends from the finalized checkpoint, it is still rejected: the gossip rule is "[REJECT] The current finalized checkpoint is an ancestor of the block", and `OnBlock` returns `ErrBlockInvalid`. If finality advances past the block, `OnBlock` returns nil without adding it, as before.
- A block that the new fallback ignores during direct gossip processing is not newly queued for a retry, the same as before, when it was rejected. If a scheduled attempt returns a non-`ErrBlockInvalid` error after adding the header, the job remains non-terminal; any later attempt skips `OnBlock` because the header is known, so the failed post-header `OnBlock` work is not run again.
- While syncing, attester slashings are still checked against the justified state. This matches the fork choice `on_attester_slashing` handler, but the gossip rule uses the head state, so a slashing of a validator that the justified state does not know yet is still rejected (unless all its intersecting indices were already seen). The fork choice spec tests process slashings in this mode.
- For a gossip slashing from Electra on, while the justified state is unavailable, each index list length is bounded only by the mainnet capacity that the SSZ decoder uses (131072). So on the minimal preset, whose limit is 8192, a slashing with more than 8192 indices that passes the other checks is ignored instead of rejected.
- Since #24771, `isUnequivocating` no longer panics on 64-bit builds for a validator index from 2^63 to 2^64-8. While the justified state is missing, the node cannot tell that such an index is out of range: a slashing that has it in both index lists and passes the checks that need no state returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced`, so gossip ignores it and the REST endpoint answers 400. With a state it is rejected, as on `main`.
- Since #24771, a slashing in which at least one intersecting index was not seen before and that passes the data, index and signature checks is rejected when no validator of the intersection is slashable. That check needs the state: while the justified state is missing, such a slashing that passes the checks that need no state returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced`, so gossip ignores it and the REST endpoint answers 400.
- The attester slashing gossip service decodes with `DecodeSSZ` (`attester_slashing.go:35`), which accepts some non-canonical encodings, for example an offset that leaves a gap before a nested index list. Most gossip services do the same; blocks and the Gloas-only topics use `DecodeSSZStrict`. With a state, `main` accepts such a slashing if it is otherwise valid. While the justified state was missing, `main` rejected such a slashing unless it was already in the operations pool; now, if it passes the checks that need no state, it returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced` and gossip ignores it. Strict decoding for these topics is a separate change.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/block_service.go`: after the existing scheduling and backoff branches, `ProcessMessage` returns `ErrIgnore` for every remaining import error except `forkchoice.ErrBlockInvalid`. The existing branches are unchanged.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block.go`: wrap the three invalid-payload returns with `ErrBlockInvalid`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_attester_slashing.go`: while syncing, a justified state load error is logged and handled like a missing state; `onProcessAttesterSlashing` checks for a missing state after the checks that need no state, then checks that both index lists are sorted sets (their lengths were already checked against their capacities), and then returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/block_service_test.go`: `TestBlockServiceIgnoresLocalOnBlockFailureOnly`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_choice_test.go`, `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_block_lock_scope_test.go`: assert `ErrBlockInvalid` in `TestOnBlockHashMismatchPreservesVerifiedPayload` and `TestOnBlockMalformedHashIsNotCachedAgainstTheClaimedHash`; new `TestOnBlockRejectsPayloadInvalidatedDuringValidation`.
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/forkchoice_test.go`: `TestOnAttesterSlashingIgnoresMissingJustifiedStateWhileSyncing` (also with an Electra-capacity slashing of 2049 indices that targets a pre-Electra epoch), `TestOnAttesterSlashingRejectsInvalidSlashingWhileSyncing` (non-slashable data and unsorted indices, with the justified state available, missing, or failing to load); the test fork graph can return a `GetState` error.

## Testing

- **Red on `main`:** with the production files from `main`, these fail: `TestBlockServiceIgnoresLocalOnBlockFailureOnly/local_failure`, all four subtests of `TestOnAttesterSlashingIgnoresMissingJustifiedStateWhileSyncing` (missing state and load error, each with the single-index and the 2049-index slashing), `TestOnBlockRejectsPayloadInvalidatedDuringValidation`, `TestOnBlockMalformedHashIsNotCachedAgainstTheClaimedHash` and `TestOnBlockHashMismatchPreservesVerifiedPayload` (its `block is invalid` assertion also fails on its own when only that marker is reverted). The `missing` and `load_error` cases of `TestOnAttesterSlashingRejectsInvalidSlashingWhileSyncing` (non-slashable data, unsorted indices) fail too: before it checks the slashing, `main` returns `no state accessible` for a missing state, or the load error. The reverse cases `TestBlockServiceIgnoresLocalOnBlockFailureOnly/invalid_block` and the `available` cases of `TestOnAttesterSlashingRejectsInvalidSlashingWhileSyncing` pass before and after; `invalid_block` fails if the block service ignores every import error.

title: cl: keep Gloas payload status when EL validation is cut short
body:
Part of #24620.

First of the focused PRs that replace #24643. This one holds the core fix for the stuck head; the other parts land after it or independently (see the landing order on #24620).

## Problem

After a restart or a deep forward sync, Gloas payloads that were persisted without an EL verdict had no payload status, and EL calls cut short by our own context were recorded as `None`. Fork choice then saw such payloads as unavailable, kept the EMPTY variant and could not move the head past them.

## Changes

- **Forward sync**: fork choice records `NotValidated` for an envelope it persists without an EL call (no engine, or `validate=false` as in forward sync), under its lock, so fork choice can build on the FULL variant. A verdict already on record is kept. Main has the same rule since #24878. See "Decision" below.
- **Interrupted validation is not `None`**:
  - `ErrPayloadValidationInterrupted` (was the private `errPayloadValidationAdmission`) marks a NewPayload that ended with our own context, while waiting for admission or inside the EL call.
  - The pending drain, the verification sweep and the stored-parent replay keep the payload pending instead of recording `None`.
  - The direct client answers no verdict, instead of `NotValidated`, when its head read fails because the caller's context ended. This applies to every fork, so a pre-Gloas block import in that window is delayed once instead of accepted optimistically.
  - A timeout of the engine client's own request, with our context still alive, is not covered: the engine client returns `None` with the error, which fork choice records before `errELBehind` persists and queues the envelope, and the drain and sweep retry under their 2 s budget without a verdict while the EL stays slow. This is pre-existing and affects only a remote EL; a follow-up is proposed (classify Gloas envelopes by the error chain: persist, `NotValidated`, queue; keep pre-Gloas IGNORE).
- **REST envelope POST**:
  - An interruption after the consensus checks is treated like a queued envelope: `202`, published, and the gossip event emitted. Fork choice parks such an envelope without persisting it, so the handler does not mark it seen and keeps its retry record; the client's re-POST is processed again.
  - Every branch publishes on a context detached from the request, bounded by one slot from the start of the publish, so a client that gave up during validation does not stop it.
  - Under `consensus` and `consensus_and_equivocation`, an interruption during the consensus pre-validation still answers `400` and is not broadcast (#24853 tracks queuing it).
- **Anchor**: `StoreAnchorEnvelope` records `NotValidated` until the EL answers, with any execution client.
- **By-hash verdict**: unchanged from main. Projecting a hash's `Validated` onto a sibling root (`payloadValidatedLocked`) is base behaviour that main tests encode; making it root-specific for Gloas is proposed as a follow-up together with INVALID by hash.
- **EL validation depth**: the embedded EL client inserts a block more than `reorgTooDeepDepth` below its head, then answers `NotValidated` without validating it. It reports that bound (`SkipsValidationBelow`, 0 when it validates every block) and whether it is known: it is not while the EL head cannot be read.
  - The drain, the replay, the sweep and the anchor retry still send such payloads to the EL, so they reach it, and only skip the requeue after a `NotValidated` answer below the bound. The bound is read once per pass.
  - Only the EL's own `NotValidated` answer, recorded as such, counts: an error answer keeps a recorded `NotValidated`, and an interrupted call is not an answer, so both are retried. The sweep and the anchor retry remember such roots after the call. While such a root is still below the current depth, which follows the EL head, the sweep skips it and walks on to its ancestors, which an interrupted batch may have left unsent, and the anchor retry skips the anchor before loading its state. The sweep also skips a remembered root among its selected and immediate heads, so it is not read and sent again on every pass. An unreadable EL head keeps the remembered roots in both, and a known zero depth checks them again. Remembered sweep roots are pruned at finalization.
  - Other EL clients report no bound and keep the old retry behaviour.

## Decision: forward-synced payloads without an EL call

`NotValidated` from forward sync makes the payload FULL-eligible without a data-availability check, and Gloas roots are not reported as optimistic. Main already takes this shortcut for pre-Gloas forward-synced blocks, and with the default direct client those payloads were executed by the EL during forward sync. This PR keeps it as the Gloas form of that shortcut. Gloas-aware optimistic tracking and a DA check for forward-synced envelopes (with #24704) are proposed as follow-ups.

## Tests

Each behaviour change has a test that failed before the change, or a mutation check.

- `on_execution_payload_test.go`:
  - an EL call cut by the context inside NewPayload leaves the envelope pending, with no status recorded. It fails without the admission wrap;
  - an envelope persisted without an EL call is `NotValidated`, with no engine and with `validate=false`.
- `execution_client_engine_test.go`:
  - a client timeout is no verdict, for Gloas and Electra;
  - `ValidationInterrupted`.
- `payload_build_test.go`:
  - the direct client's ended-context window, through a real execution module;
  - `SkipsValidationBelow`.
- `gloas_drain_test.go`, `gloas_payload_test.go`, `chain_tip_sync_recovery_test.go`:
  - interrupted drain, sweep and replay, through the real store admission;
  - below the validation depth the EL is still asked and the payload is not requeued (drain, replay); the sweep and the anchor retry ask once and stop while the root stays below the depth, also with an unreadable EL head, and again at a known zero depth; a remembered selected head is not sent again; the sweep walks past a remembered root; an interrupted forward-sync anchor validation records nothing; the sweep's pruning;
  - the anchor status and gas limit with and without an engine.
- `epbs_test.go`:
  - an interrupted and a validated envelope POST on three routes, with the request context cancelled during validation;
  - a re-POST after an interrupted validation is processed, on three routes;
  - the publish deadline starts at the publish, not before the validation.

Mutation checks (each makes a test fail): requeue regardless of the depth, no sweep or anchor memo, dropping the memo on an unreadable head, skipping the EL call below the depth, no anchor gas limit, marking an interrupted POST seen, a publish window that includes the validation, no `NotValidated` without validation in fork choice.

`go test -race` passes for `cl/beacon/handler`, `cl/phase1/{forkchoice,stages,execution_client,network}/...`; `make lint` clean twice.

TDD note: the sentinel rename in `on_block.go`, `on_block_lock_scope_test.go` and `on_execution_payload_test.go` is mechanical, so it has no new tests.

title: cl: align consensus and fork choice with v1.7.0-beta.4
body:
## Summary

Align Caplin with `consensus-specs` v1.7.0-beta.4 (from beta.2) and pin the official beta.4 mainnet fixtures. ACDT #100 asks client releases for the Hoodi Glamsterdam fork to support beta.4.

## Main changes

- **Gloas `apply_parent_execution_payload`** settles the parent's builder payment before it processes the parent's execution requests, so a builder exit request is rejected while the payment is pending. The builders sweep withdraws only the balance left after the withdrawals already selected for that builder (`get_builder_balance_after_withdrawals`). ethereum/consensus-specs#5695
- **Gloas `slash_validator`** clears every pending builder payment of the slashed proposer, for proposer and attester slashings alike. The Gloas override of `process_proposer_slashing` is removed. ethereum/consensus-specs#5719
- **`calculate_committee_fraction`** counts only unslashed active validators. This changes the proposer boost on every fork, including current mainnet, and the weak-head reorg threshold on Gloas. ethereum/consensus-specs#5679
- **Gloas `get_head`** walks the filtered node tree: the EMPTY and FULL variants of a block are filtered separately, and the justified root's EMPTY node is returned when no node is viable. ethereum/consensus-specs#5509
- **Payload envelopes** newer than the finalized checkpoint are served even outside the `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` window. ethereum/consensus-specs#5681
- **Spec test runners** read the beta.4 formats: a per-message `current_time_ms` in gossip vectors, and `head.payload_status` in fork choice checks. Before this change the runner read a `head_payload_status` key that no fixture contains, so the Gloas head payload status was never asserted.

## Implementation notes

- **Gloas filter cost.** The filter does at most one ancestor walk from the justified root to the finalized start slot, then one iterative pass over the justified subtree that carries that ancestor down the tree: O(N + D) fork-graph reads, where N is the subtree size and D the ancestor distance. A per-leaf `get_checkpoint_block` walk would cost O(N·D) under `f.mu` during long non-finality, because in the node tree almost every block has a leaf variant.
- **Gloas walk.** It reuses the children sampled by the filter, so a change of payload availability between the two passes cannot produce a PENDING head.
- **Pre-Gloas head path with the head state** (`GetHead(prevHeadState)`, the synced path on mainnet):
  - When the justified checkpoint state is not cached, the head computation loads it before taking the fork-choice lock, so the proposer boost uses the justified checkpoint state's unslashed balance, as in the spec, and the head does not depend on the cache contents.
  - A load error is not returned. The boost then falls back to the head state's unslashed active balance, an O(validators) scan.
  - The stage loads the justified checkpoint state before it enters `ViewHeadState`, so the head computation normally finds it cached. `OnAttestation` takes `f.mu` and then the head-state read lock, the stage takes them in the opposite order, and a head-state writer can queue between them; a long load inside `ViewHeadState` would make that deadlock much easier to hit.
  - The head computation still loads under the read lock if the stage's load fails, or if the justified checkpoint changes between the two calls. On a cache miss, the Gloas head computation already loads the checkpoint state under the same read lock.
- **Test coverage of the Gloas filter.** The mainnet fixtures have no `filter_node_tree_variants` cases, so new unit tests cover the node-level filtering:
  - the empty-tree fallback;
  - FULL excluded while EMPTY is viable, and the reverse;
  - a justified root below the finalized start slot;
  - a bound on fork-graph reads.


## Not changed

- **ethereum/consensus-specs#5680**, the Gloas `compute_min_epochs_for_block_requests` (14299 epochs on mainnet). Caplin keeps 33024, which serves a superset of the required range.
- **ethereum/consensus-specs#5665** (proposer preferences signing domain) and **#5706** (ENR `next_fork_version`). Caplin already behaves as specified.
- **#5672 and #5673.** They only affect the fast confirmation rule, which Caplin does not implement.
- **The `time_ms` fork-choice refactors** (#5667, #5668, #5671, #5675). Caplin's store keeps whole-second time, as before. Fork-choice vectors still tick in seconds.
- **Network gating.** The new consensus rules apply to every network where Gloas is active, including Sepolia, without a separate activation epoch. Prysm (OffchainLabs/prysm#17661) and Lighthouse (sigp/lighthouse#10307) merged the same rules without one either.
- **Spectests that are still skipped.** This PR does not change the runner's skip policy. Unregistered gossip handlers, Heze, and `get_proposer_head` are still skipped. The fork-choice runner still ignores `payload_attestation_message` steps and payload-vote checks (a stacked follow-up PR runs them), and does not assert `viable_for_head_roots_and_weights`, which no mainnet fixture uses.

## Tests

- **TDD:**
  - The beta.4 fixtures were the Red step for the consensus changes. Before the production changes, 12 vectors failed:
    - `proposer_boost_excludes_slashed_validators` in 7 forks;
    - `process_parent_execution_payload__older_than_previous_epoch_builder_exit`;
    - `builder_sweep_after_pending_withdrawal`;
    - `randomized_1` and `randomized_12`;
    - `builder_payment_removed_when_proposer_slashes_itself`.
  - The unit tests for new behaviour failed before the fix (node-level filtering, the PENDING-head case, the cached-balance boost, the envelope serve bound). `TestGloasHeadFinalizedCheckpointWhenJustifiedRootPredatesEpochStart` pins the finalized-checkpoint carry in `getFilteredNodeTree`: it fails when the carry is removed. `TestPreGloasHeadWithAuxiliaryStateDoesNotDependOnCheckpointStateCache` failed before the checkpoint-state load was added: a cold and a warm cache selected different heads. `TestComputeForkChoiceLoadsJustifiedStateBeforeViewingHeadState` fails when the stage does not load the state before `ViewHeadState`. The other tests pin preserved pre-Gloas behaviour.
  - The fixture-version bump itself is mechanical.
- **Run locally on this commit:**
  - `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`: pass.
  - `go test -short ./cl/... ./p2p/forkid/ ./execution/chain/...`: pass.
  - `make lint`: 0 issues.
  - `make erigon integration`: builds.




Closes #17334

title: cl: report why chain-tip blocks are not imported
body:
Part of #24620.

One of the focused PRs that replace #24643. Builds on #24828, now on main. Diagnostics only; no change to what gets imported.

## Problem

While the head was stuck in #24620, nothing at the default log level said why: chain-tip blocks that were not imported were logged at Debug, one line per block, or not at all.

## Changes

- **Summary** (`chainTipRejections`, `chain_tip_rejections.go`): rejections are aggregated per reason. At most every 30 s (also checked once per `chainTipSync` call, so a burst that stops is still reported), one Warn per reason is logged:

  ```
  chain tip blocks rejected reason=... attempts=... lastSlot=... lastBlockRoot=... headSlot=... lastErr=... lastErrSlot=... lastErrBlockRoot=...
  ```

  - `attempts` counts tries: a block retried on every poll counts each time.
  - The last error keeps the slot and root it came from, so a later rejection without an error does not hide it.
  - Reasons not seen for two intervals are dropped, so counts from before a forward sync are not reported as current.
- **Reasons**: anchor envelope unavailable; parent not in fork graph; parent envelope unavailable (a required parent envelope that was neither fetched nor stored); parent payload not accepted; process block failed.
- **Not counted**: blocks that are early or wait for their parent's envelope, since gossip imports them moments later; failures caused by the stage's own context; and any failure during shutdown. A required envelope still missing at the stage deadline is counted under its own reason.
- **Causes**:
  - A block whose parent is missing reports the cause the parent was rejected for, across the batches of one run.
  - The stored-parent replay returns its reason (`rejection`, `ensureStoredParentPayloadAccepted` now return an error): the payload status by name, with the EL error when there is one.
  - The Debug line is written only when a block's cause changes, compared by message, since a retry builds the same cause again.

## Tests

- `chain_tip_rejections_test.go`:
  - one summary per reason per interval, with the last error kept with its block;
  - stale reasons are dropped;
  - early, envelope-pending, own-context and shutdown failures are not counted;
  - causes are compared by message;
  - a reason that is its own cause is not repeated as the error.
- `chain_tip_sync_recovery_test.go`:
  - a rejected parent payload's cause ("parent payload invalid") reaches the child and, in a later batch, the grandchild, under the labels the summary records;
  - a parent envelope no peer serves is reported as "parent envelope unavailable", not as the deadline;
  - the replay and acceptance tests use the error API.

The rejection-propagation, envelope and context-filter tests were mutation-checked.

`go test -race` passes for `cl/phase1/stages`, `cl/beacon/handler` and `cl/phase1/forkchoice`; `make lint` is clean twice.
author: lystopad

title: cl: verify proposer slashing signatures over the header and accept one per proposer
body:
## Summary

Gossip and REST validation of proposer slashings (`cl/phase1/network/services/proposer_slashing_service.go`) computed each header's signing root over the whole `SignedBeaconBlockHeader` (header and signature) instead of over `signed_header.message`. The phase0 `process_proposer_slashing`, whose conditions the `proposer_slashing` gossip topic requires, signs `signed_header.message`, so every correctly signed proposer slashing failed with `invalid signature`:

- On gossip the slashing was rejected. Since #24629, a rejection makes the gossip manager try to queue a ban of the sending peer, so this bug can cause an honest relaying peer to be banned.
- `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/proposer_slashings` answered 400 for a valid slashing and did not add it to the pool or publish it.
- Valid slashings therefore never reached the operations pool through gossip or REST, so the node did not include them in the blocks it proposed.

Block import is not affected: proposer slashings inside a block are checked by the state transition, not by this service.

The first commit computes the signing root over `signedHeader.Header`, as the blob and data column sidecar services already do for their signed headers. The other signature checks in `cl/phase1/network/services` already sign the object the spec defines; for signed envelopes that is the inner message or header.

Once valid slashings pass, the service starts to fill its proposer cache, which makes older paths in `ProcessMessage` reachable. The second commit fixes them:

- A proposer cache hit returned nil, which the gossip manager maps to ACCEPT. After one slashing for a proposer was accepted, any later object whose first header names that proposer skipped every check and was relayed, also a malformed one. The gossip rule IGNOREs everything after the first valid proposer slashing for a proposer, so a cache hit now returns `ErrIgnore`.
- A pool hit also returned nil. The pool key hashes only the two signatures (`pool.ComputeKeyForProposerSlashing`), so the signatures of a pooled slashing copied onto other headers were accepted without validation. The shortcut is removed: such an object is now validated and rejected, and repeats are caught by the proposer cache.
- The proposer cache was checked at the start and filled at the end, so two different valid slashings for the same proposer processed concurrently were both accepted, added to the pool and emitted. The proposer is now claimed with `LoadOrStore` after both signatures verify, and the loser gets `ErrIgnore`.
- The proposer cache was an LRU of 100 entries, so once 100 other proposers had been accepted, a second valid slashing for an evicted proposer was accepted again. It is now a `sync.Map` that does not evict. An index is stored only after a slashing signed by that proposer verifies, at most once per validator index. Lighthouse also keeps observed proposer indices in a set without a size limit.

After this, every `ErrIgnore` from the service means that the proposer has already been claimed by a fully validated slashing. `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/proposer_slashings` treated both nil and `ErrIgnore` as success and published the submitted object. With the first commit alone, the cache and pool shortcuts returned nil, so the handler could publish unvalidated objects. On `ErrIgnore` it now answers 200 without publishing. The Beacon API asks the node to broadcast a slashing that passes validation. Lighthouse answers 200 without publishing for an already known proposer, and Caplin's attestation handlers do the same for an already seen attestation (`ErrAttestationAlreadySeen`).

## Not changed here

- release/3.7 has the same bug. A `[r3.7]` backport will follow once this merges.
- If `Publish` fails for a slashing submitted over REST, the handler still answers 200, as before. With the second commit, a resubmission gets `ErrIgnore` and is not published again. The slashing was added to the pool before `Publish`, so it stays in the pool unless the usual pool eviction or finalized-state pruning removes it, and the node can include it in a block it proposes while it passes the usual block production checks. Lighthouse also records the proposer before it publishes and does not publish a resubmission for a known proposer.
- The proposer set lives until restart; Lighthouse additionally clears its set at fork boundaries.
- The event is still sent inside `ViewHeadState`, under the head state read lock.
- Related services have similar gaps: concurrent valid voluntary exits or BLS changes for the same validator both return nil (only one is stored); sync committee contributions return nil for an already seen contribution; the REST handlers for voluntary exits, attester slashings, BLS changes and sync committee contributions still publish on `ErrIgnore`.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/services/proposer_slashing_service.go`: compute the signing root over `signedHeader.Header`; replace the proposer LRU with a `sync.Map`; return `ErrIgnore` when the proposer is already there; remove the pool shortcut; claim the proposer with `LoadOrStore` after the signatures verify, and only the winner adds the slashing to the pool and emits it. The `proposer_slashing` LRU hit and miss metrics go away with the LRU.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/constants.go`: remove `proposerSlashingCacheSize`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services/proposer_slashing_service_test.go`: new tests with real `fork.ComputeSigningRoot` and BLS signatures: `TestProposerSlashingServiceAcceptsSpecSignedHeaders` (a slashing signed as the spec does is accepted and pooled), `TestProposerSlashingServiceIgnoresMalformedAfterAccepted` (a malformed slashing for an accepted proposer is ignored and not pooled), `TestProposerSlashingServiceKeepsAcceptedProposerAfterManyOthers` (after 100 other proposers, a second valid slashing for the first proposer is still ignored) and `TestProposerSlashingServiceConcurrentValidationAcceptsOne` (two valid slashings for one proposer are held at signature verification until both arrive; exactly one is accepted and pooled, the other is ignored). In `TestProcessMessage`, the mocked test expects `ComputeSigningRoot` to be called with each header, the seen-proposer case expects `ErrIgnore`, and the pool case now checks that pooled signatures on invalid headers are rejected, not ignored.
- `cl/beacon/handler/pool.go`: on `ErrIgnore`, answer 200 without publishing.
- `cl/beacon/handler/pool_test.go`: new `TestPoolProposerSlashingDoesNotPublishIgnored`.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with the production file from `main`, `TestProposerSlashingServiceAcceptsSpecSignedHeaders` fails with `invalid signature`. With the production files of the first commit (the services test package then needs a one-line shim, `seenProposers.Store` to the old `cache.Add`, to compile), these fail and pass with the second: `TestProcessMessage` (the seen-proposer and pooled-signature cases return nil), `TestProposerSlashingServiceIgnoresMalformedAfterAccepted` (nil instead of `ErrIgnore`), `TestProposerSlashingServiceKeepsAcceptedProposerAfterManyOthers` (the evicted proposer is accepted again), `TestProposerSlashingServiceConcurrentValidationAcceptsOne` (both accepted, in 20 of 20 runs) and `TestPoolProposerSlashingDoesNotPublishIgnored` (unexpected `Publish`).
- `go test -race -count=50 -run TestProposerSlashing ./cl/phase1/network/services/`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/network/services/ ./cl/beacon/handler/`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/spectest: assert Gloas PTC fork-choice steps and votes, run the remaining ssz_static vectors
body:
## Summary

Execute the Gloas PTC fork-choice steps and checks that the spectest runner previously ignored silently, align `on_payload_attestation_message` with the spec so they pass, and run the remaining ssz_static vectors that had no handler.

## Fork-choice runner

- `steps.yaml` is decoded with `KnownFields`, and an unknown step type fails the test. Before this change an unknown step or check key was dropped, so a vector could pass without checking anything.
- New `payload_attestation_message` step, including `valid: false`.
- New `payload_timeliness_vote` and `payload_data_availability_vote` checks. A check fails when the root has no vote entry (the spec asserts the root is present), not only when the votes differ.
- New `genesis_time` check.

Before this change the 13 Gloas cases under `on_payload_attestation_message`, `payload_timeliness` and `payload_data_availability` ran and passed without asserting any vote. Now the votes are asserted: forcing present vote entries to contain all-zero arrays fails 11 cases (nine of those 13 plus two `get_head` payload-tiebreak cases), and removing the entries fails all 15 cases that contain vote checks.

## PTC message handling

- `OnPayloadAttestationMessage` follows the spec handler for wire messages. A vote counts only for the store's current slot. A message for another slot of the referenced block is a no-op, as in the spec's `data.slot != state.slot` return.
- `OnGossipPayloadAttestationMessage` adds the p2p first-valid rule per (slot, validator). The current-slot decision is taken under the store lock. First-valid is tracked per (slot, validator) for the store's current and previous slots; a message for an older slot is ignored. A late gossip message for the previous slot that passes validation is accepted for propagation, but its vote is not counted; fork choice reports it with `ErrPayloadAttestationNotCurrentSlot`, which is separate from `ErrIgnore`.
- Before this change a vote from a previous slot could be counted in fork choice.
- The isFromBlock path is removed: block-carried PTC votes keep going through `notifyPtcMessages`.

Red evidence: with only the runner change, `on_payload_attestation_message_valid`, `_slot_mismatch` and `_current_slot_and_signature` fail. They pass with the handler changes.

## ssz_static

`HistoricalBatch` (phase0 to bellatrix) and `NewPayloadRequest` (bellatrix to gloas) have no Caplin production type, so their 45 mainnet cases were skipped. They now run against test-only types. The Gloas `NewPayloadRequest` uses the progressive container root.

The runner's skip for `on_execution_payload_envelope__wrong_withdrawals` is removed. The case name has one underscore, so the skip never matched, and the case already ran and passed.

## Not changed

- Gossip validation still takes the PTC, public keys and domain from the referenced block's state. The p2p spec uses the head state. This deviation existed before this PR and is left for a follow-up.
- The 13 `gloas/networking/gossip_payload_attestation_message` vectors are still unregistered, like the other gossip vectors without a handler.
- The runner still ends a test early on `on_payload_info` and `pow_block` steps.
- A gossip PTC message for a slot ahead of the store's slot is ignored rather than accepted for propagation. This branch is unreachable for a known referenced block: `OnBlock` cannot import slot S while the store is before S, and `OnTick` never moves store time backwards. It is reachable only with inconsistent mocked or preloaded state, and is then not limited to the lower clock-disparity boundary. The unregistered gossip vector `valid_slot_at_lower_disparity` expects acceptance.

## Tests

Run locally on this branch:
- `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`: pass.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/network/services/... ./cl/beacon/handler/...`: pass; `-race` on the PTC tests: pass.
- `make lint`: 0 issues.
- `make erigon integration`: builds.

title: cl/das: recover the blob rows of a block in parallel
body:
Fixes #24858.

## Problem

`RecoverMatrix` recovers the blob rows of a block one after another, about 0.1 s per row with go-eth-kzg. A supernode that completes a block's columns by recovery waits for the whole sequential recovery before the block enters fork choice and reaches the EL. On a mainnet supernode running release/3.7, the time from the 64th to the 128th stored column grew by about 0.12 s per blob (0.49 s for 4 blobs, 0.76 s for 6, 0.93 s for 8, 1.08 s for 9), and the block was imported about 0.15 s after its last column.

## Change

`cl/das/utils/das_utils.go`: `RecoverMatrix` recovers the rows in parallel. A package-level semaphore of `GOMAXPROCS` slots bounds the rows in flight across all calls (Caplin runs 8 recovery workers). Each row is written to its own index, so the result keeps row order. Every row is attempted; if any fails, the error of the lowest failing row is returned, the same row the sequential version reported. go-eth-kzg ignores the `numGoRoutines` argument for recovery, so rows were never recovered concurrently. The multi-exponentiations inside FK20 already spread over the cores on their own, outside this bound; the slots bound the rows in flight and their working buffers, not cores.

## Results

`BenchmarkRecoverMatrix` (half of the columns of dense blobs, Apple M3 Max, 16 cores, 5 iterations, both versions on the same input):

| blobs | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 99 ms | 99 ms |
| 6 | 594 ms | 163 ms |
| 9 | 892 ms | 194 ms |
| 16 | 1,589 ms | 334 ms |

With `GOMAXPROCS=8` the first version of this change took 206 / 351 / 512 ms for 6 / 9 / 16 blobs. The mainnet node above runs with `GOMAXPROCS` 24.

## Tests

No unit test covered `RecoverMatrix`. This is a performance change with the same output, so the first two tests pass before and after and protect the behaviour:
- `TestRecoverMatrixRestoresEveryRowInOrder`: three blobs, the even columns given last row first; the recovered matrix equals the original one. Writing rows to the wrong index fails it.
- `TestRecoverMatrixReportsTheRowThatCannotBeRecovered`: one row with too few cells returns its error. Dropping the row errors fails it.
- `TestRecoverMatrixReportsTheLowestBrokenRow`: rows 1 and 2 broken, 20 runs, always `blob 1`. It failed with the first version of this change (first error recorded) and passes on main.
- `TestRecoverMatrixWaitsForAFreeRowSlot`: with every slot taken no row starts, and each row gives its slot back. It fails with a per-call limit and without the deferred release.
- `BenchmarkRecoverMatrix` in `das_utils_bench_test.go`.

`go test -race ./cl/das/...`, `make lint` (twice), `make erigon integration`.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: keep fork-choice store time in milliseconds
body:
## Summary

Caplin's fork-choice store kept time in whole seconds, and every tick after genesis could overwrite the store time. Two problems followed:

- Block timeliness and the proposer boost were decided with one-second resolution. On 5-second slots (Gnosis, Chiado), a block whose timeliness was sampled 1666–1999 ms into the slot was treated as timely before Gloas, although the attestation deadline is 1666 ms.
- The stage loop and block publication tick the store to the slot start. That moved store time backwards, so a locally published block could be recorded as timely late in its slot.

This aligns the store with consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4, where the fork-choice store keeps `time_ms`.

## Changes

- **Store time in milliseconds.** The store keeps time in milliseconds and `OnTick` takes milliseconds; the 2 ms ticker passes `UnixMilli()`. `Time()` still returns seconds.
- **Time never moves backwards.** The spec requires callers to call `on_tick` only with a later time; `OnTick` now enforces this itself and ignores a time that is not later than the store time. A CAS advances the store, and only the tick that crosses a slot boundary runs the slot-start work (head and proposer-boost reset, checkpoint pull-up). The boundary is published without taking `f.mu`, as before, so readers see the new slot even while another goroutine holds the fork-choice lock.
- **Millisecond timeliness.** `recordBlockTimeliness` and the proposer-boost decision use the time into the slot in milliseconds, taken from one read of store time.
- **Saturating conversion.** `utils.SecondsToMilliseconds` saturates like the spec's `seconds_to_milliseconds`.
- **Spec attestation deadline.** The pre-Gloas attestation deadline is `ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS` (3333) of the slot: 3999 ms on 12-second slots, 1999 ms on 6 s and 1666 ms on 5 s. It was `SECONDS_PER_SLOT / INTERVALS_PER_SLOT` (4000, 2000, 1666). Gloas deadlines are unchanged.

## Behaviour changes

- **Mainnet (pre-Gloas).** The attestation deadline moves from 4000 to 3999 ms. Block-production timing derived from it (builder window, publication margin, signing window, payload-preparation stale-head wait) shifts by at most 1 ms.
- **Gnosis and Chiado.** The effective timeliness cutoff moves from 2000 ms to 1666 ms before Gloas. Under Gloas it becomes 1250 ms, and the PTC cutoff 3750 ms.
- **Wall-clock steps.** If the wall clock jumps forward and is then corrected, store time stays ahead until real time catches up.
- **Custom network configs.** The pre-Gloas attestation deadline no longer follows `INTERVALS_PER_SLOT`. `ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS` is a constant, like the Gloas BPS values, so it is not loaded from a network config. Every built-in network uses 3 intervals per slot.

## Not changed

These follow-ups existed before this PR:

- The slot boundary is published before the slot-start work runs under `f.mu`. A block that takes the lock in between can lose its proposer boost.
- Before Gloas, the proposer boost does not check `is_same_dependent_root`.
- Timeliness is read after the state transition, not at block receipt.
- Slot start times are computed in seconds before the conversion to milliseconds.

## Tests

- **Red tests.** These failed on the code before the fix:
  - a late block on a 5-second slot;
  - `OnTick` moving time backwards;
  - a late locally published block after a slot-start tick;
  - the 3999 ms pre-Gloas deadline (fails with the `INTERVALS_PER_SLOT` formula).
- **Regression pin.** A genesis time near the `uint64` limit makes `OnTick` a no-op instead of wrapping the millisecond conversion.
- **Deadline table.** It checks deadline−1 and deadline for the attestation and PTC deadlines on 12-second slots before and after Gloas, the attestation deadline on 5-second slots before Gloas, the PTC deadline on 5-second slots under Gloas, and a non-zero genesis.
- **Run locally on this branch:**
  - `cd cl/spectest && make mainnet`: pass.
  - `go test ./cl/... ./cmd/caplin/...`: pass.
  - `go test -race ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/`: pass.
  - `make lint`: 0 issues.
  - `make erigon integration`: builds.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: record gloas payload status when el validation is skipped
body:
## Summary

After a restart of a node with an embedded EL, the Gloas fork choice head stayed behind the imported chain and climbed back only one block per ChainTipSync cycle. The forkchoice update for the stale head made the EL unwind, and validator duties were served on the stale head. A node that checkpoint-syncs with an embedded EL takes the same code path.

Payload verification status is kept only in memory. Startup creates a fresh fork choice store, and ForwardSync replays the downloaded Gloas envelopes into it. When the attached EL supports insertion (the embedded EL, through the direct client or the in-process Engine API client), ForwardSync replays the envelopes with `validatePayload=false`. `applyEnvelopeCoordinated` persisted these envelopes but recorded a payload status only when no engine was attached. Gloas fork choice offers the FULL variant of a block only when its payload status is `NotValidated` or `Validated`, so `computeHeadGloas` stopped at the first replayed block whose child builds on its payload. `verifyUnverifiedGloasPayloads` looks for unverified payloads only at the selected head and its ancestors, so it never reached the replayed blocks above the stale head: each cycle validated one more block and the head moved up by one.

Measured on `main`:

- Local devnet, embedded node restarted at slot 70: ForwardSync finished after 6 s with the EL at the tip, then the head went back to slot 65 and the EL unwound to block 63. The head advanced one slot at a time from 65 to 69 and then jumped to the live tip at slot 75, 55 s after startup. The node's proposal at slot 73 was built on an EMPTY parent and was missed.
- A node joining the same devnet by checkpoint sync took 373 s to catch up, with its head about 32 slots behind the tip.
- On Sepolia, catching up after a restart took about 8.5 minutes.

Now `applyEnvelopeCoordinated` also records a status when an engine is attached but the call skips EL validation: `NotValidated`, or `Validated` when a validated verdict for the root or the execution payload hash is already cached (the same rule as in `applyPayloadValidationResultLocked`). This check is needed because `markPayloadStatus` keeps a `Validated` status recorded for the same root and any known `Invalidated` status, but not a `Validated` verdict that is cached only for the execution payload hash; without it, a concurrent validating call can lose that verdict.

With `validatePayload=false`, the replay still runs the full envelope commitment checks, including the locally derived block hash, and `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, including the builder signature. It does not call `NewPayload`, and, as before, it skips `validateEnvelopeAgainstBlockAfterCommitments` and the payload arrival record; ForwardSync also passes `checkBlobData=false`, so data availability is not checked during the replay. `NotValidated` means that these checks passed and there is no EL verdict yet; it is the status that the path without an engine already records.

Replayed payloads are now eligible for FULL head selection right away, so on a single chain the head reaches the newest replayed block in one fork choice pass. The sweep then asks the EL to validate the unverified payloads on the head's ancestry.

Other callers: with an attached EL, the chain-tip parent replay passes `validatePayload=false` only for envelopes that are already stored, and those return at the `HasEnvelope` check before the new code. Gossip, the beacon API, envelope recovery and the pending-envelope retry request EL validation when an EL is attached. Without an engine, the path still records `NotValidated`, except that a cached `Validated` verdict is now kept.

## Not changed here

- Persisting payload status across restarts. With an insertion-capable EL, replayed payloads start as `NotValidated` and the sweep validates them again.
- The sweep direction: `verifyUnverifiedGloasPayloads` still looks only at the selected head and its ancestors.
- ForwardSync records the status before it queues the block and its envelope in the block collector, which it flushes after the replay; a flush failure is logged, not returned. This order is unchanged.
- A stale-head guard for block production, for example refusing to produce while the served head is far behind the highest seen slot.
- `is_syncing` and `is_optimistic` reporting.
- v3.7.1 is affected too; a `[r3.7]` backport will follow.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload.go`: in `applyEnvelopeCoordinated`, record the payload status also when `validatePayload` is false (`NotValidated`, or `Validated` if a validated verdict is cached).
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload_test.go`: `TestOnExecutionPayloadWithoutEngineMarksPayloadOptimistic` has a new case that attaches a mock engine, which fails the test on any `NewPayload` call, and calls `OnExecutionPayload` with `validatePayload=false`. Both cases now use a fork graph that tracks accepted payloads and check that the payload is not verified.
- `cl/phase1/stages/chain_tip_sync_recovery_test.go`: `TestForwardSyncReplayMakesGloasPayloadAvailableForHeadSelection` replays one envelope through the forward-sync helper `processDownloadedGloasEnvelope` with an insertion-capable EL, adds a child that builds on the replayed block's FULL payload, and checks that this child becomes the head without a `NewPayload` call.

## Testing

- **TDD:** with the production file from `main`, `TestOnExecutionPayloadWithoutEngineMarksPayloadOptimistic/without_EL_validation` fails (the payload is not available) and `TestForwardSyncReplayMakesGloasPayloadAvailableForHeadSelection` fails (the head stays at the parent instead of moving to the child that builds on its FULL payload). Both pass with the fix.
- Without the cached `Validated` check (always `NotValidated`), the existing `TestExecutionPayloadIngressAppliesTerminalResultBeforeDuplicateShortCircuit` fails.
- `TestExecutionPayloadIngressAppliesTerminalResultBeforeDuplicateShortCircuit`, `TestPersistedEnvelopeDoesNotSynthesizeValidatedELResult`, `TestLocalSelfBuildPreservesTerminalInvalidationAcrossYield` and `TestForwardSyncValidatesOnlyWhenInsertionIsUnavailable` pass unchanged.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/stages/...`
- Consensus spec tests `Test/mainnet/.*/fork_choice` (v1.7.0-beta.2): same results as on `main`, no failures.
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.
- Not yet run on a devnet or Sepolia with this change. The tests cover one replayed block and its child, with a fake block collector; they do not cover a full restart, EL insertion, the sweep or the forkchoice update.

author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/beacon/handler: proposer_lookahead reads epoch data by slot
body:
For a state outside the fork-choice cache, `proposer_lookahead` looked up epoch data with the epoch number as the key instead of the epoch-start slot, which every other `ReadEpochData` caller passes, so the lookup missed and the handler panicked on the nil result, or returned another epoch's lookahead when the epoch was a multiple of 32. It now uses the epoch-start slot, answers 404 when the data is missing and 400 for pre-Fulu states, as the Beacon API requires.

Part of #24881.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: close the persistent block collector when the stage loop exits
body:
`NewPersistentBlockCollector` closed its MDBX env only from a goroutine waiting on `context.Background().Done()`, which never fires, so the env was never closed and the goroutine leaked for the life of the process. `Close` is now part of the `BlockCollector` interface, and the Caplin stage loop closes its config, and with it the collector, when the loop exits.

Part of #24881.

The `defer stageCfg.Close()` in `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go` has no test: `RunCaplinService` has no seam for it.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/beacon/handler: attestation_data answers 503 when the head cannot be read
body:
When the fork-choice head could not be read, Gloas `attestation_data` swallowed the error and served payload index 0 (payload absent), so a validator could vote "empty" for a block whose payload is FULL. It now answers 503, as it already does for an unverified FULL payload.

Part of #24881.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/beacon/handler: expected_withdrawals answers 404 for a pruned block body
body:
`PruneBlocks` deletes block bodies but keeps the canonical index, so on a pruned node a historical `expected_withdrawals` got nil from `ReadBlockByRoot` for the next canonical block and panicked on `blk.Version()`. It now answers 404.

Part of #24881.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/phase1/stages: chain-tip sync flushes the block collector with the stage context
body:
`chainTipSync` flushed the block collector with `context.Background()`, so a Caplin stop during chain-tip sync waited for every `InsertBlocks` and `ForkChoiceUpdate` batch of the flush, behind the EL's in-flight work. It now passes the stage context, as forward sync already does.

Part of #24881.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/transition: ProcessSyncAggregate fails closed when the domain cannot be computed
body:
With full validation, `ProcessSyncAggregate` returned nil when `fork.Domain` failed, so the sync committee's BLS signature was never checked and the aggregate was accepted. The error is now returned. Today only a nil `Fork` reaches this path, but the code must fail closed.

Part of #24881.

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: bound the checkpoint state cache
body:
## Summary

`ForkChoiceStore.checkpointStates` caches the checkpoint states that `getCheckpointState` builds: effective balances, active and slashed bitsets, the shuffled active indices and a copy of the RANDAO mixes. In local benchmarks with one million validators, each entry retained about 18-22 MB. The cache has no size bound: entries are removed only by `onNewFinalized`, when finality advances, and only those below the new finalized epoch.

While finality does not advance, every checkpoint state that `getCheckpointState` builds stays in memory:

- each new justified checkpoint: `getHeadGloas`, `getHeadOnce` (when it gets no auxiliary state), the same-slot Gloas head check in `OnBlock`, `isHeadWeak` and `NewWeightStore` read the state of the current justified checkpoint;
- attestation targets in `OnAttestation`. On `main` this path runs only after fork choice is marked synced and before the first head state is published (`syncedDataManager.Syncing()`). With #24807 (open), `OnAttestation` also reads the target checkpoint state after that, when the head state does not have the target's shuffling, so during a persistent split without finality each side-branch target with a different shuffling adds an entry.

Now an insert leaves at most `maxCheckpointStates` = 10 entries in the cache, about 180-220 MB at one million validators. Prysm bounds its checkpoint state cache to 10 entries as well, and Teku's default is 20. Ten leaves nine entries next to the justified one, enough for the current- and previous-epoch targets of four branches.

After each insert, `storeCheckpointState` evicts the entries with the lowest epoch above the cap. It never evicts:

- the current justified checkpoint, which is read to compute the head. Rebuilding it took about 230-290 ms at one million validators in local benchmarks;
- the entry just stored, so that a call does not evict its own result.
