Processing the empty slots after the head carries the head root into their block roots, so until another block arrives, the dependent root of a slot at or after the head slot is the head root.

In the first case, if there is no reorg and the next block comes after the dependent slot, that block changes the answer from the older root to the root that was the head at the first query. As a result:

- validator clients can report a duties re-org even though the duties did not change, and
- Caplin rejects proposer preferences signed with the older root (`dependent root is not a possible dependent block`), because that root is neither the current head nor the parent of an imported block at or after the start of the epoch after the dependent slot.

The changed helper is used by attester duties, proposer duties v1 and proposer duties v2 (which uses the attester slot from Fulu on). PTC duties and `head_v2` events compute their dependent roots separately, sync committee duties have no dependent root, and historical duty queries use separate paths.

## Change

Return the head root when the dependent slot is at or after the head slot, not only when it is equal. While the node is syncing, the behaviour does not change.

This also affects accepted lookahead requests whose dependent slot has not occurred yet: they now get the current head root, which can still change as blocks arrive, as before. The existing lookahead limits of the handlers do not change.

## Evidence

Local Kurtosis devnet with Gloas at slot 128 (Hoodi fork rehearsal, 12 s slots). Slot 479 was empty, so the dependent slot of epoch 16 (attester and proposer v2) was after the head at slot 478:

- The Lighthouse VC whose only beacon node was Caplin logged `Proposer duties re-org` for epoch 16, from the root of block 477 to the root of block 478. The same happened for epoch 6, where slot 159 was empty.
- At epoch 16, that Lighthouse VC and a Teku VC logged `dependent root is not a possible dependent block`; the Lighthouse VC also logged it at epoch 6. The client logs do not include the submitted root, so this is a timing correlation; the validation code above explains the rejection.

## Tests

`TestGetDependentRootUsesHeadRootForSlotsAfterHead` replaces `TestGetDependentRootReturnsNotFoundWhenRootUnavailable`, which expected not found for a dependent slot beyond the scan bound. The new test calls the helper for both the attester and the proposer dependent slot after the head. It gets an older root before this change and the head root after it. It does not cover the endpoints, the syncing path, or the end-to-end sequence of a block arriving after the empty dependent slot and clients fetching the duties again.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: keep pre-Gloas get_head vote weights across calls
body:
Before Gloas, every `get_head` recompute sums all validators' latest messages under `f.mu`. On a mainnet tip node that is 40–82 ms between execution and the FCU, about twice per slot. Gloas already keeps weights incrementally (`gloasWeightTree`), so this covers mainnet until Glamsterdam.

## Changes
- `voteTally` keeps per-root vote weights across calls: a rebuild when the justified checkpoint state changes, otherwise only validators whose message or equivocation changed.
- Proposer boost, `accountWeights` and the auxiliary-state path are unchanged.

## Numbers
Mainnet tip node (`awskii/v3-commitment`), 3 interleaved 40-min arms per binary:

| | base | this |
|---|---|---|
| execution done → FCU p50 | 107 ms | 41 ms (p 4e-5) |
| FCU → head updated, after the reply | 5 ms | 8 ms |

The +3 ms is Caplin's head-state copy, no longer queued behind the recount, overlapping the flush.
author: awskii

title: cl/rpc: skip column peers that answered a by-root request with no sidecars
body:
## Problem

`runDownload` in `cl/das` requests missing columns with `DataColumnSidecarsByRoot` on a 100 ms ticker until they arrive. Peer selection rotates over the peers that custody the requested columns and does not remember how a peer answered. When the peers do not have the columns and answer quickly with nothing, each download loop can ask peers up to ten times a second. Each batch of up to four blocks has its own download loop.

In a local Kurtosis devnet with Gloas at slot 128 (Hoodi fork rehearsal), the network split after the fork. In its busiest minute, a Lighthouse node received 2,351 `DataColumnsByRoot` requests, all answered with no sidecars; 2,290 of them came from four Caplin peers. Over the whole run, 9,587 of the 9,655 by-root column requests that Lighthouse received returned no sidecars.

An empty by-root response is allowed by the spec, so the responders did nothing wrong. The requester should not ask the same peer again straight away.

## Change

When a by-root column response has no sidecars, peer selection skips that peer for 2 s. Other peers remain eligible for the next request. When every eligible peer is cooling down, the request fails with `ErrNoGoodPeer` without network traffic. The cooldown is kept by peer ID across the 15 s peer refresh, and successful refreshes remove expired entries. 2 s is the maximum backoff that blob sidecar backfill already uses (`requestBlobMaxBackoff`).

Failed requests do not start a cooldown. This keeps the `main` behaviour for the local `ErrPeerBusy`, for context failures, and for peer-reported errors such as `ResourceUnavailable`. `ErrPeerBusy` is our own limit of two concurrent streams per peer and request type.

This limits repeated requests to the same peer. It does not bound the node-wide request rate: with many eligible peers, each download loop can still send up to ten requests a second to different peers. Non-empty responses that fail validation keep their current handling.

## Tests

The first two tests use `testing/synctest`.

- `TestRunDownloadDoesNotRepeatRequestsToPeerThatAnsweredNothing` (`cl/das`): one peer that always answers with no sidecars, for 20 s, so the run crosses the peer refresh. Every gap between requests is at least 2 s; on `main` it is 100 ms.
- `TestColumnSidecarsRequestSkipsPeerThatAnsweredNothing` (`cl/rpc`): with two peers that answer with no sidecars, the second request goes to the other peer at once, the third fails with `ErrNoGoodPeer`, and after 2 s a peer is asked again. On `main` the third request is sent.
- `TestColumnSidecarsRequestKeepsPeerAfterFailedRequest` (`cl/rpc`): after a failed request, the same peer is asked again at once. This test also passes on `main`; it guards the decision not to cool down after errors.
- Two existing tests send a second request to the same single peer after an empty answer to check the wrapper; they now clear the cooldown first.

Mutation checks: removing the cooldown, a cooldown that never expires, a refresh that clears active cooldowns, and a cooldown after a failed request each fail at least one of the new tests.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: take execution payload event fields from the block
body:
Caplin could emit the wrong `slot` in the `execution_payload` and `execution_payload_available` SSE events, and the wrong `builder_index` in `execution_payload`. In a capture from a local Gloas devnet, both Caplin `execution_payload` samples had `slot` and `builder_index` at 0, and both matching `execution_payload_available` samples had `slot` at 0. A Lighthouse sample from the same run, for comparison:

```
Caplin:     event: execution_payload  {"slot":"0","builder_index":"0","block_hash":"0x2b20…","block_root":"0x038f…","execution_optimistic":false}
Lighthouse: event: execution_payload  {"slot":"599","builder_index":"18446744073709551615","block_hash":"0x9d12…","block_root":"0x78f4…","execution_optimistic":false}
```

The correct `slot` is the slot of the block named by `block_root`, and the correct `builder_index` is the builder of its payload; for a self-build that is `BUILDER_INDEX_SELF_BUILD` (2^64-1).

`emitExecutionPayloadIntegrationEvents` took the slot from `Payload.SlotNumber` and the builder index from the envelope. Its callers can pass an envelope built by `envelopeForIndexRepair`, which contains only the block number and hash, so both fields were 0.

The helper now takes the slot from the beacon block and the builder index from the block's committed bid. Envelope validation already requires the envelope's builder index to match that bid. If the block is not in the store, the helper skips both events instead of emitting a wrong slot; the fallback in `cl/beacon/handler/epbs.go` behaves the same way. All four fork-choice emission sites use this helper.

`release/3.8` has the same code. I will open a backport after this merges.

## Testing

`TestExecutionPayloadOperationEventsDoNotRequireHeadData` now makes the test fork graph return a block at slot 64 with a self-build bid, passes an envelope from `envelopeForIndexRepair`, and checks the fields of both events. `TestExecutionPayloadOperationEventsSkipMissingBlock` checks that nothing is emitted without the block. Without the production change, both fail:

```
expected: &beaconevents.ExecutionPayloadData{Slot:0x40, BuilderIndex:0xffffffffffffffff, ...}
actual  : &beaconevents.ExecutionPayloadData{Slot:0x0, BuilderIndex:0x0, ...}

emitted operation event without the beacon block: &beaconevents.EventStream{Event:"execution_payload", ...}
```

- With the change, both pass.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/beacon/...` passes.
- `make lint`: 0 issues. `make erigon integration` builds.
author: domiwei

title: cl: copy each new head into a reused beacon state instead of allocating one
body:
Since #24165 every head update copies the new head into a fresh `CachingBeaconState`, ~1 GB of allocation per slot on mainnet. This copies into a spare state instead.

## Changes
- `SyncedDataManager` keeps a spare state as the copy target, rotated per publish. A failed copy drops the spare and keeps head and previous, as #23962 expects; cost: one more state (~650 MB).
- A reused buffer is overwritten one publish after it stops being previous, so two readers that kept head-state internals past their view now finish inside it: the shuffled-set pre-cache and `validator_identities`.

## Numbers
Mainnet tip node (`awskii/v3-commitment`), 3 interleaved 40-min arms per binary:

| | base | this |
|---|---|---|
| allocation | 96 MB/s | 22 MB/s |
| process CPU | 0.258 cores | 0.232 |
| anon RSS | 18.2 GB | 12.4 GB |
| flush+commit p50 | 76 ms | 60 ms |

FCU → head and validate → FCU: no change.
author: awskii

title: cl/phase1/network/gossip, cl/p2p: subscribe to the persistent attestation subnets
body:
## Summary

Without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`, Caplin advertises attestation subnets 0 and 1 in its ENR `attnets`, but it subscribes to no attestation subnet unless a validator duty asks for one (line numbers on `main`):

- `setupENR` sets bits 0 and 1 (`cl/p2p/p2p.go:313-318`). The MetaData handlers (`cl/sentinel/handlers/heartbeats.go:72-126`) and `Sentinel.Identity` read `attnets` from the same ENR, so MetaData advertises the same bits.
- `defaultExpiryForTopic` gives every `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}` topic the expiry `time.Unix(0, 0)` (`cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go:402-407`), so `TopicSubscriptions.SubscribeWithExpiry` returns `ErrExpiryInThePast` before `Topic.Subscribe` (`gossip_subscription.go:181-188`). The topics are joined, but nothing subscribes them. The only other path that starts an attestation subscription is the beacon committee subscription of a validator duty, which lasts two epochs (`cl/validator/committee_subscription/committee_subscription.go:87-97`); the fork-digest lookahead copies existing subscriptions to the next digest.
- `TopicSubscriptions` also sets and clears the `attnets` bit of an attestation topic on its first subscription, its expiry, `Unsubscribe` and `Remove` (`gossip_subscription.go:136-141`, `159-164`, `194-200`, `232-237`). So duty subnets are advertised while their two-epoch subscription lasts, a duty that expires on subnet 0 or 1 clears the initial bit, and the removal of the old fork digest's topics, 16 slots after a fork-digest change is detected with an 8-slot lookahead (`gossip_manager.go:563-614`), clears the bits of the old digest's subscribed topics, also when the same subnet is still subscribed under the new digest. A node with `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` therefore advertises no attestation subnet after its first fork-digest change (BPO forks change the digest too), although it is still subscribed to all 64.

The phase0 p2p spec, [Attestation subnet subscription](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1804-L1845):

> each beacon node should:
> - Remain subscribed to `SUBNETS_PER_NODE` for `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` epochs.
> - Maintain advertisement of the selected subnets in their node's ENR `attnets` entry by setting the selected `subnet_id` bits to `True` (e.g. `ENR["attnets"][subnet_id] = True`) for all persistent attestation subnets.
> - Select these subnets based on their node-id as specified by the following `compute_subscribed_subnets(node_id, epoch)` function.

`SUBNETS_PER_NODE` is 2 and `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` is 256. `compute_subscribed_subnet` shuffles the 6-bit node-ID prefix with a seed from `(epoch + node_id % 256) // 256`, so each node gets two consecutive subnets, selected again every 256 epochs at an epoch staggered by its node ID (the new pair can overlap the old one). [MetaData](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L455-L477): "`attnets` is a `BitVector` representing the node's persistent attestation subnet subscriptions", and [the ENR `attnets` entry](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1733-L1747) must equal `MetaData.attnets` when it has a non-zero bit. The validator guide's [Lookahead](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/validator.md#L325-L359) says that when too few peers are subscribed to a duty subnet, the validator must find peers whose ENR `attnets` has the subnet's bit and validate them with `GetMetaData`.

Other clients:

- Prysm computes the pair with the node-ID shuffle and caches it for the epochs left in the current selection period ([subnets.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/p2p/subnets.go#L494-L577)), builds ENR and MetaData `attnets` from that cache only ([discovery.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/p2p/discovery.go#L154-L305), [subnet_ids.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/cache/subnet_ids.go#L107-L123)), and joins the persistent and aggregator subnets ([subscriber.go](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L236-L244), [persistentAndAggregatorSubnetIndices](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/120bdea8a5d74b3d8da7359a44ddcd89ce4476cb/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L799-L805)).
- Teku computes the pair and the slot at which it rotates ([MiscHelpers.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/ethereum/spec/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/spec/logic/common/helpers/MiscHelpers.java#L285-L338)), checks it on every slot and subscribes the new pair once the old one has expired ([NodeBasedStableSubnetSubscriber.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/networking/eth2/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/eth2/gossip/subnets/NodeBasedStableSubnetSubscriber.java#L51-L105)), keeps one unsubscription slot per subnet, the later of the persistent and the aggregation one, and sets the ENR from the persistent subnets only ([AttestationTopicSubscriber.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/networking/eth2/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/eth2/gossip/subnets/AttestationTopicSubscriber.java#L54-L177)).
- Lighthouse (stable) derives two consecutive subnets from the node-ID prefix, without the shuffle and the rotation, "for the duration of the node's runtime" ([subnet_id.rs](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/consensus/types/src/attestation/subnet_id.rs#L103-L128)). It subscribes to them and adds them to the ENR at startup ([subnet_service/mod.rs](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs#L116-L174)); short-lived attestation subscriptions are subscribed and removed without ENR changes; the only other ENR updates are for sync committee subnets ([subnet_service/mod.rs](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs#L433-L600)).

Consequences: a default Caplin node gives the attestation subnets none of the two-subnet backbone that the spec asks of every node. It still claims subnets 0 and 1, so peers that look for peers on those subnets through discovery and MetaData can pick a Caplin node that is not in the topic, and the duty and fork-rollover updates make the advertised bits disagree with the actual subscriptions in both directions.

The change:

- `subnets.ComputeSubscribedSubnets` implements `compute_subscribed_subnets` with the existing `shuffling.ComputeShuffledIndex`, and `subnets.SubscribedSubnetsRotationEpoch` returns the next epoch at which the seed changes (both use plain `uint64` arithmetic, which cannot overflow for an epoch a clock can reach).
- `GossipManager.SetLocalNodeID` takes the discovery node ID (`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go` passes `localNode.ID()`, as for PeerDAS). The new `subscribePersistentAttestationSubnets` computes the pair for the current epoch, calls `SubscribeWithExpiry` with the start of the second slot of the rotation epoch on every registered `beacon_attestation` topic of the pair (on every fork digest), and sets `attnets` to exactly the pair. It runs when the node ID is set, at the end of each gossip service registration, and on the existing per-slot tick of `goCheckForkAndResubscribe`. It does nothing with `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`.
- Startup: `run.go` sets the node ID before `RegisterGossipServices`, so the pair is advertised from just before the gossip services are registered. After the attestation service has joined its 64 topics, the call at the end of its registration subscribes the pair, without waiting for a tick.
- Fork-digest change: `subscribeUpcomingTopics` already copies each topic's expiry to the new digest's topic, so the pair is subscribed under both digests from the lookahead (about 8 slots before the change) on; the per-slot call covers both digests (including a rotation inside the overlap), and removing the old digest's topics no longer changes `attnets`.
- Duties: `SubscribeWithExpiry` only moves an expiry later, so a duty and the persistent subscription on the same topic do not shorten each other, and duties no longer change `attnets`.
- ENR: `UpdateENRAttSubnets(subnetIndex, on)` is replaced by `SetENRAttSubnets(subnets)`, which writes the whole field once. `LocalNode.Set` ignores an entry equal to the current one, so a per-slot call with an unchanged pair does not re-sign the ENR or bump its sequence number; `attnets` changes when the node ID is first set and when the computed pair changes. Refreshes are not serialized with each other, so one that read the epoch before a rotation can write the old pair after a newer one, until the next tick; if a subscription attempt fails, the pair is still advertised and the next refresh retries. `setupENR` no longer sets bits 0 and 1: until the node ID is set, `attnets` is all zeros. With `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` it still sets all 64 bits, and they now stay set after a fork-digest change. `syncnets` handling is unchanged.
- At a rotation, the first per-slot tick after the start of the rotation epoch subscribes the new pair (later ticks retry a failure). A topic of the old pair that is not in the new pair and has no later duty expiry keeps the start of the epoch's second slot as its expiry and is cancelled by the first run of the existing 12-second expiry check after it. The extra slot covers the time until that tick, so nominally the new pair is subscribed before the old one is dropped, and both are subscribed for up to about one slot plus 12 seconds (24 seconds on mainnet).

Relation to other changes:

- #25008 makes beacon committee subscriptions subscribe to the duty subnet only for aggregators (`cl/validator/committee_subscription`). After it, a validator node without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` and without this change would be subscribed to no attestation subnet outside its aggregation duties, so this PR should land first or together with it.
- The attestation gossip budget (#24970) is max(250, 1.5 x the attestations expected on the subscribed attestation subnets). A node without duties and without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` was subscribed to none and got the 250 floor; it now has the two persistent subnets (up to four during the overlap at a rotation), e.g. 1,224 per 6 seconds on mainnet with 835,924 active validators (the S = 2 column in #24970).

## Not changed here

- `syncnets`: `TopicSubscriptions` still sets and clears sync committee bits per topic, so the old-digest removal after a fork-digest change can still clear `syncnets` bits that are subscribed under the new digest.
- `MetaData.seq_number` is still the ENR sequence number, which the spec says is independent of it; a new pair changes the ENR, so the next signed record and MetaData get a higher sequence number, as other ENR changes do.
- The spec's note that a node subscribes to the persistent subnets of an upcoming fork at least 256 epochs before it: the next digest's topics are still joined about 8 slots before the change.
- A duty subscription received after the fork-digest lookahead subscribes only the current digest's topic.
- The MetaData v3 handler, which returns without a response before Fulu.
- Duty subscriptions for non-aggregators (#25008), and the formula of the attestation gossip budget (#24970); its result now includes the persistent subnets (see above).

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/subnets/subnets.go`: `ComputeSubscribedSubnets` and `SubscribedSubnetsRotationEpoch`.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: `SetLocalNodeID` and `subscribePersistentAttestationSubnets`, called from `SetLocalNodeID`, `registerGossipService` and the per-slot tick.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: subscribing, expiring, unsubscribing and removing an attestation topic no longer change `attnets`.
- `cl/p2p/p2p_interface.go`, `cl/p2p/p2p.go`, `cl/p2p/mock_services/p2p_manager_mock.go`: `SetENRAttSubnets` replaces `UpdateENRAttSubnets`; `setupENR` no longer sets subnets 0 and 1 without subscribe-all.
- `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`: pass the node ID to the gossip manager.
- Tests: new `cl/phase1/network/subnets/subnets_test.go` and `cl/phase1/network/gossip/persistent_attestation_subnets_test.go`, new tests in `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription_test.go` and `cl/p2p/p2p_enr_cgc_test.go`; the `UpdateENRAttSubnets` expectations are removed from `gossip_subscription_test.go` and `cl/phase1/network/registry/register_attestation_budget_test.go`, and the stub in `cl/sentinel/ban_on_connection_test.go` implements `SetENRAttSubnets`.

## Testing

- **TDD**, with the production files from `main`:
  - `TestAttestationDutySubscriptionDoesNotUpdateENR`, `TestAttestationDutyExpiryDoesNotUpdateENR` and `TestAttestationOldDigestRemovalDoesNotUpdateENR` (strict P2P mock) fail with `Unexpected call to *mock_services.MockP2PManager.UpdateENRAttSubnets([3 true])`, `([3 false])` from the expiry check and `([3 false])` from `Unsubscribe`.
  - `TestSetupENRAttestationSubnets` fails without subscribe-all (`expected: 0x0, actual: 0x2` set bits); its subscribe-all case passes before and after.
  - `TestComputeSubscribedSubnets`, `TestSetENRAttSubnets` and the gossip manager tests `TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsStartupOrder`, `TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsRotate`, `TestPersistentAttestationSubnetDutyDoesNotShortenExpiry`, `TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsSurviveForkRollover` and `TestPersistentAttestationSubnetsSubscribeAll` use the new functions and do not build on `main`. Mutations of the change also make the gossip manager tests and `TestSetENRAttSubnets` fail: removing the call at the end of `registerGossipService` or in `SetLocalNodeID` breaks the startup order test, limiting the refresh to the current fork digest breaks the fork rollover test, removing the subscribe-all check breaks the subscribe-all test, an expiry at the start of the rotation epoch or one hour later breaks the startup, rotation, duty and fork rollover tests, and a `SetENRAttSubnets` that keeps existing bits breaks `TestSetENRAttSubnets`.
- `TestComputeSubscribedSubnets` checks 16 vectors from a Python transcription of the spec's `compute_subscribed_subnet` (with `SHUFFLE_ROUND_COUNT` 90): node IDs 0x00..00, 0xff..ff, 0x0c..0c and 0xa000..07 (offsets 0, 255, 12 and 7) on both sides of their rotation epochs, and the wrap from subnet 63 to 0.
- The gossip manager tests call the persistent-subnet and fork helpers directly with a mocked clock instead of waiting for the tickers.

title: cl/validator/committee_subscription: subscribe to the duty subnet only for aggregators
body:
## Summary

On a synced node, each entry of `POST /eth/v1/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions` that `CommitteeSubscribeMgmt.AddAttestationSubscription` processes requests a subscription to the `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}` topic of the entry's slot and committee on the current fork digest (the subnet is computed with the head state's committee count), with an expiry two epochs after the request (an existing later expiry is kept). It does this whether or not the validator is an aggregator: `is_aggregator` only decides whether the duty is registered in the aggregation pool (`AddAggregatorDuty`).

Each validator has one attestation duty per epoch, and a subscription lasts two epochs, so with V validators about 2V duties are subscribed at any time, on subnets that are spread uniformly. That is about 64 x (1 - (63/64)^(2V)) subnets:

| Validators | Subscribed subnets now | Attestations per slot on them (mainnet) | Aggregator subnets (expected) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2.0 | ~810 | 0.08 |
| 10 | 17 | ~7,060 | 0.8 |
| 32 | 41 | ~16,590 | 2.5 |
| 64 | 55 | ~22,640 | 4.9 |

From Electra on every attester publishes one `SingleAttestation`, so with 835,924 active validators (the mainnet figure #24970 uses) a subnet carries about 408 attestations per slot. The last column assumes 408-member committees, where a validator is an aggregator with probability 1/25 (`TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_COMMITTEE` = 16).

The node receives the attestations of every subscribed subnet, and the gossipsub message-ID function decompresses each one. Attestations admitted by the attestation gossip budget then go through decoding and validation, which includes a committee check against the head state and signature verification, and accepted ones are relayed to mesh peers. Since #24970 the budget, shared by all subnets, is set at the start of each 6-second window to max(250, 1.5 x the attestations expected on the subscribed attestation subnets in that window), with integer arithmetic rounding down, so above its 250 floor the decoding and validation work it admits grows with the number of subscribed subnets.

The consensus specs only require the subscription for aggregators. The phase0 validator guide, [Lookahead](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/12c8b24bc09b12f62688d439ba20ef00b1fdfe1f/specs/phase0/validator.md#lookahead): "If the validator is assigned to be an aggregator for the slot (see `is_aggregator()`), then subscribe to the topic." and "If the validator is _not_ assigned to be an aggregator, the validator only needs sufficient number of peers on the topic to be able to publish messages. The validator does not need to _subscribe_ and listen to all messages on the topic." The [beacon API](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/01e99a6530b22941f619bde525cbf8bb61991d42/apis/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions.yaml#L4-L10) says the same:

> If validator `is_aggregator`, beacon node must:
> - announce subnet topic subscription on gossipsub
> - aggregate attestations received on that subnet

For committee subscriptions, Lighthouse, Prysm and Teku subscribe to the requested subnet only for aggregators: [Lighthouse](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/6db6ae9382b7d6f5bd1e0ca0d349bc0dc94adba2/beacon_node/network/src/subnet_service/mod.rs#L265-L275) calls `subscribe_to_subnet` only if `subscription.is_aggregator`; [Prysm](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/948f8d2052432ebae3f6e2194c83b35f46566a99/beacon-chain/rpc/core/subnets.go#L50-L53) records an aggregator subnet only for aggregators and [joins](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/948f8d2052432ebae3f6e2194c83b35f46566a99/beacon-chain/sync/subscriber.go#L236-L243) only persistent and aggregator subnets (attester subnets are used to find peers); [Teku](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/e59e16e32aea108df97ca40a9e68df582735e8da/beacon/validator/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/validator/coordinator/ValidatorApiHandler.java#L726-L729) calls `subscribeToCommitteeForAggregation` only if `request.isAggregator()`.

A non-aggregator's attestation does not need the subscription to be published. All 64 attestation topics are joined when the gossip service is registered (and again for the next fork digest before a fork), `PublishToForkDigest` only needs the joined topic handle, and go-libp2p-pubsub publishes on a joined topic without a subscription through fanout peers.

Now a non-aggregator request returns before the subscription. Aggregators keep the duty registration and the subnet computation, and still request the two-epoch expiry. A syncing node still answers 503 for both kinds of request.

With this change, the local aggregates that Electra block production takes from the aggregation pool (#24813) are built only from attestations on subscribed subnets (the subnets of local aggregators and, with #25007, the node's two persistent subnets, or all of them with `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`) and from attestations submitted to the node over the validator API. Other committees can reach block production only as aggregate-and-proofs, received on the `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` topic (which every node subscribes to) or submitted over the validator API.

## Not changed here

- Persistent subnets: on `main`, without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics`, the initial ENR advertises attestation subnets 0 and 1, but Caplin does not subscribe to them (attestation topics are registered with an expiry in the past), so with this change alone a validator node without an unexpired aggregator subscription would be subscribed to no attestation subnet, like a node without validators today. #25007 subscribes every node to the two persistent subnets returned by `compute_subscribed_subnets`, as the phase0 P2P spec recommends; this PR should land after it or together with it.
- The attestation gossip budget (#24970).
- Peer discovery for duty subnets: the beacon API asks the node to look for peers on the subnet of every request. Caplin does not do this per request; independently of these requests, the sentinel looks every 12 seconds for peers on subnets with fewer than 4 peers, at most 16 subnets per round.
- ENR `attnets`: not changed here. On `main`, subscribing to an attestation topic sets its subnet's bit and expiry or removal clears it, and non-aggregator requests no longer trigger these updates; #25007 removes these per-topic updates, so without `--caplin.subscribe-all-topics` `attnets` advertises only the two persistent subnets, while with the flag it advertises all 64.

## Changes

- `cl/validator/committee_subscription/committee_subscription.go`: return before the subnet subscription when the request is not for an aggregator. The `gossipManager` field uses the `gossip.Gossip` interface instead of `*gossip.GossipManager` (the constructor is unchanged), so the tests can use its mock.
- `cl/validator/committee_subscription/committee_subscription_test.go`: two new tests.

## Testing

- **TDD:** `TestAddAttestationSubscriptionDoesNotSubscribeNonAggregator` fails without the new early return (only the field type changed): `Unexpected call to *mock_services.MockGossip.SubscribeWithExpiry([beacon_attestation_1 ...])`, and passes with it. `TestAddAttestationSubscriptionSubscribesAggregator` passes before and after; it pins the aggregator subscription to the duty's subnet (subnet 1) and fails if the condition is inverted.
- A probe test on `main`, not part of this PR, published from a joined but unsubscribed attestation topic through `GossipManager.PublishToForkDigest` to a second host subscribed to it, and the message was delivered.
- `go test -p 2 ./cl/validator/committee_subscription/ ./cl/beacon/handler/`, `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/phase1/stages: take the fork-choice lock before the synced-data lock
body:
## Summary

Fixes #24923.

`ForkChoiceStore.mu` and `SyncedDataManager.mu` are both `sync.RWMutex`. The fork-choice stage took them in the opposite order to the rest of fork choice:

- The stage called `GetHead` inside `syncedData.ViewHeadState`. It also called `saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded` inside the same kind of view, and at head slots that are a multiple of 5 epochs that helper calls `GetStateAtBlockRoot`. In both cases the stage held the synced-data read lock while it waited for `f.mu`.
- `OnAttestation` and `OnAttesterSlashing` can take the synced-data read lock while they hold `f.mu`. `OnBlock` can do the same indirectly while it reconstructs a state.

When a node publishes its own block, the request goroutine updates the synced head state in `storeBlockAndBlobs` and can wait for the synced-data write lock behind existing readers. A queued writer blocks new readers, so these three goroutines could block each other permanently.

## Changes

- **One lock order: `f.mu`, then the synced-data lock.** No production caller takes `f.mu` while it holds a synced-data lock any more. I checked every production `ViewHeadState`, `ViewHeadStateWithIdentity` and `ViewPreviousHeadState` callback in `cl/`. Only the two stage sites above took `f.mu`; the other callbacks call only fork-choice methods that do not take it.
- **`GetHeadWithSyncedHeadState`.** A new method on `*ForkChoiceStore`. It computes the head the same way `GetHead(headState)` did with the synced head state, but it reads that state itself while it holds `f.mu`, as `OnAttestation` does. The synced-data read lock is held only while the votes are computed.
  - If a pre-Gloas recomputation needs the synced head state and there is none, it returns `synced_data.ErrNotSynced` without changing the cached head. The stage then falls back to `GetHead(nil)`, as before. The cached-head, anchor and Gloas paths do not read the synced head state.
  - The head-selection code and the source of its inputs do not change. Vote weights come from the synced head state, with optional LMD sampling. The proposer boost uses the cached justified checkpoint state when it is available, and the synced head state otherwise. Because the view is now opened after `f.mu` is taken, a head state published in the meantime can be the one used.
  - `GetHead` keeps its signature and behaviour for its other callers.
- **Stage.**
  - `computeAndNotifyServicesOfNewForkChoice` calls the new method outside any synced-data view.
  - `postForkchoiceOperations` calls `saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded` after the view returns and passes the stage's `headSlot`. The head-state dump and the shuffling pre-cache stay inside the view.
- **`LoadJustifiedCheckpointState` removed.** The stage called it before `ViewHeadState` only so that the justified checkpoint state was not loaded under the synced-data read lock. `getHeadOnce` and `getHeadGloas` already load it before they take `f.mu` or the synced-data lock.

## Behaviour changes

- **`f.mu` waits.** While the stage holds `f.mu`, it can now wait for the synced-data read lock if a head-state writer is queued: until the readers already in progress finish and the writer releases the lock. `OnAttestation`, `OnAttesterSlashing` and `OnBlock` already wait like this. In return, the stage holds the synced-data read lock for a much shorter time: only while the votes are computed, instead of during the whole `GetHead` call, including the wait for `f.mu`.
- **Finalized-state cadence.** The finalized-state persistence cadence uses the head slot that the stage selected. Before, it used the slot of the synced head state viewed afterwards. They differ only if a published block replaces the synced head state between the two calls. If the two slots are on different sides of a 5-epoch boundary, that call can save when the old code would not, or the other way round. The saved state is the finalized checkpoint state in both cases. The pre-cache call now comes before the save, so a save error no longer prevents the pre-cache from being scheduled.
- **Justified state loading.** The stage no longer loads the justified checkpoint state itself before each head computation. The state is loaded when the head is recomputed, before `f.mu` or the synced-data lock is taken. Before, a load that failed in the stage was tried again in `getHeadOnce` or `getHeadGloas`. With a synced head state there is now no immediate second attempt: if the load fails, the pre-Gloas proposer boost uses the synced head state and Gloas gives zero attestation weight, as both did before when both attempts failed. Without a synced head state, the stage falls back to `GetHead(nil)`, which tries the load again.

## Not changed

- `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` still runs inside the synced-data view, as before. It does not take `f.mu`.

## Tests

- **Red tests.** `TestComputeForkChoiceDoesNotInvertSyncedDataLockOrder` and `TestPostForkchoiceOperationsDoesNotInvertSyncedDataLockOrder` fail on `main` with "operation deadlocked". They reproduce the cycle with the real locks:
  - the stage holds the synced-data read lock, paused in a `ViewHeadState` wrapper;
  - `OnAttesterSlashing` holds `f.mu`;
  - an `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` writer is queued.

  Short sleeps (250 ms) arrange these steps, and the waits on the stage operation have time limits, so the deadlock makes the test fail instead of hanging. On the fixed code, `computeAndNotifyServicesOfNewForkChoice` does not enter the wrapped view at all.
- **Lock order inside fork choice.** `TestGetHeadWithSyncedHeadStateTakesForkChoiceLockFirst` pauses the call while it loads the checkpoint state. It checks that neither lock is held at that point, and that the synced-data lock is not taken before `f.mu`. Mutation checks confirmed that it fails in each of these cases:
  - the synced-data view wraps the head computation;
  - the view is entered before `f.mu`;
  - the checkpoint load moves under `f.mu`.
- **Behaviour.** Further tests check that:
  - the new method returns the same head as `GetHead(headState)` on a pre-Gloas store with votes and a proposer boost (without LMD sampling);
  - it leaves the cached head unchanged when it returns `ErrNotSynced`;
  - a failed checkpoint load still gives a head;
  - the stage falls back to `GetHead(nil)` when there is no synced head state.
- **Removed test.** `TestComputeForkChoiceLoadsJustifiedStateBeforeViewingHeadState` is removed, because the stage no longer views the head state around `GetHead`. The new lock-order test checks that the checkpoint state is loaded outside both locks.
- **Validation.**
  - `go test` for `cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`, `cl/phase1/stages/...`, `cl/beacon/...` and `cl/phase1/network/...`;
  - `-race -count=10` for the new tests;
  - the CL spec tests (v1.7.0-beta.4);
  - `make lint`;
  - `make erigon integration`.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network/services: verify gossip aggregates on nodes with validators
body:
Part of #24554 (point 2).

## Problem

Since #18521, a Fulu node verifies a gossip aggregate only when a local validator proposes in the current or next epoch (`isLocalValidatorProposer`). In other epochs every aggregate returns `ErrIgnore`. So a validator node:

- does not relay `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` in most epochs (gossipsub forwards only accepted messages);
- fills its block attestation pool only after a local proposal is detected, and keeps stale entries between proposals;
- does not pass aggregate votes to fork choice.

On a mainnet validator node (release/3.8), accepted bytes on `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` are 0 outside proposal epochs.

## Change

- A node with validators verifies every aggregate, as before #18521.
- Nodes without validators still skip them, which keeps the goal of #18521.
- `isLocalValidatorProposer` and its proposer-index cache are removed.

## Cost

About 1,000 aggregates per slot on mainnet, three signature sets each, verified in batches. The attestation op pool already holds 10 slots × 64 committees × 16 aggregators (10,240 entries), so a constant fill keeps about the last 10 slots.

## Tests

- `TestAggregateAndProofIsVerifiedWhenTheNodeHasValidators`: a Fulu head state and a local validator that proposes neither in this epoch nor the next. With validators the aggregate is verified and stored; without validators it is ignored. Fails on `main`. Mutations caught: the old gate, an always-on gate.
- `go test -race` for `cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/aggregation`, `cl/beacon/handler`; `make lint` (twice); `make erigon integration`.

## Follow-up

`sync_contribution_service.go` has the same proposer gate for sync committee contributions.

title: cl: look up execution bodies by block hash in standalone Caplin
body:
## Summary

Standalone Caplin stores pre-Gloas beacon blocks blinded and rebuilds them on read with the execution body from `ExecutionEngineReader`. That reader ignored the execution block hash:

- it asked the EL for the body at the block number (`GetBodiesByRange(number, 1)`), which is the canonical body at that height;
- it returned empty transaction and withdrawal lists when the EL had no body;
- its cache of recently produced bodies was keyed by block number.

So for a block that was not canonical on the EL, or whose payload the EL did not have yet, Caplin could rebuild the requested block with the transactions and withdrawals of another block, or with empty lists. When those lists differed, the root of the rebuilt block did not match the requested root. On a Hoodi shadow fork, a Lighthouse node on its own fork asked a standalone Caplin node for a block by root and got the canonical body at that height: 66 transactions instead of 121. Lighthouse penalised each such response as `UnrequestedBlockRoot` and then banned the Caplin peer.

Caplin's gossip path stores a block before the EL has its payload, so a by-root read in that window could also rebuild the block with empty lists.

## Changes

- **Body by hash.** `ExecutionEngineReader` gets the body with `GetBodiesByHashes`. If the EL has no body for the hash, it returns the new `snapshot_format.ErrExecutionBodyNotFound` instead of empty lists. `GetBodiesByRange` is removed from `ExecutionEngineBodyFetcher`.
- **Cache.** The body cache is keyed by block hash, so it never returns a body for another hash, and two bodies at the same height can both be cached. It holds up to 64 block hashes and evicts the oldest inserted one. `CacheBody` and `CacheBlockBody` take the block hash, and block production passes `payload.BlockHash`.
- **Embedded mode.** `ExecutionSnapshotReader` already looked bodies up by hash and returned an error when it found none. It now wraps `ErrExecutionBodyNotFound`, so both readers report a missing body in the same way.
- **Req/resp handlers.**
  - BlocksByRoot uses the existing fork-choice fallback. If the block is still unavailable, it leaves the block out and continues with the next root.
  - BlocksByRange stops at the first block whose body is unavailable. The spec allows a shorter response and requires the returned blocks to be consecutive, so stopping avoids sending a later block after a missing one.
  - BlocksByHead uses the existing fork-choice fallback and ends the response if the block is still unavailable.
- **Liveness.** The endpoint reads blocks with `ReadBeaconBlockBodyBySlot`, because it only uses consensus fields. Otherwise a missing execution body would now make it fail.

## Behaviour changes

- In standalone mode, a missing execution body for a stored pre-Gloas block makes these Beacon API endpoints return 500: the full-block and block-attestation endpoints, and the blinded-block, sync-committee-rewards and `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{block_id}` endpoints. So do expected-withdrawals reads for a state other than the head, which read the next stored block. Before, these endpoints worked with a block rebuilt from the wrong body or from empty lists, so full and blinded blocks could have the wrong root. The blob-sidecars endpoint is not affected.
- Other readers of pre-Gloas blocks, such as the state antiquary and the historical states reader, now get the error in standalone mode too, as they already did in embedded mode.
- In embedded mode, a missing body no longer returns an error that resets the BlocksByRoot, BlocksByRange or BlocksByHead stream. BlocksByRoot leaves the block out and continues; BlocksByRange and BlocksByHead end the response.
- Gloas blocks are not affected, because they do not carry an execution payload.

## Tests

- `TestExecutionEngineReaderUsesBlockHash`: with bodies for two hashes, a request for the side-chain hash returns its transactions and withdrawals.
- `TestExecutionEngineReaderRejectsMissingBody`: no body for the hash, or no engine, gives `ErrExecutionBodyNotFound`.
- `TestExecutionEngineReaderCacheMatchesBlockHash` and `TestExecutionEngineReaderCacheKeepsBodiesAtSameHeight`: the cache does not return a body for another hash, and it keeps both bodies at one height.
- `TestExecutionSnapshotReaderReportsMissingBody`: the embedded reader returns `ErrExecutionBodyNotFound`.
- `TestBeaconSnapshotReaderPropagatesUnavailableExecutionBody`: the error reaches `ReadBlockByRoot` and `ReadBlockBySlot` callers. This already worked; the test protects it because the handlers now rely on it.
- `TestBlockHandlersOmitUnavailableExecutionBody`: BlocksByRange does not send the block after an unavailable one. With no fork-choice fallback configured, BlocksByRoot and BlocksByHead send nothing.
- `TestLivenessEndpointReadsConsensusBodyWithoutExecutionData`: liveness works when the full block cannot be read.
- `TestCacheExecutionBodyUsesBlockHash`: block production passes the payload number and hash to `CacheBlockBody`.

Mutation checks: each of these changes, reverted on its own, makes the matching test fail: the lookup by hash, the not-found error instead of empty lists, the hash-keyed cache, the payload hash in block production, the stop in BlocksByRange, and the body-only read in liveness.

Validation: `go test` for `cl/persistence/...`, `cl/sentinel/...`, `cl/beacon/...`, `cl/phase1/...`, `cl/antiquary/...`, `cl/das/...` and `db/snapshotsync/freezeblocks/...`; `-race -count=5` for the new tests; `make lint`; `make erigon integration`.

release/3.8 and release/3.7 have the same `ExecutionEngineReader` and need backports.
author: domiwei

title: cl: pick the sync committee by the message slot
body:
Fixes #24694.

## Problem

Members assigned to slot `S + 1` sign sync committee messages and contributions for slot `S`. Caplin chose the committee from the head slot instead, in three places:

- the gossip subnet check (`subnets.ComputeSubnetsForSyncCommittee`);
- the sync contribution service (`getSyncSubcommitteePubkeys`);
- the sync contribution pool (`AddSyncCommitteeMessage`).

At the last slot `P − 1` of a period, the next committee signs. A message that arrives before the node imports block `P − 1` is checked with the head still at `P − 2`, so against the current committee. The node rejects valid next-committee members with `validator is not into any subnet N` and bans their peers. The issue's case, a previous-slot message seen with the head already at `P − 1`, is the opposite mistake.

A Hoodi validator node logged this at every period boundary between 2026-09-19 and 2026-10-16 (13 bursts, all in slot `P − 1`, 0.5–4.1 s into the slot, up to ~100 rejected messages and 1–9 banned peers each). Details in the issue.

## Change

- `state.SyncCommitteeForMessageSlot(state, slot)` returns the current committee when `slot + 1` is in the state's period, the next committee when it is in the following period, and `ErrSyncCommitteeNotInState` otherwise.
- The subnet check, the contribution service and the pool use it with the message or contribution slot. A slot whose committee the state does not hold is ignored, not rejected.
- `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` computes the subnets for the message slot. The subscription endpoint keeps the head slot.
- The pool's cleanup dropped every contribution whose slot differed from the head slot, so a message for the slot after the head was aggregated and then deleted at once. It now keeps the head slot and the next one, so a stalled head cannot let later slots accumulate.
- Conditions that do not need the committee run before the committee lookup: the validator index in `ComputeSubnetsForSyncCommittee` (an unknown index stays a REJECT) and the aggregator selection proof in the contribution service.
- `POST /eth/v1/validator/contribution_and_proofs` reports a contribution whose committee is not in the head state as a failure instead of publishing it.

## Tests

- `TestSyncCommitteeForMessageSlot`: committee choice around a period boundary, and slots outside the state.
- `TestSyncCommitteesChecksTheCommitteeOfTheMessageSlot`: the issue's case, the last slot before its block is imported, a current-committee member signing for the last slot (still rejected), and a committee outside the head state (ignored).
- `TestSyncSubcommitteePubkeysUseTheCommitteeOfTheContributionSlot` and `TestSyncContributionPoolAggregatesTheLastSlotOfAPeriodBeforeItsBlock`.
- `TestSyncContributionServiceCommitteeNotInHeadState`, `TestPoolContributionsAndProofsReportsCommitteeNotInHeadState`, `TestPoolSyncCommitteesPublishesTheLastSlotOfAPeriodOnTheNextCommitteeSubnet`, `TestSyncContributionPoolKeepsTheHeadSlotAndTheNextOne`, and an unknown-validator row in `TestSyncCommitteesChecksTheCommitteeOfTheMessageSlot` (added after review).
- The new tests fail on `main`. Mutations caught: swapped committees, the period of `slot` instead of `slot + 1`, the head slot in each of the three call sites, a rejection instead of an ignore, the old pool cleanup, either pool bound removed, the committee lookup before the index check, the selection-proof check after it, the head slot in `PostEthV1BeaconPoolSyncCommittees`, and publishing an ignored contribution over REST.
- `go test -race` for `cl/phase1/core/state`, `cl/phase1/network/services`, `cl/validator/...`, `cl/beacon/handler/...`; `make lint` (twice); `make erigon integration`. The spec tests were not run locally (fixtures not downloaded); CI runs them.
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon/handler: keep payload preparation state work away from the builder cutoff
body:
Part of #24119 (item 1). Items 2 and 3 are not covered here.

## Problem

Payload preparation admitted an attempt while more than `minimumPreparationLead` (500 ms) remained before the proposal slot, and the same 500 ms was the builder cutoff. The head-state copy and slot processing cannot be cancelled mid-call. So an attempt admitted late spent its remaining lead on state work and was then discarded by the post-work check, after it had competed with production for CPU and for the head-state read lock.

The loop ticks every quarter slot from when it starts, not from a slot boundary, so the last tick before a proposal can fall anywhere from 0 to 3 s before the slot. A head that changes late in the slot (a late block) makes the loop start the state work again near the cutoff.

## Change

- `stateWorkLead(slotDuration)` = `minimumPreparationLead` + one eighth of a slot: 2 s on 12-second slots.
- The loop admits an attempt only with more than `stateWorkLead` left.
- `preparePayloadForWithScratch` checks it again inside the head-state view, right before the copy, because the view can wait behind a head-state writer.
- The builder cutoff is unchanged: the post-work check and the deadline of the builder start still use 500 ms.
- The "Gloas preparation window is too short" warning compares the post-PTC window with `stateWorkLead`. On 12-second slots the window is 3 s, so the attempt at the payload attestation deadline is still admitted.
- The "primed execution layer" log line reports `stateWork`, the time from the start of the copy to the end of slot processing, so the budget can be checked on live nodes.

With 12-second slots, a head selected in the first two thirds of the slot is still prepared on a later tick. A head that changes in the last 2 s is left to normal production, which stays the fallback.

## Why an eighth of a slot

From two validator nodes on release/3.8 (one mainnet, one Hoodi):

- Head-state copy (`CachingBeaconState.CopyInto`): 2.81 s and 1.77 s of CPU in 60-second CPU profiles, about five copies each, so roughly 0.56 s (mainnet) and 0.35 s (Hoodi) of CPU per copy.
- Epoch processing (`epoch_processing_time`): 275 ms (mainnet) and 210 ms (Hoodi), the last observed value.

A copy plus an epoch transition is under 1 s on mainnet, so 1.5 s of budget leaves headroom for a loaded node. The figures are per-copy CPU estimates and single samples, not wall-clock percentiles; the new `stateWork` field gives the wall-clock value.

## Tests

- `TestPreparePayloadLoopSkipsStateWorkWithoutItsLead`: with 1 s left on 12-second slots, the loop does not open the head-state view.
- `TestPreparePayloadForRejectsStateWorkWithoutItsLead`: with 1 s left inside the view, the attempt returns `errPreparationTooLate` and does not copy the state.
- `TestPreparePayloadLoopWarnsWhenGloasWindowCannotFitStateWork`: on 4-second slots, the 1 s post-PTC window triggers the warning.
- These fail on `main`. Mutations caught: the loop using the builder cutoff, no check before the copy, the old warning threshold, no state-work budget, and a budget of a quarter slot (which breaks the Gloas post-PTC tests).
- Three existing loop tests used leads at the new boundary (2 s on 12-second slots, 600 ms on 1-second slots) and now use 2.5 s and 700 ms. `TestPreparePayloadLoopMemoizesRealPreparation` checks two eligible ticks instead of three: with a 2 s margin and the attestation-due wait, its 7-second window can no longer hold three.
- `go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler/...`, `make lint` (twice), `make erigon integration`.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/network/registry: sweep idle peer limiters inside acquire
body:
`newTokenBucketRateLimiter` started a `cleanup` goroutine that slept 10 s in a loop forever, 13 per `RegisterGossipServices`. `acquire` wrote `lastAccess` to a copy of the map value, so the sweep wiped every bucket every 10 s. Closes #20663.

## Changes
- Sweep buckets idle over 3 min inside `acquire`, at most once per 10 s, under the existing mutex; no goroutine.
- The map holds `*tokenBucketLimiter`, so `lastAccess` persists. Per-peer limits now hold at their configured rate instead of gaining `burst` tokens every 10 s.

## Notes
Mainnet tip node, internal Caplin, 30-min windows: `cleanup` goroutines 13 → 0, head blocks 145/145 and 151/151 slots, equal accepted column bytes across 8 subnets, 0 EROR.
author: awskii

title: cl: keep a wider sync contribution window and publish only accepted contributions
body:
Follow-up to #25027, from yperbasis's review.

## Changes

- **Sync contribution pool window.** The pool kept only the head slot and the next one. After two empty slots, the next proposer reads `GetSyncAggregate` for head+2, and an aggregator at head+2 reads `GetSyncContribution` for it; both got an empty result, because the entry was removed right after it was aggregated. The pool now keeps slots from the head to one epoch after it. That still bounds what is kept while the head stalls.
- **`POST /eth/v1/validator/contribution_and_proofs`.** The handler published a contribution the service ignored, for example one rejected by the clock check, although it was not verified. It now reports every ignore as a pooling failure instead of publishing it. A contribution for an already-seen (aggregator, slot, subcommittee) still returns `nil` before the signature checks and is published, as before; that is tracked separately.
- **Spec-test harness.** The contribution harness picks the committee with `state.SyncCommitteeForMessageSlot(beaconState, contribution.Slot)`, like the message harness, and returns "ignore" when the state does not hold it.

## Tests

- `TestSyncContributionPoolKeepsOneEpochFromTheHead`: head−1 removed; head, head+2 and head+epoch kept; head+epoch+1 removed.
- `TestSyncContributionPoolKeepsOneEpochFromTheHeadForBlocks`: the same window for the contributions the proposer reads through `GetSyncAggregate`.
- `TestPoolContributionsAndProofsReportsIgnoredContributions`: a plain ignore and a committee-not-in-state ignore both return 400 and publish nothing.
- Mutations caught: the old head+1 window, no upper bound, publishing ignored contributions.
- `go test -race` for `cl/validator/sync_contribution_pool`, `cl/phase1/network/services/...`, `cl/spectest/consensus_tests`, `cl/beacon/handler/...`; `make lint` (twice); `make erigon integration`.

The fixture head is at slot 160, so `nextPeriod` was 8192 and `SetSlot(nextPeriod - (1+2*period))` wrapped around: the two "committee not in the head state" rows tested a message period older than the head, not a head two periods behind the message. The test now starts three periods after the fixture, asserts the head stays above zero, and the `headBehind` comment says that 1 puts the head at the last slot.

No production change. The test passes; `make lint` is clean twice. To be cherry-picked to release/3.8 after merge, so the branch stays aligned with main.
author: lystopad

title: cl/gossip, cl/p2p: enforce per-topic gossip payload bounds and spec size limits
body:
Closes #24930. Part of #24417 (gossip half; the req/resp half is a separate PR).

Supersedes #24618: this branch keeps its first commit (author yperbasis), rebased on main, and adds the fixes from review.

## Problem

Gossip messages were decompressed in full twice before any check on what the topic's type can hold: once in the message-id function, which then copied the decompressed bytes again into a hashing buffer, and once in the validator. Both paths accepted up to 15 MiB uncompressed on every topic, even where the SSZ type caps the payload at a few hundred bytes. The pubsub frame limit was also 15 MiB, while the spec uses `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (10 MiB).

## Changes

- `gossip.MaxUncompressedSize`: the SSZ bound per topic for aggregates, attestation subnets, attester and proposer slashings, exits, BLS changes, sync committee messages and contributions, capped by `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`. Other topics use `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` alone.
- `gossip.DecompressMessage`, used by both the message-id function and the validator:
  - rejects `Message.data` above `max_compressed_len(MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE)`;
  - checks the per-topic bound against the snappy header before allocating.
  The message-id falls back to the invalid-snappy domain for such data, as it already did for undecodable data.
- The message-id is hashed incrementally instead of concatenating domain, topic and payload into a second buffer.
- The pubsub frame limit is the spec's `max_message_size()` (12,234,442 bytes on mainnet) instead of 15 MiB.
- `NetworkConfig.GossipMaxSize` is read from the YAML key `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, the key current spec configs use. Before this PR, nothing read the field and the key was ignored. The JSON key served by `/eth/v1/config/spec` is unchanged.
- The `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` exclusion in `cl/spectest/mainnet_config_test.go` is removed, because the key now maps to `GossipMaxSize`, which matches the spec.

For a maximal message on a small-type topic, the work before rejection goes from three decompressed copies to one varint read.

## Changes compared to #24618

- Rebased on main, with conflicts resolved against the reworked topic subscriptions.
- `MaxUncompressedSize` is capped by `GossipMaxSize`, so a topic bound never exceeds the network limit.
- The race in `TestNewPubsubValidator_RejectsPayloadAboveTopicBound`: it assigned the manager's config after `NewGossipManager` had started its goroutines. It now uses its own manager.
- `register_gloas_boundary_test.go` passed an empty `NetworkConfig`, so its gossip limit was 0 and every message was rejected. It now uses the mainnet network config.
- The compressed-size check, the `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` YAML key and the spectest exclusion are new.

## Behaviour changes to note

- RPC frames between 12,234,442 bytes and 15 MiB are now dropped. Spec-compliant clients already drop them. Peers that still use a 15 MiB frame, such as older Erigon nodes on mixed-version devnets, can lose an RPC that batches several large messages.
- A custom config that sets only the legacy `GOSSIP_MAX_SIZE` key now gets the default 10 MiB.

## Not changed (possible follow-ups)

- Static-size Gloas and light-client topics (`payload_attestation_message`, `proposer_preferences`, `light_client_*`) still use the network limit, not a type bound.
- Self-published messages skip the validator, and `PublishToForkDigest` does not check the uncompressed size. This is the same as on main.
- `GossipMaxSizeBellatrix` and `DecompressSnappy(..., true)` no longer have production readers. They stay in this PR to keep config and API compatibility, and can be removed separately.
- The bounds are not fork-aware: pre-Electra topics get the larger Electra bound, and SSZ decoding still rejects anything above the real bound.

## Testing

TDD, each behaviour red first:

- `TestDecompressSnappyWithLimit`: rejects above the limit with zero allocations.
- `TestMaxUncompressedSizeMatchesLargestEncoding`: cross-checks every hand-derived bound against `EncodingSizeSSZ()` of max-shaped `cltypes` values. `TestMaxUncompressedSizeIsCappedByNetworkLimit` covers the network cap.
- `TestDecompressMessageRejectsCompressedDataAboveMaxCompressedLen`: a valid snappy stream within the uncompressed limit but above `max_compressed_len` is rejected.
- `TestMsgIDUsesInvalidDomainAbovePayloadBounds`: covers the network limit, the per-topic bound and the compressed limit.
- `TestNewPubsubValidator_RejectsPayloadAboveTopicBound`: the message is rejected before `DecodeGossipMessage` runs.
- `TestMaxGossipMessageSizeFollowsSpec` and `TestPubsubFrameLimitFollowsMaxGossipMessageSize`: an RPC exactly at `max_message_size` is delivered, and one byte more resets the stream.
- `TestCustomConfigReadsMaxPayloadSize`.
- Mutation checks:
  - Restoring the 15 MiB frame limit makes the frame test fail.
  - Bypassing the compressed check in the message-id function makes the message-id test fail.

Checks run:

- `go test -race` for `cl/p2p`, `cl/phase1/network/gossip` and `cl/phase1/network/registry`.
- `go test -short` for `cl/gossip`, `cl/utils`, `cl/p2p/...`, `cl/clparams`, `cl/phase1/network/...` and `cl/sentinel/...`.
- `make lint`, twice.
- `make erigon integration`.

`cl/spectest` `mainnet_config` was run only against an older local fixture set, where `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` matched. CI uses the pinned fixtures.

The branch had two independent reviews, each cross-checking the other's findings, until no in-scope findings remained.
author: domiwei

title: cl/clparams, cl/rpc, cl/sentinel: bound req/resp chunks by MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE and max_compressed_len
body:
Part of #24417 (req/resp half). The gossip half is #25078.

## Problem

Caplin's req/resp read paths did not use the consensus-spec limits (`specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md`, v1.7.0-beta.2):

- `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 10 * 2**20`: the maximum uncompressed size of an RPC chunk. The length prefix must be within the SSZ type bound or `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`, whichever is smaller.
- "A reader MUST NOT read more than `max_compressed_len(n)` bytes after reading the SSZ length-prefix `n`", where `max_compressed_len(n) = 32 + n + n / 6`.

Before this PR:

| Path | Uncompressed limit | Compressed limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request / status decode (`ssz_snappy.DecodeAndReadNoForkDigest`, used by every sentinel handler, the handshake and peer selection) | 16 MB | none (only the `Exact` variant had one) |
| Client response parsing (`rpc.parseResponseData`) | 18 MB | none |
| Response byte budgets (`cl/rpc`) and the multi-chunk ceiling (`httpreqresp.maxMultiChunkResponse`) | derived from `clparams.MaxChunkSize` = 15 MiB | — |

## Changes

- `cl/clparams`: add `MaxPayloadSize = 10 MiB`.
- `cl/sentinel/communication/ssz_snappy`: reject a length prefix above `MaxPayloadSize`, and bound the compressed input of every decode by `snappy.MaxEncodedLen(n)` (identical to `max_compressed_len(n)`). The two limits are applied separately: 10 MiB applies to the decoded length, never to the compressed bytes.
- `cl/rpc`: apply the same two limits to each response chunk. The compressed limit is an `io.LimitReader` around the snappy input of one chunk, so the next chunk's result byte and context bytes stay aligned. Remove the per-envelope `len(raw) > MaxChunkSize` checks, which the per-chunk 10 MiB check now covers.
- `cl/rpc`, `cl/sentinel/httpreqresp`: compute the response byte budgets and the multi-chunk ceiling from `MaxPayloadSize`.

The sentinel handlers need no change: they decode through `ssz_snappy` and get the new limits from there.

No legitimate object exceeds 10 MiB on any supported network. The largest are `DataColumnSidecar` (about 8.8 MB at `MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK` = 4096), `BlobSidecar` (about 131 KB), and blocks, which are capped network-wide by the 10 MiB gossip limit and by EIP-7934. Compliant snappy writers emit at most `10 + n + 8 * ceil(n / 65536)` framed bytes, which is below `max_compressed_len(n)`.

## Why #13058 raised the limit, and whether that still holds

#13058 ("Bump limits from 10MiB to 15Mib", no description) changed only `cl/clparams/config.go`, in the same week as the 30M → 36M gas-limit bump (#13057):

- `GossipMaxSizeBellatrix`: 10 MiB → 15 MiB. This was the change that had an effect.
- `MaxChunkSize`: 1 MiB → 15 MiB. At that time no req/resp code read `MaxChunkSize`; req/resp used the hardcoded 16 MB and 18 MB limits shown above.

`MaxChunkSize` became the req/resp ceiling later, in #21562. So the bump was about large blocks on gossip, not about req/resp.

That reason no longer holds:
- The EIP-7623 calldata floor (Pectra) and the 8 MiB RLP block cap of EIP-7934 (Osaka) keep execution blocks well below 10 MiB.
- Every other client enforces 10 MiB, so a larger object does not propagate.

## Non-wire uses of `MaxChunkSize` (unchanged)

`clparams.MaxChunkSize` (15 MiB) stays as it is for these uses. None of them is a req/resp chunk limit.

| Use | What it bounds | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cl/cltypes/epbs_payload.go` (`ValidateForPersistence`, `EncodeSSZ`) | envelope SSZ size | unchanged, see below |
| `cl/cltypes/solid/transactions.go` | transaction list decode bounds | unchanged, local sanity bound |
| `cl/cltypes/execution_requests.go`, `cl/beacon/handler/block_production.go` | progressive execution-request list decode limit | unchanged, local sanity bound |
| `cl/phase1/core/checkpoint_sync/remote_checkpoint_sync.go`, `cl/phase1/network/beacon_downloader.go` | Beacon API HTTP body size | unchanged, not req/resp |
| `cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph/fork_graph_disk_fs.go` | envelope file size on disk | unchanged, see below |
| `cl/phase1/network/services/execution_payload_service.go` | pending-envelope memory budget | unchanged |

Possibly wrong, not fixed here: envelope validation and persistence still accept up to 15 MiB, and so does gossip until #25078 lands. A 10–15 MiB envelope can therefore be imported from Erigon gossip, but it can no longer be fetched over req/resp: an Erigon peer will serve it, and the receiver rejects the chunk. Before this PR, Erigon-to-Erigon req/resp accepted it. Other clients already reject such objects, so this only affects Erigon-only networks with very large payloads. The fix belongs at ingress (envelope validation and gossip), so it is left for #25078 and a follow-up.

`NetworkConfig.MaxChunkSize` (yaml `MAX_CHUNK_SIZE`) is not read anywhere. It is left as it is.

## Spec-config test

The `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` exclusion in `cl/spectest/mainnet_config_test.go` is kept. Gossip is not aligned on main yet. #25078 maps `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` to `NetworkConfig.GossipMaxSize` and removes the exclusion.

## Follow-ups (pre-existing, not changed by this PR)

- After #25078 merges, read the req/resp limit from the configured `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` instead of the `clparams.MaxPayloadSize` constant.
- Non-exact decodes do not check the length prefix against the SSZ type bound before decompressing. For example, a 24-byte `BeaconBlocksByRange` request may declare up to 10 MiB. Fixed-size requests could use `DecodeAndReadNoForkDigestExact`.
- Decoded bytes after the declared `n` in the same snappy frame are dropped instead of rejected, both in `parseResponseData` and in the non-exact decoder.
- `httpreqresp.ResponseCode.ErrorMessage` ignores the declared length and has no `max_compressed_len` bound. The response body cap still bounds it.
- The serving side (`EncodeAndWrite`) has no `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` check.

## Tests

TDD: each new or changed test was run against the old production code first and failed for the expected reason.

- `ssz_snappy`:
  - `TestDecodeAndReadNoForkDigestMaxPayloadSize`: 10 MiB of random bytes is accepted; 10 MiB + 1 is rejected.
  - `TestDecodeAndReadNoForkDigestBoundsCompressedInput`: a padded frame of exactly `max_compressed_len(n)` is accepted and the bytes after it stay unread; +1 is rejected.
- `rpc`:
  - `TestParseResponseDataAcceptsMaxPayloadSize`: a random 10 MiB chunk round-trips.
  - `TestParseResponseDataRejectsOversizedCompressedChunk`: a chunk of exactly the limit is accepted and the following chunk stays aligned; +1 fails in the snappy read.
  - `TestExecutionPayloadEnvelopeRequestsRejectOversizedDecompressedChunk`: now uses 10 MiB + 1.
  - The response budget assertions use `MaxPayloadSize`.
- `httpreqresp`: `TestMaxMultiChunkResponse` pins the ceiling to `1024 * (max_compressed_len(10 MiB) + 64)`.

I mutated each new limit to `-1`, and the at-limit cases failed.

Commands run, all passing:

- `go test -race -count=1 ./cl/sentinel/... ./cl/rpc/... ./cl/clparams/...`
- `go test -count=1 -run Mainnet ./cl/spectest/`
- `make lint`, several times, clean
- `make erigon integration`

## Review

Before opening, the change went through two independent reviews (standards, spec, adversarial and complexity passes), and then each review cross-checked the other's findings.

- **Round 1:** no defect in the production change. The confirmed in-scope findings were test gaps: the limits were not pinned at equality, the next chunk after an at-limit chunk was not checked, incompressible payloads were not tested, and one assertion was too weak. They were fixed in tests only.
- **Round 2:** a fresh pass over the cumulative diff by both reviewers found nothing new in scope. Only optional test nits were left: one length assertion that repeats the full-equality check that follows it, and the magic frame offsets in one test.
- The remaining findings predate this PR and are listed under "Follow-ups" above. They include the 10 MiB / 15 MiB asymmetry.
author: domiwei

title: execution/builder, txnprovider: stop waiting for the parent block once a payload is collected
body:
## Problem

`engine_getPayload` collects a payload through `GetAssembledBlock`, which calls `BlockBuilder.Stop`. `Stop` sets the interrupt flag and then waits until the build function returns or the caller's context ends. The build reads that flag only between transaction provider calls.

During transaction selection, `TxPool.best` waits until the pool has seen the build's parent block. If a forkchoice update moves the head below that parent after the build has started, the pool's `lastSeenBlock` drops below the parent and the build parks in that wait. Only a new block or the end of the build context wakes it. While the node runs, the build context ends only on `Discard`. The max-build-time watchdog calls `Stop` first and calls `Discard` only after the stop grace of half a slot. So `getPayload` blocks until the pool sees a block at the parent's height again, the grace runs out, or its own context ends. In the last two cases it gets no payload. The shutter provider has its own parent-block wait with the same effect. It is bounded by one slot, and when that deadline passes the whole build fails.

We saw this on a local Gloas shadow fork. 9 ms after a build started, a forkchoice update moved the EL head one block back. `getPayloadV6` arrived about 12 s later and waited until the head was back at the parent, about 9 s later. The consensus client gave up after 2 s and the slot was missed.

A smaller source of latency: between provider polls, the selection loop sleeps for 50 ms with `time.Sleep`, and `Stop` cannot wake it.

The spec says that for `engine_getPayloadV1` the client software MUST return the most recent version of the payload that is available in the build process at the time of the call, and gives the method a 1 s timeout.

## Fix

- New provide option `txnprovider.WithParentBlockWaitStop(stop <-chan struct{})`. Once `stop` is closed, a provider that waits for the parent block stops waiting and returns no transactions and no error. Other waits are not affected.
  - txpool: the goroutine in `best` that already wakes the condition variable on context cancellation also wakes it when `stop` is closed. The wait loop then returns no transactions and logs at Debug. A call that starts with `stop` already closed does not start that goroutine: the wait loop sees the closed channel itself, and the goroutine would only take `p.lock` to broadcast for nothing.
  - shutter: the parent-block wait context is cancelled when `stop` is closed. If the tracker has still not seen the parent, `ProvideTxns` returns no transactions, logs at Debug and counts it in the new `shutter_parent_block_wait_stopped` counter. If it has, the call goes on as before. The stop is read from the channel after the wait, not inferred from the error type, and the goroutine that watches it is started only when a stop channel is given and ends as soon as the wait returns.
  - shutter: when the one-slot parent-block deadline passes and the caller's context is still live, `ProvideTxns` now falls back to the base txn provider and logs at Warn (and counts `shutter_parent_block_missed`, as before), like the other degraded exits of the function (unknown eon, decryption-keys timeout). Before, the deadline error failed the whole build, so a `getPayload` near the end of the call's slot, or a shutter block listener that lags, gave no payload at all. `BlockTracker.Wait` now also checks the caller's cancellation before the tracker's stopped state, so a stop-driven cancellation that races a tracker shutdown is reported as a cancellation. For this, `BlockTracker.Wait` now decides its result from the tracker state: a cancellation that races a parent already there returns success, and one for a parent not yet seen always returns the context error (before, the waiter goroutine could finish first and `Wait` returned `nil`). `Wait` also broadcasts under the condition lock and joins its waiter, so a cancellation can no longer be lost between the waiter's check and `Cond.Wait`. The decryption-keys wait is not affected on purpose. The Gnosis shutter spec says the proposer holds off until it receives the decryption keys, so ending that wait at `getPayload` would drop the slot's encrypted transactions.
- `BlockBuilder.Stop` closes two channels, once. `stopped` closes at once and ends the 50 ms idle wait of the selection loop. `parentBlockWaitStopped` closes `parentBlockWaitGrace` (500 ms) later, and the selection loop passes it to every provider call as `WithParentBlockWaitStop`. This also covers the max-build-time watchdog, which calls `Stop`. The channels reach the selection loop through the build context (`stopSignalsOf`), so `BlockBuilderFunc` keeps its signature.
- Packing and finalization still use the build context, and `Discard` works as before.

A provider call that starts after the stop, when the parent is already seen, still returns transactions as before. So the packing after a stop does not change.

Why the grace: if `getPayload` arrives right after a `forkchoiceUpdated` that moved the head, the txpool may not have processed the new head yet. On `main`, the build waits until the pool catches up and then packs transactions. Ending the wait at once made such a payload empty. CI showed this: `TestAssembleBlockGasOverflow` and `TestEngineApiUnwindToSnapshotBoundaryPreservesDeletedSlots` call `getPayload` right after the forkchoice update and failed on slow runners with blocks that had no transactions. With the grace, a pool that catches up within 500 ms after the stop still fills the payload, as on `main`. A pool that stays behind the parent costs at most 500 ms more, plus finalization, instead of an unbounded wait. 500 ms is half of the Engine API's 1 s `getPayload` timeout.

Trade-off for the max-build-time watchdog: it calls the same `Stop`, so a build that is still parked in the parent-block wait when its budget ends now finishes 500 ms later with the transactions it has, possibly none, and a later `getPayload` gets that block. On `main` the build kept waiting for up to the stop grace (half a slot) and could still pack a full block if the pool caught up in that time; otherwise it was discarded and `getPayload` got no payload. The budget ends a third of a slot into the payload's own slot (`buildDuration`), so a `getPayload` that arrives after the watchdog fired is already late. I kept one grace for both cases rather than adding a `Stop` argument for it.

I did not cancel the provider call's context on stop, and treat that cancellation as the end of selection, although that would be a smaller change in the builder. It would also end the shutter decryption-keys wait. And every txpool call made after the stop would fail, because `BeginRo` checks the context, so selection would end with only what had been collected before the stop. For a `getPayload` that arrives right after `forkchoiceUpdated`, that can be nothing, although the pool has transactions. Without that extra handling, the cancellation error would make the whole build fail.

## Remaining latency (not changed here)

- `BlockAssembler.AddTransactions` (`execution/exec/block_assembler.go`) keeps packing for 500 ms after the stop request ("ensure we run for at least 500ms after the request to stop comes in from GetPayload"). The timer is checked only between transactions, and it starts again in each `AddTransactions` call.
