So the packing after a stop can take longer than 500 ms, for example while the provider keeps returning full batches. I leave this trade-off to the owners of the builder.
- Finalization (commitment, sealing) and a single heavy transaction still add to the latency.

## Relation to #22835

#22835 fixed a deadlock in the same txpool wait: `Stop` now honours the caller's context, so a cancelled or expired `getPayload` returns an error and releases the execution semaphore. The consensus client still gets no payload in that case. With this change, a `getPayload` with a live context gets the payload that has been built so far.

## Tests

Each new test was written before the production change it covers, and failed for the expected reason:

- `TestGetAssembledBlockDoesNotWaitForTxPoolBehindParent` (`execution/execmodule`): the existing `rewindingTxnProvider` seam moves the txpool head back to the block before the parent when selection starts. `GetAssembledBlock` with a live context and a 5 s deadline must return a payload built on the original parent. On `main`: `context deadline exceeded`.
- `TestGetAssembledBlockIncludesTxnsOnceTxPoolCatchesUpSoonAfterStop` (`execution/execmodule`): the same seam, with two pending transactions. The build runs in a `testing/synctest` bubble, and the txpool head goes back to the parent once the stopped build is parked in the parent-block wait, so the 500 ms grace has not passed yet. The payload must contain both transactions. With the grace set to 0: 0 transactions (10 of 10 runs).
- `TestStopWakesBuilderWaitingForMoreTransactions` (`execution/execmodule`): runs in a `testing/synctest` bubble. The provider runs dry, and `Stop` must return without any time passing. Without the idle-wait change, fake time advanced by exactly 50 ms.
- `TestProvideTxnsReturnsNothingOnceTheParentBlockWaitIsStopped` (`txnprovider/txpool`): a call parked in the parent-block wait returns no transactions and no error once the stop channel is closed. With the option added but not yet honoured by the txpool, it was still waiting after 5 s.
- `TestPoolProvideTxnsReturnsNothingOnceTheParentBlockWaitIsStopped` (`txnprovider/shutter`): the same for the shutter parent-block wait. With the option not yet honoured by shutter, it was still waiting.
- `TestPoolProvideTxnsKeepsProvidingAfterTheStopOnceTheParentBlockIsSeen` (`txnprovider/shutter`): with the stop channel already closed and the parent already seen, 1000 calls must all return the decrypted transaction. Without the tracker check, some calls returned no transactions (20 of 20 runs failed).
- `TestBlockTrackerWaitReportsCancellationForAnUnseenBlock` (`txnprovider/shutter`): a `synctest` context lets the waiter goroutine finish before `Wait` selects, so both cases are ready. `Wait` must return `context.Canceled` for a block it has not seen. Before: `nil`.
- `TestProvideTxnsReportsCancellationWhenTheParentBlockWaitIsAlsoStopped` (`txnprovider/txpool`): with the caller's context cancelled and the stop closed, `ProvideTxns` must return `context.Canceled`. Before: `nil` for some calls.
- `TestPoolProvideTxnsFallsBackToBaseProviderWhenTheParentBlockWaitTimesOut` (`txnprovider/shutter`): the parent never arrives and fake time passes the one-slot deadline. `ProvideTxns` must return the base provider's transactions and no error. Before: `issue while waiting for parent block 2: context deadline exceeded`.
- `TestBlockTrackerWaitReportsCancellationAfterTheTrackerStops` (`txnprovider/shutter`): a stopped tracker and a cancelled context; `Wait` must return `context.Canceled`. Before: `block tracker stopped`.
- `TestBlockTrackerWaitReturnsWhenCancelledRightAfterItsWaiterChecks` (`txnprovider/shutter`): a test context is cancelled by the waiter's own check, which still sees it as live, so the cancellation lands before the waiter's `Cond.Wait`. `Wait` must return `context.Canceled`. Without the lock around the broadcast: the wakeup was lost and `Wait` never returned (5 of 5 runs).

Test harnesses: tests that call `getPayload` right after a forkchoice update would otherwise depend on the txpool processing the new head within the 500 ms grace. `ExecModuleTester.AssembleBlock` and `MockCl.StartBuilding` (engine API tester) now wait, for at most a minute, until the txpool has seen the parent block (`txpoolwait.WaitForParent`), and the two Caplin block production tests that build through the execution module directly call `ExecModuleTester.WaitForTxPool`. For the engine API tester this needs a `TxPool()` accessor on `eth.Ethereum`. With the grace set to 0 locally, `TestAssembleBlockGasOverflow` and the whole `./execution/engineapi` package still pass.

No new test for the txpool watcher change: it does not change behaviour, and the existing tests in `pool_best_lock_test.go` cover the wait loop.

Refactor step: two helpers, `assembleWithTxPoolBehindParent` and `newLoggingPool`, now hold the setup that the new tests share with existing tests.

Mutation check: I removed each production piece on its own (passing the option, waking the idle wait, closing the channel in `Stop`, the txpool wait-loop case, the txpool wake-up case, the shutter cancellation, the shutter "no transactions" return, and the state check in `BlockTracker.Wait`). Each time, the test that covers it failed.

The new tests pass with `-count=20` and with `-race`. `go test` passes for `./execution/builder/...`, `./execution/execmodule/...` and `./txnprovider/...`. With `-race`, it passes for `./execution/builder/...`, `./execution/execmodule`, `./txnprovider/txpool/...` and `./txnprovider/shutter`.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network/gossip: keep sync subnets and duties across fork-digest changes
body:
## Summary

Around a fork-digest change (a fork or a blob-parameter-only fork), `goCheckForkAndResubscribe` joins the next digest's topics about 8 slots before the change with `subscribeUpcomingTopics`, which copies each topic's expiry, and about 16 slots later a goroutine calls `Unsubscribe` and `Remove` on every topic of the old digest. Two problems in that window:

- **syncnets cleared while still subscribed.** `TopicSubscriptions.Remove`, `Unsubscribe` and the expiry check call `UpdateENRSyncNets(subnet, false)` whenever a `sync_committee_{subnet}` topic's subscription is cancelled. When the old digest's topics are removed, the same subnet is still subscribed under the new digest, but its `syncnets` bit is cleared, and since `SubscribeWithExpiry` only sets the bit when it subscribes a topic that was not subscribed, nothing sets it again while that subscription lasts. Peers then do not see the subnet in the ENR or MetaData `syncnets`.
- **Duty subscriptions miss the next digest.** `GossipManager.SubscribeWithExpiry(name, expiry)` subscribes only `composeTopic(CurrentForkDigest(), name)`. Its callers are beacon committee subscriptions for aggregators (`cl/validator/committee_subscription`), sync committee subscriptions (`POST /eth/v1/validator/sync_committee_subscriptions`) and PeerDAS custody (`cl/das`). A request made after the next digest's topics were joined subscribes the current digest only, so for a duty slot after the change the node is not subscribed to the subnet under the digest in use.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_subscription.go`: when a sync committee topic's subscription is cancelled, the `syncnets` bit is cleared only if no registered topic with the same name (the same subnet under another digest) is still subscribed. Setting the bit is unchanged.
- `cl/phase1/network/gossip/gossip_manager.go`: `SubscribeWithExpiry` subscribes the current digest's topic as before (including the deferred subscription and the error when that topic is not registered), then also subscribes every other registered topic with the same name with the same expiry. An error on one of those topics is logged and does not fail the request, so a topic that the old digest's cleanup removes between the listing of the topics and the call does not fail it (that topic is then left as a deferred subscription, which is never used because the old digest is not registered again).

## Not changed here

- The 8-slot lookahead and the removal of the old digest's topics. The phase0 P2P spec [says](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1840-L1845) a node must subscribe to the persistent subnets of the future fork at least `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` epochs before it; Caplin joins them about 8 slots before. Lighthouse subscribes to the next digest's topics one epoch before the change ([`SUBSCRIBE_DELAY_EPOCHS`](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/014ba06b56514d383426f2c727e7233dad973e0d/beacon_node/network/src/service.rs#L59), [timer](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/014ba06b56514d383426f2c727e7233dad973e0d/beacon_node/network/src/service.rs#L1658-L1665)) and Prysm when the change is in the next epoch ([`ensureRegistrationsForEpoch`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/64c1dfc98abaf55d1d091049afc3f479385be6bc/beacon-chain/sync/fork_watcher.go#L65-L69)).
- `subscribeUpcomingTopics` copies the expiry the old topic has when the next digest's topic is added; a duty that extends the old topic's expiry while the next digest's topic is being added can leave the earlier expiry on the new topic.

## Testing

- **TDD**, with the production files from `main`:
  - `TestSyncCommitteeOldDigestRemovalKeepsENRWhileNewDigestSubscribed` (strict P2P mock) fails with `Unexpected call to *mock_services.MockP2PManager.UpdateENRSyncNets([1 false])` from `Unsubscribe` of the old digest's topic.
  - `TestSyncCommitteeTopicsExpiringTogetherClearENROnce` fails with the same unexpected call from the expiry check: the first of the two expired topics clears the bit while the other is still subscribed.
  - `TestDutySubscriptionIncludesUpcomingDigest` fails because the next digest's topic is not subscribed after `GossipManager.SubscribeWithExpiry`.
  - `TestRemovingSubscribedSyncCommitteeOldDigestKeepsENR` (strict P2P mock) fails with `Unexpected call to *mock_services.MockP2PManager.UpdateENRSyncNets([1 false])` from `Remove` of the old digest's topic while it is still subscribed.
  - `TestDutySubscriptionContinuesAfterAnotherDigestFails` closes the topic handle of one other digest and checks that the request succeeds and the remaining digest is subscribed; it fails on `main` because that digest is not subscribed, and it also fails if the closed topic's error is returned instead of logged.
- `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/ ./cl/validator/committee_subscription/ ./cl/beacon/handler/ ./cl/das/... ./cl/p2p/... ./cl/sentinel/...`, `go test -race -p 2 -count=1 ./cl/phase1/network/gossip/`, `make lint`, `make erigon integration`.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon/handler: serve fork-epoch PTC duties once the clock reaches the fork
body:
## Problem

`POST /eth/v1/validator/duties/ptc/{epoch}` answers 503 ("PTC duties for fork epoch F are not available until the head reaches the Gloas fork") for the Gloas fork epoch while the head is still the last Fulu block. It does so even after the wall clock has entered the fork epoch.

The Lighthouse VC starts asking for PTC duties only once its clock reaches the Gloas fork epoch, and after a failed request it waits until the next slot. On a local Gloas shadow fork, its request for the fork-epoch duties got this 503. The VC logged the failure 4 ms into the first Gloas slot, before Caplin had imported that slot's block, and it missed every PTC duty of that slot. PTC participation in that slot was 64%. The Teku VC on the other Caplin node fetches one epoch ahead and retries every second, so it got its duties in time.

The 503 was added on purpose in #24393. Computing the fork epoch's PTC directly from the Fulu state is only a prediction: `upgrade_to_gloas` computes it after the last Fulu epoch processing, which can change effective balances, and the PTC is drawn by effective balance.

## Fix

The handler already copies the head state and processes slots on the copy when the head lags the clock by one epoch. It now does the same for a pre-Gloas head once the clock has reached the requested epoch, which can only be the fork epoch with the head in the epoch before it. The copy is processed to the first slot of the fork epoch, which runs the last Fulu epoch processing and `upgrade_to_gloas`, and the duties are read from its PTC window. Lighthouse serves this request the same way.

Unchanged:

- While the clock is still in the epoch before the fork, the answer is still 503.
- The dependent root is still the one the Beacon API defines, the block root at the last slot of epoch F-2. At the fork epoch this root does not cover the blocks of epoch F-1, which feed the PTC. Lighthouse returns the root at the last slot of epoch F-1 for the fork epoch instead. I did not copy that here, because it differs from the API definition.
- The head state is not modified, and a Gloas head still reads its PTC window directly.
- A head two epochs before the fork still gets 503: the existing lag path advances it only to epoch F-1, which is still Fulu.

As on the existing lag path, concurrent requests each copy and process the state; there is no cache.

## Tests

- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUsesAdvancedFuluState`: a real Fulu head at the last slot before the fork (minimal preset, 64 validators) with the clock in the fork epoch. The fixture zeroes the balances of most validators that a direct Fulu prediction puts in the PTC, so the last Fulu epoch processing lowers their effective balances, and it asserts that the direct prediction differs from the PTC of a state advanced into the fork. The response must be 200, with the duties of the advanced state and the API dependent root. On `main`: 503.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUnavailableBeforeClockReachesFork`: the same head with the clock one epoch before the fork must still get 503. It replaces `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochUnavailableBeforeGloasHead`, which did not fix the clock. It passes on `main` and pins the clock condition of the fix.
- `TestPostPtcDutiesForkEpochDoesNotMutatePublishedHead`: after a successful request, the published head is still the same Fulu state (version, slot, root and state root). On `main`: 503.

Mutation check: without the clock condition, the second test fails; without the new branch, the first and third fail.

`go test ./cl/beacon/handler/...` passes, and the new tests pass with `-race -count=5`.

## Release branches

`release/3.8` has the same handler, so the change applies there. `release/3.7` lacks the copy-and-advance path for the PTC duties handler, so a backport would need that first.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon/handler: wait for the voted block before rejecting REST attestations
body:
Fixes #25093.

`POST /eth/v1|v2/beacon/pool/attestations` rejected an attestation with 400 `ignore: block not seen` when its block was not imported yet, and did not publish it. On mainnet, blocks with blobs are often imported 2–2.5 s into the slot, so a validator client can attest before that.

Now the handlers wait for the voted block, then process and publish the attestation:
- `ErrBlockNotSeen` sentinel (wrapped in `ErrIgnore`; error text unchanged) marks this case.
- The wait polls fork choice every 50 ms, bounded by one slot per request (shared by all attestations in the request) and by the request context.
- A failure is reported only if the block does not arrive in time.

This matches Lighthouse, which requeues such attestations and waits up to one slot.

Tests: a block that arrives after submission gives 200 and one publish; a block that never arrives gives 400 for every attestation after about one slot (not one slot per attestation).
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: check header presence instead of loading a state for pending envelopes
body:
Part of #25120.

## Problem

`validatePendingEnvelopeCommitments` (`cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload.go`) calls `forkGraph.GetState(root, false)` under `f.mu.RLock` only to test that the block's state exists. When the root is not the fork graph's current state, this reads a dumped state from disk and replays blocks while the fork-choice lock is held. The state is then thrown away: the envelope apply that follows loads the state again by itself.

## What changed

`validatePendingEnvelopeCommitments` checks header presence (`forkGraph.GetHeader(root)`) instead of loading the state. The block is stored before the transition runs and the header is published only after the transition succeeds, so header presence (not `GetBlock`) is the marker of a validated post-state. The `GetBlock` check and the rest of the function are unchanged.

Effects:
- The work under `f.mu.RLock` drops from a possible disk read plus block replay to two map lookups.
- When the header exists (the normal case), each pending-envelope retry now loads the state once (in the apply) instead of twice. In the rare case where `AddChainSegment` stored the block and its state but failed before it published the header, the apply still loads the state twice, as before, but now both loads run under the write lock.
- When a header exists but its state cannot be loaded, the envelope's commitments are now checked before the apply. These checks use only the block and the envelope, so an envelope with invalid commitments is now rejected at this point instead of waiting in the queue until it ages out.

No interface changed and no new constants were added.

## Testing

TDD. `TestValidatePendingEnvelopeCommitmentsUsesHeaderAsReadinessMarker` fails on the base production code for the intended reason and passes with the change: a stored block without a header is not ready, a block with a header is ready, and neither case loads a state (a fake fork graph counts `GetState` calls). The existing pending-envelope test fakes got a `GetHeader` method.

Commands: `go test ./cl/phase1/stages/ ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... -count=1`, `go test -race ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/`, `go build ./...` and `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) all pass.

## Not included

- Head event state root: an earlier version of this PR also took the head event's state root from the fork-choice header instead of calling `headState.HashSSZ()` in `emitHeadEvent`. Review showed that this does not remove the cold hash. That hash also fills the Merkle caches of the head state that is then copied into synced data. Without it, the next block import on that head hashes the cold copy in full while it holds the fork-choice write lock. That change was dropped; a later change that reuses warm states can handle it.
- Reusing warm head and previous-head states for `alwaysCopy` loads, moving state loads out of `f.mu`, and parallel hashing are separate follow-ups.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8. This is a small improvement: it removes one unneeded state load per pending-envelope check. It does not fix a correctness problem.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes/solid, cl/merkle_tree: build the validator Merkle tree in parallel on cold rebuilds
body:
Part of #25120.

## Problem

A beacon state decoded from disk has no validator Merkle cache. Its first `HashSSZ` (or `NextSyncCommitteeBranch`, or the first `transitionSlot` after an empty slot) rebuilds the whole validator tree on one goroutine. On a Hoodi node (Xeon E-2288G, 8 cores / 16 threads, about 1.14M validators) this takes 3.45 s of the 3.52 s cold state hash, and the time is the same with 1, 4, 8 or 16 threads. Several of these paths run under the fork-choice lock. The same happens after the Fulu to Gloas upgrade, because `SetProgressiveHashing` drops the tree: the first Gloas hash took 3.56 s.

## What changed

- `cl/cltypes/solid`: on a cold build (`MerkleTree == nil` in `HashSSZ`, `progressiveTrees == nil` in `HashSSZProgressive`) of at least 4,000 validators, the validator leaf roots are computed in parallel into a temporary buffer, and the tree (or every progressive segment tree) is built from that buffer. After the build, the normal per-validator leaf function is installed again, so warm updates work exactly as before, and the buffer is released. Both paths publish the cache (`v.MerkleTree`, `v.progressiveTrees`) only when it is fully built. Before this, the Gloas path published an empty slice and appended the segment trees one by one, so a concurrent copy (`BeaconState.CopyInto` takes no state lock) could take only the first segments and keep a permanently wrong root; the leaf functions were also rebound afterwards without a lock.
- Leaf hashing in workers calls gohashtree directly (no global hasher mutex) and each worker has its own scratch array. A test checks it against `CopyHashBufferTo` + `MerkleRootFromFlatLeaves` on random validators.
- Workers per build: at most 8 and at most `GOMAXPROCS/2` (at least 1). On the node, 8 workers were as fast as 16 in wall time with about 40% less CPU; hyperthreads add CPU, not speed.
- A process-wide budget is shared by all cold builds: an atomic count of live helpers, limited to `GOMAXPROCS` in total. Each build still takes at most its own cap minus one, so two overlapping builds both run with full parallelism on a 16-thread node (7 + 7 helpers), and a third one gets what is left. The calling goroutine always works; it takes helpers only with a non-blocking try-acquire and holds them for the whole build (leaf roots and tree layers). A build that gets no helper runs the old serial code in its own goroutine. It never waits, so it cannot deadlock under a caller lock.
- The limit counts helpers, not the calling goroutines, so with three or more overlapping cold builds the number of hashing goroutines can go a little above `GOMAXPROCS`, and each build allocates its own leaf-root buffer (32 bytes per validator). Overlapping cold builds are rare; two at once was the case seen on the node.
- `cl/merkle_tree`: new `BuildFromLeafRoots(leafRoots, leavesCount, maxDepth, limit, workers, computeLeaf)`. It builds a new tree from a precomputed leaf-root buffer in parallel and returns the finished tree with the caller's normal leaf function installed. There is no exported way to run the parallel code on an existing (warm) tree. `ComputeRoot` and all other users are unchanged. Only layers with at least 4,096 nodes are split across workers; narrower layers stay serial. This was needed because with only the leaves parallel, the serial upper layers were 43–50% of the cold wall time.
- Warm hashing stays serial. The prototype parallelized any layer wider than 8,192 nodes, and a warm change of 100 validators then cost 22.7 ms CPU instead of 8.5 ms. Here only cold builds fan out.

### Thresholds

- `parallelMinValidators = 4000`: smallest cold build size where parallel was consistently faster (Apple M3 Pro, 3 samples): 1k serial 0.83–1.24 ms vs parallel 0.36–1.04 ms (overlap); 4k 1.73–2.10 ms vs 0.57–0.85 ms; 16k 6.5–7.3 ms vs 1.6–2.7 ms; 64k 25.6–26.0 ms vs 6.8–7.1 ms.
- `parallelLayerMinNodes = 4096`: smallest layer width where 6 workers were consistently faster: 2,048 nodes 210–225 µs vs 132–239 µs (inconsistent); 4,096 327–340 µs vs 233–293 µs; 8,192 687–784 µs vs 446–462 µs; 16,384 1.30 ms vs 0.85–0.90 ms.
- No parallel path for "many dirty validators": warm `HashSSZ` on 1M validators costs 2.5 ms (1 dirty), 2.5 ms (100), 2.9 ms (1,000) and 7.0 ms (10,000) serially, so there is little to gain.

## Benchmarks

Node (Hoodi, prototype with the same approach), cold hash: serial 3.89 s CPU; 4 / 8 / 16 workers = 0.97 / 0.53 / 0.49 s wall, 3.77 / 4.07 / 6.64 s CPU. First Gloas hash 0.47 s instead of 3.56 s. Roots identical.

Local (Apple M3 Pro, 12 cores, so 6 workers; other jobs were running, numbers are noisy), `validator_set_bench_test.go`, 1M validators, `-benchtime=3x -count=3`:

| Benchmark | serial | parallel |
|---|---|---|
| Cold `HashSSZ` (Fulu) | 395–457 ms (some samples up to 1.3 s under load) | 66–96 ms (one outlier at 133 ms) |
| Cold `HashSSZProgressive` (Gloas) | 397–431 ms | 69–127 ms (one outlier at 218 ms) |

The parallel cold build allocates about 32 MB more per build (the temporary leaf-root buffer, 32 bytes per validator).

## Tests

TDD: the new tests were written first (they did not compile on main because the hooks and the parallel tree builder did not exist; the fan-out test then failed with zero helpers).

- `TestValidatorRootMatchesSerialReference`: parallel leaf hasher equals the existing serial one.
- `TestValidatorSetRootsMatchSerialReferences`: Fulu and Gloas roots against an independent serial reference for lengths 0–7, progressive segment boundaries and neighbours (20–22, 83–86, 340–342, 1364–1366) and 21,845 / 21,846 random validators (parallel tree layers); cold, warm no-op, one dirty, many dirty, copy then mutate (original unchanged).
- `TestValidatorSetProgressiveAppendAcrossSegmentBoundary`, `TestValidatorSetParallelColdHashThenAppend` (parallel cold build, with the cold root checked, then append across the segment boundaries at 5,461 and 21,845 and into the partly filled segment at 50,003, Fulu and Gloas), `TestValidatorSetDecodedColdRootsAndCacheModeSwitches` (decode, then Fulu → Gloas → Fulu).
- The root-equality tests use a fixed 4-worker pool and check that helpers were used, so they run the parallel path on every host, also when `GOMAXPROCS` is below 4.
- `TestValidatorSetParallelFanOutIsColdAndSizeBounded`, `TestValidatorSetProgressiveParallelFanOutIsColdOnly`: a large cold build takes helpers; a set below the threshold and warm hashes with 1 and 100 dirty validators take none.
- `TestValidatorSetParallelWorkerBudget`: with a cap of 3, while one build holds both helper slots, six other cold builds finish without waiting and the live helper count never goes above 2.
- `TestValidatorSetParallelColdHashCopy`: a `CopyTo` made while another goroutine is in the middle of a cold parallel build gets a correct, usable tree. `HashSSZ` now publishes the new tree only after it is built, so a copy or hash during the build never sees an empty tree.
- `TestValidatorRootWorkerPoolHonorsRuntimeBudgetAcrossBuilds`: with a static maximum of 8, a runtime per-build cap of 4 and a total cap of 5, three builds get 3, 2 and 0 helpers.
- `TestValidatorRootWorkerPoolLetsOverlappingBuildsRunInParallel`: with `GOMAXPROCS` 16, three overlapping builds get 7, 7 and 2 helpers. Before the second commit they got 7, 0 and 0: on the Hoodi test node a second cold build that overlapped another one ran serially and held the fork-choice read lock for 3.7 s.
- `TestValidatorSetProgressiveParallelColdHashCopy`: the same for Gloas; a copy taken after the first segment tree is built gets a correct root. It fails when the trees are published segment by segment, as before.
- `TestValidatorRootWorkerPoolTracksGOMAXPROCS`, `TestBuildFromLeafRootsMatchesComputeRoot` (against `ComputeRoot` and `MerkleizeVector`, and a warm update after the build).

Mutation checks: removing the size threshold makes the fan-out test fail (2 helpers on a small set); removing the process-wide limit makes both budget tests fail (12 live helpers instead of 2, and 9 instead of 5); a wrong segment offset in the parallel Gloas build makes the root-equality, append and decode tests fail.

Commands run:
- `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid/ ./cl/merkle_tree/ -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/phase1/core/state/... ./cl/transition/... -count=1`
- `go test ./cl/spectest/... -run 'SSZ|ssz|Gloas|gloas' -count=1`
- `go build ./...`, `make lint`

## Not included

- Persisting the Merkle caches to disk.
- Caching for Gloas balances and inactivity scores.
- Any change to fork-graph, locks or state loading.
- Parallel warm hashing for many dirty validators (see the numbers above).

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8 for now. This is a performance improvement, not a correctness fix, and it changes how the consensus layer computes state roots. It should run on main and in an A/B test on a Hoodi node first. If the cold-hash stalls turn out to hurt release/3.8 users, we can reconsider it for a 3.8.x release.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes/solid, cl/phase1/core/state/raw: cache Gloas balances and inactivity scores roots incrementally
body:
Part of #25120.

## Problem

From Gloas on, `raw.BeaconState` hashes `balances` and `inactivity_scores` as progressive lists (EIP-7916). The Gloas branches of `computeDirtyLeaves` called `merkle_tree.ProgressiveBasicListRoot(list.Bytes(), ...)`, which re-merkleizes the whole list on every hash. There was no cache like the binary `MerkleTree` that Fulu uses.

Measured on the Hoodi node (about 1.14M validators): on a warm state, changing 600 balances and hashing costs 41 ms in Gloas and 3.7 ms in Fulu. Inactivity scores have the same cost. Balances change in every block, so every block import (`VerifyTransition`, under the fork-choice write lock) pays this, and so do many state copies and validations. Hoodi upgrades to Gloas on 2026-10-26.

## What changed

- `cl/cltypes/solid/uint64slice_byte.go`: `byteBasedUint64Slice` gets a progressive tree cache (`progressiveTrees`), built the same way as `ValidatorSet.progressiveTrees`: one `merkle_tree.MerkleTree` per progressive segment (capacities 1, 4, 16, ... chunks). Leaves are packed 32-byte chunks (4 values per leaf), and the length mix-in uses the element count. `Set` and `Append` mark only the touched chunk as dirty; a new leaf starts when `l%4 == 0`. `Pop`, `Clear` and `DecodeSSZ` drop the cache. `CopyTo` deep-copies the trees, binds the leaf functions to the destination buffer, and reuses the destination's tree storage when it has some.
- `cl/cltypes/solid/uint64_list.go`: `uint64ListSSZ` forwards the new `HashSSZProgressive` and `SetProgressiveHashing`.
- `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/hashing.go`: the Gloas branches for balances and inactivity scores use the cached root. Other `Uint64ListSSZ` implementations (which `SetBalances` / `SetInactivityScoresRaw` accept) still use `ProgressiveBasicListRoot`.
- `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/setters.go`: `SetVersion` switches the cache mode of both lists when crossing the Gloas boundary, like it already does for validators, so the binary tree is released and not kept next to the progressive one.

Pre-Gloas hashing is not changed. `cl/merkle_tree` is not changed. No locking was added: the lists keep the same caller-serialized contract as the existing binary tree and validator set caches.

## How it was tested

TDD. The new list tests did not compile on the base commit (the API was missing). `origin/main` cost is the `gloas_uncached` benchmark below.

New tests:
- `cl/cltypes/solid/uint64_list_progressive_test.go`: root equals `ProgressiveBasicListRoot` for lengths around chunk and segment boundaries (0, 1, 4, 5, 20, 21, 84, 85); after `Set`; after an append inside a chunk, across a chunk and across a segment; after `Clear` then `Append`; after `Pop` and `DecodeSSZ` (including empty); a randomized test mixing `Set`/`Append`/`Pop`/`DecodeSSZ`; copy independence (copy, then mutate source and destination differently); copy between lists with different backing buffer sizes; copy from a cold source clears a stale destination cache; destination tree reuse; cache-mode switch; and `TestUint64ListWarmProgressiveHashIsIncremental`, which checks that 600 changes on a warm 1.14M list recompute at most 1,200 leaves instead of the whole list.
- `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/hashing_gloas_test.go`: `SetVersion` switches both lists in and out of progressive mode and Gloas hashing uses the list's cache; a fallback test for non-list implementations; `TestSetVersionAcrossGloasInvalidatesRoots` now has non-empty lists.
- `cl/phase1/core/state/upgrade_test.go`: `TestUpgradeToGloasStateRootMatchesDecodedState`: a Fulu state with warm caches upgraded with `UpgradeToGloas` hashes to the same root as the same state decoded fresh.

Commands:
- `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid/ ./cl/merkle_tree/ -count=1`: pass.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/core/state/... ./cl/transition/... -count=1`: pass.
- `go build ./...` and `make lint` (clean twice): pass.
- Spec tests: the local consensus-spec fixture cache is older than the v1.7.0-beta.4 fixtures that `test-fixtures.json` pins, so many Gloas cases fail on the base commit too. I ran `go test -tags=spectest -run='Test/mainnet/gloas/' -v` in `cl/spectest` on the base commit and on this branch: the same 1,483 cases ran with identical pass/fail results (322 pass, 1,161 fail). For all five `gloas/ssz_static/BeaconState` cases, both builds compute the same state roots. `fulu` and `electra` `ssz_static/BeaconState`, `sanity` and `epoch_processing` pass (543 cases); only `mainnet_config` fails, because of the same fixture drift. CI with the pinned fixtures still has to confirm the Gloas spec tests.

Benchmarks (`cl/cltypes/solid/uint64_list_bench_test.go`, Apple M3 Pro, 1.14M-element list, 600 random `Set`s then hash, `-benchtime=20x -count=3`):

| Case | Time | Allocated |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fulu, binary cache (`HashSSZ`) | 0.99-1.00 ms | 0 B |
| Gloas, new progressive cache | 1.00 ms | 0 B |
| Gloas, origin/main (`ProgressiveBasicListRoot`) | 16.8-22.4 ms | 18.2 MB |
| `CopyTo` a warm list into a new list | 1.0-1.2 ms | 24.6 MB |
| `CopyTo` a warm list into a reused list | 0.6-1.0 ms | 320 B |

So the warm Gloas hash now costs the same as Fulu. The progressive cache holds 14.9 MB per 1.14M-element list (measured with `runtime.MemStats` after GC), so about 29.7 MB per state for both lists. In Gloas this replaces the binary cache, which is released on the fork switch. The fresh-copy allocation includes the 9.1 MB value buffer.

## Not included

- Validator tree parallelism, participation lists, fork-graph / state-loading / lock changes, and persisting caches (other PRs).
- Two pre-existing bugs in `byteBasedUint64Slice`, left for a follow-up: `UnmarshalJSON` sets the length before it appends, so the list doubles in length; and the binary `MerkleTree` path does not add a leaf when appending after `Clear` or after decoding an empty list, because it detects new chunks by buffer growth (both panic with index out of range on the base commit).

## Backport
Not planned for release/3.8 for now. Without it, a Gloas block costs about 41 ms more hashing on the measured node; that is slower, not wrong. We will decide after watching Hoodi run Gloas (from 2026-10-26) on release/3.8.
author: domiwei

title: cl/sentinel: check cancellation before returning responses
body:
`httpreqresp.Do` could return a nil error for a cancelled request when the handler response and context cancellation were both ready. This caused `TestRequestContextCancelClosesEstablishedStream` to fail in [the consensus race-test job](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/39371425311/job/118459972799).

Check the request context again after receiving a response. If it is cancelled, close the response body and return the context error.

This makes `Do`'s cancellation contract consistent: the service caller already checks the context after `Do`, and the handshake caller treats either error shape as a handshake failure during shutdown.

Add a focused `synctest` regression that makes both select cases ready and checks the context error and body cleanup. It reproduced the nil-error failure before the production fix and passed afterwards. The existing libp2p regression remains unchanged.

Validation:

- Both cancellation regressions passed 100 repetitions with `-race`.
- `ERIGON_COMMITMENT_PARALLEL=true go test -race -count=1 -timeout=5m ./cl/sentinel/httpreqresp ./cl/sentinel/handshake ./cl/sentinel/service`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
author: yperbasis

title: cl/beacon/handler: report sync committee messages from validators outside the committee
body:
Fixes #25046.

`POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` computes the subnets of each message from the validator's positions in the sync committee for the message slot. For a validator outside the committee the list is empty, so the message was neither validated nor published, but the handler still returned 200.

Now such a message is reported as a pooling failure (`validator N is not in the sync committee for slot S`), so the response is 400 with the failing index, as the [Beacon API](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Beacon/submitPoolSyncCommitteeSignatures) requires. Other messages in the same request are processed as before.

A head state from before Altair has zero-filled sync committees, so such a head is reported as `head state is before Altair and has no sync committee` instead.

Tests (red before the fix):
- `TestPoolSyncCommitteesRejectsValidatorOutsideCommittee`: `[member, outsider, member]` gives 400 with one failure at index 1, and both member messages are still published.
- `TestPoolSyncCommitteesReportsPreAltairHead`.

`cl/beacon/handler` tests pass; `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds.
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon/handler: derive sync committee subscription subnets from the requested indices
body:
Fixes #25047.

`POST /eth/v1/validator/sync_committee_subscriptions` decoded `sync_committee_indices` but never used them. It computed the subnets from the head state's committee for the validator. A validator client subscribes before the period in which its validator joins the committee (see the [Beacon API](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Validator/prepareSyncCommitteeSubnets)), so the node got the current committee's subnets or none, and was not on the right sync subnets when the new period started.

Changes:
- The subnets come from `sync_committee_indices`: `index / (SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE / SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT)`, each subnet once. Lighthouse does the same.
- Every request is validated before any subscription. A missing or `null` `sync_committee_indices`, or a non-numeric or out-of-range index, gives 400. An empty list is a valid request with nothing to subscribe.
- The subnets no longer depend on the head state, so the endpoint no longer returns 503 while the node is syncing. The Beacon API declares only 200, 400 and 500 for it, and Lighthouse has no syncing check here.
- The subscription still lasts until the start of `until_epoch`.

Tests (red first):
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionUsesRequestedIndices`: validator 1 requests positions on subnets 1 and 3; the head committee would give it subnets 0 and 2, which the old handler subscribes.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionRejectsInvalidIndices`: out-of-range, non-numeric and negative indices give 400, and nothing is subscribed.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionRequiresIndices`: missing indices give 400; `[]` gives 200.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionSucceedsWhileSyncing`: a syncing node subscribes and returns 200.
- Mutation checks: removing the range check or the de-duplication fails the tests.

`cl/beacon/handler` tests pass; `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/transition/impl/eth2: verify the Gloas envelope builder signature once
body:
Part of #25120 (item 2, the two quick parts).

## Problem

When a Gloas execution payload envelope is applied on the validated fork-choice path, two pieces of work run twice or for nothing while the fork-choice write lock is held:

- The builder signature is BLS-verified twice: once by `validateEnvelopeAgainstBlock` and again by the transition (`ValidatingMachine`, full validation), on the same state and envelope.
- `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` builds a full `PayloadHeader`, which hashes the transaction list, withdrawals and the block access list, only to read five scalar fields.

## What changed

- `applyEnvelopeCoordinated` uses `DefaultMachine` when `validatePayload` is true, because that branch has already verified the signature on the same state and envelope without yielding the lock. With `validatePayload` false the transition still verifies it (`ValidatingMachine`).
- `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForConsensus` uses `DefaultMachine` after `validateEnvelopeAgainstBlock`.
- `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` reads `prev_randao`, `gas_limit`, `block_hash`, `parent_hash` and `timestamp` from the payload directly. Error messages are unchanged; the other `PayloadHeader` callers are untouched.
- `ProcessExecutionPayloadEnvelope` rejects a payload with nil transactions, like nil withdrawals and execution requests. `PayloadHeader` used to dereference the list; ingress validation (`ValidateForConfig`) already rejects nil transactions, so no valid envelope changes outcome.
- `verifyEnvelopeBuilderSignature` calls a package-level `blsVerify` so tests can count verifications.

Every path still verifies the signature at least once:

| Path | Verification |
|---|---|
| Fork choice, `validatePayload` true (gossip, API publish, pending retry, sync with EL validation) | once, in fork choice |
| Fork choice, `validatePayload` false (forward / chain-tip sync) | once, in the transition |
| `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForConsensus` | once, in `validateEnvelopeAgainstBlock` |
| Operations spec tests | once, in the transition |
| Local self-build | none, as before (no production caller) |

The post-state root is unchanged.

## Testing

TDD for the behaviour changes. These tests fail on the base production code and pass with the change:
- the validated path and the consensus validation path each verify the signature exactly once (a stubbed fork-choice verifier plus a signature from another key, which any second verification would reject);
- the transition no longer builds the payload header;
- the transition rejects nil transactions with both machines.

Further tests: invalid signatures are rejected with `validatePayload` true and false, by the consensus validation path and by `ValidatingMachine`; self-build uses the proposer key.

The scalar-check table and the state-root checks pass both before and after the change. They are characterization tests for the refactor part (reading five fields instead of building the header), so that part does not follow red/green.

`BenchmarkApplyEnvelopeValidatedPath` (Apple M3 Pro, interleaved runs), per envelope:
- 300 txs / 100 KB BAL: 2.99 ms → 1.36 ms
- 1500 txs / 400 KB BAL: 9.09 ms → 3.66 ms

Commands:
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/transition/... ./cl/beacon/... ./cl/persistence/... -count=1` passes.
- `go test -race` passes on `cl/phase1/forkchoice` and `cl/transition/impl/eth2`.
- `go build ./...`, `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make erigon integration` pass.
- Gloas spec tests: the local fixtures are older than the pinned ones, and the set of failing cases is identical to the base (envelope cases fail to decode on both). CI runs the pinned fixtures.

## Not included

- Caching the Gloas payload hash and the transaction / BAL progressive roots.
- Moving `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` out of the fork-choice lock.
- The REST publish path and the gossip "indices pending" branch still verify the signature once more on the caller side; that code is not changed here.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8. This is a performance improvement for Gloas envelope processing. It does not fix a correctness problem.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/core/caches, cl/phase1/core/state, cl/phase1/stages, cl/transition: share lookahead shuffles and active sets across state copies
body:
Part of #25120 (item 1).

## Problem

During epoch processing at the E → E+1 boundary, `ProcessPtcWindow` (Gloas) and the proposer lookahead (Fulu and later) need the active set and the attester shuffle of epoch E+2. The global caches (`ShuffledIndiciesCacheGlobal`, `ActiveValidatorsCacheGlobal`) are keyed by `(epoch, decision block root)`, where the decision root is the block root at slot `(E+1)*SLOTS_PER_EPOCH-1`. During epoch processing that slot is the state's own slot, and `GetBlockRootAtSlot` rejects `slot >= state.slot`. So the lookup never hits, the result is never stored, and every fresh state that crosses the boundary scans the registry and reshuffles the full validator set again: block import (under the fork-choice write lock), gossip validation, replays, payload preparation.

`ProcessPtcWindow` on a fresh copy with 500k validators took ~110-137 ms locally; at Hoodi/mainnet scale on our test node this is several hundred ms per state per epoch.

## What changed

- When the decision slot equals `state.slot` and the slot transition has already run for that slot (the latest header's state root is set and `block_roots[slot]` equals the header root), the main caches use that block root as the decision root. `transitionSlot` writes exactly this value before `ProcessEpoch`, so it is the root the spec would return one slot later. If the slot transition has not run yet (a block at the current slot was just processed), the lookup misses as before and nothing is stored.
- Values computed in this case go into two small lookahead caches (4 entries each, separate metric names) keyed by `(epoch, state_roots[slot])`. The state root identifies the registry and RANDAO, so states that share a header but differ in their registry cannot share an entry, and replays of old states cannot evict the fork-choice precache entries in the main caches. Lookahead active-set entries carry no total active balance.
- The fork-choice precache promotes a lookahead shuffle into the main cache instead of computing it again.
- `ComputeCommittee` returns a capped slice (`[start:end:end]`), so callers cannot append into the shared array.

Why the key is safe: with the mainnet configuration (`MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD = 1`), the active set and the seed of epoch E+2 are fixed by the chain up to the decision block. Activation and exit epochs are always at least `current epoch + 1 + MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD` ahead, execution requests are applied in the child block, and the Gloas envelope does not change the registry or the header. The total active balance is not covered by this argument (it also depends on effective balances updated at the end of the previous epoch), which is why lookahead entries never carry it. The existing main-cache total active balance has a separate problem, tracked in #25138; this PR does not change it.

## Testing

TDD. These tests fail on the base for the intended reason and pass with the change:
- a second fresh copy crossing the same boundary reuses the E+2 shuffle (`Same` assertion) instead of recomputing it;
- `ProcessSlots` across a boundary stores the result in the lookahead cache;
- two states that share a header but have different registries get different results (registry collision, 16383 vs 16384 active validators).

Differential tests check that the PTC window and the proposer lookahead are identical with and without the caches for: branches with different registries, the Fulu → Gloas upgrade epoch, a latest header whose state root is not set yet, empty slots vs slots with a block, replay of old states (no eviction of precache entries), and concurrent first lookups under `-race`.

Commands:
- `go test -race` on `cl/phase1/core/state/...`, `cl/phase1/core/caches/...`, `cl/transition/...` passes, also after the squash.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/beacon/... ./cl/persistence/...` passes.
- `go build ./...`, `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make erigon integration` pass.
- Mainnet spec tests (twice): the failing set is identical to the base. The local fixtures are older than the pinned ones, so the Gloas spec tests are left to CI.

`ProcessPtcWindow` on a fresh copy, 500k validators, Apple M3 Pro: ~110-137 ms/op before, ~14-25 ms/op after.

## Not included

- Concurrent cold misses for the same key are not merged (both compute); this existed before.
- The precache does not promote the lookahead active set, so the head state still scans the registry once per epoch for it.
- The 4-entry lookahead caches can be evicted while the antiquary catches up; that only costs a recomputation.
- The Gloas upgrade boundary itself is not shared between copies.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8. This is a performance improvement for epoch processing; it does not fix a correctness problem.
author: domiwei

title: cl/transition/impl/eth2/statechange: avoid contended and no-op dirty marks in epoch processing
body:
Part of #25136 (direction 1).

## Problem

On Hoodi (~1.14M active validators), the first block of each epoch runs `ProcessEpoch` and the following state-root hash under the fork-choice write lock. On our test node this takes about 0.85 s per epoch. More than half of it comes from two implementation inefficiencies, not from the spec work:

- **Rewards and penalties.** The parallel loop writes each balance directly. Every write goes through `MarkLeafAsDirty`, which takes the balances Merkle tree `RWMutex` read lock. Readers do not block each other, but they all update the same reader count, so most of the step's CPU is contention on that counter. This applies when the balances tree exists, which is the normal case for a warm Fulu state.
- **Effective balance updates.** The effective balance is written whenever the hysteresis condition is true, also when the new value equals the old one. Validators at the maximum with excess balance meet the condition in every epoch. On the Hoodi state, 120,912 validator leaves become dirty but only 9 effective balances change, and the next `HashSSZ` rehashes all of them.

## What changed

- The reward/penalty deltas are computed in parallel into a slice and applied serially in eligible-index order. The delta computation does not read balances and the eligible indices are unique, so the result is the same.
- `ProcessEffectiveBalanceUpdates` skips the write when the new effective balance equals the current one.

The post-epoch state bytes and root do not change.

Behaviour changes in callbacks, with no production consumer:
- `OnNewValidatorEffectiveBalance` no longer fires for no-op writes.
- `OnNewValidatorBalance` fires serially in eligible-index order instead of concurrently.
- A compute error now leaves no balance written.

The antiquary installs neither hook (`state_antiquary.go`); it derives historical balances and effective balances from the raw state bytes, so state snapshots are not affected.

## Measurements

Real Hoodi state (~1.14M active validators, 1.67M registry), Apple M3 Pro, warm hashed state as on block import, base and this change run interleaved, medians:

| | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| **Fulu** rewards and penalties | ~115 ms (~1.3 s CPU) | ~17 ms (~53 ms CPU) |
| **Fulu** `ProcessSlots` across the boundary | ~193 ms | ~87 ms |
| **Fulu** post-epoch `HashSSZ` | ~101 ms | ~20 ms |
| **Gloas** rewards and penalties (no balances tree) | ~27 ms | ~14 ms |
| **Gloas** `ProcessSlots` across the boundary | ~316 ms | ~305 ms |
| **Gloas** post-epoch `HashSSZ` | ~102 ms | ~23 ms |

A Gloas state upgraded from a hashed Fulu state keeps the balances tree; there the rewards step goes from ~130 ms to ~17 ms. On Gloas the boundary is dominated by the PTC window (~216 ms), which is handled separately in #25143. The post-epoch root was identical between base and this change on both forks.

`BenchmarkEpochProcessing` (synthetic, 200k validators, Fulu):
- RewardsAndPenalties: ~19 ms → ~3.3 ms
- EffectiveBalanceUpdatesAndHashSSZ: ~60 ms → ~1.3 ms

## Testing

TDD. These tests fail on the base for the intended reason and pass with the change:
- only changed effective balances are written (Deneb, Fulu, Gloas; Deneb covers the pre-Electra maximum);
- balance writes are serial and in eligible-index order;
- a compute error writes no balance.

`TestProcessEpochWarmRootMatchesColdRoot` runs a full `ProcessEpoch` on Fulu and Gloas and checks that the warm post-epoch root equals the root of the re-decoded state. It guards the dirty-mark changes and also passes on the base. Output equivalence is covered by the existing golden-state tests and the consensus spec tests.

- `go test -race` on `cl/transition/...`, `cl/phase1/core/state/...`, `cl/merkle_tree/...` passes.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/transition/...` and `go build ./...` pass.
- `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make erigon integration` pass.
- epoch_processing and sanity spec tests: the failing set is identical to the merge base (outdated local Gloas fixtures and `mainnet_config`); the pinned fixtures run in CI.

## Not included

- The other directions in #25136 (`attestation_data` without a full state advance, gossip validation of the boundary block, precomputing the next-epoch state).
- Rewards are still applied as one net delta per validator; this is the same as before.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8. This is a performance improvement; it does not fix a correctness problem.
author: domiwei

title: cl/transition/impl/eth2/statechange: apply rewards and penalties per delta set as in the spec
body:
Stacked on #25144, which restructured the same function. Please review and merge #25144 first; the diff of this PR is only the last commit.

## Problem

The post-Altair rewards and penalties step sums all flag rewards and penalties and the inactivity penalty into one net delta per validator and applies it with a single clamp at zero.

The spec applies the delta sets in order (source, target and head flag deltas, then inactivity penalties). For each set it calls `increase_balance` with the reward and then `decrease_balance` with the penalty, and `decrease_balance` clamps at zero. When a penalty is larger than the current balance, the results differ. Example: balance 10, source penalty 15, target reward 8. The spec gives 8; the net delta gives 3.

On real chains this is very likely unreachable: active unslashed validators are ejected long before a single penalty is larger than their balance, and slashed validators get no rewards, so they only see decreases, where both orders give the same result. This PR makes the code match the spec anyway.

## What changed

- The parallel loop reads the current balance (read only; no balance is written during the parallel phase) and applies the rewards and penalties in spec order, clamping at zero after each penalty.
- The resulting balances are written serially in eligible-index order, as in #25144, and a compute error still writes no balance.
- When no clamp is hit, the result is the same as before.

## Testing

TDD. `TestProcessRewardsAndPenaltiesClampsEachDeltaSet`: a validator with balance 1 that misses source and head and hits target ends with exactly the target reward. It fails on the previous code (balance 0) and passes with the change.

- `go test -race ./cl/transition/... ./cl/phase1/core/state/...` passes.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/transition/...` and `go build ./...` pass.
- `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make erigon integration` pass.
- Mainnet `epoch_processing`, `rewards` and `sanity` consensus spec tests, phase0 to gloas: 2119 pass, 0 fail on both the base and this change, run locally on the v1.7.0-beta.2 fixtures (the pinned beta.4 fixtures run in CI). The spec fixtures do not reach this case, so they also pass on the previous code; the new unit test is the regression guard.
- `BenchmarkEpochProcessing/RewardsAndPenalties` (200k validators): median ~3.25 ms → ~2.48 ms, same allocations.

## Not included

The phase0 path is unchanged. It also differs from the spec (penalties are subtracted without a clamp, and the inclusion-delay and proposer rewards are added after the penalties), but only when a penalty exceeds the balance, which is also very likely unreachable.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8: the case is very likely unreachable on real chains.
author: domiwei

title: cl, cmd: make beacon state copies cheap and keep the fork graph's current state inside fork choice
body:
Fixes #25111.

## Problem

Block import mutates the fork graph's current state in place under the fork-choice write lock. `GetStateAtBlockRoot(root, false)` handed the same object to callers that hashed and copied it after the lock was released, and some current-state copies (checkpoint states, the operation pruner, Beacon API collection getters) were taken without the lock. `raw.CopyInto` and the Merkle branch methods also did not take the raw state mutex.

Reproduced on main (details in #25111): torn copies with stale Merkle caches (wrong state roots in the synced head, head event and attestation data), and a reader's `HashSSZ` that corrupted the fork graph's state, so a valid block was rejected, stored in `badBlocks`, and `currentState` was cleared.

## What changed

Two commits; reviewing them one by one is easier. The full reasoning, the registry-mutation audit and the test list are in the commit messages.

**Commit 1: make beacon state copies cheap.** Private copies under the read lock are only acceptable if a copy is cheap, so this comes first. It does not change any locking.
- The pubkey index is an immutable base map with full 48-byte keys, shared by a state and its copies, plus a small per-state delta. A copy no longer rebuilds the map. Full keys remove the 64-bit hash collision risk of the old map. The base is still built eagerly where it was built before (New, InitBeaconState, decode).
- Registry setters keep the index correct; this also fixes the historical states reader, which left the index empty.
- Gloas `ValidatorSet.CopyTo` reuses the destination progressive trees, `ParticipationBitList.CopyTo` copies in bulk, and `ptcWindow` is deep-copied (it was shared and raced on the first hash).
- Copy into a reused spare, 1.14M validators: Fulu ~81 ms → ~11.7 ms, Gloas ~80 ms / 70.9 MB → ~11.1 ms / 9.3 MB.

**Commit 2: keep the fork graph's current state inside fork choice.** No pointer to the current state object leaves fork choice anymore.
- `ForkGraph.GetState(root, alwaysCopy)` is replaced by `CurrentStateLocked` (valid only under `f.mu`) and `ReplayState` (a private state from disk).
- `ForkChoiceStore.GetStateAtBlockRoot(root)` always returns a private state: the current state is copied under `f.mu.RLock`, other roots are replayed without `f.mu`. Callers that already hold `f.mu` use locked variants that do not lock again.
- Checkpoint-state builds keep sharing in-flight work (including the OnTick prefetch from #23981) without deadlocking callers that hold `f.mu`.
- The raw state mutex is an `RWMutex`: copies take the read lock, hashing and branch methods the write lock.
- `postForkchoiceOperations`, block production and forward sync take private copies of the head state; the rest of their flow is unchanged.
- New metric `caplin_forkchoice_current_state_copy` (copy time under the fork-choice lock).

Lock order: `f.mu` (read) → raw state mutex.

## Cost

`postForkchoiceOperations` now copies the head state twice per slot: a private copy under `f.mu.RLock` (~14-15 ms and ~300 MB locally for 1.14M validators), then the existing copy into the synced-data spare without `f.mu` (~10-11 ms, reused memory). Both are far below the ~250 ms of a single copy on main today. Removing the extra copy is left to a follow-up, after the cost is measured on a Hoodi node.

## Testing

TDD; the failing tests were seen failing first.
- `TestCurrentStateReadersDoNotShareStateWithBlockImport`: readers copy the head state while `OnBlock` imports its child. Ported to the old API, it fails under `-race` with data races and a wrong cached state root.
- The two reproduced failure modes from #25111 (writer inside `hashList.CopyTo`; reader `HashSSZ` inside `hashList.Set` during the transition) fail on the old code and pass with this change. They need temporary hooks in `solid/hash_list.go`, which are not committed.
- Deterministic lock tests (no re-locking with a queued writer), checkpoint singleflight tests, a randomized differential test over every registry mutator, ptcWindow copy tests and a Gloas reused-spare root check.
- `go test -race` on the affected packages passes; `go test ./cl/...` passes except spectest, which needs a mainnet config fixture missing locally (same on the base).
- Consensus spec tests on local fixtures: the failing set is identical to the base. The pinned fixtures run in CI.
- `go build ./...` and `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) pass.

## Not included

- Removing the extra head-state copy per slot (see Cost).
- Building the pubkey base lazily for decoded states.
- Compaction of the pubkey delta. Deposits add at most 16 validators per epoch after Electra; the gauge `beacon_state_pubkey_index_delta_size` reports its size.
- Pre-existing issues found during review: a late publish of an older head root can move the synced head back, and `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` does not check that the root is still retained.

## Backport

Planned for release/3.8 after this has run on main for a while.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/core/caches, cl/phase1/core/state, cl/phase1/stages, cl/transition/impl/eth2/statechange: stop sharing the total active balance across branches
body:
Fixes #25138.

## Problem

The global active-validators cache stores the total active balance of epoch E under the key (E, block root at the last slot of E-2). That key fixes the active set of E, but not the total: the effective balances that make up the total are written at the E-1 → E boundary from the balances at the end of E-1.

Two branches that fork during E-1 share the key. After the head precache stores branch A's total, a state of branch B in epoch E reads A's total on `SetSlot` at the epoch start, on `Copy`/`CopyInto` and on `InitBeaconState`. Rewards, justification, slashing penalties, churn limits and the Gloas builder-payment quorum are then computed with the wrong total, and B's valid blocks fail the state root check.

## What changed

- The global cache keeps only the active indices, which the key does identify. The total is removed from the cache value, so `Get` returns `([]uint64, bool)` and `Put` no longer takes a total.
- Each state sums the effective balances of its own active validators when its per-state value is empty (`_refreshActiveBalancesIfNeeded` no longer reads the global cache).
- The head precache (`preCacheActiveValidatorsForEpoch`) stores only the active set.

Copying the source's per-state total in `CopyInto` was considered and rejected: the source can be mutated while it is copied, and promoted raw setters such as `SetValidators` do not invalidate the value.

## Cost

One registry scan per state at the epoch start and on every `Copy`/`CopyInto`/`InitBeaconState`: about 2-6 ms at 1-2M validators (measured locally). A full state copy is much more expensive than that today, so a copy is about 1-2.5 % slower. The canonical head's own epoch-boundary refresh did not hit the global cache before either, so that path costs the same.

## Testing

TDD. `TestTotalActiveBalanceIsNotSharedAcrossBranchesForkedInPreviousEpoch` builds two branches that share the decision root, fork during E-1 and get different effective balances through the real epoch transition, then runs the real precache writer. The precache of one branch must not change the total that the other branch reads, directly or through `Copy`, in both directions. On the previous code all four subtests fail with the other branch's total (2047 ETH expected, 2048 ETH read, and the reverse); with the change they pass.

`TestLookaheadActiveValidatorsDoNotSupplyTotalBalance` is removed: the cache value no longer has a total, so the type enforces what it checked. Other tests only follow the new `Get`/`Put` signatures.

- `go test -race` on `cl/phase1/core/caches`, `cl/phase1/core/state`, `cl/phase1/stages` and `cl/transition/impl/eth2/statechange` passes.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/... ./cl/transition/...` and `go build ./...` pass.
- `make lint` (clean on repeated runs) and `make erigon integration` pass.
- Consensus spec tests on local fixtures: the failing set is identical to the base. The pinned fixtures run in CI.

## Backport

release/3.8 and release/3.7 have the same cache read (`cl/phase1/core/state/cache.go`). Planned backport to release/3.8 after this has run on main for a while.

title: cmd/capcli, freezeblocks: don't freeze holes over good blob segments
body:
Fixes #24037. `capcli dump-blobs-snapshots` passed no blob count, so a slot with a pruned count row froze as an empty entry, and it rewrote every segment from Deneb at v1.1. One run hollowed ~1,580 gnosis segments and exited 0.

## Changes

- `DumpBlobSidecarsRange` requires a count fn: the antiquary's, moved to `freezeblocks.BlobCountFromBlocks`. It errors on a slot outside every frozen block segment.
- `--from` (lystopad's) starts at a segment boundary at or above Deneb.
- Ranges on disk or in `preverified.toml` are skipped. `--overwrite` refuses pinned or other-version ones.
- Old `.idx` and `.torrent` files go only after the new segment replaces the old one.
- Only beacon-block segments are opened; the dump stops at their frontier.

## Notes

Without `--overwrite` a damaged blob segment counts as present; `erigon snapshots integrity` detects it.

title: cl: learn attached validators from subscriptions and proposer preferences
body:
## Problem

Caplin learns which validators are attached to it only from `POST /eth/v1/validator/prepare_beacon_proposer`. Teku 26.10.1 and Prysm v7.3.0 validator clients stop sending that call once Gloas is active (Teku at its first Gloas slot), because signed proposer preferences replace it. When Caplin restarts in Gloas while such a validator client keeps running, the in-memory set is empty, and validators added after Gloas are never added to it. For such a Caplin node:

- validator custody is never raised (custody is recomputed in `OnBlock` only when the set is non-empty; on a test network it stayed at 4 custody groups instead of 96);
- gossip aggregates skip signature verification and return `ErrIgnore`, so they are not pooled, relayed or applied to fork choice, and blocks are packed from a smaller attestation pool (on the test network 4 to 10 attestations instead of about 390);
- gossip sync committee contributions are ignored;
- block production falls back to the zero fee recipient for slots without a per-slot preference.

Lighthouse keeps sending `prepare_beacon_proposer` after Gloas and is not affected.

## What changed

- `ValidatorParams` keeps a set of attached validator indices, and `GetValidators` returns it. `SetFeeRecipient` also adds the index to this set, so every `prepare_beacon_proposer` registration stays attached. Adding an attached validator changes neither `GetFeeRecipient` nor `Generation`.
- `POST /eth/v1/validator/beacon_committee_subscriptions` records every validator index in a non-empty request before subscribing, so it records them also when the node is still syncing (503). `POST /eth/v1/validator/sync_committee_subscriptions` records the indices of a request that passes validation, also for entries that have already expired. Like `prepare_beacon_proposer`, neither endpoint checks the validator index. Prysm also learns attached validators from beacon committee subscriptions, but only after a successful request, for indices in its head state, and for one hour.
- Once the wall clock is in Gloas, `POST /eth/v1/validator/proposer_preferences` stores the fee recipient of each item whose signature is valid for the validator's key in the head state. It does this also when gossip validation ignores the item, for example a slot that already passed. Before Gloas, `prepare_beacon_proposer` stays the only source, so preferences sent in the epoch before the fork do not replace the registered fee recipient. `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/proposer_preferences` and preferences received over gossip do not record anything. The response, gossip validation, the pool and publishing do not change. Teku also fills its prepared proposers from the preferences its validator client submits after Gloas. The signature check is shared with gossip validation (`VerifyProposerPreferencesSignature`).

## Tests

- `TestAttachedValidatorsAreIndependentFromFeeRecipients`: an attached-only validator is listed once, also when it later gets a fee recipient. A validator registered only through `SetFeeRecipient` is listed. Adding an attached validator creates no fee recipient and does not change the generation.
- `TestBeaconCommitteeSubscriptionRecordsAttachedValidatorsBeforeSubscribing`: a batch for validators 7 and 8 records both when the first subscription returns `ErrNotSynced`.
- `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionRecordsAttachedValidatorWhenExpired`. `TestSyncCommitteeSubscriptionRejectsInvalidIndices` now also checks that an invalid batch records nothing.
- `TestAggregateAndProofIsVerifiedWhenTheNodeHasValidators/attached`: an attached-only validator makes the aggregate verified and pooled instead of ignored.
- `TestOnBlockUpdatesCustodyForAttachedValidatorWithoutFeeRecipient`: an attached-only validator makes `OnBlock` update validator custody.
- `TestPostProposerPreferencesRecordsFeeRecipientFromValidPastPreference`: a signed preference for a past slot, posted to the validator endpoint, sets the fee recipient that block production's resolver (`feeRecipientForProposal`) then returns for a later slot. An invalid signature, a missing head state, an unknown validator, the beacon pool endpoint and a wall clock before Gloas store no fee recipient.

The new attached-only, subscription and preference positive cases failed before the fix; the fee-recipient cases and the negative cases guard existing and new code. Each of these mutations makes at least one test fail: removing a recording call, moving the committee recording into the subscription loop, moving the sync committee recording before validation or after the expiry check, not adding fee-recipient registrations to the attached set, skipping the signature check, recording from the beacon pool endpoint, or dropping the Gloas check.
author: domiwei

title: cl/das, cl/persistence/beacon_indicies, cl/phase1/forkchoice: persist the highest custody group count across restarts
body:
Part of #23566

## Problem

consensus-specs `fulu/validator.md` says a node SHOULD keep advertising the previous (highest) `custody_group_count`, and that this value SHOULD persist across node restarts. Caplin keeps it only in memory: `NewPeerDasState` starts at `CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT`, so after a restart a node that had raised its count advertises the minimum again. In a devnet, a standalone Caplin with 96 attached validators advertised `cgc=96`, was restarted, and came back with `cgc=4` (column subnets 96 -> 8).

## What changed

- `beacon_indicies`: `WriteHighestCustodyGroupCount` / `ReadHighestCustodyGroupCount` store the count under a new key in the existing `DbInfo` table of the Caplin indexing DB. For any valid custody group count, a write never lowers the stored value.
- `peerdas.UpdateValidatorsCustody` persists the count when the advertised count increases. `NewPeerDas` now takes a `kv.RwDB` for this.
- `peerdas.Start` reads the stored count and raises the advertised count before it subscribes to column subnets. This runs after `SetLocalNodeID`, so the raise also updates the ENR `cgc` entry, and the subscriptions, the ENR and the metadata use the stored value from then on. Both the standalone and the embedded Caplin go through `RunCaplinService`, so both are covered. Archive mode still subscribes to all subnets.
- `PeerDasState.RaiseAdvertisedCgc` raises only the advertised count. `SetCustodyGroupCount` uses the same code and still sets the real count.
- `PeerDasState.GetMyCustodyColumns` now computes and caches the custody columns under the cgc read lock. Before, a read that started before a raise could store the columns for the old count after the raise had cleared the cache, and the node then subscribed to and checked the old columns while it advertised the new count. The restore in `Start` adds one more raise at startup, so this change goes with it.
- `OnBlock` now calls `UpdateValidatorsCustody` after it releases the fork-choice lock. The call writes the indexing DB now, and the fork-choice stage holds an indexing-DB write tx while it waits for that lock, so the write must not happen under it. Concurrent `OnBlock` calls can now reach `UpdateValidatorsCustody` in a different order than they took the lock. The advertised and the stored counts only take the maximum, so when the DB writes succeed the order does not change them. The real count can reflect an older block until the next `UpdateValidatorsCustody` call, but nothing reads it in production.

The ENR seed in `cl/p2p` is unchanged. Discovery and the sentinel metadata handler start before `peerdas.Start`, so for a short time during startup the ENR and the metadata still show `CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT`. When `Start` raises the count, the ENR gets the stored value with a higher sequence number.

A failed DB write or read is only logged. A failed write is not retried until the advertised count increases again, so after a restart the node can come back with an older stored value. A failed read in `Start` is not retried for that run.

Out of scope, for later PRs:
- `earliest_available_slot` following the custody group count change (a later sentence in the same section of the spec). For this reason this PR does not close #23566.
- Backfill of columns when the custody group count increases.
- #24787.

## Tests

- `TestPeerDasRestoresHighestCustodyGroupCount`: raises the count to 96 through `UpdateValidatorsCustody` on an in-memory MDBX test DB (the chain-DB tables, which the Caplin DB also uses), then builds a new `PeerDasState` and `peerdas` on the same open DB and calls `Start`. It checks that the advertised count and the ENR `cgc` entry are 96. Before the fix it failed with `expected: 0x60, actual: 0x4`.
- `TestPeerDasStartWithoutStoredCustodyGroupCountKeepsRequirement`: with nothing stored, the count stays at `CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT`.
- `TestHighestCustodyGroupCountNeverDecreases`, `TestHighestCustodyGroupCountDefaultsToZero`: storage semantics.
- `TestRaiseAdvertisedCgcDoesNotChangeRealCgc`: raising to 96 updates the ENR and keeps the real count; a later lower value leaves the advertised count and the ENR unchanged.
- `TestRaiseAdvertisedCgcIsNotLostToAConcurrentCustodyColumnsRead`: in 1000 rounds, four goroutines call `GetMyCustodyColumns` on a new state while the main goroutine raises the count to 128; a final call must then return 128 columns. Before the fix it failed in 30 of 30 local runs (GOMAXPROCS 2, 4 and the default) with `should have 128 item(s), but has 8`. The test is probabilistic: in local runs with GOMAXPROCS=1 it did not catch the old code.
- `TestOnBlockUpdatesValidatorsCustodyWithoutForkChoiceLock`: fails if `UpdateValidatorsCustody` is called under the fork-choice lock.

The new non-error branches were mutation-checked locally: removing one makes one of these tests fail. The DB error paths in `Start`, `UpdateValidatorsCustody` and the storage accessors have no tests. The restart test reuses one open DB; it does not close and reopen MDBX.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes: cache the Gloas block body root by its encoding
body:
Part of #25120 (item 6).

## What and why

The node computes the root of a Gloas block body about 14 times for each block it imports from gossip. Each time, it hashes the full body again. This PR caches the root for Gloas and later bodies. Fulu and earlier bodies are not changed.

## Design

`BeaconBody.HashSSZ` encodes the body and compares the encoding with the cached one:

- byte-equal: it returns the cached root;
- different, or nothing cached yet: it hashes the body and stores `(encoding, root)` in an `*atomic.Pointer` that `NewBeaconBody` allocates.

Why byte-equality and not a dirty flag: the body fields are exported and mutable, nested values such as `AggregationBits` can change in place, and block production copies bodies by value. A flag cannot see these changes, but the encoding always does. Encoding is much cheaper than hashing.

- Struct copies share the pointer. A changed copy encodes differently, so it can only miss and store its own entry. It never returns a wrong root.
- Bodies built with a struct literal have a nil pointer and are hashed without the cache.
- The capacity hint for the encoding buffer uses the length of the cached encoding.
- Concurrent callers are safe: the entry is immutable and is swapped atomically.

## Cost

Each cached body keeps its encoding, about 41 KB for a full mainnet body. That is about 41 MB at 1,000 unfinalized blocks and about 410 MB at 10,000.

## Benchmark

`BenchmarkGloasBodyHashSSZ` in `cl/cltypes`, mainnet config, 8 full attestations and 4 full payload attestations, Apple M5 Pro, `-count 5`, run twice. The machine was under load, so the table shows the fastest run of each case.

| case | ns/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline: `hashSSZGloas()`, uncached (same as `main`) | 76,231 | 130,528 | 281 |
| miss: encode + hash + store | 80,884 | 269,144 | 445 |
| hit: encode + compare | 5,278 | 48,440 | 161 |

The benchmark file does not compile on `main` because it uses the new cache field, so the baseline calls `hashSSZGloas()` directly. On `main`, that is what `HashSSZ` runs for a Gloas body. A miss costs about 6% more than the baseline. A hit is about 14x faster.

## Tests

`cl/cltypes/beacon_body_root_cache_test.go`:

- a cache hit returns the stored entry, and a changed field replaces it;
- an in-place change of nested `AggregationBits` changes the root;
- changing a struct copy changes only the copy's root, and the original body still returns its own correct root;
- version gate: Fulu does not cache, Gloas and Heze do;
- a nil cache pointer falls back to hashing without the cache;
- `TestGloasBodyRootCacheConcurrent` checks concurrent callers. It is a `-race` guard: without the race detector it only checks that every root is correct.

Every root is also checked against an uncached `hashSSZGloas()`.

## Known limits

Two cases give equal encodings but different roots. In both, the cache could return the root of the other value. Neither can be reached, because decode, JSON parsing and block production validation reject both:

- `CommitteeBits` nil compared with a 0-bit vector;
- payload-attestation bitvectors with a non-standard width.

## Follow-up

`EncodingSizeSSZ` undercounts Gloas bodies by 396 bytes. Here it affects only the first capacity hint. It also backs the decode lower-bound check, so it needs a separate change.

## TDD note

The tests pin the cache behavior: a hit, invalidation after a change, struct copies, the version gate and concurrent callers. The branch was developed in review rounds and then squashed, so the commit does not show a separate red step. I checked this with a mutation: when the cache returns the stored root without comparing the encoding, the hit, nested-change and struct-copy tests fail.
author: domiwei

title: cl/transition, cl/phase1/core/state: verify Gloas bid and payload attestation signatures in the block batch
body:
## What and why

Part of #25120 (item 4).

Gloas block processing verified the execution payload bid signature and every payload attestation signature one by one, outside the block's batched BLS check. This PR adds them to the existing `bls.VerifyMultipleSignatures` batch in `machine.ProcessBlock`, the same way proposer slashings and voluntary exits already work.

## Changes

- `machine.ProcessBlock` adds the bid signature to the batch (not for self-build bids).
- `machine.ProcessOperations` adds one entry per payload attestation: the signature, the signing root, and the aggregated public key of the attesting PTC members.
- `impl.ProcessExecutionPayloadBid` and `impl.ProcessPayloadAttestation` no longer verify signatures. All other checks stay in place.
- `state.IsValidIndexedPayloadAttestation` becomes `state.IndexedPayloadAttestationSignatureSet`, and the bid signature helper moves to `state.ExecutionPayloadBidSignatureSet`. Both return signature-set inputs instead of verifying.
