- `ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadBid` moves from `impl/eth2` to `machine`. Block production uses it to evict a bad bid, as before.
- The spectest handlers for `execution_payload_bid` and `payload_attestation` verify the signature after the impl call, so the operation tests still cover signature failures.
- `CLAUDE.md` spec maps updated.

## Behaviour notes

- Accepted and rejected blocks are unchanged. Only the place where the signatures are checked moves.
- Error classification for bid eviction: when the batch fails and the block has a non-self-build bid, the bid signature is verified alone. If it is invalid, the error wraps `ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadBid` and production evicts the bid. If the bid is valid, the batch error is returned as before, so an invalid payload attestation or RANDAO signature does not evict a good bid.
- Known, accepted case: if an operation fails before the batch runs, an invalid bid signature is not seen, so production does not evict that bid. The block is rejected either way. `TestProcessBlockEarlierOperationFailureMasksInvalidBidSignature` pins this.
- The PTC signing domain still uses `compute_epoch_at_slot(attestation.data.slot)`, as in the spec.
- Aggregated PTC public keys go through the existing BLS public key cache.

## Benchmark

`BenchmarkProcessOperationsPayloadAttestationSignatures` (4 payload attestations, 512 validators, one extra signature in the batch), `-count 5`, Apple M5 Pro. The base run uses the same benchmark file on `origin/main`.

| | ns/op (median) | B/op | allocs/op |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base | 5,308,567 | ~210,100 | 452 |
| this PR | 2,661,125 | ~173,250 | 418 |

About 2x faster for this workload.

## Tests and spectests

- New `cl/transition/machine/block_signatures_test.go`: invalid bid and payload attestation signatures are rejected; an invalid bid takes precedence over an invalid payload attestation for classification; self-build does not classify as a bid error; duplicate PTC members; infinite or undecodable keys and signatures; pre-Gloas and Gloas batch errors are preserved; the masking case above.
- New handler tests: an invalid bid signature is evicted through the machine path, and a valid bid is kept when only a payload attestation signature is invalid.
- `go test ./cl/transition/... ./cl/phase1/core/state/... ./cl/beacon/handler/...` pass.
- Consensus spectests v1.7.0-beta.4, `-run '/mainnet/(gloas|fulu)/'`: 2932 pass, 0 fail.
- `make lint` clean, `make erigon integration` build.

## TDD

The new machine and handler tests pin the batch behaviour and the bid eviction classification for the moved checks. The helper renames in `state` and the move of `ErrInvalidExecutionPayloadBid` are refactors; the existing tests and the spectests cover them.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes/solid, cl/phase1/forkchoice: cache Gloas payload roots and hash them outside the fork-choice lock
body:
Part of #25120 (item 2: the uncached payload hash; the disk write under the lock is not in this PR).

## What and why

In Gloas, the execution payload uses progressive SSZ lists for `transactions` and `block_access_list`. `TransactionsSSZ.HashSSZProgressive` and `ByteListSSZ.HashSSZProgressive` did not cache their roots, so every `HashSSZ` call on the payload re-hashed every transaction and the whole block access list. `applyEnvelope` hashed the payload while it held `f.mu`, so this work blocked every other fork-choice reader and writer.

This PR caches the two progressive roots and computes them in `applyEnvelope` before it takes `f.mu`. The hash calls under the lock then read the cache.

## Changes

- `TransactionsSSZ` and `ByteListSSZ` get a separate progressive-root cache, `progressiveRoot *atomic.Pointer[[32]byte]`. Every mutation (`DecodeSSZ`, `UnmarshalJSON`, `SetBytes`, constructors) installs a new pointer, so a hash that loaded the old pointer can only fill the old, discarded cache. Hashing while another goroutine mutates the same object is still a data race, as before. The cache is filled with `CompareAndSwap(nil, ...)`, so concurrent hashers are safe.
- The legacy `TransactionsSSZ.root` cache is unchanged and stays separate from the progressive root.
- `applyEnvelope` warms the payload root caches before `f.mu.Lock()`, for both `validatePayload` values. It skips the warm-up when the envelope is already stored (`HasEnvelope`), because that path returns early without hashing.
- The transaction-aliasing contract is unchanged: `UnderlyngReference()` callers only read the slices, and the existing legacy root cache already relies on the same contract.

## Benchmark

`BenchmarkEth1BlockHashSSZGloas` in `cl/cltypes/eth1_block_bench_test.go`, `-count=5`, Apple M5 Pro, `main` vs this PR, runs interleaved. The machine was under load, so the cold numbers are noisy (the cold difference is not significant, p=0.690).

| Case | main | this PR | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300 tx / 100 KB BAL, cold | 543.5 µs, 430.3 KiB, 1534 allocs | 479.7 µs, 430.3 KiB, 1536 allocs | ~ |
| 300 tx / 100 KB BAL, warm | 534.1 µs, 430.3 KiB, 1534 allocs | 1.92 µs, 2.4 KiB, 20 allocs | -99.6% |
| 1500 tx / 400 KB BAL, cold | 2.32 ms, 1.87 MiB, 7537 allocs | 2.08 ms, 1.87 MiB, 7539 allocs | ~ |
| 1500 tx / 400 KB BAL, warm | 2.11 ms, 1.87 MiB, 7537 allocs | 1.99 µs, 2.4 KiB, 20 allocs | -99.9% |

"Cold" hashes a freshly decoded payload; "warm" hashes the same payload again. On `main` both cases do the full work.

## Tests

- `TestTransactionsSSZProgressiveRootMemoized`, `TestByteListSSZProgressiveRootMemoized`: a second progressive hash allocates nothing, so it is served from the cache.
- `TestTransactionsSSZMutationInvalidatesProgressiveRoot`, `TestByteListSSZMutationInvalidatesProgressiveRoot`: after `DecodeSSZ` (also empty input), `UnmarshalJSON` or `SetBytes`, the root matches a fresh object with the new data, not the cached old root.
- `TestTransactionsSSZDecodeFailureInvalidatesProgressiveRoot`: a `DecodeSSZ` that fails after it has partly replaced the data still drops the old cached root.
- `TestTransactionsSSZLegacyAndProgressiveRootsAreSeparate`: the legacy and progressive roots do not overwrite each other, in either call order.
- `TestTransactionsSSZProgressiveRootConcurrent`, `TestByteListSSZProgressiveRootConcurrent`: concurrent first hashes all return the correct root; with `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid/` they guard the cache against data races.
- `TestApplyEnvelopeWarmsPayloadRootCachesBeforeLock`: with `f.mu` held by the test, `applyEnvelope` fills both payload root caches before it gets the lock, for `validatePayload` true and false.
- `TestApplyEnvelopeSkipsPayloadRootCacheWarmupForStoredEnvelope`: for an envelope that is already stored, `applyEnvelope` does not hash the payload.

## TDD note

The cache behavior was driven by the `solid` tests above. The warm-up line in `applyEnvelope` adds no logic beyond what the two forkchoice tests pin. The benchmark adds no production logic; it only provides the numbers above.
author: domiwei

title: cl: batch-verify gossip PTC signatures and re-check failed batches in parallel
body:
Part of #25120 (item 3).

## What and why

Each gossip PTC message (`payload_attestation_message`) was verified on its own with `bls.VerifyAggregate`. With up to 512 messages per slot, that is about 0.6–0.7 ms of CPU per message. This PR sends gossip PTC signatures through `BatchSignatureVerifier`, which verifies them in randomized batches.

A failed batch is expensive: `handleIncorrectSignatures` re-checked every entry one by one on the queue goroutine, so one invalid signature in a 50-entry batch cost about 50 serial verifications before any waiter got its result. This PR also makes that fallback parallel, which helps every queue, not only PTC.

The PR has two commits:
1. `cl/phase1/network/services: re-check failed batch entries in parallel`
2. `cl: batch-verify gossip PTC signatures`

## Changes

### Parallel fallback (first commit)

- The entries of a failed batch are verified in parallel. Callbacks, error reports and the peer ban still run in the original input order, after all checks finish.
- One `semaphore.Weighted` per verifier limits the fallback work. Its size is `GOMAXPROCS` at construction, and it is shared by all queues and by `ImmediateVerification`.
- Each entry takes a weight of `min(len(signatures), budget)`, so an entry with more signatures than the budget can still run.

### PTC batch verification (second commit)

- `OnGossipPayloadAttestationMessage` takes a `PayloadAttestationSignatureVerifier`. When it is nil, the signature is verified immediately as before. The signature is still the last check, and the vote is applied only after it passes.
- `payloadAttestationService` passes the batch verifier for gossip messages only. REST and pending messages are still verified immediately.
- A dedicated PTC queue in `BatchSignatureVerifier` flushes every 20 ms instead of the default 50 ms. PTC votes are due at 75% of the slot, so a shorter wait keeps them closer to the deadline.
- **Per-slot fallback:** after the batch verifier reports an invalid signature for a slot, later gossip messages for that slot are verified immediately. The marker keeps the highest such slot, so a late failure report for an older slot cannot cancel the fallback for a newer one. Cancellation and shutdown (`ErrIgnore`) do not set it.
- An invalid signature is still REJECT with one peer ban.

## Trade-offs

- Without forged signatures, a PTC vote waits up to one batch interval: p50 about 13 ms and max about 30 ms in the harness below, compared with about 1–2 ms before.
- One forged signature makes its batch fail, so the honest votes in it wait for the parallel fallback. With the per-slot fallback, this costs at most the batches that are already queued when the first failure is reported, once per slot. If all votes of a slot arrive within about one batch round-trip, the fallback helps little for that slot.
- `validationAdmission` (512) is held while a message waits for its batch, so during a burst, local REST submissions can wait longer (measured 60–170 ms).
- An attacker who sends invalid signatures can now use all cores for fallback checks, not about one core per queue. The total work is the same as before.
- At `GOMAXPROCS=1`, nothing runs in parallel, and the mean waiter latency for a failed batch is about twice as high: before, an early entry got its result as soon as its own check finished.
- `Acquire` does not use the verifier context. A wait is bounded by the running checks, also at shutdown.

## Benchmark

All numbers are from an Apple M5 Pro (18 cores).

`BenchmarkBatchSignatureVerifierFallback`, a 50-entry batch with one invalid signature, base vs this PR at the same `GOMAXPROCS`:

| GOMAXPROCS | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 47.8 ms | 48.6 ms |
| 4 | 43.7 ms | 18.2 ms |
| 8 | 45.4 ms | 11.7 ms |
| 18 | 45.6 ms | 9.3 ms |

The all-valid case is unchanged. Total CPU time for the failed case is 4–7% higher.

PTC cases of the same benchmark, concurrent `individual` baseline vs batch, time per message:

| Case | `-cpu 1` batch | `-cpu 1` individual | `-cpu 8` batch | `-cpu 8` individual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all valid | 313 µs | 596 µs | 78 µs | 90 µs |
| 1 invalid in batch | 944 µs | 595 µs | 169 µs | 88 µs |

Latency harness, 512 PTC messages arriving at random times within 1 s, GOMAXPROCS 18, all valid: p50 / max latency 13.5 / 26 ms at 20 ms, 29.9 / 59 ms at 50 ms, 1.2 / 3 ms for immediate verification. CPU per run: 534 ms, 387 ms and 758 ms.

The "1 invalid" rows were measured before the per-slot fallback; with it, only the first batches of a slot can fail.

## Tests

Parallel fallback:
- `TestBatchSignatureVerifierChecksFailedBatchEntriesConcurrently`: the checks of a failed batch run at the same time, and callbacks still run in input order when the checks finish in a different order.
- `TestBatchSignatureVerifierSharesFallbackConcurrencyBudget`: two failed batches on different queues together never run more checks at once than the shared budget allows.
- `TestBatchSignatureVerifierCapsFallbackWeightAtBudget`: an entry with more signatures than the budget does not block forever.

PTC batch verification:
- `TestOnGossipPayloadAttestationMessageUsesInjectedSignatureVerifier`, `TestOnGossipPayloadAttestationMessageInjectedVerifierErrorRejects`: fork choice uses the injected verifier, and its error is a REJECT, not an IGNORE.
- `TestVerifyPayloadAttestationBatchMatchesSinglePath`: the batch path accepts and rejects the same signatures as the immediate path.
- `TestBatchSignatureVerifierUsesPayloadAttestationFlushInterval`: the PTC queue flushes after exactly 20 ms, all other queues after 50 ms, also after a full batch.
- `TestPayloadAttestationServiceSelectsSignatureVerifierByIngress`: gossip uses the batch verifier; REST and pending do not.
- `TestPayloadAttestationServiceBatchSignatureOutcomes`: invalid gossip is rejected, valid gossip is accepted, an invalid batch result switches only its slot to immediate verification, a raw fallback error also does, an older failure does not replace a newer fallback slot, and cancellation is a retryable IGNORE that does not set the fallback.

The concurrency and timing tests use `testing/synctest`, so a regression fails fast instead of hanging.
author: domiwei

title: cl/antiquary, cl/persistence, db: store the Gloas PTC window once per epoch
body:
Part of #25120 (item 7).

## What and why

The Caplin archive stored the Gloas `ptc_window` (96 slots × 512 validator indices, 393,216 bytes raw) in `PtcWindowTable` for every slot. The window changes only at epoch boundaries (`process_ptc_window`), so 31 of every 32 rows were copies. On mainnet this would cost about 0.74–1.2 GB per day.

This PR stores the window once per epoch in a new table and Caplin state snapshot type, `PtcWindowEpoch`. The estimate is about 23 MB per day at Sepolia size and about 37 MB per day at mainnet size, roughly 32× less.

A new type is used instead of changing the meaning of the existing `PtcWindow` rows: old binaries would misread sparse rows in the old type, and a minor file-version bump does not stop them, because Caplin state snapshots accept minor bumps as content-only.

## Changes

- New `kv.PtcWindowEpochTable` and snapshot type `PtcWindowEpoch` (`MinCaplinEnum+35`). The key is the epoch-start slot. The value is the zstd-compressed SSZ of the exact window.
- The antiquary writes one row per Gloas epoch:
  - in `addGenesisState`, which covers a fork at genesis and the anchor state;
  - at each Gloas epoch boundary, which also covers epochs without blocks;
  - at the fork. If the first Gloas block is after the fork slot, the state is advanced to the fork slot first.
- `ReadHistoricalState` reads the row at `RoundSlotToEpoch(slot)`. A missing row returns `ErrMissingGloasData`. A row that does not decode, or has the wrong SSZ length, is a hard error.
- `PtcWindowTable` is no longer written or read. Its table, snapshot type and existing data stay, so old binaries keep working.
- Startup: if states were already processed past the fork but the fork-epoch row is missing (in the DB and in snapshots), the antiquary re-processes from the last pre-Gloas epoch start that has a block.
- Snapshot dump: a range with an empty epoch-start row at or after the fork is not dumped yet, and is retried later.
- Availability: `IndicesMax` treats `PtcWindowEpoch` as covered up to the Gloas fork slot (`GloasForkEpoch × SlotsPerEpoch`, saturated), because its files are empty by definition before the fork. Without a beacon config the strict rule stays.
- `seg publishable` requires `PtcWindowEpoch` files ending at the common end of the other state types only when that end is past the fork slot; otherwise present files get only the structural checks. If the beacon config cannot be resolved, the files are always required. For a known chain, it also checks that every epoch-start word at or after the fork is non-empty and that each file has the expected word count. `seg integrity --check=Publishable` runs the same check.
- A no-op migration, `create_ptc_window_epoch_table`, creates the new table in existing databases, so tools that open chaindata in accede mode do not fail. `DBSchemaVersion` is unchanged.

## Rollout

`PtcWindowEpoch` limits state-snapshot availability only at and after the Gloas fork slot.

- Chains before the fork (mainnet and Gnosis, where it is not scheduled, and Hoodi until 2026-10-26): Caplin state snapshots work as before, without any `PtcWindowEpoch` files. Nodes that dump state snapshots write the all-empty pre-fork files themselves, so publishing them is optional.
- Chains past the fork (Sepolia today, Hoodi after its fork): until `PtcWindowEpoch` files are published, state-snapshot availability ends at the last pre-fork slot, and the antiquary processes the rest locally from just before the fork. To keep full availability, publish the new files before releasing:
  1. Run the snapshot generator with this binary. It re-processes from the fork and produces the post-fork range.
  2. Publish the new files in the preverified lists. Keep the old `PtcWindow` files, because older releases still need them.
  3. Then release the binary.

Effects:
- Existing archive nodes continue from their DB progress. A Sepolia node that is past the fork re-processes from just before the fork once.
- Older binaries ignore the new type. On Sepolia, their state snapshots end at the last `PtcWindow` file, and they antiquate the rest locally.
- Existing `PtcWindowTable` rows on upgraded nodes are not deleted (on Sepolia, about 10 GB since the fork, estimated, not measured).
- Downgrading after running this binary leaves slots without old rows; the old binary then re-antiquates them through its normal backoff.

## Tests

- `TestPtcWindowStoredOncePerEpoch` (`cl/antiquary/ptc_window_epoch_test.go`) checks the exact row for every epoch over six Gloas spec fixtures: a block exactly at the fork, a first block later in the fork epoch, the only block in the epoch after the fork, a fork at genesis, an anchor followed by two epochs without blocks, and a 64-block chain. It also checks that `PtcWindowTable` stays empty. The expected rows come from replaying the fixture blocks through the state transition and taking the window of each Gloas state, independently of the antiquary code.
- `TestPtcWindowEpochSnapshotRead`: the row is read from a snapshot segment.
- `TestPtcWindowEpochRestart`: a restart in the middle of an epoch.
- `TestPtcWindowEpochUpgradeReplay`, `TestPtcWindowEpochUpgradeReplayStartsBeforeFork`, `TestPtcWindowEpochReconstructionStart`: upgrade from a DB without new rows, for a fork at genesis and a later fork.
- Missing and corrupt rows: `gloas_roundtrip_test.go`.
- Dump guard: `db/snapshotsync/caplin_state_ptc_window_epoch_test.go`.
- Fork-aware availability: `TestCaplinStateBlocksAvailableBeforeUnscheduledGloasFork`, `TestCaplinStateBlocksAvailableAtGloasFork`, `TestCaplinStateBlocksAvailableRequiresPtcWindowEpochFromGenesis` (`db/snapshotsync/caplin_state_lifecycle_test.go`).
- Publishability and content check: `cmd/utils/app/publishable_check_test.go` (including the fork-aware cases before an unscheduled or future fork, after the fork, and at the fork boundary), `db/integrity/caplin_state_integrity_test.go`.
- `TestGloasHistoricalStateRoots` (`empty_epoch_transition`) checks the full state root across an epoch boundary. Multi-block and later-fork fixtures cannot be used for a full-root check yet because of #25199 and #25200, which exist on `main` already. In those fixtures, a field-by-field diff shows that the PTC window matches.

The Gloas spec fixtures under `cl/antiquary/tests/test_data/gloas/` add 3.8 MB.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon/handler: retry payload preparation within the post-PTC window
body:
Part of #24119 (item 2).

## Problem

After the wake-up at the PTC deadline, any skip (block work in flight, an import, a still-pending payload path) waited for the next quarter-slot tick. With 12 s slots that tick can come after the state-work cutoff (10 s), so a short contention at the PTC deadline lost the whole preparation window for a Gloas EMPTY path. #24939 and #24938 list this as a known limitation.

## Change

While the selected head is a current-slot Gloas head and no outcome has settled for its target slot, the loop also wakes every `slot/48` (250 ms on 12 s slots). It stops retrying when:
- an outcome settles (success, a memoized failure, `unchanged`, or a FULL path that needs a fork-choice update), or
- the next retry would fall inside the state-work lead (`stateWorkLead`), so no work starts after the existing cutoff.

Other slots keep the quarter-slot ticker. Normal production and the gate, head and deadline checks are unchanged.

## Tests

`TestPreparePayloadLoopRetriesBusySkipAfterPTCDeadline` runs the real loop and gate in `testing/synctest` with ticks at 3, 6, 9 and 12 s and block work held from 8.999 s:
- block work ends at 9.1 s: exactly one attempt, after 9.1 s and before the 10 s cutoff (on main: none);
- block work ends at 10.1 s: no attempt.

`go test -race ./cl/beacon/handler/` passes; `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/network/services, cl/phase1/forkchoice: validate gossip attestations and aggregates against the target shuffling
body:
## Problem

Caplin validates `beacon_attestation_{subnet_id}` and `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` with the committee of its head state. The committees of an epoch depend on the chain up to the epoch's shuffling dependent slot. When a vote is for a known block on a branch whose shuffling for the target epoch differs from the head branch, the head committee is the wrong one, and an honest, correctly signed vote can fail the committee checks:

- an Electra or later attestation fails with `attester is not a member of the committee`;
- a pre-Electra attestation fails the aggregation bits length check, or the set bit maps to the wrong validator;
- an aggregate fails the aggregation bits length, aggregator membership or signature checks. The attesting indices that the aggregate path passes to fork choice (`ProcessAttestingIndicies`) also come from the head committee.

Each failed committee or signature check is a REJECT. On the attestation subnets a REJECT counts as an invalid message in the gossipsub peer score (`InvalidMessageDeliveries`, weighted with the square of the count), and the gossip manager also tries to queue a ban of the sending peer.

The order of the checks makes this worse. Subnet attestations ran all committee checks before the "[IGNORE] The block being voted for has been seen" check, so a vote for a block that is not imported yet (the usual case for the other branch during a split) was rejected instead of ignored and queued. Aggregates ran the committee index range check before it.

Spec, consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4:
- `validate_beacon_attestation_gossip` and `validate_beacon_aggregate_and_proof_gossip` in `specs/phase0`, `specs/electra` and `specs/gloas` `p2p-interface.md` check that the voted block has been seen (IGNORE, may be queued) before the committee count, lookup, size and membership checks.
- Fork choice `on_attestation` (`specs/phase0/fork-choice.md`) takes the committees from `store.checkpoint_states[attestation.data.target]` (`store_target_checkpoint_state`), so for fork choice the head committee does not decide whether such a vote counts. Caplin's `OnAttestation` already does this when the head state does not have the target's shuffling.
- The beta.4 gossip pseudocode itself reads the committee from the head state, so this change deviates from it on purpose. See "Deviation from the gossip pseudocode" below.

Devnet evidence (Kurtosis, Gloas): according to the operator, one client followed its own branch from slot 194. From slot 256, the first epoch whose shuffling depends on a slot after the split, the two Caplin logs contain 141 and 143 rejections of that client's subnet attestations (same peer) with `attester is not a member of the committee`. The operator reported that after that the client received no gossip at all.

## What changed

- `cl/phase1/forkchoice`: `headStateHasTargetShuffling` is exported as `HeadStateHasTargetShuffling` and added to `ForkChoiceStorageReader`, unchanged. New `TargetBeaconCommittee(target, slot, committeeIndex)` returns the committee and the committee count per slot from the target checkpoint state. It uses the existing cached and singleflight `getCheckpointState`. The committee slicing is shared with `checkpointState.getAttestingIndicies`.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: a shared `beaconCommittee` helper reads the committee from the head state when `HeadStateHasTargetShuffling` is true, which keeps the head-branch fast path, and otherwise from `TargetBeaconCommittee` after the head-state view is released. If the target state is not available, the message is ignored.
- A vote on another shuffling can make us build a checkpoint state before all of its signatures are checked, so the build path is bounded:
  - the services ask for the checkpoint of the voted block's own target, `(target.epoch, Ancestor(beacon_block_root, start slot of target.epoch))`, instead of the target root from the message. If that ancestor is unknown, the message is ignored; the message root is never used for a build. If the committee lookup succeeds, a message whose target root does not match is still rejected by the existing target-ancestor check;
  - `TargetBeaconCommittee` serves cached checkpoint states with no limit. For a missing state it allows at most 2 concurrent calls (`maxConcurrentTargetCommitteeBuilds`). It returns an error, so the message is ignored, when no slot is free or when the target does not descend from the finalized checkpoint read at that moment. The slot is taken before the finalized ancestor lookup and the state read. Otherwise it builds the state with the existing `getCheckpointState`: concurrent calls for the same checkpoint share one build through singleflight, and later calls reuse it while it stays cached. Each call takes a slot, so this bounds concurrency, not the total work over time.
  - before asking for the target committee, the services apply the seen-cache IGNORE and verify the signatures that do not need the committee: the attestation signature of an Electra or later single attestation (it names the attester), and the selection proof and aggregator signature of an aggregate. An invalid signature is a REJECT. So an Electra or later single attestation must carry a valid validator signature before a state is built, and two attestations of one validator with different data for the same target epoch form a slashable double vote. For an aggregate that reaches full verification (immediate processing, or a node with local validators), the aggregate attestation signature is checked later; other aggregate gossip keeps the existing IGNORE before that step. Pre-Electra single attestations name the attester only through the committee, so they have no pre-check;
  - for a missing state, `TargetBeaconCommittee` also refuses a target whose block is unknown or more than 4 epochs older than the attestation slot (`maxTargetCheckpointBlockAge`). Together with the finalized precondition, this limits uncached targets to known descendants of the finalized checkpoint within a 4-epoch window, by the target block's slot. It does not bound the replay distance to the nearest stored state, nor the total work over time.
- The head committee is copied inside the head-state view, because the view must not leak slices of the head state.
- Subnet attestations: the block-seen IGNORE (with the existing queue) now runs before the committee lookup. The Electra/Gloas `data.index` checks stay before the block-seen check, as in the spec, so they now run before the committee index and subnet checks (all three are REJECT). The other REJECT and IGNORE checks keep their relative order from `main`; the public key and domain lookup moves to just before signature verification. A nil subnet is passed through to the queued retry instead of being dereferenced.
- Aggregates: the committee lookup and the committee index range REJECT now run right after the block-seen IGNORE (on the target path the lookup first does the checks described below). The other checks keep their order. The attesting indices are computed from the committee and the aggregation bits, so fork choice is credited with the target-shuffling validators.
- Public keys and the signing domain still come from the head state. Committee members are active, activation needs a finalized eligibility epoch, and both the head and the voted block descend from the finalized checkpoint, so each committee member has the same index and key in the head state.
- A real non-member of the committee selected by its target shuffling is still rejected.

## Tests

Test-first (author-reported): the new acceptance, ordering, unavailable-state and build-bound tests were written first and failed before the production change. The REJECT and fast-path tests are guards that keep the existing behavior; the mutation checks below show that they are not vacuous.

- `TestElectraAttestationUsesTargetShuffling`, `TestPreElectraAttestationUsesTargetCommitteeMember`, `TestAggregateAndProofUsesTargetShuffling`, `TestAggregateAndProofElectraUsesCommitteeBitsIndexForTargetShuffling`: a vote on another shuffling is accepted, the target committee is requested with the message's target epoch, the voted block's ancestor at the start of that epoch as the root, the attestation slot and the committee index, the pre-Electra public key is the one of the target committee member, and the aggregate credits the target committee in fork choice.
- `TestElectraAttestationRejectsNonMemberOfTargetCommittee`, `TestAggregateAndProofRejectsAggregatorOutsideTargetCommittee`: a member of the head committee that is not in the target committee is rejected.
- `TestAttestationForUnseenBlockIsIgnoredBeforeCommitteeChecks`, `TestAggregateAndProofUnseenBlockIsIgnoredBeforeCommitteeRange`, `TestAttestationForUnseenBlockWithNilSubnetIsIgnored`: a vote for an unseen block is ignored before the committee checks.
- `TestAttestationIgnoresUnavailableTargetCheckpointState`, `TestAggregateAndProofIgnoresUnavailableTargetCheckpointState`: a missing target state gives IGNORE.
- `TestAttestationKeepsHeadShufflingFastPath`: when `HeadStateHasTargetShuffling` is true, the service does not ask for the target committee and does not do the extra ancestor lookup that derives the target root from the voted block.
- Order guards: `TestElectraAttestationAlreadySeenBeforeTargetAncestor`, `TestAggregateAndProofAlreadySeenBeforeTargetAncestor`, `TestElectraAttestationRejectsNonMemberBeforeFinalizedAncestor`, `TestAggregateAndProofRejectsCommitteeRangeBeforeFinalizedAncestor`, `TestElectraAttestationChecksEpochRangeBeforeStructuralIndex`.
- `TestTargetBeaconCommitteeUsesCheckpointState` uses a real fork choice store with a side branch.
- Build bound: `TestTargetBeaconCommitteeLimitsUncachedBuilds` (at the limit no state is read and fork choice looks up no ancestor, one build below the limit is admitted, cached states are still served, the slot is released after a failed build), `TestTargetBeaconCommitteeRejectsTargetOutsideFinalizedChain` (no state is read for a target outside the finalized chain; the finalized root itself is admitted), `TestElectraAttestationBuildsVotedBlockTargetBeforeRejectingMessageTarget` and `TestAggregateAndProofBuildsVotedBlockTargetBeforeRejectingMessageTarget` (the target is derived from the voted block root, and a wrong message target is still rejected).
- Signature and age checks: `TestElectraAttestationRejectsInvalidSignatureBeforeTargetShuffling`, `TestElectraAttestationAlreadySeenBeforeTargetShuffling`, `TestAggregateAndProofRejectsInvalidSignatureBeforeTargetShuffling`, `TestAggregateAndProofAlreadySeenBeforeTargetShuffling` (an invalid signature is rejected and a seen vote is ignored, both before the target committee is requested; the valid target-path tests check that the signature is verified before the lookup), `TestTargetBeaconCommitteeLimitsCheckpointBlockAge` (more than 4 epochs old and unknown target blocks are refused without reading a state; exactly 4 epochs is allowed), and `TestAttestationIgnoresUnknownVotedBlockTargetAncestor` and `TestAggregateAndProofIgnoresUnknownVotedBlockTargetAncestor` (an unknown voted-block ancestor is ignored before any signature check or lookup).
- Existing REJECT cases in `TestAttestationProcessMessage` and the aggregate tests now set up a known block so that they still reach their rule. They also assert that the error is not an IGNORE.
- Mutation checks: removing each new branch (target path, head fast path, IGNORE on a missing state, block-seen order, aggregate attesting indices, the out-of-range guard in fork choice, seen-before-target order, the build limit and its exact capacity, the limit before the ancestor lookup, the finalized precondition, the cache bypass of the limit, the counter release, the derived target root, the IGNORE for an unknown ancestor, the age limit and its boundary, the unknown target block, the signature pre-check, its position before the lookup and its absence on the fast path, the seen checks in the pre-check) makes at least one of these tests fail.
- `go test -race -p 2 ./cl/phase1/network/services/ ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/`, `go test -p 2 ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/... ./cl/phase1/network/...`, `make lint`, `make erigon`.

## Deviation from the gossip pseudocode

The executable gossip checks in consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4 read the committees from the head state, `store.block_states[get_head(store).root]` (phase0 [attestation](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L1037) and [aggregate](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#L746), electra [aggregate](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/electra/p2p-interface.md#L284)). For a vote whose shuffling differs from the head, this PR uses the shuffling of the vote's target checkpoint instead. That is the state fork choice `on_attestation` uses, [`store.checkpoint_states[attestation.data.target]`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/aa16bb4c156184e9548a997d53efaf2a228a6304/specs/phase0/fork-choice.md#L1025). When the shuffling is the same, both states give the same committees, so nothing changes for votes on the head branch.

Why:
- The head-state wording was added in consensus-specs #4902 (first released in v1.7.0-alpha.4). A reviewer [asked](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4902#discussion_r2896273921) which `state` the validation should use and noted that clients use different approaches. The editor [answered](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4902#discussion_r2925049154) with a commit that "tells the reader that the state is the head state", and added: "This feels a bit lazy, so maybe we can follow up later which explains why for each one." consensus-specs #5563 (v1.7.0-beta.1) then loaded the state from the store with `get_head(store)` to remove the ambiguous `state` parameter. The discussions in #4902 and #5563 do not cover votes on a branch with a different shuffling.
- The clients take the shuffling of the voted branch. The target is checked to be an ancestor of the voted block, so this is the same as the target checkpoint shuffling:
  - Lighthouse v8.3.0, [`with_committee_cache(target.root, ...)`](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/014ba06b56514d383426f2c727e7233dad973e0d/beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/attestation_verification.rs#L1617-L1663);
  - Prysm v7.3.0, [`AttestationTargetState`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/d01132449756e217d7f6c460e780174c34139b41/beacon-chain/blockchain/process_attestation_helpers.go#L23-L47), which uses the head state only when its dependent root matches the target's;
  - Teku 26.10.1, [`AttestationStateSelector`](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/115ab400185bebee063ce13d0ab7f9f80b296c4e/ethereum/statetransition/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/statetransition/validation/AttestationStateSelector.java#L57-L184);
  - Nimbus v26.10.1, [`getShufflingRef(target.blck, target.slot.epoch, false)`](https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/963756c91c19b7824cea57e7aab5857ce2c776c7/beacon_chain/gossip_processing/gossip_validation.nim#L1081-L1089);
  - Lodestar v1.50.0, [shuffling keyed by the voted block's dependent root](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/003bd66543fa65b5c1e954eec9e8077054c226dc/packages/beacon-node/src/chain/validation/attestation.ts#L712-L748);
  - Grandine 3.0.0-rc.1, [the target state](https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/blob/e60be4773c0c87648ad399df58a8fdafa38b1cdd/fork_choice_store/src/store.rs#L2904-L2933).

## Not changed here

- Failed checkpoint state builds are not cached. With the limits above, validators can still keep up to 2 uncached calls running, for checkpoints of known blocks that descend from the finalized checkpoint and are at most 4 epochs older than the attestation. On the target path the pre-checked signatures are verified again when the message reaches the normal batch verification, also when the checkpoint state is cached.
- Empty pre-Electra subnet attestations are still ignored, while the spec rejects them. This is unchanged by this PR.

This replaces the approach of draft #24808, which only skipped the peer ban and kept the REJECT.
author: domiwei

title: cl/persistence, cl/antiquary: apply Gloas payload match in historical participation replay
body:
## Summary

`HistoricalStatesReader.ReadParticipations` rebuilds the Gloas participation lists by replaying block attestations. The replay did not apply the Gloas payload-match rule, and it dropped errors from the attestation callback. A rebuilt Gloas state could have wrong `TIMELY_HEAD` flags and a wrong state root, or a partial participation list with a nil error.

Fixes #25199

## Payload-match rule (consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4)

`get_attestation_participation_flag_indices` now applies the Gloas rule in the historical path:

- a same-slot attestation (`is_attestation_same_slot`) needs `data.index == 0`;
- any other attestation gets `TIMELY_HEAD` only when `data.index == execution_payload_availability[parent_slot % SLOTS_PER_HISTORICAL_ROOT]`.

`parent_slot` is `state.latest_block_header.slot` before `process_block_header`, which is the slot of the block at `block.ParentRoot`. The replay resolves it from the block index and falls back to the genesis state's latest block header. The availability bit is read from the stored post-state of the including block. `process_parent_execution_payload` runs before `process_operations` and nothing later in the block changes the bit, so the stored value is the one the spec uses. Blocks without attestations skip the lookup; this keeps the synthetic genesis block of a Gloas-at-genesis chain (zero `ParentRoot`) a no-op. Pre-Gloas behaviour of the rule is unchanged.

Errors from the replay (randao mix, attesting indices, flag computation, parent lookup, availability) are now returned.

## Genesis-boundary fixes

The fixture tests could not pass without three more fixes:

- `readHistoricalBlockRoot` returned an error for the root at the genesis slot, so attestations that target epoch 0 were dropped. It now reads the DB for every slot from the genesis slot on and uses the genesis `block_roots` vector only for slots before it.
- In the genesis epoch, attestations were written to the previous epoch participation. An attestation now goes to the current epoch list exactly when its target is the epoch of the requested slot (`data.target.epoch == get_current_epoch(state)`). This also changes epoch-0 output for Altair through Fulu, to the value the spec state has.
- The antiquary wrote the active validator indices of the genesis epoch only at the next epoch boundary. `addGenesisState` now writes them too.

## Tests and fixtures

- `TestReadHistoricalStateGloasParticipation` rebuilds two Gloas mainnet chains through the antiquary and compares current/previous participation and the block state roots with the live transition. The fixtures are copied from consensus-spec-tests **v1.7.0-beta.2** (`sanity/blocks/attestations_after_missed_slot_use_applied_parent_payload_availability` and `sanity/blocks/attestation`); the beta.4 transition accepts them with full validation.
- `TestReadHistoricalStateGloasGenesisBlockWithoutAttestations`: synthetic Gloas genesis block with a zero parent root.
- `TestReadParticipationsReturnsBlockRootError`: error propagation.
- Unit tests: `TestReadHistoricalBlockRootAtGenesisSlot`, `TestGloasSameSlotAttestationRejectsNonzeroIndex`, `TestGloasSameSlotAttestationAfterGenesisSlot`, `TestPayloadMatchAppliesFromGloas` (Fulu keeps `TIMELY_HEAD`, Gloas drops it).

TDD note: `TestGloasSameSlotAttestationAfterGenesisSlot` and `TestPayloadMatchAppliesFromGloas` were added in the second commit, after the behaviour landed in the first one, to close coverage gaps found in review. They were checked by mutation: disabling the `data.slot != 0` same-slot branch, or removing the Gloas version gate, makes them fail. The genesis-block test was red before its fix.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/state/... ./cl/antiquary/...`
- the pre-Gloas reader round-trips with `ERIGON_RUN_HEAVY_TESTS=1`
- `make lint` (clean, repeated)
- `make erigon integration`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `ReadRandaoMixBySlotAndIndex` has the same genesis off-by-one as `readHistoricalBlockRoot` had: on chains with genesis slot 0 it uses the genesis mix instead of the final epoch-0 mix for epoch-2 attestations, so states in epochs 2 and 3 are rebuilt with wrong committees.
- The replay needs the `BlockRootToSlot` index and the availability rows for Gloas blocks with attestations; while the snapshot index is rebuilt, direct `ReadParticipations` callers (liveness, lighthouse) return an error, and antiquary init does not back off on that untyped error.
- A missing `ActiveValidatorIndicies` row is still read as an empty list.
- No test crosses the Fulu→Gloas fork or covers Heze; pre-Gloas reader tests run only with `ERIGON_RUN_HEAVY_TESTS`.
- The Gloas predicate is not shared with the live path in `cl/phase1/core/state`.
- Anchors at a slot other than 0 are only partly handled.
- `attestingIndicies` picks the attestation format from the attestation slot's epoch, not from the including block's version.
author: domiwei

title: cl/persistence: read Gloas queues before the first Gloas dump
body:
Fixes #25200

## Problem

`ReadHistoricalState` reads `builders`, `builder_pending_withdrawals` and `payload_expected_withdrawals` from the dump at `slot - slot % SlotsPerDump` plus the per-slot diffs. `ReadRequiredQueueSSZ` returned `ErrMissingGloasData` whenever that dump was missing. The antiquary writes these dumps only for a Gloas state, so every state between the Gloas fork slot and the first Gloas dump slot could not be read. On Sepolia these are slots 11296768–11297279. The same happens for an aligned fork slot whose block is missed.

## Fix

The change is reader-only. There is no antiquary change and no persistence-format change.

- `ReadHistoricalState` passes the Gloas fork slot to `ReadRequiredQueueSSZ`.
- A missing dump at or before the fork slot is read as an empty list. The antiquary does not initialize the Gloas queue writers from a pre-Gloas state, so the first Gloas diff holds the full list.
- In that case the replay starts at the dump slot itself, so a diff stored there is not skipped. When the dump is present, the replay still starts at the slot after it.
- A missing dump after the fork slot still returns `ErrMissingGloasData`.

## Tests

- `TestReadRequiredQueueSSZ_MissedForkSlotBlock`: aligned fork slot with a missed block. There is no dump, and the full diff is at the next slot.
- `TestReadRequiredQueueSSZ_MissingDumpAtForkSlotWithBlock`: the dump at an aligned fork slot is missing and the full diff is at the fork slot.
- `TestReadRequiredQueueSSZ_MissingDump`: adds a dump slot right after an unaligned fork, which still returns an error.
- `TestReadHistoricalState_GloasQueuesBeforeFirstDump`: end-to-end read with fork epoch 49, which is not a multiple of 48. The fork slot is 1568 and the pre-fork dump slot is 1536.
- `TestReadHistoricalState_GloasQueuesMissingDumpAfterFork`: end-to-end reverse case. The dump slot is after the fork and the dumps are missing, so the read returns `ErrMissingGloasData`.

**TDD:** each new test was written first and failed on the previous code for the intended reason:
- `MissedForkSlotBlock`, `MissingDumpAtForkSlotWithBlock` and `GloasQueuesBeforeFirstDump` failed with `ErrMissingGloasData` on the origin/main reader.
- `MissingDumpAtForkSlotWithBlock` returned `[b]` instead of `[a, b]` before the replay-start fix.
- The added `MissingDump` case expects an error, so it also passes on origin/main. It guards the relaxed check against admitting a dump slot after the fork.
- The two `ReadHistoricalState` tests fail under the mutations `gloasForkSlot := r.cfg.GloasForkEpoch` and `gloasForkSlot := ^uint64(0)`. Both mutations passed the suite before these tests existed.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/state/historical_states_reader/ ./cl/antiquary/ -count=1`
- `make lint`, two runs, 0 issues
- `make erigon integration`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Builders queue encoder: in-place updates are lost, and a duplicate trailing entry breaks the truncate count (#25205).
- If every slot from the fork slot through the next dump slot is missed, there is no Gloas dump there and reads still return `ErrMissingGloasData` until the following dump. This needs 33+ missed slots; on Sepolia it needs 513.
- `GloasForkEpoch * SlotsPerEpoch` overflows for a far-future fork epoch. It is reachable only when the reader's config differs from the config that wrote the DB, for example in capcli.
- There is no writer-to-reader test across the Gloas fork.
- The empty-base path cannot tell a lost first full diff from a missed slot. This happens only with lost rows, not with data the antiquary writes.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes/solid: cache progressive list roots across state copies
body:
Part of #25120 (item 5).

## What and why

Gloas hashes six state lists with `ListSSZ.HashSSZProgressive(nil)`: pending deposits, pending partial withdrawals, pending consolidations, builders, builder pending withdrawals and payload expected withdrawals. `HashSSZProgressive` had no cache, and raw `CopyInto` marks every top-level leaf dirty, so the first hash after each state copy recomputed all six lists. With about 7.6k pending deposits, that is about 4.6 ms per hash after a copy, while Fulu uses the cached legacy root. Gloas copies the state several times per slot.

`ListSSZ.HashSSZ()` cannot be used instead: its cached root is the pre-Gloas list root.

## Changes

All production changes are in `cl/cltypes/solid/list_ssz.go`.

- `ListSSZ` gets a progressive-root cache, separate from the legacy `root`. It is filled with `CompareAndSwap(nil, ...)` after a `HashSSZProgressive(nil)` call. A call with a custom element hasher never reads or writes it.
- Every mutator (`Set`, `Append`, `Clear`, `Truncate`, `Cut`, SSZ decode, `UnmarshalJSON`) clears both caches through one `invalidateRoots` helper. A list reuses its cache holder, so a mutation does not allocate after the first one.
- The cache holder records its owner, and only the owner uses it. A Go value copy of a `ListSSZ` (for example inside `ExecutionPayloadBid`) therefore never reads a root that belongs to another list.
- `ShallowCopy` always gives the copy its own holder and carries the source's progressive root into it, filled or not. A copy of an unchanged list hashes for free, a copy of a list that was not hashed yet caches its root on its first hash, and a later mutation on either side invalidates only that side.
- `raw/hashing.go`, `raw/copy.go` and the state setters are unchanged.

## Contract

The cache relies on the same rule as the existing legacy root: list contents change only through `ListSSZ` methods or by replacing the whole list. I audited every writer of the six lists. All of them use `ListSSZ` methods or set a new or `ShallowCopy`'d list, and no production code writes fields of an element obtained through `Get` or `Range`. Writing through a Go value copy (`cpy := *list; cpy.Set(...)`) shares the backing array and leaves the original's caches stale, as it already did for the legacy root. No production code does that.

## Benchmark

Apple M-series, 6 runs each, `origin/main` vs this PR:

| Benchmark | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `BenchmarkHashSSZAfterCopyInto/gloas` (7.6k pending deposits) | ~4.6 ms, 2.83 MB, 39,746 allocs | ~375 µs, 280 KB, 1,442 allocs |
| `BenchmarkHashSSZAfterCopyInto/fulu` | ~310 µs, 265 KB, 1,187 allocs | ~292 µs, 265 KB, 1,190 allocs |
| `BenchmarkListSSZAppend` (7,600 appends) | ~21.5 µs, 17 allocs | ~25.9 µs, 19 allocs |

The append loop is about 4 µs slower per 7,600 appends, from the cache check on each mutation. Fulu `CopyInto` has 3 more allocations, from the holders of the copied lists.

## Tests

- `cl/cltypes/solid/list_ssz_progressive_root_test.go`: memoization; invalidation by each mutator; `ShallowCopy` with a cold and a warm root, mutated on the source and on the copy; a cold copy and a copy of it cache their root after the first hash (`TestListSSZColdShallowCopyCachesProgressiveRoot`); Go value copies; the legacy and progressive caches stay separate in both call orders; custom element hashers; concurrent first hashes; `Clone`; steady-state `Append` allocations.
- `cl/phase1/core/state/raw/hashing_copy_gloas_test.go`: for each of the six lists, mutated on the source and on the copy, the state root matches a freshly decoded state.
- `TestUpgradeToGloasStateRootMatchesDecodedState` (`upgrade_test.go`) now has non-empty queues before the Fulu hash, so warm legacy roots cannot leak into the Gloas root.
- Gloas spectests with the beta.4 fixtures: the same PASS/SKIP set as `main` (operations, epoch_processing, sanity, transition, fork, ssz_static). `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid/ ./cl/phase1/core/state/...` passes.

Each invalidation and copy path was checked by removing it and confirming that a test fails.
author: domiwei

title: cl/persistence, cl/antiquary: write queue diffs from the longest overlap
body:
Fixes #25205

Stacked on #25212: review only the last four commits. The last commit updates one test of this PR for the `ReadRequiredQueueSSZ` signature from #25212.

This PR must ship in the same release as #25231 (builders per-index diff) and #25234 (builder pending payments base plus deltas), which are stacked on it. Without them, a Gloas node writes `builders` rows that rewrite the whole list on every in-place change.

## Problem

The state antiquary stores per-slot diffs of the Electra queues (`pending_deposits`, `pending_consolidations`, `pending_partial_withdrawals`) and the Gloas lists (`builders`, `builder_pending_withdrawals`, `payload_expected_withdrawals`) with `SSZQueueEncoder`. The encoder remembered only the previous size and the previous last element. It searched the new list backwards for that element and wrote "truncate N from the front" plus the elements after it. Two cases broke this:

- `builders` changes in place (withdrawals, deposits, exits). When a builder that is not the last one changed, the diff was "truncate 0, append nothing", so the change was lost until the next dump.
- When an appended entry equalled the previous last entry, the search picked the appended copy, the truncate count went negative and wrapped in `uint32`, and replay emptied the queue.

## Fix

The diff byte format and the replay format are unchanged.

- `Initialize` keeps a copy of the previous list's element pointers in a slice the encoder owns.
- `WriteDiff` first tries a fast path based on pointer identity: queue elements are copy-on-write, so equal pointers hold equal values. If the previous list's tail and the new list's head hold the same pointers, it writes the diff directly. This covers unchanged queues, append-only slots and front pops plus appends.
- Otherwise it finds the longest suffix of the previous list that equals a prefix of the new list with KMP, which is linear in the list sizes, and writes `truncate = prevLen - overlap` plus `new[overlap:]`. An in-place builder change becomes a full rewrite of the list for that slot.
- `ApplySSZQueueDiff` returns the new `ErrCorruptQueueDiff` when the truncate count is larger than the queue length, before it changes the queue. The readers wrap it, and the antiquary resume backs off on it like it does for `ErrMissingGloasData`.

## Upgrade note

There is no migration: the stored bytes of a wrong diff cannot be repaired, and each wrong window ends at the next dump (at most 1535 slots). Re-antiquation does not repair rows already frozen in Caplin state snapshot files, and nothing regenerates a frozen range automatically. On Sepolia the Gloas range written by older releases stays wrong. Electra ranges are affected only in the rare case where two equal queue entries were appended in a row.

## Tests

- Collector tests: an in-place change to builder 0 is kept, and an appended duplicate builder pending withdrawal no longer empties the queue.
- Encoder tests: in-place `Set` on the same list, duplicate last append, front cut plus postponed re-append, the fast path and its fallback when equal values have different pointers, `truncate == len` accepted and `truncate > len` rejected without changing the queue, an exhaustive round trip over all small lists with duplicates, and a check that the overlap search makes a linear number of equality calls.
- Reader and antiquary tests: the corrupt-diff error is wrapped by both readers, and the antiquary backoff includes it.
- Benchmark in `ssz_queue_bench_test.go`: at 100k `pending_deposits` entries, a diff takes about 0.24 ms.

TDD: the tests were written first and failed on the old code for the intended reason, except the `truncate == len` check and the linear-call check, which also pass on the old encoder and guard the new one. The fast-path test failed before the fast path was added.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/... ./cl/antiquary/... -count=1`
- `make lint`, two runs, 0 issues
- `make erigon integration`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `builders` gets its own per-index row format in #25231, so an in-place builder change no longer rewrites the whole list.
- No end-to-end test drives the antiquary backoff through a stored corrupt row.
- Copy-on-write of queue elements is a convention, not enforced by the type.
author: domiwei

title: cl/persistence, cl/antiquary: store builders history as a per-index diff
body:
Stacked on #25230 (which is stacked on #25212): review only the last two commits.

## Problem

The state antiquary writes one `kv.Builders` row per processed Gloas block with `SSZQueueEncoder`. Builders is a registry, not a queue: deposits, withdrawals and exits change builders in place. With the overlap encoder from #25205, any change to a builder that is not the last one rewrites the whole list for that slot, about 97 bytes per builder. At 200 builders that is about 19 KB per block, roughly 46–51 GB a year. The format has to change before Gloas reaches Hoodi and mainnet, because after that old rows would need a migration.

## Fix

`kv.Builders` gets a per-index diff format. Same table, same snapshot type. `kv.BuildersDump` and the other five queues are unchanged.

Row layout, little-endian, not compressed:

```
00 00 00 00 | 00 00 00 00 | 47 4c 4f 41 ("GLOA") | 01 (version) | 01 (kind)
newLength u64 | count u32 | count × (index u64, 93-byte Builder SSZ)
```

- The total length must be exactly `26 + 101*count`. A block with no builder change writes a 26-byte row. With one change at 200 builders a row is 127 bytes, against 19404 with the queue encoder.
- The writer, `BuildersDiffWriter`, keeps the pre-block builders as copied values. It writes every changed index plus the appended indices, in increasing order. The first Gloas row after the fork (empty baseline) carries the full list as appends. A shrink is an error.
- The decoder, `ApplyBuildersDiff`, checks the whole row before it changes the list. It rejects:
  - a wrong preamble, version or kind;
  - a wrong exact length;
  - a length above the registry limit, or a shrink;
  - indices that are not strictly increasing, or not below the new length;
  - appends that are not contiguous;
  - a builder that does not decode.
- `ReadBuildersSSZ` replays the rows on top of the dump, using the same dump rules as `ReadRequiredQueueSSZ` (#25212). A processed block (one with `kv.SlotData`) at or after the fork slot that has no row is an error. A missed slot is skipped. The Gloas genesis state writes a no-change row at its own slot, so it can be read when its slot is not a dump slot.
- Every rejection wraps the new `ErrHistoryRebuildRequired`, and the antiquary backs off on it like it does for `ErrMissingGloasData`.

The first 8 zero bytes are for old binaries. An older reader takes them as "truncate 0", then a zero-length builder, and fails decoding the empty builder before it changes the list. It does not mistake the row for a corrupt queue diff, so it does not back off and rewrite new rows in the old format.

## Upgrade note (for the release notes)

Hoodi operators must upgrade before the Gloas fork on 2026-10-26. This release changes the on-disk format of Caplin historical state rows for builders (per-index diff).

- The Caplin state snapshot types keep their file version.
- A node that reads an old-format row from its DB backs off and re-antiquates from before the Gloas fork.
- An older release that reads a new-format row fails with a decode error and does not read wrong data. Downgrading after new rows were written is not supported.
- #25205 must not ship without this format change.
- Sepolia is not repaired. Rows already frozen in Caplin state snapshot files, including the published Sepolia range 11250000–11300000, stay in the old format. Snapshot files are read before the DB and frozen ranges are not regenerated, so historical state reads that replay those rows keep failing until the range is reset or republished.
- The same applies to a node that passed a Gloas fork on an older release and has already frozen Gloas state snapshots.

## Tests

- **Codec:**
  - round trip over: no change, first, middle or last change, several changes, index reuse, append, reuse plus append, empty to one;
  - a change to each single non-balance field;
  - exact byte layout;
  - the baseline is a value copy;
  - shrink is an error;
  - about 20 rejected rows, each with no mutation;
  - both legacy queue decoders, before and after #25205, fail on a new row without changing the list.
- **Reader:** exact fork slot, missed fork slot, dump plus change plus append, a processed-block hole at the target and between the dump and the target, a missed slot, a pre-fork slot, and a legacy row (sentinel, with table and slot in the error).
- **Antiquary:**
  - backoff on the sentinel;
  - collector → mdbx → reader round trip;
  - the hook across the Fulu → Gloas fork;
  - a Gloas genesis state at a dump slot (0) and at a slot that is not a dump slot (32): the genesis row is the 26-byte no-change row, and both the genesis state and the next block's change read back;
  - a seam test with real 1000-slot snapshot files, pruning, and reads that cross the file boundary and the snapshot/DB boundary, compared with the lists actually written.
- **Benchmark:** `BenchmarkBuildersRowSize`. At 200 builders with one change per block, Initialize plus WriteDiff takes about 1.7 µs, 7 allocs and 127 bytes per row.

TDD: the codec, reader and backoff tests were written first and failed for the intended reason, either on undefined symbols or with the backoff predicate returning false. The genesis test also failed first: at slot 32 with `historical state row needs a rebuild: missing row from table Builders at slot 32`, and at slot 0 because the genesis slot had no row (an empty value where a 26-byte row was expected). Some later tests, the append-end check, the hole after a dump, and the single-field changes, guard existing behaviour and passed on first run. Each one was checked to fail when its target branch is disabled.

The snapshot file version is deliberately not bumped, so no Caplin snapshot republish is needed. The raw preamble tells old and new rows apart.

## Validation

- `go test ./cl/persistence/... ./cl/antiquary/... ./db/snapshotsync/... -count=1`, and `-race` on `cl/antiquary`
- `make lint`, two runs, 0 issues
- `make erigon integration`
- Dual review until converged: two review rounds, a fix-delta review and a fresh adversarial pass. The genesis-row commit had its own dual review, with no blocker.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Gloas required-queue history is unreadable when every slot from the fork through the next dump slot is missed: no Gloas dump is written at that slot. This is pre-existing and affects all three Gloas queues.
- `LatestExecutionPayloadBidTable` stores a redundant full bid per slot. It can be changed after the Hoodi fork.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network/registry: let one peer forward a slot's aggregates at once
body:
Fixes #25235.

The `beacon_aggregate_and_proof` topic allowed 8 messages per second per peer, with a burst of 16. Aggregates for a slot are published at the same point in the slot, so peers forward them in bursts. Gossipsub marks a message as seen before Caplin validates it, so an aggregate the limiter ignored was also dropped when other peers sent it, and the node lost whole committees.

One peer may now forward a whole slot's expected aggregates in one burst (`MaxCommitteesPerSlot * TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee`, 1,024 on mainnet), refilled over the slot. The other topics' limits are unchanged.

## Measurement

Mainnet node, pool read 1.4 s into the next slot, 40 slots each:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| committees with no aggregate (vs a Lighthouse reference: 0) | 24 | 0 |
| votes in the pool vs finally included | 98.8–99.0% | 99.87% |

## Tests

`TestAggregateAndProofRateLimiterAdmitsSlotBurstFromOnePeer` covers the mainnet and minimal presets; it fails on the old limit. `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds.
author: lystopad

title: cl: hand the post-fork-choice head state to synced data without copying it
body:
## Problem

`postForkchoiceOperations` copies the head state twice per slot:

1. `GetStateAtBlockRoot(headRoot)` returns a private copy. On the normal path it is a copy of the fork graph's current state, taken under the fork-choice read lock. Hoodi p50 is about 56 ms.
2. The head event, the payload attributes event and the attestation data producer read that copy.
3. `OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot` then copies it again into synced data. Hoodi p50 is about 38 ms.

After step 3, `postForkchoiceOperations` reads the head state only through `ViewHeadState`, so the second copy is not needed.

## What changed

- `synced_data`: new `OnOwnedHeadStateWithBlockRoot`. It takes ownership of a state that is already private and does not copy it. It uses the same `writeLock -> mu -> accessLock` order as the copying publish. The head becomes the new state, the previous state becomes the old head, and the spare is not touched. It rejects nil and any state the manager already holds, and in that case it changes nothing.
- `forkchoice`: new `GetOwnedStateAtBlockRoot`, a method on `ForkChoiceStore` only (the interface does not change).
  - Current-state path: the same copy as `GetStateAtBlockRoot`.
  - Replay path: the replayed state is copied. Replay applies stored fork-graph blocks, and some transition setters keep the block's pointers in the state: `AddEth1DataVote` / `SetEth1Data` (block `Eth1Data`) and `SetLatestExecutionPayloadBid` (Gloas bid). The copy makes sure that the published state shares no storage with fork-graph blocks.
  - `GetStateAtBlockRoot` and its other callers (for example `saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded`) keep the same behavior and cost. The locked current-state copy moved into a small `copyCurrentState` helper that both getters use.
- `stages`: `postForkchoiceOperations` uses both new methods and does not use its local head state after the publish. Block production, forward sync and startup still use the copying publish.

## Cost

- Normal path (head is the fork graph's current state): one full state copy per slot instead of two.
- Replay path (head is not the current state, for example after a side-branch block): the copy work is the same as before, one full copy. The difference is that the copy is a new allocation instead of a `CopyInto` into synced data's spare state. This path is not the steady state, and it already allocates a full state when it reads the base state from disk.
- Synced data still keeps at most three full states (head, previous, spare).

## Hoodi results

Measured on a Hoodi node (about 1.14M validators) with probe timings, comparing the same build with and without this commit (about 2,000 slots each, after warm-up):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Second copy (`OnHeadStateWithBlockRoot`) p50 | 38 ms | 0 ms |
| `postForkchoiceOperations` total p50 | 189 ms | 150 ms |
| `postForkchoiceOperations` total p99 | 1648 ms | 1629 ms |
| First copy (`GetStateAtBlockRoot`) p50 / p99 | 55 / 141 ms | 55 / 147 ms |
| Epoch transition p50 | 428 ms | 428 ms |
| Go anonymous memory | 9.0-9.5 GB | 8.0-8.4 GB |
| GC pause per hour | ~0.02 s | ~0.03 s |

No errors, no invalid blocks and no fork-choice writer waits of 1 s or more in either run. The p99 is dominated by the head-state dump every fourth slot, which this change does not touch.

## Tests

All new tests were written first and failed before the production change:

- `cl/beacon/synced_data`: owned publish on a cold manager; copy -> owned -> copy rotation; owned -> owned; rejection of nil and of the head, previous and spare pointers with no state change; disabled manager; concurrent copy publish, owned publish, `UnsetHeadState` and readers (run with `-race`).
- `cl/phase1/forkchoice`: `GetOwnedStateAtBlockRoot` on the replay path returns a state that does not change when the block's `Eth1Data` and Gloas bid are mutated; on the current-state path it returns a copy with the same root.
- `cl/phase1/stages`: `postForkchoiceOperations` publishes through the owned method exactly once and never calls the copying publish. The published state is not the fork graph's current state object, and the state visible through `ViewHeadState` is the same object it handed over.

Verification: `go build ./...`; `go test -race` for `cl/beacon/synced_data/...`, `cl/phase1/stages/...` and `cl/phase1/forkchoice/...`; `go test ./cl/...` (only `cl/spectest` `Test/mainnet_config` fails, because the mainnet spec fixtures are not downloaded locally; this is not related to the change); `make lint` clean twice.

title: all: remove unused function parameters and dead code
body:
Same treatment as #24375, #24385, #24492 and #24518, applied to the remaining directories, plus a repo-wide pass for dead test code: removes unused parameters from functions that are not bound to an interface, callback type or reflection, and updates every caller. Also deletes dead code.

- Parameters: 48 removed across `cmd`, `db`, `execution`, `node`, `rpc` and `txnprovider`, including cascades (e.g. `Ethereum.Init`'s `chainConfig`, `SetUpBlockReader`'s `dbReadConcurrency`, `rpc.newClient`'s `cfg`).
- Dead test code repo-wide: unused test helpers, types, vars and fields in `cl`, `db`, `execution` and `p2p` (e.g. `FakeChainHeaderReader`, the `transaction_test` random generators, commitment test-kit helpers).
- Dead code with no references anywhere: `maphash.NonConcurrentMap`, `math.Decimal256`, `ntoh.U64/U32/U16/U8`, three `ssz` helpers, `hexutil.MustDecodeBig`, `testlog.Handler`, `flags.DirectoryString`, `ethapi.FormatLogs`, `jsonstream.HexUint64/HexUint256`, `gointerfaces.ConvertBytesToH2048`, `cli.ApplyFlagsForEthConfig`, `shards.WalkWrites`, `Generator.GetCachedReceipt`, shutter `DegreeFromThreshold` / `InterfaceListenAddresses`, and unused test declarations.

Kept on purpose: params used through reflection (`debug_*` RPC methods, kong `Run`, gob), interface methods from packages outside the module, lifecycle `ctx` on component providers, and in-progress code (`node/app`, the storage inventory).

Possible follow-ups, out of scope here:
- `rpc.Server.ServeCodecWithContext` ignores its `CodecOption`.
- `gointerfaces.EnsureVersionCompatibility` (#20504) is never wired into the four methods it was meant to replace.
- `diagnostics` code orphaned by the `diag` CLI removal (#21351).

No behavior change. TDD skipped: pure refactor, covered by existing tests.
