author: yperbasis

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph: stop fsyncing fork-graph dump files
body:
## Problem

Caplin's fork graph writes two kinds of dump files and calls `File.Sync()` on each one:

- the head state, in `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` (`cl/phase1/forkchoice/fork_graph/fork_graph_disk_fs.go`), every 4th slot (`dumpSlotFrequency = 4`);
- the execution payload envelope, in `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` (same file), after Gloas.

On a Hoodi node (1.14M validators) one head-state dump writes about 143 MB. `dumpMs` is p50 ~540 ms, p90 ~1.06 s and max 2.65 s. Measured locally, encoding takes ~4 ms and snappy + write ~100 ms, so most of the node time is likely writeback and fsync. The split on the node was not measured separately.

Every dump holds a shared lock, and the head dump after fork choice also holds a lock and a transaction, so every millisecond counts:

- every dump holds `stateDumpLock` (`fork_graph_disk_fs.go:122`). The same lock is needed by fork-graph replay (`readBeaconStateFromDisk`, `:57`), by req/resp and API envelope reads (`ReadEnvelopeFromDisk`, `:205`), and after Gloas by envelope import (`DumpEnvelopeOnDisk`, `:354`), which runs while it holds the fork-choice `f.mu` (`cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload.go:780`, `:1176`);
- the head dump after fork choice runs inside `syncedData.ViewHeadState`, which holds the synced-data read lock (`cl/phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:469`, `cl/beacon/synced_data/synced_data.go:167`). A waiting writer makes new readers queue behind it;
- it also runs inside the stage's `indiciesDB` RW transaction (`cl/phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:498-518`).

## Why removing fsync is safe

The durability that fsync gives (data survives a power loss or a kernel crash) is never used, because nothing reads these files after such an event:

- Both files live in `path.Join(dirs.Tmp, "caplin-forkchoice")`. Caplin removes and recreates this directory on every start, before it builds the fork graph (`cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go:365-384`). This is the only production fork-graph filesystem; the spectests use `afero.NewMemMapFs()` (`cl/spectest/consensus_tests/fork_choice.go:314`). The removal came in the same PR that added the dump and its Sync (#8546). Comments in `cl/phase1/stages/forward_sync.go` call the forward-sync dumps "restart checkpoints", but they are also wiped on start; the real restart anchor is the finalized-state save.

Inside the running process the files stay usable without fsync:

- Reads see written data through the page cache, fsynced or not.
- All content reads and writes of these files hold `stateDumpLock` (`fork_graph_disk_fs.go:57`, `:122`, `:205`, `:354`). `Prune` removals and the `hasBeaconState` existence check run outside it (`fork_graph_disk.go:755`, `:850-858`); this is unchanged.
- If a head-state dump cannot be read, replay walks back to an older dump when the block is still kept (`fork_graph_disk.go:639-645`), or returns no state when only the header is kept, for example for the anchor (`:623-633`). This is the same as for any missing dump.
- Envelopes are still written to a `.tmp` file, closed with a checked `Close`, and renamed (`fork_graph_disk_fs.go:377-427`). Readers never see a partial file, and a write, flush, close or rename error keeps the existing final file (`TestDumpEnvelopeFailurePreservesExistingFinal`).

History: the head-state Sync came with the original feature (#8546, which gives no rationale; its error was always returned) and was moved in #8851. The envelope dump copied the pattern in #18956, and #23548 moved envelopes to tmp+rename and kept the Sync. No change relies on the durability of these files.

Trade-off: fsync is also the point where the kernel reliably reports a delayed writeback error (EIO). `close(2)` on a local filesystem usually does not report it. Such an error may now go unnoticed by the dump and show up later, for example when the data is read again after the pages were evicted. Before, the dump itself failed. A head-state read error makes replay fall back as described above. An envelope that fails to decode is marked invalid and can be fetched again. If the re-read itself returns EIO, the envelope stays marked as present, so normal ingestion skips it while the error lasts: until a later read succeeds, the anchor envelope is rewritten, or the block is pruned. This needs a failing disk, and it is accepted here for the cost above.

## What changed

- `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk`: removed `Sync()`. The file was closed by an unchecked `defer`. It is now closed once in a defer that joins the `Close` error into the returned error, like the envelope dump, so errors reported at close (for example on NFS) are not lost.
- `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk`: removed `Sync()`. The order stays write, flush, checked `Close`, `Rename`.

## What is not changed

- The finalized-state save under `dirs.CaplinLatest` (`saveFinalizedStateOnDiskIfNeeded` / `replaceDurableFile`, `cl/phase1/stages/forkchoice.go:372-430`) is the restart anchor. It keeps its file fsync, rename and directory fsync.
- Every dump still holds `stateDumpLock`, and the head dump after fork choice still runs under the synced-data read lock and inside the `indiciesDB` RW transaction. This PR only makes the dumps shorter.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):

- Move the head-state dump and the finalized-state save after `tx.Commit()`. This also fixes a silent rollback: today a failed dump makes `postForkchoiceOperations` return an error, so the canonical-chain and finalized-slot writes in the same transaction are rolled back.
- Gloas envelope import holds the fork-choice `f.mu` while it waits for `stateDumpLock` (`on_execution_payload.go:780` → `:1176`), so a long head-state dump still stalls fork choice. Either release `f.mu` around persistence or give envelopes their own lock and buffer.

## Tests

- `TestForkGraphDumpsDoNotRequireSync`: with an afero file whose `Sync()` fails, `NewForkGraphDisk` (forced anchor dump) and `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` must succeed, and the state and the envelope must read back with equal SSZ hashes. Fails on `main` with the injected Sync error.
- `TestDumpBeaconStateReturnsCloseError`: with an afero file whose `Close()` fails, `DumpBeaconStateOnDisk` must return that error and close the file exactly once. Fails on `main` because the error was dropped.
- `TestDumpEnvelopeFailurePreservesExistingFinal`: removed the `"sync"` stage, because Sync is no longer called. The open, write, close and rename stages still pass.
- `go test -race ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...` passes. `go test ./cl/...` passes except `cl/spectest` `Test/mainnet_config`, which needs the downloaded `mainnet` fixtures (not present locally, unrelated to this change). `make lint` is clean.

## Backport

Not planned for release/3.8.
author: domiwei

title: cl: validate boundary blocks without a state copy
body:
Part of #25136 (direction 3).

## What and why

Gossip validation of a block needs four values from its parent: the expected proposer, `latest_block_hash`, and the latest bid's block hash and presence. A parent in the same epoch is already read in place. A parent in an earlier epoch was copied (under `f.mu.RLock` when it is the fork graph's current state), advanced with `ProcessSlots` across the epoch boundary, and then thrown away. On a Hoodi node this costs about 0.45 s for the first block of every epoch, before the block is forwarded and imported.

From Fulu on, the advanced state does not differ from the parent in these values when no fork upgrade happens in between:

- `ProcessProposerLookahead` only shifts `proposer_lookahead` and appends a new last epoch, so the parent's entry for a slot in the next `MinSeedLookahead` epochs is the entry the advanced state reads.
- `latest_block_hash` and the latest bid are written only by block processing and `UpgradeToGloas`, not by slot or epoch processing. The bid was already read before advancing.

## Changes

- `cl/phase1/core/state`: extract the lookahead read of `GetBeaconProposerIndexForSlot` into `ProposerIndexFromLookahead(slot) (uint64, bool)`. It returns false before Fulu or when the slot's epoch is outside `[stateEpoch, stateEpoch+MinSeedLookahead]`. `GetBeaconProposerIndexForSlot` calls it first; its behaviour does not change.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: `computeBlockValidationContext` also reads a parent from an earlier epoch in place when:
  - the header shows the parent at most `MinSeedLookahead` epochs back (checked before viewing, so a non-head parent is not replayed twice),
  - the scheduled state version is the same at the parent's and the block's epoch and is at least Fulu (this excludes the Fulu and Gloas activation epochs and any later fork's activation epoch),
  - the viewed state has the block epoch's version, and `ProposerIndexFromLookahead` covers the slot.

  In all other cases the existing copy path runs.

The in-place read under `f.mu.RLock` is a few field reads, which is much less work than the state copy it replaces. It adds no new lock edges.

## Trade-off

The copy path's `ProcessSlots` used to fill the global lookahead shuffle and active-set caches, and block import's `ProcessEpoch` (under `f.mu`) then found them already filled. After this change import computes them itself: about 10-15 ms on Fulu, and more on Gloas when no bid was gossiped. This PR adds no warm-up code for it.

## Tests

- `TestProposerIndexFromLookahead`: window edges (pre-Fulu false, first and last slot of the window true, one epoch past the window and one slot before the state epoch false).
- `TestBlockValidationContextReadsParentFromPreviousEpochWithoutCopy` (Fulu and Gloas subtests): parent at the last slot of epoch E-1, block at the first slot of E, +1 and +5 (empty slots at the start of the epoch). The copy path returns an error. All four values equal a `Copy` + `ProcessSlots` oracle, and the parent state's slot and hash tree root do not change. The Gloas case uses a distinct `latest_block_hash` and bid hash. This test fails on `main`.
- `TestBlockValidationContextCopiesFuluParentFromTwoEpochsBack`: the state is not viewed and is fetched once.
- `TestBlockValidationContextCopiesParentAtFuluActivation` (earlier forks at 0, Fulu at E, Gloas far future): the state is not viewed and is fetched once.
- `TestBlockValidationContextFallsBackWhenViewedParentCannotServeLookahead`: the viewed state has a different version from the schedule, or is outside the lookahead window. Each case falls back to one copy.
- Existing `TestBlockValidationContextReadsSameEpochParentStateWithoutCopy`, `TestBlockValidationContextAdvancesCopiedParentStateAcrossEpoch` and `TestBlockServiceGossipUsesPostUpgradeExecutionHeadAtGloasBoundary` still pass.

Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the named test failed, and the guard was restored:

| Mutation | Failing test |
|---|---|
| Remove the header distance check | `...CopiesFuluParentFromTwoEpochsBack` (state viewed) |
| Remove the header version-equality check | `...CopiesParentAtFuluActivation` (state viewed) |
| Remove the header `>= Fulu` check | `...AdvancesCopiedParentStateAcrossEpoch` (state fetched twice) |
| Remove the callback version check | `...FallsBack.../state version differs` (no copy) |
| Ignore the `ok` of `ProposerIndexFromLookahead` | `...FallsBack.../slot is outside` (proposer 0) |
| Lookahead index `slot % SlotsPerEpoch` only | `...ReadsParentFromPreviousEpochWithoutCopy` (Fulu and Gloas) |
| Remove both version checks | `...UsesPostUpgradeExecutionHeadAtGloasBoundary` (wrong execution head) |

`make lint`, `make erigon integration` and `go test -race ./cl/phase1/core/state/ ./cl/phase1/network/services/` pass.

## Expected gain

We estimate about 0.4 s less at each epoch boundary on a Hoodi node, based on the cost of the same copy-and-advance step measured elsewhere. We will measure it after merge.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/stages: publish a fork choice head that moved at the slot start
body:
## Problem

The proposer boost expires when a slot starts, so the fork choice head can move back to another branch without a new block. When SleepForSlot ended at that moment, its transition could send a node that was behind to ChainTipSync even though `ArgsFunc` had marked the fork choice head as unpublished, and ChainTipSync can wait up to 25 seconds for the next block. Until the ForkChoice stage ran, the synced head state and the state-based Beacon API reads stayed on the old head, and the EL was not sent the new head.

On Gloas, block production started from the old synced head state and saw a different fork choice head. It waits for the synced state to catch up before it retries, but nothing published the new head before the proposal cutoff, so no retry started and it returned the head-change error. We saw this in a local multi-client network after a network partition ended: a Caplin node that had to propose right after the boost expired did not produce its block. Before Gloas, block production does not check for a head change and builds on the synced head when the validator client asks, so the change helps there only when the publication comes first. On large states that is less likely.

## What changed

- SleepForSlot's transition uses `catchUpPublishingHead`, which was `catchUpAfterImport`, like the stages that import blocks. When `MetaCatchingUp` would select ChainTipSync and the head is unpublished, it selects ForkChoice first.
- The stage `ArgsFunc` ticks fork choice to the start of the current slot before it reads the head, so the boost expiry is processed even when the 2 ms fork choice ticker has not reached the slot yet. `OnTick` only moves the stored time forward, and after genesis the start of the current slot is never later than the wall clock. If `GetHead` fails there, the error is logged at Debug and the head counts as published.
- At the tip, CleanupAndPruning goes back to ForkChoice when the head is still unpublished. Gossip imports blocks outside the stage loop, so the slot's block can arrive during the slot-start ForkChoice pass or during CleanupAndPruning. Before Gloas, SleepForSlot does not poll the head, so without this the block would be published at the next slot start, about ten seconds late. Before this PR, ChainTipSync was waiting at that moment and published the block on arrival.
  - The rerun is allowed once per `sleepForSlotRewakeInterval` (1 s). A publish that keeps failing therefore costs at most one extra pass per second, and CleanupAndPruning still runs between the passes.
  - The bound is time-only. A second head change within that second waits for the next slot start before Gloas. Before this PR such a head was not published before the next slot either.
  - The check is not in the ForkChoice transition: CleanupAndPruning runs right after it and also covers a block that arrives during CleanupAndPruning.
  - Dropping the Gloas gate on the SleepForSlot head poll would also close the gap. It is not used because on pre-Gloas networks attestations invalidate the head cache, so it would add five head computations a second under the fork choice lock and wake the stage on every attestation-driven head move.

A race remains: the ticker advances the stored time with a lock-free compare-and-swap and takes the fork choice lock afterwards to clear the boost and the head cache. Readers that get the lock in between, for example the `GetHead` in `ArgsFunc`, can still see the cached, boosted head. The window is the time the ticker waits for the lock, not a single preemption point. Closing it needs the cached head to carry the slot it was computed at, which this PR does not do.

This PR does not change the fork choice weight calculation or branch selection. The added tick only processes the boost expiry earlier, so the existing rules can select another branch at the slot start sooner than before.

## Tests

- `TestCatchUpPublishesForkChoiceHeadBeforeChainTipSync`:
  - SleepForSlot selects ForkChoice when the node is behind, has peers and has an unpublished head. Before the change it selected ChainTipSync.
  - At the tip with an unpublished head, ForkChoice goes on to CleanupAndPruning, and CleanupAndPruning goes back to ForkChoice.
  - CleanupAndPruning goes to SleepForSlot when the head is published, when the node has no peers and is behind, and when a rerun happened less than a second ago.
- `TestCleanupAndPruningRerunsForkChoiceOncePerInterval`: two transitions on the same `Cfg` give ForkChoice and then SleepForSlot.
- `TestStageArgsTickForkChoiceToTheTargetSlot`: the fork choice store starts one slot behind the clock, and the test checks that `ArgsFunc` moves it to the target slot. Before the change the store stayed at the anchor slot.
- Each change has a test that fails without it:
  - the SleepForSlot transition change;
  - the `OnTick` call;
  - the CleanupAndPruning rerun;
  - each of its three conditions;
  - the timestamp update.
- No test checks that `OnTick` runs before `GetHead`: that needs a head that changes when the proposer boost expires, and this package has no such fixture.
- `go test ./cl/phase1/stages/ ./cl/phase1/forkchoice/...` and `-race` on `./cl/phase1/stages/` pass. `make lint` reports 0 issues, and `make erigon integration` builds.

## Follow-ups

These are not in this PR:
- the tick and boost race above;
- SleepForSlot with no peers still goes to ChainTipSync;
- a slot boundary inside ForkChoice or CleanupAndPruning;
- `payload_attributes` events with a past `proposal_slot` when the head goes back to an older slot.

This change is on release/3.8 through #25287. The rerun commits need a separate backport.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network/services, cmd/caplin: republish queued execution payload envelopes
body:
## Problem

An execution payload envelope that arrives over gossip before its beacon block is IGNOREd and, if the queue has room, kept pending for about 30 seconds until the block is known, as the Gloas p2p spec allows for the `execution_payload` topic. Gossipsub does not forward IGNOREd messages, and Caplin did not publish the envelope after it processed it from the pending queue. Peers that could only receive the envelope through Caplin nodes never got it over gossip, so they built on an EMPTY parent and their PTC votes did not count the payload as present. We saw this in a local multi-client network, where Prysm publishes its envelope a few milliseconds after its block.

## What changed

- `NewExecutionPayloadService` takes the gossip manager, wired in `cmd/caplin/caplin1/run.go`.
- When an envelope from the pending queue is processed without error, the service SSZ-encodes it and calls `PublishBackground` on the `execution_payload` topic. These are the same outcomes for which the direct gossip path returns ACCEPT. Envelopes that fail processing are not published.
- go-libp2p-pubsub v0.17.0 validates and forwards a local publish of a message that it saw and ignored before. Caplin's message ID hashes the topic, including the fork digest, and the decompressed SSZ. Outside a fork transition the relayed message is published on the same topic, so it has the same ID as the original, and peers that already have it drop it as a duplicate. Caplin's validator accepts its own messages without processing them again.
- Prysm and Teku also publish an envelope after deferred validation; Lighthouse does it only for envelopes of the current slot. The spec has no current-slot rule for this topic (the only time rule is IGNORE before the finalized slot), so Caplin adds no current-slot check either. It still checks the finalized slot, and only envelopes that leave the pending queue before it expires are published.

Not changed here: Caplin still forwards an envelope only after `processMessage` succeeds, which normally includes the EL call, and not right after the gossip checks.

## Tests

- `TestExecutionPayloadServiceRepublishesPendingEnvelopeAfterBlockArrives`: an envelope ignored while its block is unknown is passed once to the gossip manager's `PublishBackground` after the block arrives (mocked; the test does not cover delivery to peers). Before the change the expected publish call was missing.
- `TestExecutionPayloadServiceDoesNotRepublishInvalidPendingEnvelope`: a pending envelope that fails fork choice validation is not published.
- Removing the publish call, or publishing without the success check, makes the matching test fail.
author: domiwei

title: cl/merkle_tree, cl/cltypes/solid: round merkleize depth up for non-power-of-two limits
body:
## Summary

SSZ merkleization pads chunks to `next_pow_of_two(limit)`, but `GetDepth` rounded log2 down. Every limit-bound root path built a tree one level too short when the chunk limit was not a power of two, so the root was wrong and the chunks past the first half were dropped from it.

Example: `ByteList[96]` has a chunk limit of 3. The spec root is `H(H(c0, c1), H(c2, 0))`. Before this change, `MerkleizeVector` returned `H(c0, c1)`.

`MerkleProof` was the only caller that relied on the floor result, and it rounded the depth up by hand right after the call.

This change rounds `GetDepth` up and removes that adjustment. The affected paths are:

- `MerkleizeVector`, which is also used by `BitlistRootWithLimit`, `BitvectorRootWithLimit` and `ListObjectSSZRoot`
- `merkleizeTrieLeavesFlatWithStart`, used by `MerkleRootFromFlatLeavesWithLimit`, `ByteListSSZ.HashSSZ` and limit-bound `MerkleTree`, plus the empty-tree root of `MerkleTree`
- `ParticipationBitList.HashSSZ` and `RawUint64List.HashSSZ`
- `ListSSZ.ElementProof`, which passed the floor depth to `MerkleProof` and so panicked for any limit that is not a power of two (`depth is different than maximum depth, have 1, want 2` for limit 3)

`GetDepth` now returns `log2(next_pow_of_two(v))`, which is what `MerkleProof` was computing by hand. `MerkleProof` now rejects an empty schema, as `HashTreeRoot` does; before, the round-up made it fail with a depth mismatch.

Mainnet consensus limits are powers of two, so this does not change any existing consensus root. The bug only affects types whose chunk limit is not a power of two.

I found this by running the [ethereum/ssz-specs](https://github.com/ethereum/ssz-specs) conformance vectors against Caplin's SSZ code. 26 of 380 vectors in the `ssz` format failed, all on chunk limits that are not powers of two (for example `bytelist96`, `bitlist640`, `bitvector513`, `list5`). With this change, all 380 pass. The runner for those vectors is not part of this PR.

## Tests

Followed TDD: the tests were added first, and they failed on `main` before the fix.

- `cl/merkle_tree/merkleize_limit_test.go`: `MerkleizeVector`, `MerkleRootFromFlatLeavesWithLimit` and `MerkleTree` against a spec-literal reference (pad to `next_pow_of_two(limit)`, then hash pairwise), for limits 3, 5, 6 and 12 and every chunk count up to the limit. Before the fix, 79 of 86 cases failed with a wrong root. The 7 that passed are `MerkleTree` cases with enough leaves to reach the full depth before the limit is applied.
- `cl/cltypes/solid/limit_hash_test.go`: `ByteListSSZ`, `ParticipationBitList`, `Uint64ListSSZ`, `RawUint64List`, `BitList` and `BitVector` against roots from the ssz-specs vectors (8 cases, all failing before the fix), and `ElementProof` for limits 3 and 5, which panicked before the fix.
- `TestAttesterSlashing` pinned the floor-depth root for a `RawUint64List` with limit 9192, which no preset uses. It now uses `attestingIndicesLimit` (2048), and the expected root matches a spec-literal computation.
- `TestMerkleProofRejectsEmptySchema`: `MerkleProof` with no schema returns an error.
- `TestGetDepth` in `cl/cltypes/solid/hashutil_test.go` pins the old floor results; updated to the rounded-up depth.

Verified locally:

- consensus-spec `ssz_static` mainnet vectors, v1.7.0-beta.4: 1935 cases pass, 0 fail. The 75 skips are the `heze` fork, which the suite already excludes.
- the 380 ssz-specs vectors
- `go test ./cl/... ./execution/engineapi/... ./common/ssz/...`
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`
author: JackCC703

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice, cl/phase1/network/services: apply block attestations in OnBlock
body:
## Problem
Fork choice received the attestations of a block only when a new block came over gossip (`importBlockOperations`). Blocks imported by ChainTipSync and ForwardSync go through `OnBlock`, and blocks the node publishes itself go through `OnBlock` or `OnBlockWithEquivocationCheck`. None of these read `Body.Attestations`. The on_block step of the spec fork choice tests runs `on_attestation` for each body attestation after `on_block`, so these blocks left fork choice without votes that other clients count. In a local Gloas devnet, a Caplin node that caught up through ChainTipSync after a network partition chose a different head than the other clients.

## What changed
- After a new block reaches `fork_graph.Success` and the rest of the block bookkeeping succeeds, `onBlock` applies each body attestation while it still holds the fork choice lock. The votes are in the store before `OnBlock` returns, so the next head calculation uses them. An attestation that fails validation is logged at debug level and dropped, as on the gossip path before.
- New `onAttestationLocked`: when the block's post-state passes `headStateHasTargetShuffling` for the target, committees come from that state. Other attestations use the existing head-state or checkpoint-state path. This avoids building a checkpoint state when the block's post-state has the target's shuffling.
- The new `OnBlock` path applies body attestations also while `f.synced` is false. The sync guard in the public `OnAttestation` is unchanged. The spec's `on_attestation` has no such guard, and with it a restarted node would choose its first head without the body votes of the blocks it imported before that.
- `importBlockOperations` no longer applies body attestations, so gossip blocks do not apply them twice. Body attester slashings stay on the gossip path (follow-up).

## Tests
- `TestOnBlockAppliesBodyAttestations`: for bellatrix, capella and electra fixtures, and for synced import, published block (`OnBlockWithEquivocationCheck`) and unsynced import, `OnBlock` leaves the same latest messages as a reference store that applies the body attestations through `OnAttestation` with the block as head. Before the fix, the capella case failed locally with `expected: 405, actual: 0`.
- `TestOnBlockReadsBodyAttestationCommitteesFromBlockState`: after importing the capella fixture, no checkpoint state is cached in `checkpointStates` for the targets of the last block's body attestations.
- `TestOnAttestationLockedUsesBlockStateOnlyWithTargetShuffling`: a side-branch target still uses the target checkpoint state.
- `TestImportBlockOperationsLeavesAttestationsToOnBlock`: `importBlockOperations` no longer calls `OnAttestation` for body attestations.
- Local runs of the mainnet fork choice spectests (v1.7.0-beta.4 fixtures, every fork the runner does not skip) pass with and without the fix: no fixture is sensitive to block votes. `make lint`, `make erigon integration` and `go test -race` on the changed packages pass locally.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon, cl/phase1/stages: emit the Gloas payload_attributes event
body:
## Problem
Caplin sends no `payload_attributes` event once the head is in Gloas. At the fork boundary it sends a "gloas" event with the pre-Gloas field set. External builders that start building from this event (for example buildoor) get nothing after the fork. The event also uses execution-API JSON inside `payload_attributes`: camelCase names such as `prevRandao` and `validatorIndex`, and hex quantities such as the timestamp. This does not match the beacon-API encoding, and clients that follow the schema can reject it.

## What changed
- The Gloas event follows beacon-APIs v5.0.0-beta.0 (ethereum/beacon-APIs#621, ethereum/beacon-APIs#638): no `parent_block_number`, new `safe_block_hash` and `finalized_block_hash`, and `PayloadAttributesV4` with `slot_number` and `target_gas_limit`.
- The Beacon API handler computes the event on the current fork choice head, for the slot after the later of the wall-clock slot and the head slot. It uses the FULL/EMPTY payload source and withdrawal logic of block production, takes the fee recipient and target gas limit from the proposer preferences (with the same fallbacks), and takes the safe/finalized hashes that production passes to forkchoiceUpdated (now one shared helper).
- It requests a recomputation on every `head_v2` (head change, head payload becoming FULL) and at each payload attestation deadline, so missed slots and same-root decisions also get an event. Requests that arrive while one is pending are merged.
- The state work runs only while an HTTP stream subscribes to `payload_attributes` and the proposal slot is within the proposer lookahead. Before publication the event is dropped if the fork choice head or its payload status changed, or if the proposal slot has started.
- The stage keeps the pre-Gloas event and stops at the first Gloas proposal slot.
- `payload_attributes` uses the beacon-API encoding for every fork: snake_case, quoted decimals, and only the `PayloadAttributesV<N>` fields of the event version. Pre-Gloas consumers see the new encoding too.

## Limits
- A PTC vote that changes the FULL/EMPTY decision after the deadline tick, or while an event is being computed, without a head change, does not trigger a new event, so the last event can be stale. Publication does not check `ShouldBuildOnFull` again.
- `safe_block_hash` and `finalized_block_hash` come from the checkpoints of the state block production uses, so at an epoch boundary they can differ from the checkpoints the ForkChoice stage sends to forkchoiceUpdated.

## Tests
- JSON test against the spec's gloas example, and field sets for V1–V4.
- Handler tests: FULL parent (parent hash, withdrawals after the parent payload effects, safe/finalized, fee recipient, gas limit), EMPTY parent, unreadable FULL envelope, Fulu→Gloas boundary, missed slot, the payload-decision tick without a head change, no subscriber, far-behind head, head changed before publication, and the state feed not blocked during state work.
- Stage test: the stage emits nothing for a Gloas proposal slot and still emits before it.
- `make lint`, `make erigon integration`, `go test -race` for the changed packages, and `go test ./cl/beacon/...` pass locally.
author: domiwei

title: cl/persistence: read the stored epoch-0 randao mix for epoch-2 seeds
body:
## Problem

On a Caplin archive node (`--caplin.states-archive`), historical data that depends on the epoch-2 seed is wrong:

- `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/committees` for epoch 2, and historical attester and proposer duties for epoch 2
- the participation replay (`ReadParticipations`): `current_epoch_participation` in epoch-2 states, `previous_epoch_participation` in epoch-3 states, epoch-2 attestation rewards, and the historical Lighthouse validator inclusion and liveness responses that use it
- `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/randao?epoch=0` on the historical path, for later states whose randao vector still holds epoch 0 (epochs 1 to 65535 on mainnet)

In a local shadow-fork run, the archive's slot-64 committees differed from Prysm in all 32 entries. `/states/{state_id}/root` still matched, because it returns the stored state root and does not hash the reconstructed state. Consensus is not affected. On mainnet, epoch 2 was in Phase 0, so reconstructed states have no participation fields there, but epoch-2 committees, duties, attestation rewards and the participation-based responses are affected.

## Root cause

`ReadRandaoMixBySlotAndIndex` had two bugs in the path that reads a past epoch's mix:

1. The guard `epoch > (epochSubIndex - index)` rejected the equality case, so a lookup for epoch 0 fell back to the genesis state. The epoch-2 seed uses the final mix of epoch 0, which the antiquary stores at `RandaoMixes[slot 0]`, so the reader returned the genesis mix.
2. The genesis fallback read `GetRandaoMixes(epoch)` (index `epoch % EpochsPerHistoricalVector`) instead of the requested index. This is masked on real networks because all genesis randao mixes are equal.

## Fix

Compute the ring distance once (like `readHistoricalBlockRoot`), use it for both checks, and read the requested index from the genesis state.

## Tests

New `randao_mix_test.go`:

- `TestReadRandaoMixBySlotAndIndex_Epoch2SeedMix` pins the first fix.
- `TestReadRandaoMixBySlotAndIndex_GenesisFallbackUsesIndex` pins the second fix.
- `TestReadRandaoMixBySlotAndIndex_WrappedIndex` covers the rewritten branch for an index after the current ring position.

The first two tests fail on the old code. Locally, mutating each fixed or rewritten branch (`distance > epoch` to `>=`, the genesis index, the wrapped distance) turns the matching test red.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes/solid: clear reused uint64 list hash buffer
body:
`RawUint64List.HashSSZ` reuses a buffer but did not clear padding after the current values. Decoding a shorter list into an already-hashed object could therefore produce a different root from a fresh list with the same values.

Clear the resized buffer before writing the values. Add a regression that decodes and hashes 12 values, then decodes shorter lists and checks their roots against fixed SSZ roots and fresh lists. It covers the reported five-value case, other partial chunks, a complete chunk, and an empty list.

Fixes #25278.

Validation:
- The regression fails without the fix for lengths 1, 5, and 9, including the exact five-value mismatch from the issue.
- `go test ./cl/cltypes/solid ./cl/merkle_tree -count=1`
- `go test -race ./cl/cltypes/solid ./cl/merkle_tree -count=1`
- `make lint`
- `make erigon integration`
author: joxerx

title: cl/phase1/stages: backfill the custody columns of blocks the chain tip sync imports
body:
Part of #24704.

After forward sync, the chain tip sync imports the blocks up to the live head with the data availability check off (and, from Gloas, applies their parents' envelopes without the blob check). Those blocks were left to the blob history downloader, which runs only with `--caplin.archive-blobs` or `--caplin.blobs-immediate-backfill`. On a default node nothing fetched their custody columns, so after every restart the block right after the forward sync range stayed without them. The custody backfill from #25148 covers only the forward sync range.

`processChainTipBatch` now asks the custody backfill for the slots it imported, including the parents whose envelopes it handled. The backfill already skips blocks whose columns are stored, waits for the canonical chain, queues a Gloas block only once its envelope was processed, and gives up on blocks peers do not serve.

## Measurement

Sepolia node, default flags, two restart cycles each (10 min offline, then a 20 min watch of every slot of the forward sync range up to 10 slots past it):

| | block right after the forward sync range | other blocks with blobs |
|---|---|---|
| release/3.8 | no custody columns in 2 of 2 cycles, still missing after the watch (also 2 of 2 with `--caplin.blobs-immediate-backfill`, after a 60 min watch) | complete |
| release/3.8 + this change | complete in 2 of 2 cycles | complete (424 and 286) |

## Tests

`TestChainTipBatchRequestsCustodyBackfillForImportedSlots` fails without the change; `TestChainTipBatchWithoutImportsRequestsNoCustodyBackfill` covers a batch that imports nothing. `make lint` is clean twice; `make erigon integration` builds; `go test -short ./cl/phase1/stages/ ./cl/das/` passes.
author: lystopad

title: cl/beacon/handler: accept blobless execution payload envelope contents
body:
## Summary

A stateless `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes` with `Eth-Blob-Data-Included: true` and a `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelopeContents` body with `blobs: []` and `kzg_proofs: []` was rejected with HTTP 400 `execution payload envelope column 0 has invalid KZG proof`. The beacon API allows empty `blobs` and `kzg_proofs` arrays for a payload without blobs.

The cause was in `storeExecutionPayloadEnvelopeContents`. When the bid had zero blob commitments, the count check passed (0 == 0), `GetDataColumnSidecarsGloas` built `NumberOfColumns` empty sidecars, and `das.VerifyDataColumnSidecarKZGProofsWithCommitments` returned false because there were no commitments.

The fix returns early after the count check when the bid has no blob commitments, so the handler does not build, verify, store or publish sidecars. Other zero-blob paths already skip sidecar work with a `Len() > 0` guard (for example block publishing in `block_production.go`). The handler still passes the envelope to forkchoice through `processExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, and forkchoice `checkDataAvailability` returns nil for zero commitments, so forkchoice does not need sidecars for a blobless payload.

Found in a Hoodi shadow-fork rehearsal with external builders.

## Tests

- TDD: `TestPostExecutionPayloadEnvelopesAcceptsBloblessStatelessContents` was added first and failed with the 400 above. With the fix, it passes and also checks that the handler passes the envelope to forkchoice with the blob data check enabled. It fails with the same 400 again when the fix is reverted.
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/... ./cl/das/... -count=1` passes.
- `make lint` and `make erigon integration` pass.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon/handler: resolve execution payload envelope block_id via the canonical index
body:
## Summary

`GET /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelope/{block_id}` resolved a numeric slot through the head state's `block_roots` ring (`GetBlockRootAtSlot`). This had two bugs:

- A slot equal to the head slot returned HTTP 500 `GetBlockRootAtSlot: slot in the future`, because the ring only covers slots before `state.slot`.
- A skipped slot older than the head returned 200 with the parent block's envelope, because the ring repeats the previous block root for empty slots.

The handler now uses the shared `rootFromBlockId` resolver, the same one used by `/eth/v2/beacon/blocks/{block_id}`, headers, blobs and rewards. A numeric slot is read from the canonical block-root index, and an empty slot returns 404. The private `blockRootFromBlockId` helper is removed. The read transaction covers only the root lookup, so it is not held while the envelope is read from disk.

The shared resolver now also returns 404 for a slot above `math.MaxUint32`. The canonical index key is 4 bytes, so without this guard a request for slot `(1<<32)+S` reads the entry of slot `S` and returns the block at slot `S`. The blocks, headers and blob sidecars endpoints already had this problem, and moving the envelope endpoint to the canonical index would have added it there. The guard is in `rootFromBlockId`, so it covers every endpoint that uses that resolver.

Found in a Hoodi shadow-fork rehearsal with external builders.

## Behavior changes

- Head-slot request: 500 → 200.
- Skipped slot: 200 with the parent's envelope → 404.
- Future slot, or slot more than `SlotsPerHistoricalRoot` slots behind the head: 500 → canonical index lookup (404, or 200 if the block and its envelope are still in fork choice).
- Slot above `math.MaxUint32`: 500 → 404 on the envelope endpoint. On the blocks, headers and blob sidecars endpoints it was 200 with the block at the truncated slot, and is now 404. `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs` and the data column sidecars debug endpoint already map every resolver error to 500, so they now return 500 for it.
- `finalized` now reads the fork-choice store's finalized checkpoint instead of the head state's, like the other block endpoints. The response's `finalized` flag already used the store.
- `head` errors keep their status code (503 while syncing) instead of a plain 500.
- `genesis` still returns 400. Block IDs given as a root resolve to the same root as before, but the request now opens a short indices DB read transaction first, like the other block endpoints.

## Tests

TDD: each test was added first and seen red on the old code, then green after the fix.

- `TestGetExecutionPayloadEnvelopeBySlotOfHeadBlock`: red with 500 "slot in the future", now 200.
- `TestGetExecutionPayloadEnvelopeBySkippedSlotIsNotFound`: removes the canonical index entry and puts the parent root in the head state's ring. Red with 200 and the parent's envelope, now 404.
- `TestGetExecutionPayloadEnvelopeBySlotBeyondUint32IsNotFound`: added after the move to the canonical index, where it was red with 200 (the envelope of the truncated slot); now 404. On the base commit it returns 500.

`make lint`, `make erigon integration`, `go test ./cl/beacon/... ./cl/persistence/...` pass.
author: domiwei

title: cl/beacon/handler: fall back to historical pending queues on cache miss
body:
## Problem

`/eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/pending_deposits`, `pending_partial_withdrawals` and `pending_consolidations` returned 404 for many recent finalized slots. In a shadow-fork rehearsal, an archive node returned 404 for slots a few epochs behind the head, while Prysm returned 200 for the same slots, and the validators and committees endpoints on the same node returned 200.

## Root cause

For slots above `LowestAvailableSlot()`, the three handlers read only the fork choice LRU caches. These caches keep 128 block roots and are filled only when a block is processed. The fork graph keeps slots down to `(finalizedEpoch-3)*32`, which is usually more than 128 slots behind the head. When a root in that range was evicted from the cache, the handlers returned 404 and did not try the historical reader.

## Fix

- Serve the cached queue whenever the block root is in the cache, whatever its slot. The cache is keyed by block root and holds that block's post-state queues.
- On a cache miss, read the queue from the historical tables (`ReadQueueSSZ`) only when the root is canonical and state reconstruction progress covers the slot. This is the same progress check as `getHistoricalProposerDuties`. Otherwise return 404. This follows the randao handler, which already falls back to history for canonical roots.
- Return 400 for pre-Electra states, as the Beacon API requires ("Should return 400 if the state retrieved is prior to Electra").

Observable status changes besides the fix:
- Slots at or below `LowestAvailableSlot` used to read history unconditionally. A node without state reconstruction, or a non-canonical root at an old slot, got 200 with an empty or wrong queue. These requests now get 404, unless the root is still cached.
- Pre-Electra states now return 400 instead of 200 with an empty list, or 404 on a cache miss.

## Test

- `TestGetPendingQueuesFallBackToHistoricalOnCacheMiss` is added in its own commit first and fails on `main` with 404. It now checks the historical result against the fixture post-state queues, with progress exactly at the requested slot.
- New tests:
  - `TestGetPendingQueuesRejectPreElectraState` expects 400.
  - `TestGetPendingQueuesRejectNonCanonicalCacheMiss` and `TestGetPendingQueuesRejectUnreconstructedCacheMiss` expect 404 on a cache miss.
- `TestGetPendingQueuesConsensusVersionHeader` now checks that cached values are served both above and at `LowestAvailableSlot`.
- I checked each new guard with a mutation: the matching test fails when the guard is removed.
- `go test ./cl/beacon/handler/ -count=1`, `make lint` and `make erigon integration` pass.
author: domiwei

title: cl/cltypes, cl/phase1/core/state/raw: encode Gloas builder version and payload availability per beacon-APIs
body:
## Summary

Caplin's debug state JSON (`GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{state_id}`) did not follow beacon-APIs for two Gloas fields:

- `builders[].version` was a JSON number. beacon-APIs `types/gloas/builder.yaml` uses the `Uint8` primitive, which is a decimal string (`"0"`). The `Builder` struct tag now has `,string`.
- `execution_payload_availability` was base64, because the state encoder converted the bitvector to a raw `[]byte`. beacon-APIs `types/gloas/state.yaml` uses the `Bitvector` primitive, which is a `0x`-prefixed hex string. The state encoder now passes the bitvector to `encoding/json`, which calls `solid.BitVector.MarshalJSON`, and that already emits hex. The comment that said Go tooling expects base64 is removed.

Found in a Hoodi shadow-fork rehearsal with external builders.

## Compatibility

- The `POST /eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/builders` endpoint uses its own response type and already returned `version` as a string, so it does not change.
- SSZ encoding does not change.
- The spec form (a quoted decimal) round-trips through `encoding/json`. The old numeric form is no longer accepted on decode. No Erigon code decodes `Builder` from JSON.
- Go clients that parse this endpoint as JSON need the spec format:
  - attestantio/go-eth2-client (master at `6d6c831`) already decodes `execution_payload_availability` as hex.
  - attestantio/go-eth2-client and ethpandaops/go-eth2-client (v0.1.2, used by Assertoor) still decode Gloas `Builder.version` as a JSON number.
  - The ethpandaops fork also decodes `execution_payload_availability` as base64.
  - ethpandaops v0.1.2 asks for SSZ first and JSON as a lower-priority fallback (`WithEnforceJSON` forces JSON). Erigon serves SSZ for this endpoint, and SSZ does not change.
- Prysm v7.3.0 already emits both fields in the spec format.

## Tests

TDD: both tests were added first and seen red for the right reason. The fix then made them green. Reverting each production change makes its test red again.

- `cl/cltypes`: `TestBuilderJSONVersionIsDecimalString` (red: `float64(3)` instead of `"3"`).
- `cl/phase1/core/state/raw`: `TestGloasStateJSONExecutionPayloadAvailabilityIsHex` (red: base64 `AQAA...` instead of `0x01` followed by zero bytes; the test checks the full hex string).
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network/services, cl/phase1/core/state: cache a small bid validation view instead of a full state
body:
## Problem

Gloas execution payload bid gossip validation caches, per `(parent block root, bid slot)`, a full parent state advanced with `ProcessSlots`. Measured with a synthetic Gloas state with 1.2M validators:

| Step | Time | Allocated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Copy()` | 15–50 ms | 308 MB (retained in the cache) |
| `ProcessSlots`, same epoch | 3–5 ms | 4.8 MB |
| `ProcessSlots`, across an epoch | 240–440 ms | 86–105 MB |

With four cache entries that is about 1.2 GB resident, and about 300 MB of allocation for each new key (about one per slot on a Gloas network). Validation only reads the builder's pubkey, execution address, version, activity and bid capacity, the latest bid block hash and the builder domain.

## Change

- The cache keeps an immutable `bidValidationView` with these values instead of the state. It is about 80 bytes per builder (0.88 MB for 10k builders).
- The view is loaded with one `ViewStateAtBlockRoot` call:
  - When the parent state is in the bid epoch, the view is built in place, without a copy. Within an epoch, `ProcessSlots` changes none of the values the view reads.
  - Otherwise, including the Gloas fork epoch, the state is copied inside the callback, the copy is advanced with `ProcessSlots`, and it is dropped after the view is built. `ProcessSlots` therefore no longer runs on an uncopied replayed state.
- `BuilderBidCapacity` and `ForEachPendingBuilderWithdrawal` in `cl/phase1/core/state/epbs.go` hold the coverage rule and the pending-withdrawal rule once; `CanBuilderCoverBid`, `GetPendingBalanceToWithdrawForBuilder` and the view use them. `BuilderBidCapacity` returns `(capacity, ok)` so that a builder below the minimum balance still cannot cover a zero-value bid.
- Check order and accept / reject / ignore classes are unchanged. The view is built in one pass over builders and pending entries: about 0.13 ms for 10k builders and 10k pending withdrawals, under the fork-choice read lock when the parent is the current state.

## Trade-offs

- A same-epoch miss on a root that is not the in-memory fork-graph state still replays a full state through `ViewStateAtBlockRoot`; the state is no longer retained. The gain is "no copy for the current state and no full state in the cache", not "no state reconstruction".
- A cross-epoch miss on a root that is not the in-memory state replays it and copies it, so two full states exist briefly. This matches `GetOwnedStateAtBlockRoot`, and happens at most once per key per epoch.
- The cross-epoch copy is no longer timed by the `currentStateCopy` metric.
- A nil builder entry, which decoding and the state transition never produce, now reports "not active" instead of "not found". It is still a reject.

## Tests

- `TestBidValidationStateSameEpochDoesNotCopyState`: a same-epoch miss builds the view in place and the entry is reused.
- `TestBidValidationStateAdvancesPendingPaymentsAcrossEpoch`: a miss across an epoch boundary runs the real `ProcessSlots` (payment rotation and promotion, finalization activating a builder) and matches an independently advanced copy; the callback state is not mutated. It fails if the copy path stops advancing.
- `TestBidValidationViewMatchesState`: accept / reject / ignore and absolute capacity for builder range, version, activity, capacity boundaries, overflow, and pending withdrawals and payments of two builders. Breaking the payments loop or the builder-index filter fails it.
- `TestBidValidationStateConcurrentSameKeyLoadsOnce`: 16 goroutines miss the same key while the first load is blocked; the state is loaded once. It fails without the per-entry lock.
- The fork test now also checks the view's domain at the first Gloas slot.
- `TestBuilderBidCapacity`, `TestCanBuilderCoverBidZeroCapacity`.

## Not in this PR

- Gossip and direct bid validation do not apply builder top-ups from the parent payload's execution requests, which block processing applies before the bid. This predates the change.
- Strict singleflight for in-flight loads and TTL measured from publication.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: verify execution payload envelopes before taking the fork-choice lock
body:
## Problem

`applyEnvelope` takes the global fork-choice write lock `f.mu`. When the envelope's block root is not the in-memory fork-graph state, it then replays that state from disk (`ReplayState`), and only after that checks the bid match and the builder signature.

A replay of a Gloas state with 1.2M validators, measured on an Apple M3 Pro with a warm page cache:

| Step | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Read and decode (162 MB SSZ) | ~150 ms |
| First full `HashSSZ` | 90–100 ms |
| Epoch transition, when the replay crosses an epoch | 150–330 ms |

That is about 0.25–0.35 s per replay on Hoodi, 0.45–0.65 s at mainnet size, and about 540 MB allocated. During that time `OnBlock`, attestation and PTC processing and `get_head` wait.

A gossip peer needs only a commitment-matching envelope with a bad signature for a block whose envelope is not yet applied. Changing the signature bytes gives a new message ID, and the peer ban is skipped below 32 peers, so one peer can repeat this about twice per second.

## Change

Verify the envelope before taking the write lock, on the `validatePayload && commitmentsValidated` path (gossip, REST, chain-tip sync with an EL, the pending-envelope path):

- **Current in-memory state:** check the bid match and the builder signature under `f.mu.RLock`.
- **Any other root:** replay without `f.mu` and check against the replayed state.
  - Replays use the existing single envelope-validation slot. They skip the replay if the envelope was applied while waiting for the slot.
  - The slot is held until the write lock is taken, so at most one replayed state waits for `f.mu`. It is released before `NewPayload` can yield the lock. Every other exit, including a panic, releases it before any `f.mu` acquisition.
  - A replay that returns no state gives an ignore-class error without taking the write lock. Only that error (`errEnvelopeStateUnavailable`) queues the envelope as pending.
- **Under the write lock:** `HasEnvelope` and the block are checked again, the replayed state is reused, and the signature is not checked again.
  - An envelope that was not verified off-lock is never replayed under the lock: if its root is not the in-memory state, it is ignored and queued like an unavailable state.

Lock order: slot, then `f.mu` (write). The slot is only taken without `f.mu`. `acquireExecutionPayloadValidationRead` only uses `TryRLock` while holding the slot, and gives the slot back before it waits for `f.mu`.

Valid envelopes keep the same fork-choice result, persisted data, events, EL calls and error classes.

## Trade-offs

- If an envelope was verified against the current state under the read lock and `OnBlock` moves the current state before the write lock is taken, its state is replayed under the write lock. This is likely for a late envelope racing the next block. Only verified envelopes reach this path; before this change every such replay ran under the lock.
- During an off-lock replay, which only happens for a root that is not the in-memory state, payload production and the PTC do not see the envelope as in flight. Before, they waited behind the write lock. Marking an unverified envelope as in flight would let invalid envelopes make proposers wait.
- Bad-signature envelopes for non-current roots now wait for the single validation slot. This can delay REST envelope validation and honest late envelopes for other non-current roots, but it no longer blocks `f.mu`.
- An invalid envelope that races a valid apply now gets REJECT where it got IGNORE. The check is deterministic for a given envelope and block, so honest peers are not affected.

## Not in this PR

- The wait for the validation slot does not observe `ctx`. The old `f.mu.Lock` did not either. A ctx-aware wait needs an error that the REST handler treats as a failure: `ErrPayloadValidationInterrupted` makes it answer 202 and publish.
- An off-lock replay holds `stateDumpLock` while it reads and decodes the state, and `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` waits for that lock under `f.mu`. The wait is bounded by one state decode, which is less than before.
- Paths that still replay under the lock, as before: `validatePayload=false` (sync without an EL), `commitmentsValidated=false` when the block appears between the commitment lookup and the lock, and local self-build.

## Tests

In `cl/phase1/forkchoice/on_execution_payload_signature_test.go`:

- A bad signature is rejected without the write lock, for the current state and for a replayed state. Fails on main.
- A replay runs outside `f.mu`, and a root that stops being current is replayed under the lock only after it was verified.
- A valid envelope is applied once when a concurrent apply wins during the replay. Fails on main.
- A second replay does not start while the first replayed state waits for the write lock.
- An unverified envelope is never replayed under the write lock.
- A replay is skipped when the envelope was applied while waiting for the slot.
- A replay that returns no state does not replay again under the lock. The envelope is queued only in queue mode, and not after a concurrent apply.
- Locks and the slot are released after a panic in signature verification.

The new tests were also checked against single-change reverts of each fix. Three existing tests used `ReplayState` as their signal that the apply holds the write lock. Each got one `require.Eventually` on an explicit state predicate instead; no assertion was removed.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network/services: bound the seen sync contributions set
body: The seen sync committee contributions sync.Map was never pruned and grew every slot; it is now an LRU of 4 * SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE entries, like the sibling seen caches.
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl: answer attestation_data from fork choice without waiting for the head state
body:
## Problem

`GET /eth/v1/validator/attestation_data` answered only after the new head state had been copied and published to synced data. To cover that gap, `waitForHeadSlot` polled for up to 1 s. On an empty slot nothing is published, so the handler always waited the full second. On a Hoodi node (about 1.14M validators) 300 empty slots each waited about 1000 ms. The votes were correct, but the validator client got its data at +5 s instead of +4 s. At an epoch boundary, the state-based producer also copied the head state and ran `ProcessSlots` on the request path.

By the spec, the beacon node answers from its current fork-choice head. Waiting for a block is the validator client's job.

## Design

### Fork-choice query

`ForkChoiceStore.AttestationData(headRoot, slot)` builds the attestation data only from data that fork choice keeps for every imported block:

- `beacon_block_root`: the head root.
- `target`: `(epoch(slot), Ancestor(head, epoch start slot))`. This is the head itself when the head is at or before the epoch start.
- `source`: the head state's `current_justified_checkpoint` after `process_slots` to `slot`, as the honest validator guide defines it:
  - head in the same epoch as `slot`: the realized current justified checkpoint of the head's post-state (`finalityCheckpoints`);
  - head in the previous epoch: the head's unrealized justification (`unrealizedJustifications`). The pull-up runs the same `ProcessJustificationBitsAndFinality` that runs first in `ProcessEpoch`, on the same participation and balances, so it equals the value after one epoch transition.

The query returns `false` when it cannot give the spec answer cheaply. The handler then uses today's path unchanged: the attestation producer cache, then the state-based producer. This happens when:

- the head is two or more epochs behind `slot`. A second justification pass works on balances and an active set changed by the first epoch transition, so it can justify a checkpoint that the pull-up did not;
- the head is after `slot` (a late request);
- the head has no `finalityCheckpoints` or no `unrealizedJustifications` entry. This covers the checkpoint-sync anchor, whose unrealized entry is only the anchor checkpoint, LRU eviction, and pruning after finalization;
- the target ancestor cannot be resolved.

The query takes no lock: the values are keyed by block root and never change after `OnBlock` writes them, which it does under `f.mu`.

### Fresh head

The handler reads the head with `GetHeadNode`, which is `get_head`.

- The head that synced data publishes (`SelectedHead`) is not used. It is only refreshed on the next head computation of the stage loop, and on Hoodi it lagged right after a block import (see the evidence below).
- Gossip attestations clear the cached head, so a request often recomputes it under the fork-choice lock. Vote counting is incremental, so this is cheap:
  - a cached read takes about 34 ns;
  - a recompute takes about 31 µs of tree walk on a 96-block chain, plus the votes changed since the last computation;
  - `BenchmarkVoteTally` measures about 2.8 ms for a whole slot of vote changes at 1.1M validators, and 22 ms for a full recount, which happens only when the justified checkpoint changes.
- Before Gloas, a caller that waited for the lock now reuses a head that another caller computed meanwhile, as the Gloas path already does. Without this, concurrent requests that all saw an empty cache recomputed the head one after another under the lock.

### Wait only for a block that is being imported

If a block for the requested slot is being imported (a `BeginPayloadImport` claim for that slot is active) and fork choice has not seen the slot yet, the handler polls until the claim is released or `HighestSeen() >= slot`, then reads the fresh head. With no claim it answers at once, so empty slots never wait.

The wait is capped at 1 s, the bound of the old wait:

- In the Hoodi data, every in-flight import that finished at all finished within 424 ms of the request.
- The imports that were still running after 1 s did not deliver block S to the old path within its 1 s either, so a longer cap gains nothing.
- An answer at +5 s is still far from the aggregation deadline (+8 s) and from inclusion in the next block, so a cap that is too short costs a wrong head vote, while a long one costs little.

A slot whose wait reached the cap is remembered, so later requests for the same slot do not wait again. A block whose data is not available can keep its import claim for up to 30 s, and without this every request for that slot would pay the full second. The old code had the same per-slot memory.

There are no new goroutines. The loop polls every 5 ms: an atomic read (`HighestSeen`) and, while that is below the slot, a scan of the active import claims, of which there are only a few. It stops when the request context is cancelled. The database read transaction is opened only on the fallback path, so a request never holds it while it waits.

`waitForHeadSlot` and `slotWaitedForAttestationProduction` are removed. Committee index rules (required and echoed before Electra, 0 from Electra, the payload meaning from Gloas via `gloasAttestationIndex`) and aggregation pool pinning are unchanged. The attestation producer and the places that feed its cache are unchanged; they serve the fallback.

## Hoodi shadow evidence

A shadow probe ran next to the handler on a Hoodi node (about 1.14M validators). A script requested attestation data at +4.0 s every slot. For every request, the probe recomputed in the background what the old handler would have served (wait up to 1 s, then cached or state-based data, with no cache writes), and compared both with the canonical block of slot S.

Run 1: about 7 h, 2155 requests, head from synced data (`SelectedHead`), no wait.

- Every request was answered within 3 ms; it used to take 1 s on empty slots. The source was always equal.
- In 4 cases fork choice already had block S as head, but synced data still pointed to S-1. The new code voted for S-1; the canonical block was S. Three of them were at the first slot of an epoch, so the target was wrong too. This led to the fresh head (`GetHeadNode`).

Run 2: about 7 h, 2174 requests, fresh head, no wait.

- Source and target were always equal, and there were no stale-head cases.
- Request latency: p50 16 µs, p90 150 µs, p99 9 ms, max 177 ms.
- The head root differed from the old path 17 times, all for late blocks:

| Late block of slot S at request time | Cases | Canonical = S | S orphaned | Wrong head votes: no wait | Old 1 s wait | Wait while importing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Being imported (claim held, `HighestSeen < S`); import finished 6-424 ms later | 8 | 8 | 0 | 8 | 0 | 0 |
| Not seen yet; fork choice saw it 79-859 ms later | 9 | 3 | 6 | 3 | 6 | 3 |
| Total | 17 | 11 | 6 | 11 | 6 | 3 |

Five more requests had a block in flight whose import took longer than 1 s. The old path did not get block S in time either, which is why the wait is capped.

A third run with the final branch (including the wait for in-flight imports) is pending. Its results will be added here.

Run 3: about 20 h, 6011 requests, the code in this PR (fresh head and the wait while a block is being imported). It was built from the same four commits before the rebase onto main; the rebase changed only a mock field context.

- Source was always equal. Target differed twice, both at slots where the head root also differed (see below).
- Only 9 requests waited, for 5, 5, 101, 107, 261, 304, 395, 454 and 547 ms. No request reached the 1 s cap.
- Request latency, including the wait: p50 12 µs, p90 27 µs, p99 200 µs, max 614 ms (the 547 ms wait).
- 17 requests found a block of slot S being imported. All 17 were answered with block S, as the old path did; 15 of these blocks became canonical.
- The head root differed from the old path 22 times, all for a block of slot S that fork choice had not seen at +4.0 s and that held no import claim. Fork choice saw 20 of them 62-828 ms after the request, and 2 not within 1 s. Compared with the canonical block:

| Late block of slot S at request time | Cases | Canonical = S | S orphaned | Wrong head votes: this PR | Old 1 s wait |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Not seen yet | 22 | 9 | 13 | 9 | 13 |

Most of these blocks must have reached the node after the request: for 8 of the 9 canonical ones, fork choice saw the block 254-828 ms later, longer than a normal gossip validation and import. For a block that arrives after the request, answering with the previous head is what the spec asks for. The old 1 s wait won the 9 votes only by also voting for the 13 blocks that were orphaned, and it cannot tell the two cases apart at +4 s. A block that arrived just before the request and was still in gossip validation holds no import claim either; this is listed under known follow-ups.

- Over the whole run, the wrong head vote rate measured against the canonical chain was 1.1% at the first slot of an epoch (2/186) and 1.1% at other slots (65/5781).

## Tests

Fork choice (`cl/phase1/forkchoice`):

- `TestAttestationData`: genesis epoch and the first slot of epoch 1, same epoch, previous epoch, two epochs behind, empty slot, empty and non-empty epoch-start slot, and every miss case.
- `TestAttestationDataMatchesProducer`: imports the 96-block Bellatrix chain (`tests.GetBellatrixRandom`) into a real store. For every block B and every slot in `[B.slot, B.slot + 2 epochs)`, the query must equal today's state-based `attestation_producer` on the state of B where it answers, and return false when B is two epochs behind. It checks that the chain covers a justification change and both target cases. It takes about 12 s and uses the `testing.Short()` guard.
- `TestGetHeadOnceReusesCachedHead`: a pre-Gloas head computation that finds a cached head after taking the lock returns it without recomputing the weights.
- A unit test for the per-slot import claim (`ImportInProgress`).

Handler (`cl/beacon/handler`):

- `TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataUsesForkChoiceHead`:
  - an empty slot answers at once with the previous head;
  - a block imported into fork choice at the first slot of an epoch, while synced data still points to its parent, is used as head and as target.
  - Neither calls the producer.
- In-flight wait:
  - a block for the slot that finishes importing after about 50 ms is used;
  - without a claim the answer is immediate;
  - an import that never finishes is cut at the cap and answered with the previous head;
  - a claim for another slot does not cause a wait;
  - a block of the slot that fork choice has already seen does not cause a wait;
  - a cancelled request stops waiting;
  - after a wait reached the cap, a second request for the same slot answers at once, and a request for another slot still waits;
  - a request that started waiting before the cap was reached by another request for the same slot stops at that moment, not at its own cap.
- `TestGetEthV1ValidatorAttestationDataGloasPayloadIndex`: new rows serve the data from fork choice and expect the same Gloas index as the producer rows.
- Existing producer-based rows cover the fallback.

Every new test was run red first, against the code before the matching change.

## Known follow-ups

- The handler does not return 503 when the response root is execution-optimistic (Beacon API, Gloas and later). The old path did not check this either.
- `gloasAttestationIndex` reads the head a second time, so a reorg between the two reads can pair the root with the other head's payload status. This also existed before.
- A late request for a slot whose epoch had no processed head can find no producer cache entry and return 500.
- When the head's `finalityCheckpoints` entry was evicted (more than 1024 imports since the head), the fallback can serve a different root than the fork-choice head.
- Before Gloas, `ProcessAttestingIndicies` does not clear the cached head.
- The error "no slot for head is stored" leaves a partly computed head in the cache.
- The wait covers only the time a block holds an import claim. A block that is still in gossip validation, or between a failed import and its rescheduling, holds no claim, so the request does not wait for it.
- `HighestSeen` is raised before the state transition and never lowered. A block of slot S that later fails import stops the wait for another block of S.
- The wait memory holds one slot. Requests that alternate between two slots whose imports both stall each wait again, up to the cap.

## Release

Not planned for release/3.8.
