title: common/log/v3, db/downloader, cl/beacon/handler: fix three CI flakes
body:
Three tests failed in CI for reasons unrelated to the code under test:
- `TestStreamHandlerNoContention` asserted that SyncHandler is at least 2x slower than StreamHandler (failed at 270 ms vs 451 ms on a loaded runner). It now checks the property directly: two StreamHandler writes overlap.
- `TestTorrentPeerManager_*` listened on uTP too, and Windows refused the UDP bind on the dynamic port the TCP listener took. They now use the package's `newTestClientConfig`, which disables uTP for this reason.
- `TestPayloadAttributesLoopDrainsStateFeedDuringStateWork` sent the new head right after a 1024-block burst. `SendHeadV2` is a `TrySend`, so when the burst left the loop's buffer full, the head was dropped and the loop never woke (5 in 600 runs). The test now retries the send until the loop takes it (0 in 1000 runs).
author: AskAlexSharov

title: cl/beacon/handler: fix flaky TestPayloadPreparationCollectionWithExecutionModule
body:
Fix the flaky `TestPayloadPreparationCollectionWithExecutionModule`. The test intermittently hangs until the package timeout.

## Root cause

The fixture inserts a 2-block chain with `InsertChain` and then moves the head back with `client.ForkChoiceUpdate(..., canonical, ...)`.

- **`InsertChain` returns early.** It waits only for the header notifications. The forkchoice goroutine of its own FCU can still hold the execution module semaphore at that point.
- **The busy FCU is silently accepted.** When the semaphore is still held, `updateForkChoice` returns `ExecutionStatusBusy`. `ExecutionClientDirect.ForkChoiceUpdate` reports Busy as success when no payload attributes are passed. The head is therefore never moved, and the `WaitIdle` that follows does not help.
- **The test then retries forever.** `startPayloadBuild` sees a forkchoice head that differs from the requested one and returns `ErrPayloadBuildHeadMismatch`. `startPayloadBuildForPreparation` retries that error until its context is cancelled, but the test passes `t.Context()`, which has no deadline. The test hangs.

## Effect on CI

- **`tests` jobs:** they run with `-timeout 20m`, so they print a goroutine dump that points at this test.
- **sonar:** it runs with `-timeout 60m`, the same as the job timeout. The job is killed without a dump and fails at 60 minutes in `cl/beacon/handler`.

## Fix

- **Wait before the FCU.** The fixture calls `WaitIdle` before its `ForkChoiceUpdate`, so the FCU cannot see a busy module.
- **Fail fast on a regression.** The fixture asserts that the forkchoice head is the expected one. If this regresses, the test fails right away instead of hanging.

## Testing

- **Red.** With a temporary 1s delay before the semaphore release in `updateForkChoice` (local only, not part of this PR), the new assertion fails deterministically in every subtest: the head stays at the `InsertChain` tip.
- **Green.** With the `WaitIdle` fix and the delay still in place, the assertion passes.
- **Repeated runs.** Without the delay, the test was run 150 times in parallel with `GOMAXPROCS=2`: 0 failures. Before the fix, the hang reproduced about once every 180 runs of the package.
author: lupin012

title: cl/persistence, cl/phase1, db/kv: persist Gloas execution payload envelope signatures
body:
Part of #21680. It follows the agreed design in https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/issues/21680#issuecomment-6394752054.

## Problem

Caplin keeps Gloas `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope`s only in the fork-graph disk cache, and that cache is pruned soon after finalization. A later PR will rebuild historical envelopes from the beacon block, the next canonical block's `parent_execution_requests` and EL data. The 96-byte builder signature is the only field that cannot be rebuilt. If we do not store it, history before the serve-path PR is lost.

## Change

- New Caplin table `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignatures` in `ChaindataTables`. The key is `slot (8 bytes, big-endian) || beacon block root`, the same layout as `kv.BeaconBlocks`. The value is the 96-byte signature. There is no schema version bump and no snapshot change. A no-op migration, `create_execution_payload_envelope_signatures_table` (the same as `create_ptc_window_epoch_table`), records the schema change. The table is created by a writable open: erigon start-up or `integration run_migrations`. Accede and read-only openers (rpcdaemon, downloader, seg, capcli) cannot create it, so on an old chaindata they need one of those to run first. Other `integration` commands reopen the database in exclusive mode when a migration is pending, but that reopen kept `Accede` and so could not create the table either. This predates this PR, also affected `create_ptc_window_epoch_table`, and is fixed in #25438.
- `beacon_indicies`: `WriteExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignature`, `WriteExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignatureIfAbsent` (used by backfill), `ReadExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignature` and `PruneExecutionPayloadEnvelopeSignatures`. The reader reports a stored value that is not 96 bytes long as not found, and the if-absent writer decides presence with the reader. Forkchoice and backfill therefore follow one rule: a malformed row counts as absent and the next writer replaces it.
- The signature is written in the same transaction as the execution envelope indices:
  - forkchoice import, local self-build, `StoreAnchorEnvelope` and the index-repair retry. These paths share `writeExecutionPayloadEnvelopeIndices`. The row is keyed by `Payload.SlotNumber`, which every entry path checks against the beacon block slot. The repair token now carries the slot and the signature, so a retry still works after the fork graph drops the envelope;
  - history backfill (`writeDownloadedBlock`), keyed by the block slot, only for a verified signature (see below). This also covers downloaded blocks that are already in CL snapshots, because snapshots do not hold signatures. Backfill writes only when no valid row exists for (slot, root), so it never replaces a signature that forkchoice or the anchor path verified; it does replace a malformed row.
- The forkchoice "indices already present" checks now also require a matching signature row. An envelope that is processed again on a node that already has its indices therefore gets the row too. Forkchoice still replaces a different row, so a verified signature replaces an earlier backfilled one. A malformed row reads as missing, so forkchoice replaces it; any other read error still fails the write. Both checks use one reader of the index state and keep their own predicates (structurally usable for the early check, exact values for the write).
- Backfill verifies the envelope signature and stores it only when the check ran. The check runs in the backward downloader's envelope validation hook, after the bid check, so it covers the range batch, the single P2P fetch and the HTTP fallback. It uses the anchor state the backfill starts from, which is newer than every backfilled block:
  - self-build: the pubkey of the block's proposer (validator indices are never reused);
  - builder `i`: `builders[i].Pubkey` when `builders[i].DepositEpoch` is before the envelope epoch;
  - domain: `DOMAIN_BEACON_BUILDER` with the fork version of the envelope epoch.

  An invalid signature fails the hook, so the envelope is discarded and fetched again through the existing retry path. When the anchor state does not name the key (a builder index outside the registry, or a builder deposited in or after the envelope epoch, so the index may have been reused), the envelope is still accepted, because backfill needs it to progress, and its block and EL indices are written as before, but no signature row is written. One helper selects the key; the hook and `BackwardBeaconDownloader.GloasEnvelopeSignatureVerifiable` both use it, and the history stage asks the downloader before it writes the row. The history stage and `capcli chain` both set the validator and share this write path. Without a validator nothing is verified, so no row is written.
- `PruneBlocks` (non-archive cleanup) also prunes signatures below the same bound as the blocks, which since #25412 is the block-serving window clamped to the finalized epoch start. Like the block prune, one call deletes at most `snaptype.CaplinMergeLimit` signature rows; later runs delete the rest, so one cleanup run never holds a long write transaction. The antiquary does not prune them (`PruneBlocksLimit` is unchanged), because they are not in snapshots yet, so archive nodes keep every row (about 140 bytes per Gloas slot, roughly 0.4 GB per year on mainnet).

Nothing reads the table yet. The serve path (ByRange, ByRoot, Beacon API) comes in a later PR.

## Trade-offs

- Backfilled signatures are stored only when they were verified: always for self-build, and for builders whose index was not reused after the envelope. The remaining case (builder exit, full withdrawal and reuse of the index by a new builder in or after the envelope epoch) is not stored, so it will not be served: a missing row only ends a ByRange response early, while a stored unverified signature could never be replaced on those blocks (forkchoice does not write rows below the anchor, backfill never overwrites a valid row, archive nodes never prune). Storing it would need the historical builder registry.
- `DepositEpoch < envelope epoch` is strict on purpose: a builder registered in the envelope epoch may have taken the index after the envelope, and checking against its key would reject a valid envelope and stall backfill.
- Rows written on import for blocks that later become orphans are kept. Non-archive pruning removes them. Rows are keyed by root, so they never answer a lookup for the canonical root.

## Not in this PR

- Reading the table and rebuilding envelopes for ByRange, ByRoot and the Beacon API.
- Shipping signatures in Caplin snapshots.
- Filling signatures for history that is not processed again: Gloas blocks that backfill skips because their indices and EL blocks already exist, blocks below the point where backfill stops, and envelopes lost to a restart before their index write was retried.
- Signatures of backfilled envelopes whose builder key the anchor state does not name (index outside the registry, or reused in or after the envelope epoch).
- The pre-existing `applied=false` index-repair race in `ensureClaimedEnvelopeIndexRepair`; it gets its own PR after this one.

## Tests

- `beacon_indicies`: round-trip, not found, a stored value of 0, 95 or 97 bytes reads as not found, the if-absent writer replaces a malformed row and keeps a valid one, and prune boundary (slot `to-1` deleted, slot `to` kept).
- forkchoice: import stores the signature; `StoreAnchorEnvelope` stores it; a redelivered envelope and the untracked repair path both add a missing signature when the indices already exist; the retry path stores it after the fork graph has pruned the envelope or has no header; the existing panic-recovery test now also checks the signature.
- forkchoice: a redelivered envelope replaces a stored signature of 0, 95 or 97 bytes and leaves no repair pending; `TestPendingEnvelopeRepairsMalformedIndices` stores a matching signature, so each case fails only because of the malformed index row.
- stages: backfill stores the signature of a verified downloaded envelope, also for a block already in CL snapshots; an unverified envelope is accepted and its block and EL indices are written, but no signature row is written (also for a block already in CL snapshots); backfill keeps an existing valid row and replaces a malformed one; an EMPTY slot stores no row.
- stages cleanup, under the #25412 bound: non-archive cleanup prunes the row at slot 943,231 and keeps the row at 943,232 (the first slot of the block-serving window for head 2,000,017); archive cleanup keeps both; one run deletes exactly `CaplinMergeLimit` blocks and `CaplinMergeLimit` signature rows when both tables have a backlog (slot `CaplinMergeLimit-1` pruned, slot `CaplinMergeLimit` kept in each table).
- migrations: an old chaindata without the table, with every earlier migration applied, has the new migration pending; after the exclusive open runs it, an accede open can read the table.
- network: the backfill signature check accepts a self-build envelope signed by the proposer and a builder envelope signed by a builder deposited before the envelope epoch, and rejects both when signed by another key; it accepts, without a check, a builder deposited in the envelope epoch and an index outside the registry. `GloasEnvelopeSignatureVerifiable` is true for the first two cases and false for a builder deposited in or after the envelope epoch, an index outside the registry, a nil builder list, a proposer outside the validator set, and when no validator is set. The tests sign with the Gloas fork version independently of production and put the envelope in the first Gloas epoch, so a lookup of the wrong epoch gets the Fulu version and fails.
- network: with the validator set, the range filter drops an invalidly signed envelope and keeps a valid one.
- The tests cannot tell the envelope epoch from the anchor epoch for the signing domain (passing the anchor epoch to `ComputeDomainAtEpoch` stays green), because the anchor state is in the same fork. Consensus pins it today: the domain must use the envelope epoch. Gloas is the last fork in `GetCurrentStateVersion`, so the two fork versions cannot differ yet.
- The tests cannot tell the block slot from `Payload.SlotNumber` for the row key: forkchoice rejects an envelope whose `Payload.SlotNumber` differs from the block slot, and backfill checks it against `bid.slot`, which consensus requires to equal the block slot. Consensus pins that equality today.
- The one-line wiring in `clstages.go` and `cmd/capcli/cli.go` has no test seam; it is covered by build and review (TDD skipped as a mechanical wiring change).
- `git diff origin/main -- cl/antiquary/` is empty.
author: domiwei

title: cl, execution/execmodule: do not count a busy forkchoice update as applied
body:
## Problem

Caplin can treat a forkchoice update as applied even though the execution layer never applied it. On Gloas the EL head can then stay stale until the next normal ForkChoice stage pass, usually at the next slot boundary. We saw this on a devnet, for example when the FCU to the FULL payload after an envelope import hit Busy. Most cases there were corrected by a later FCU within a second.

## Root cause

1. `ExecModule.updateForkChoice` answers `ExecutionStatusBusy` when the execution semaphore is taken, without applying the update.
2. `ExecutionClientDirect.ForkChoiceUpdate` returns `nil, nil` for every status except InvalidForkchoice and BadBlock when there are no payload attributes. So Busy looks like success.
3. The ForkChoice stage then records `cfg.executionHead` as sent.
4. Within a slot, `SleepForSlot` wakes the stage when the beacon root differs from the published head, or (the execution head wake added in #24938) when a resolved fork choice execution head differs from `cfg.executionHead`. For the same beacon root and execution head, neither fires, so nothing re-sends the update before the next slot.

`ExecutionStatusBusy` had a second meaning in direct mode: an admitted update that ran past the caller's deadline (`--fcu.timeout`, 1s by default) and keeps running in the background. That case is the direct-mode version of the tolerated Engine API timeout. The stage must keep recording the head for it.

## Fix

- `execution/execmodule`: `UpdateForkChoice` now takes the semaphore before it starts the background update, so a rejection is known before the deadline wait. The admitted update keeps the semaphore as before: the update goroutine releases it, or the background goroutine it hands the semaphore to. The deadline case sets the new `ForkChoiceResult.UpdateInProgress`, which means the update was admitted and may still be running. Busy with `UpdateInProgress == false` now always means "not started".
- `cl/phase1/execution_client`: the direct client returns the new `ErrForkChoiceUpdateBusy` for a not-started update without payload attributes. A Busy result with `UpdateInProgress` still returns `nil, nil`. Updates with payload attributes are unchanged and still go to `retryAssembleBlock`.
- `cl/phase1/stages`: the ForkChoice stage treats `ErrForkChoiceUpdateBusy` as non-fatal but does not record the execution head. It still updates the wake throttle key, so `SleepForSlot` wakes the stage again once `sleepForSlotRewakeInterval` (1s) has passed since the previous wake, and the update is re-sent. The stage does not run at every 200ms poll.
- `cl/beacon/handler`: storing a produced block tolerates `ErrForkChoiceUpdateBusy` like a timeout, so a busy EL does not fail block publication.
- The persistent block collector already logs a failed forkchoice update at Warn, and it keeps doing so.

I chose to surface Busy instead of retrying inside `ForkChoiceUpdate`. When the budget of a retry runs out, it still has to return this error. The existing wake mechanism already re-sends the update without blocking the stage.

I also tried a short retry inside `ExecutionClientDirect.ForkChoiceUpdate` for this busy answer, and dropped it. The client only sees call order, not how fresh a head is: a caller that sampled an older head could retry and apply it after another caller had applied a newer one. The prototype used a mutex with sequence numbers to keep the order safe, and a cancelled caller could still wait on that mutex. The ForkChoice stage already re-sends a busy update through the `SleepForSlot` rewake, so the client does not retry.

## Tests

- `TestGloasForkChoiceRejectedAsBusyIsResent` uses a real direct client over an execution module stub that answers Busy once and then Success. It failed on main before the fix in two ways: the busy head was recorded, and with that assertion removed, `SleepForSlot` did not wake again before the next slot.
- `TestDirectForkChoiceUpdateReportsBusyWhenUpdateWasNotStarted`, `TestDirectForkChoiceUpdateAllowsBusyUpdateInProgress` and `TestDirectForkChoiceUpdateKeepsBuildingAfterBusyWithAttributes` pin the direct client mapping. The last two keep existing behaviour.
- `TestRepeatedForkchoicePersistsAfterCallerTimeout` now checks that the deadline case sets `UpdateInProgress` and that a busy answer does not.
- `TestStoreBlockAndBlobsToleratesBusyForkchoice` covers block publication.
- Two tests sent a setup forkchoice update right after `execmoduletester.InsertChain`, whose own update can still hold the execution semaphore while it commits: `TestDirectPreparationAndForkChoiceReuseTheSameExecutionBuild` and `TestPayloadPreparationCollectionWithExecutionModule`. Before this change the busy answer was reported as success; now it is `ErrForkChoiceUpdateBusy`, and the race CI job with parallel commitment failed on it ([run](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/actions/runs/40361387508/job/121707625334)). Both tests already waited for an idle execution module after the setup update to isolate what they test from that contention. They now also wait before it. In a local experiment with a 100 ms sleep added before the semaphore release in `updateForkChoice`, both tests failed without this wait and passed with it.
- Mutation check: removing each part of the fix makes the matching test fail. This covers the direct client sentinel, the `UpdateInProgress` check, the stage's skip of the record, the stage's tolerance, the throttle key update, the deadline marker, the early semaphore acquire (40 of 40 local runs failed) and the block production tolerance.

## Behaviour change

- In direct mode, a forkchoice update rejected as busy is no longer reported as success. On Gloas the stage re-sends it about once per second while the head stays the same.
- This includes an update sent right after another one, while the previous commit still holds the execution semaphore (the comment above `retryAssembleBlock` puts this at tens of milliseconds). Such an update used to be dropped silently; now the caller gets `ErrForkChoiceUpdateBusy`, and on Gloas the stage re-sends it at its next rewake, at most about one second later.
- An update that only ran past its deadline stays tolerated by the direct client and the stage, as before.
- Engine server, testing API and block downloader keep the same Busy status semantics.

## Known limitations

- Engine API mode (`--caplin.use-engine-api`, or Caplin with an external Erigon EL) has the same problem in another form: Erigon's engine server maps every Busy to SYNCING, and the Engine API client treats SYNCING without payload attributes as success. There SYNCING cannot be told apart from a missing segment or a sync in progress, so this PR does not change it.
- An update with payload attributes that hits a rejected Busy still goes on to assemble a block. If the requested head is not canonical yet, the builder later fails with "wrong head block". This is existing behaviour and is not changed here.
- The re-send within a slot needs a resolved Gloas execution head (`GetExecutionHead` ready). When the stage falls back to `GetEth1Hash` for an unresolved head, a rejected update waits for the next slot, as before.
- Before Gloas there is no polling inside a slot, so a rejected update waits for the next stage pass, as before.

## Related

- #24938 added the `SleepForSlot` execution head wake that this fix relies on.
- #23368 (draft) separates busy from caller timeout for `SetHead` and block assembly. It does not cover this forkchoice update status.

## Release branches

The non-stage files of the first commit (b51ec3fc792) apply cleanly to `release/3.8`; the stage files do not, because #24938 is not on that branch. On `release/3.8`, the execution module still answers Busy without applying the update, and the direct client still reports that as success, so the EL head stays stale until the next ForkChoice stage pass. There is no execution head wake there that could re-send it earlier. A backport of only the non-stage files would surface the busy answer, but the release stage would also need to tolerate the new error, and it would still not re-send earlier. I have not opened a backport.
author: domiwei

title: cl/clparams, cl/persistence, cl/phase1/stages: keep beacon blocks the specs require
body:
## Problem

Non-archive Caplin pruned beacon blocks `seenSlot - 1_000_000` in `cleanupAndPruning`, in one write transaction. The phase0 p2p spec (`BeaconBlocksByRange`) requires two things this did not do:

- Keep and serve blocks for `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` epochs, measured by the wall clock. On mainnet that is 33,024 epochs = 1,056,768 slots, so the oldest ~56,800 slots of the window were already deleted. Networks with a smaller window (Gnosis and Chiado 528,384 slots, `--chain=dev` 264,192) kept more than required.
- Keep and serve every block after the latest finalized checkpoint, even outside that window, because peers need them to sync through a long period of non-finality.

## Change

- New `BeaconChainConfig.BlockServeRangeStartSlot(currentSlot)`, next to the existing blob and data column helpers and using the same `serveRangeStartSlot` (epoch-aligned, configured `MinEpochsForBlockRequests()`).
- `cleanupAndPruning` prunes below `min(BlockServeRangeStartSlot(min(seenSlot, wallClockSlot)), finalizedEpochStart)`:
  - the wall clock follows the spec; taking the smaller of it and the stage head keeps the existing rule of never pruning further while the stage lags;
  - `finalizedEpochStart` comes from `HighestFinalized`, which fork choice already writes to the same database. While it is 0 (fresh node, just after a restart), nothing is pruned.
- `beacon_indicies.PruneBlocks` deletes at most `snaptype.CaplinMergeLimit` (10,000) blocks per call, the batch size the antiquary uses for the same table. The stage runs every slot, so a large backlog, for example the first run on a network whose window shrank, is deleted over several runs instead of in one long write transaction. The antiquary calls `PruneBlocksLimit` directly and is unchanged.

## Trade-offs

- Mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi keep 56,768 more slots of beacon blocks (without execution payloads) than before.
- Slots that the old bound already deleted inside the new window are not downloaded again; that gap ages out of the window within about 8 days.

## Not in this PR

- `MinEpochsForBlockRequests()` does not apply the Gloas formula (`compute_min_epochs_for_block_requests`); it keeps more than required after Gloas, which is safe.
- Erigon's hardcoded bloatnet config does not set `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` and falls back to 66 epochs; this change makes that value matter there.
- StatusV2 `earliest_available_slot` is derived only from the data column floor.

## Tests

Each test was written first and seen failing on the code before its fix:

- `TestCleanupAndPruningKeepsBlocksForTheBlockRequestWindow`: slot 943,232 (first slot of the window for head 2,000,017) is kept, 943,231 is pruned. Fails on the old 1,000,000 bound.
- `TestCleanupAndPruningKeepsBlocksAfterTheFinalizedCheckpoint`: blocks from the finalized epoch start are kept even below the window.
- `TestCleanupAndPruningBoundsBlocksPrunedPerRun`: one run deletes exactly `CaplinMergeLimit` blocks.
- `TestCleanupAndPruningUsesTheWallClockWhenItIsBehindTheStageHead`: the window follows the wall clock when the stage head is ahead of it.
- `TestCleanupAndPruningKeepsBlocksWhileFinalityIsUnknown`: nothing is pruned while `HighestFinalized` is 0.

Reviewed by Claude and Codex (dual review, then a fix-delta review). `make lint` (twice), `make erigon integration`, `go test ./cl/phase1/stages/ ./cl/clparams/ ./cl/persistence/beacon_indicies/ ./cl/antiquary/...` pass.
author: domiwei

title: cl/phase1/network: keep block ranges in flight in the backward beacon downloader
body:
Caplin's history download sends one 64-slot `BeaconBlocksByRange` at a time and waits for it, so catching up ~438k blocks on mainnet runs at ~30 blk/s, about 4 h. Profiling showed 9% of one core in use; goroutine dumps showed the walk waiting on its one P2P request.

While the current range is in flight, each `reqInterval` tick prefetches the next 64 slots below, up to 8 pending; a pending range is used only when it holds the block with `expectedRoot`, otherwise the range is requested fresh. Still one request per tick. snap-arb1 mainnet: 27.4 → 91.6 blk/s median, 5 runs × 600 s per arm, Mann-Whitney p 0.0079, all over P2P (at `da902279fa4`).

With 64+ empty slots right below the last processed block, every range request came back empty and the walk stalled for good, on main too. An empty range is now followed by a `BeaconBlocksByRoot` for `expectedRoot`.
author: awskii

title: cl/phase1: rate history ETA by downloaded blocks, not skipped slots
body:
The history download's blk/sec and "Downloading Execution History" ETA come from the backward downloader's slot pointer. `trySkipToExistingBlock` moves that pointer past blocks the persistent collector or the EL already holds without downloading them, so after a restart the skipped slots count as speed.

The downloader now counts blocks whose `onNewBlock` succeeded, and the rate uses that count. Restart at ~11.5k blocks, snap-arb1 mainnet, `--no-downloader`:

| | main `478c481407f` | this PR `4a35e1175ad` |
|-|-|-|
| before restart | 25.9 blk/s, 4h37m | 25.5 blk/s, 4h41m |
| first line after | 436.3 blk/s, 16m23s | 20.8 blk/s, 5h44m |
| after 7 min | 59.2 blk/s, 1h57m (32.2 measured) | 22.3 blk/s, 5h14m (22.4 measured) |

Closes #17264. Its earlier symptoms (per-tick swings, underflow, progress past 100%) were fixed by #18320, #22461 and #21912.
author: awskii

title: cl/phase1/forkchoice: count FULL votes for optimistically imported payloads
body:
Addresses item 3 of #21866.

In the Gloas fork choice, the payload-specific requirement of `validate_on_attestation` for an index-1 attestation is `is_payload_verified(store, beacon_block_root)`, which is `root in store.payloads` (consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4, `specs/gloas/fork-choice.md`, "Modified `validate_on_attestation`" and `is_payload_verified`). Under optimistic sync, `verify_and_notify_new_payload` MUST return `True` when the execution engine returns `NOT_VALIDATED` (`specs/bellatrix/optimistic-sync.md`, "How to optimistically import blocks"). So an optimistically imported payload is in `store.payloads`. A payload that is rejected as `INVALIDATED` at import, or that has not been imported, is not.

`ValidateOnAttestation` used `IsPayloadVerified`, which is true only after the EL returns VALID. While the EL returned `SYNCING` or `ACCEPTED`, every index-1 attestation carried in a block (`OnBlock` -> `onAttestationLocked`) was dropped from fork choice, including its LMD weight, and the `OnBlock` path did not queue it for retry. This was also inconsistent inside fork choice: `getNodeChildren` already uses `isPayloadAvailable` to create the FULL child of such a block, so a FULL node could exist while every vote for it was rejected.

The fix uses the same `isPayloadAvailable` predicate (NOT_VALIDATED or VALID, envelope locally available, block not invalid, payload not marked unavailable). It also removes the wrong "PTC attestation" comment and changes the error text: index 1 is an ordinary attestation that votes `payload_present = true`, not a PTC vote.

Gossip is not affected and not changed: index-1 attestations for an optimistic payload get an `IGNORE` result during gossip validation before they reach fork choice, as the Gloas p2p spec requires ("[IGNORE] The attested execution payload is optimistic"). Outside unit tests, the public `OnAttestation` method is used only by the fork-choice spec runner.

Tests: `TestValidateOnAttestationPayloadPresentVote` fails on main for the optimistic case. It also checks that index-1 attestations are still rejected when the payload is invalidated, not imported, missing its envelope, part of an invalid block or marked unavailable, and that index 0 is not gated on the payload. With v1.7.0-beta.4 fixtures, the Gloas fork-choice spec tests pass with and without the change, and the full Gloas mainnet suite passes with it. The fork-choice runner always answers VALID from the engine, so it does not reach the optimistic case.
author: domiwei

title: cl: give envelope disk I/O its own lock
body:
## Problem

`ReadEnvelopeFromDisk` and `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` took `stateDumpLock` and used the shared `sszBuffer`. The same lock serializes full beacon-state dumps and reads. On mainnet a head-state dump takes 420 ms p50 and 700 ms max (Hoodi: 254 ms p50, 681 ms max), while an envelope dump takes only 0.2-3.6 ms locally for 100 KB to 10 MiB.

`DumpEnvelopeOnDisk` runs while the fork-choice write lock `f.mu` is held (normal import, self-build and `StoreAnchorEnvelope`). When an envelope dump collided with a state dump or read, fork choice waited for the whole state I/O. There was also a second path: an envelope read held `lifecycleMu.RLock` while it waited for `stateDumpLock`, so `Prune` (waiting for `lifecycleMu.Lock` under `addPruneMu`) and then `AddChainSegment` (under `f.mu`) waited too.

## Fix

Envelope reads and dumps now use their own `envelopeMu` and a reusable `envelopeSSZBuffer`. The buffer is reused rather than allocated per call, because per-call buffers made dumps 20-35% slower in a prototype. The new lock is still needed: the `.tmp` file name is fixed per root, so dumps of the same root must stay serialized, and a read must not overlap a write.

Unchanged: `lifecycleMu` usage, the transaction clone after decode, the second validation in `DumpEnvelopeOnDisk`, and the `f.mu` scope in the callers.

## Tests

- An envelope dump and an envelope read finish while `stateDumpLock` is held (both fail on main).
- A state read finishes while `envelopeMu` is held.
- Concurrent dumps of the same root all succeed and the file reads back valid (fails under `-race` without `envelopeMu`).
- An envelope dump and a state dump run at the same time and both read back intact (fails under `-race` if the envelope dump uses the shared `sszBuffer`).
- Envelope reads of one root and dumps of another root run at the same time (fails under `-race` without the read-side `envelopeMu`).
- The buffer reuse test now pins `envelopeSSZBuffer`. The `HasEnvelope` no-disk-I/O test also holds `envelopeMu`.

## Out of scope

- Moving the envelope write out of `f.mu`: it is a few ms at most.
- A metric for the envelope dump time.
- The duplicate head-state dump on the Gloas execution-head ForkChoice rerun.
- Checkpoint-state replay under `f.mu`.

Part of #25120
author: domiwei

title: cl: persist beacon blocks only after fork choice accepts them
body:
Rejected P2P beacon blocks could overwrite `StateRootToBlockRoot` before validation and break exact-state-root Beacon API reads. Both sync and gossip imports now persist blocks and their indices only after fork choice accepts them.

- **Acceptance:** `OnBlock` can return nil for an old block without importing it, so initial acceptance is confirmed by a header in fork choice.
- **Persistence retries:** Sync, gossip, and Beacon API publishing retain accepted blocks after a failed database write. Pending writes survive job expiry, header pruning, and sync-stage transitions. Forward-sync retries also preserve the pending execution insertion.
- **Canonical updates:** Updates wait for the required block indices along the path from the new head to an existing canonical block or the trusted anchor. The anchor may come from a checkpoint state, so it can lack block indices. This prevents a concurrent reorg from marking the new head canonical while leaving ancestors from the previous fork.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-bounty/erigon/issues/56.

Regression tests reproduced the state-root overwrite in both import paths and the ignored-block case before the fixes. They also cover acceptance, storage retries, sync-stage handoffs, and canonical publication. Refactors use existing coverage without a new red/green cycle because they do not change behavior.

This prevents new corruption; it does not rebuild index entries already damaged on an existing node. The live devnet reproduction was not rerun.
author: yperbasis

title: cl/das, cl/phase1/network/services: build custody columns from engine_getBlobsV2
body:
Part of #25446

From Fulu, Caplin does not use `engine_getBlobsV2`, so a gossip block waits for all its custody columns from peers. This PR adds the spec's EL path:

- `PeerDas.ImportColumnsFromBlobs` builds the column sidecars of a Fulu block from a `getBlobsV2` response. It stores the custody columns (all columns, plus recovery scheduling, in archive mode). It requires every blob, with one proof per cell. All cells are batch-verified against the block's commitments, so empty or partial responses (for example from the embedded txpool, see #24546) store nothing.
- `blockService.ProcessMessage` starts the import in the background after gossip validation, for pre-Gloas Fulu blocks with blobs whose data is not yet available. The block's regular retry picks up the stored columns.
- `NewBlockService` takes the execution engine.

Columns built this way are not published to gossip.

Tests:
- `cl/das`: custody and archive storage, sidecar validity, and rejection of incomplete, malformed, swapped or wrong-proof responses. A mutation check (verification disabled) fails the swapped and wrong-proof cases.
- `cl/phase1/network/services`: the engine is called with the commitments' versioned hashes, and is skipped when data is available, there are no blobs, the block is pre-Fulu, or there is no engine.
author: lystopad

title: cl/phase1/network/services, cl/phase1/forkchoice: accept execution payload envelopes before the EL verdict
body:
### Problem

Gossip validation of `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` ran the whole import inside the pubsub validator: it could replay state, and it ran the state transition and `NewPayload` before returning the verdict. An `INVALID` response from the EL became a gossip REJECT. The forwarding peer always got the gossipsub invalid-delivery penalty and, with at least 32 active peers, was normally banned for 30 minutes. The same happened for import-only CL checks that are not part of the gossip rules: `prev_randao`, `gas_limit`, `parent_hash`, `parent_beacon_block_root`, the expected-withdrawals-root and timestamp checks in the state transition, and the local block-hash recomputation. Every Erigon hop also waited for the EL before forwarding.

So a builder with a winning bid could publish a correctly signed, CL-valid but EL-invalid envelope. Other clients would forward it, and Erigon nodes would then penalize, and usually ban, those honest peers.

### Spec

`validate_execution_payload_envelope_gossip` (consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4, `specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md`) has no EL step, no data-availability step and no state transition:
- IGNORE: an already-seen envelope, an unknown block root, a slot below the finalized slot.
- REJECT: a known block without a validated state, slot mismatch, builder index, block hash, `execution_requests` root, request and withdrawal limits, builder signature.
- On success, the envelope is marked seen and its payload is cached by block hash (`seen.execution_payloads`).

The `prev_randao`, `gas_limit`, `parent_hash`, timestamp and expected-withdrawals-root checks belong to `verify_execution_payload_envelope` in fork choice, which is part of the import, together with `verify_and_notify_new_payload`. Bellatrix `p2p-interface.md`, "Why allow invalid payloads on the P2P network?", says: "nodes should never downscore/disconnect nodes due to such invalid payloads".

### Other clients

None of them waits for the EL before ACCEPT, and none turns an EL-invalid payload into a gossip REJECT.

| Client | Waits for the EL? | Forwarder penalty on EL INVALID |
|---|---|---|
| Lighthouse | No: `verify_envelope_for_gossip`, then Accept, then import | none |
| Prysm | No: the validator returns Accept, the EL runs in the subscriber | none (`setBadPayload`) |
| Teku | No: no EL call in the gossip validator, the import runs async | none |
| Nimbus | No: `validateExecutionPayload`, then `enqueuePayload` | none (`addUnviable`) |
| Grandine | No: `notify_new_payload` only enqueues | none |
| Lodestar | No: the import runs in `callInNextEventLoop` | application-level `reportPeer`; the gossip verdict stays ACCEPT |

Lighthouse and Lodestar were checked again at their dev-branch heads. The references for the other four clients were not checked again. Erigon's own REST `broadcast_validation=gossip` path publishes after the synchronous import attempt, not before it. An EL `INVALID` import result does not stop the publication.

### Change

- The import result no longer decides the gossip verdict. The verdict comes from the service's existing structure, limit, finality, block-availability, builder-index and duplicate checks, and then from `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForGossip`, which checks the block content and the builder signature. As before, a known block whose state is not available gets IGNORE (beta.4 says REJECT), and `seen.execution_payloads` is not implemented yet.
- On success, the node records the payload arrival (used for PTC `payload_present`), takes the payload-preparation hold, marks the envelope seen, emits `execution_payload_gossip` and returns ACCEPT.
- The import runs in a goroutine on the service context. The goroutine owns the admission token, the seen entry and the hold until the import ends, and it recovers a panic. A panic during the gossip-event emission before the hand-off also releases the admission token, the seen entry and the hold.
- Import results never change the verdict and never ban. An EL `INVALID` still marks the payload invalidated, as before.
- A transient import failure that leaves the envelope unpersisted rolls back the seen markers, so a later copy can still be imported. Terminal invalid results and missing data availability keep them.
- If the block state is not available yet, the envelope is ignored and parked in the fork-choice pending queue, as the import did before. A replay error is ignored without parking.
- Envelopes from the service pending queue are already off the gossip path, so they still import synchronously. A local import error that is not classified as IGNORE or invalid keeps the service job for retry. A block state that is not available yet moves the envelope to fork choice. After a successful or terminal attempt, including a persistence failure that fork choice queues, the service emits the gossip event once and republishes once.
- `ValidateExecutionPayloadEnvelopeForGossip` no longer copies the state for each envelope. It hashes the payload and the execution requests before taking the read lock and verifies against the cached current state in place. Only when that state is not cached does it run the state-free bid checks first and then replay off the lock, under the validation semaphore. It releases the semaphore before the lock-free finality recheck.

### Tests

Service-level tests now check that:
- an injected EL-invalid, import-only-invalid or state-transition-invalid import result still gives ACCEPT, and the envelope stays seen;
- the verdict is returned while the import is blocked, the import runs on the service context, and a concurrent admission claim (as used by REST) waits for the token;
- an injected gossip-validation error still gives REJECT, and an injected `ErrIgnore` still gives IGNORE;
- the seen markers roll back after a transient failure;
- the payload-preparation hold stays active after ACCEPT while the import is blocked, and is released when the import ends (this covers payload preparation only, see the known limitations);
- the arrival is recorded before the import ends;
- a block state that is not available yet parks the envelope in fork choice, and a plain `ErrIgnore` from the gossip check (for example a replay error) does not park it, both on the direct path and on the pending path;
- a panic during the gossip-event emission or inside the import releases the admission token, the seen entry and the hold.

Pending-queue tests now check: retry on a local failure with exactly one `execution_payload_gossip` operation event; moving an envelope to fork choice and removing the service job when the block state is not available; and publishing once after a persistence failure.

Fork-choice tests now check current-state validation without the semaphore, replay-error classification as IGNORE rather than state-unavailable (so the service does not park it), rejection of a bid mismatch before replay, the parking API, and that the arrival API keeps the first arrival time.

Four tests run against a real `ForkChoiceStore` and an `ExecutionClientDirect`-backed client: EL `INVALID` and a blocked `NewPayload` (both through a `NewPayload` test hook), a `prev_randao` mismatch, and a bad signature. They take about 11 s each and use the file's `testing.Short()` convention.

Existing tests that tied the gossip verdict to the import result were updated, and renamed where their meaning flipped. Six old service tests were removed. Five were replaced, and their scenarios are covered by new or renamed tests. The sixth, the forged-envelope-slot test, did not exercise the real slot check: its mock returned the slot-mismatch error, and the test checked that error text and the REJECT class; the REJECT path is covered by the gossip-validation service test, and the slot check by `TestValidateEnvelopeAgainstBlock_SlotNumberMismatch`. A bad signature is covered by an integration test, and a bid mismatch before replay by a fork-choice test.

The hashing before the read lock in gossip validation is not directly tested.

### Known limitations (follow-ups)

- Some import failures after ACCEPT have no automatic retry: an inconsistent EL status/error result, some refresh failures after the EL call, and a recovered panic inside the import. (Missing data availability, interrupted EL validation and persistence failures are queued by fork choice.) The seen markers are rolled back, but nothing retries the import unless another copy arrives (req/resp, a REST re-POST, another publication). Before this change such a non-panicking failure gave IGNORE and pubsub dropped identical copies, so another copy was needed then too. The difference is that the envelope is now forwarded, its arrival is recorded, and the gossip event is emitted before the import.
- The Beacon API can answer "already seen" for an envelope that this node has not imported, when a gossip copy was accepted and its import then failed with a terminal result. The seen state is kept on purpose, as the spec does.
- `blob_data_available` still requires `HasEnvelope`, so it stays false until the envelope is persisted, and it remains false after an import that fails before persistence.
- The spec's `seen.execution_payloads` cache, used for a child bid's parent gas limit, is still missing.
- There is no per-import deadline. The existing 1024-identity admission bound applies.
- The fork-choice pending queue keeps one unverified envelope per block root, and the latest envelope replaces the previous one for that root, unchanged from before. A later forged envelope can replace a valid one that was parked while the state was not available.
- Block production's parent-envelope wait (`envelopeParked` in `cl/beacon/handler/payload_preparation.go`) does not see the payload-preparation hold. For an envelope that is not persisted yet, it checks only the fork-choice pending queue and `ExecutionPayloadApplyInFlight`. The service starts the import goroutine and returns ACCEPT, but the import reaches `beginEnvelopeApply` only after the goroutine is scheduled, the second signature check and, when the state is not cached, a replay. In that window, a proposal that builds on the EMPTY head does not wait for the envelope. This window existed before in kind and is slightly longer now.
- On the P2P gossip path, an accepted envelope normally has its builder signature verified twice: once in gossip validation and once in the import. If the block state is not cached at a check, that check replays it, so the state can be replayed twice; on the `main` branch, the normal successful gossip import replayed it once. The uncached case should be uncommon: only the state of the most recently processed block is cached, and an envelope usually arrives before the next block.
author: domiwei

title: cl, cmd/caplin: precompute the next-epoch state off the fork-choice lock
body:
Part of #25136 (direction 4, block import only).

## Problem

The first block of each epoch runs the epoch transition inside `AddChainSegment`, under the fork-choice write lock `f.mu`. Head updates, attestation processing and `get_head` wait during that time.

On a mainnet node on `main` (24 h, 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-28), this transition took 467 ms p50. At the boundary, `f.mu` was held 491 ms after `newPayload`, compared to 61 ms in the slot before.

Public Xatu head events for 2026-10-27 show the effect. We compared each slot with the per-slot median of each client:
- Normal slots: our node is within about 0.1 s of Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku and Lodestar.
- First slot of an epoch: these clients update the head 0.3-0.5 s earlier than our node. That matches the transition time.

Directions 1-3 of #25136 are merged. This PR does the remaining part for block import.

## Change

- `ForkChoiceStore.RunNextEpochPrecompute` runs in a goroutine started by `RunCaplinService`. At 2/3 of the last slot of each epoch, if the node is synced and the head is in that epoch, it copies the head state, runs `ProcessSlots` to the first slot of the next epoch and hashes the state. None of this holds `f.mu`.
- The result goes to the fork graph with `SetNextEpochState(parentRoot, state)`, keyed by the head root. The fork graph keeps one entry.
- The first `AddChainSegment` that reaches the state transition with a block at or after the entry's slot takes the entry. It uses it only when the block's parent root matches and full validation is on, and drops it otherwise. An import that stops before the transition (for example `MissingSegment`) leaves the entry in place; it is still correct for any later child of the same parent.
- With the entry, the import calls the new `TransitionStateFromPrecomputedEpochState`. It runs only the block part when the state is already at the block slot, and the normal `TransitionState` otherwise.
- If that fails, the import falls back to the normal transition on the parent state, so a wrong precomputed state cannot reject a valid block. A failure only on the precomputed path logs `Precomputed epoch state diverged` at Warn.
- `AddChainSegment` records the highest block slot that reached the state transition, valid or not. `SetNextEpochState` ignores a state at or below that slot, so a precompute that finishes after the boundary block was imported is dropped. The precompute stops without publishing once ctx is cancelled.
- `caplin_next_epoch_state_outcomes_total{outcome}` counts what happens to the precomputed state. At an import: `hit`, `no_entry` (a block that crosses an epoch and finds no entry, also while the node is not synced and no precompute runs), `parent_mismatch`, `no_full_validation`, `diverged`, `invalid`. At publication: `late`. Each outcome is also logged at Debug, except `diverged`, which stays at Warn.
- `machine.TransitionState` is split into `ProcessSlots` and `transitionBlock`. Its behavior does not change.

Not in this PR: payload preparation, block production, checkpoint states, gossip validation and the Beacon API do not use the precomputed state. After #25359, `attestation_data` no longer advances the state at the boundary. Payload preparation already advances its own copy before the slot, outside `f.mu`.

## Why 2/3 of the last slot

From the mainnet node's logs over 87 epochs:
- The head at 2/3 (8 s) of the last slot was the parent of the next epoch's first imported block in 87 of 87 epochs. The head never changed between that point and the boundary block.
- Starting when the last slot's block becomes the head would have missed one epoch, where the last slot was empty.
- The earliest boundary block arrived 4.7 s after the trigger. The precompute takes about 0.5 s.

On the canonical chain, 998 of the last 1000 epochs had a block in the last slot.

These numbers use the fork-choice head. The precompute reads the head from synced data, which is published at the end of the fork-choice pass, so a last-slot block imported just before the trigger but not yet published is a miss. The node measurement below will show the real hit rate.

## Cost

- In the background, once per epoch: one copy of the head state (taken under the synced-data read lock), one epoch transition and one state hash.
- One extra beacon state in memory from the trigger until the boundary import, about 4-5 s per epoch.

## Tests

- `cl/transition`:
  - The precomputed path gives the same state, state root and rewards as the normal path at every epoch boundary of the Bellatrix test chain.
  - A state ahead of the block is rejected.
  - `TestTransitionStateRejectsBlockAtStateSlot` guards the `TransitionState` split and passes on `main`.
- `fork_graph`: the matching entry is used, also when empty slots remain before the block (Electra fixture: entry at 8288, block at 8290); a wrong parent, a missing full validation and an invalid block drop it; a missing segment keeps it; a corrupted entry falls back to the normal transition; a late publication is ignored, also after an invalid block; each import or late publication counts exactly one outcome, and a block that does not cross an epoch counts none.
- `forkchoice`: the target epoch calculation, the trigger slot of the loop, the synced and head-epoch gates, the published state is used by `OnBlock`, and no publication after cancellation.
- Spectests: `sanity/blocks`, `finality` and the transition `core` vectors that cross an epoch also run the precomputed path. Both paths must agree on whether the block is valid, and when it is valid they must produce the same state. Error messages are not compared, because the two paths can fail with different messages for the same invalid block.

## Measurements

Mainnet dev node, same machine and datadir, about 24 h per run:
- without: `main` 85258cd2fd + #25359 + #25258 + #25274, 2026-10-27 07:31 to 2026-10-28 11:58 UTC;
- with: `main` cdf7da1af3 + this PR + #25423 + #25274, 2026-10-28 12:00 to 2026-10-29 13:12 UTC.

The base moved between the runs, but none of the other changes touch the epoch transition. The first row is measured directly in `AddChainSegment`.

| | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| Epoch transition under `f.mu`, first slot of an epoch, p50 / p90 | 463 / 528 ms | 45 / 56 ms |
| EL "head validated", first slot of an epoch, p50 (time after slot start) | 2.58 s | 2.13 s |
| First slots of an epoch with "head validated" after 3.5 s | 25% | 12% |
| EL "head validated", other slots, p50 | 1.87 s | 1.89 s |
| `attestation_data` latency, first slot of an epoch, p90 / p99 | 46 / 470 ms | 0 / 25 ms |

Precomputed state: used in 215 of 224 epochs, not available in 9, and never diverged. In most of the 9 misses, the first block of the epoch arrived late and used the entry, and the next block was built on the same parent, so no entry was left for it.

Per-slot comparison with other clients, from the public Xatu `beacon_api_eth_v1_events_head` data. For each slot, the value is the client's median head time minus the Caplin node's head time; positive means Caplin is earlier. Without: 2026-10-27 07:32-24:00 UTC; with: 2026-10-28 12:01-24:00 UTC.

| Client | first slot of an epoch, without | first slot of an epoch, with | other slots, without | other slots, with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grandine | -0.676 s | -0.240 s | -0.227 s | -0.231 s |
| Teku | -0.454 s | -0.009 s | -0.118 s | -0.095 s |
| Lighthouse | -0.395 s | +0.040 s | -0.068 s | -0.067 s |
| Lodestar | -0.467 s | -0.021 s | -0.081 s | -0.067 s |
| Prysm | -0.261 s | +0.205 s | -0.082 s | -0.074 s |
| Nimbus | -0.375 s | +0.062 s | +0.049 s | +0.060 s |

On other slots the difference stays almost the same, so the network conditions were similar. On the first slot of an epoch, the node moved from behind all clients to level with Teku and Lodestar.
author: domiwei

title: cl/das, cl/persistence/beacon_indicies: move earliest_available_slot to the custody group count raise
body:
Part of #24787: this PR covers the case of a custody group count increase.

## Problem

`fulu/validator.md`:

> When a value for `custody_group_count` is set, the `earliest_available_slot` field in the status RPC message SHOULD reflect the slot at which the `custody_group_count` was updated.

On an increase, `PeerDasState.SetCustodyGroupCount` raises the advertised count and updates the ENR at once, but `earliest_available_slot` only follows the column prune floor in `PeerDas.PruneBelow`. The increase does not schedule a fetch of the new custody columns for older slots. So the node advertises columns it does not have, and `DataColumnSidecarsByRange`/`ByRoot` leave them out of the response for slots before the increase.

This happens only when the increase adds custody columns. Erigon custodies `max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, advertised cgc)` groups, and for the same node ID a larger count gives a superset. With the default config, the usual 4 → 8 step for a validator node adds no columns. The first count that adds columns is 9, which needs 288 ETH of attached effective balance.

## Change

- `PeerDasState` keeps a custody raise slot separately from the prune floor. `GetEarliestAvailableSlot` returns the larger of the two.
- `SetCustodyGroupCount(cgc, raiseSlot)` moves the raise slot only when the increase adds custody columns, and never lowers it. In that case it calls `raiseSlot` under `cgcMutex`, after the new count is installed and the custody column cache is cleared, so a raiser that stalls across a slot boundary cannot record a slot whose block was checked with the old columns.
- `UpdateValidatorsCustody` passes a function that returns the current slot + 1, where the current slot is the larger of the wall-clock slot and the fork-choice slot. It runs in `OnBlock`, after the Fulu data availability check of that block, which used the old custody columns. Fork choice rejects a block above its own slot (`ErrBlockTooEarly`) and ignores backward ticks, so a wall clock that steps back cannot put the raise slot at or below a block that was already checked with the old columns. `PeerDas` reads the fork-choice slot through a new `BlockGetter.Slot()` method. A node without a fork choice uses only the wall clock.
- The raise slot is written in the same transaction as the highest custody group count, and `Start` restores both from one read transaction. Neither stored value can decrease, and `SetCustodyRaiseSlot` does not lower the in-memory value either.
- When `Start` finds a stored count above `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` without a stored raise slot, it treats the restore as a raise: it sets the raise slot to the current slot + 1 with the same function and then writes it to the database. At that point the fork choice is still at its anchor slot, so the function uses the wall-clock slot when it is higher.
- `GetMyCustodyColumns` takes `SamplesPerSlot` from the injected beacon config instead of the global one, through the same helper as the raise check.

## Limitations

- A node that raised its count above `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT` while running v3.8.1, or `main` after #25187, has the stored count but no stored raise slot, and the database does not record when the raise happened. On the first start after the upgrade, `Start` uses the current slot + 1. The node stores the new columns from its real raise on, so it advertises less history than it has until the prune floor passes that slot, which takes about 18 days with the mainnet retention window (4096 epochs). A node that upgrades from v3.8.0 or older has the same trade-off: it has no stored count, and it records the current slot + 1 at its first increase that adds custody columns after the restart.
- After a restart, the fork choice starts again at its anchor slot, so its slot bounds only the blocks imported since the start. If the wall clock steps back across a restart, an increase before the clock catches up can still record a slot at or below a block that the previous run checked with the old columns. The restored raise slot is a lower bound, but it does not cover blocks above it.
- The spec allows lowering `earliest_available_slot` again as a backfill fills the gap. This PR does not do that.
- The other cases of #24787 (empty column store, bucket granularity, gaps inside the window, `ByRange` without `ResourceUnavailable`) are not covered.

## Tests

- `cl/das`:
  - `TestPeerDasCustodyRaiseMovesEarliestAvailableSlot`: an increase to `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT + 1` at slot 1000 moves `earliest_available_slot` to 1001, and a later `PruneBelow` keeps it there. It fails on `main` (expected 1001, actual 100). The count is the first one that adds a custody group, so the test also covers the boundary of the raise check.
  - `TestPeerDasCustodyRaiseWithinSampledColumnsKeepsEarliestAvailableSlot`: an increase to 8 keeps the prune floor.
  - `TestPeerDasRestoresCustodyRaiseSlot`: a new `PeerDas` over the same database restores the stored raise slot.
  - `TestPeerDasRestartAfterRaiseWithinSampledColumnsKeepsEarliestAvailableSlot`: after an increase to 8 and a restart, `earliest_available_slot` follows the prune floor. It fails if `UpdateValidatorsCustody` writes the slot of the call instead of the raise slot of the state, or if `Start` also treats a stored count of 8 as a raise.
  - `TestPeerDasStartRecordsRaiseSlotForCountStoredWithoutOne`: a stored count of 96 without a raise slot, restored at slot 5000, gives 5001, and a second restart at slot 9000 keeps 5001. Without the `Start` change it fails (expected 5001, actual 200).
  - `TestPeerDasStartInstallsRecordedRaiseSlotBeforeWritingIt`: `GetEarliestAvailableSlot` already returns the recorded raise slot when `Start` begins the database write.
  - `TestPeerDasReadsCustodyRaiseSlotAfterInstallingRaise`: the clock is read after the raised count is in the ENR. It fails if the slot is read before `SetCustodyGroupCount`.
  - `TestPeerDasCustodyRaiseAfterClockStepsBackIsAboveForkChoiceSlot`: a block at slot 1001 passes its availability check with the old columns while the clock and the fork-choice slot are at 1001. The clock steps back to 1000, and an increase to `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT + 1` follows. The block is no longer available, and `earliest_available_slot` is 1002. Without the fork-choice bound it fails (expected 1002, actual 1001).
  - `TestPeerDasStartRecordsRaiseSlotFromClockAheadOfForkChoice`: at `Start` the fork choice is still at its anchor slot (4000 here) and the clock is at 5000, so a stored count without a raise slot gives 5001. It fails if the raise slot uses only the fork-choice slot when a fork choice is set (actual 4001).
- `cl/das/state`: `TestSetCustodyGroupCountNeverLowersTheCustodyRaiseSlot` and `TestSetCustodyRaiseSlotNeverLowersIt`: a lower slot from a later raise or a restore keeps the higher one.
- `cl/persistence/beacon_indicies`: `TestCustodyRaiseSlotNeverDecreases`: writing a lower slot after a higher one keeps the higher one.
